The man had applied for a gun license, which prompted the police to search his home. The subsequent investigation revealed that the man was associated with right-wing extremists and violent circles. His DNA and a clear fingerprint were found on the remains of the exploded backpack. The morning after the incident, the perpetrator wrote a bragging post in an internet forum set up by the the right-wing Blood and Honour group. He was sentenced to four years in prison.

The perpetrator shouted something abusive about Polish people. When a Polish man confronted him, the perpetrator ran back to his girlfriend's house, got a knife, returned, and stabbed the victim four times. The victim died from the injuries sustained. The perpetrator had been brought up in a violent domestic setting, was in care between the ages of 9 and 16, was in 5 different foster homes, had never worked in his life, and had repeatedly committed offences of violence. The perpetrator was jailed for life.

A 58-year-old Imam was blinded after being attacked by a stranger in the mosque. The perpetrator had entered the premises and told the Imam he wished to convert to Islam before launching the assault. The perpetrator punched and rammed his fingers into the victim's eyes. He also used a key in the attack. The victim suffered heavy blood loss and required emergency surgery on both eyes, and lost sight on one of them. The attack happened in a period with a rise in Islamophobic attacks, which was suspected to be connected to two recent attempted Islamist terror attacks in London and Glasgow. A 43-year-old Irishman was later arrested. In court, he was found not guilty by reason of insanity. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

Eight Indian men who was attending a town festival were severely beaten by a mob of around 50 alledged neo-Nazis. The perpetrators were shouting right-wing extremist slogans like, “Foreigners out!” and “Germany for the Germans!”. The victims seeked shelter in a pizza parlor. The perpetrators attacked the restaurant, breaking the windows, and assaulted the victims again. All of the victims were injured, and two of them had to be treated in the hospital with severe facial injuries. Two perpetrators and two police officers were also injured. It was reported that the local authorities were warned in advance that neo-Nazis planned to disrupt the festival.

weapon_description: Broken bottle, wine bottle, and beating/kicking
description: A 26-year-old Sudanese man and his 39-year-old Egyptian work colleague were attacked while visiting a wine festival. In the afternoon, the victims were approached by a group of four young men who insulted them by saying, "N****r, piss off". After a short discussion, the victims decided to ignore the victims and enjoy the festival. When the victims were on their way home around 3 AM, the perpetrators reappeared shouting, "We are going to kill the blacks!". The Sudanese victim was brutally kicked and hit on the head with a wine bottle that shattered. The Egyptian victim tried to help his unconscious friend. He was attacked by the perpetrator who beat him and cut off his index finger with the broken bottle. The police were alerted, and the perpetrators were arrested.

A group of about fifteen masked people armed with bottles and batons from Nordic Resistance Movement [Swedish at the time] attacked a Young Left's anti-racist concert. The perpetrators attacked ten people who were standing on the outside. One person was knocked to the ground and kicked in the head while lying on the ground. Four people were taken to the hospital after blows to the head with batons, a broken bottle to the head, and wounds after broken glass.

A 32-year-old woman stabbed a 17-year-old boy while he was standing at a bus stop. The perpetrator missed the bus and was angry, and stabbed the victim in the chest and arm unprovoked. She had recently watched a TV program about the 9/11 terror attack. She told the victim: "You're all terrorists." Later, she told police: "I just stabbed a guy with the same colour of skin as a terrorist." In trial, the judge called the attack "completely unprovoked" and sentenced the perpetrator to six years in prison.

weapon_description: Molotov cocktails, chains, sticks, and stones
description: Four molotov cocktails were thrown at a Roma camp. When they hit the ground, the molotov cocktails caused a blaze but did not start a fire. Two days later, around 40 people attacked the camp again, this time with balaclavas and armed with chains, sticks, and stones. The local carabinieri were out patrolling and managed to stop the attack. A 40-year-old man was arrested and said he was part of a "spontaneous committee" of residents who were intolerant to the presence of Roma people in the town.

A 15-year-old boy, who was a former refugee from the Democratic Republic of the Congo, was verbally abused and stabbed by a white man. The attack happened during the day when the victim was headed back to class at his school after lunch. He was approached by the perpetrator, a stranger to the victim, who called him a "Black bastard", which he reacted to. They started fighting, and during the fight, the perpetrator pulled out a knife. The victim ran away but the knife was plunged into his back. The perpetrator fled the scene. The victim was rushed to hospital with stab wounds and hospitalized with a kidney injury. Police treated the attack as racially motivated. The main suspect was white and around 19 years old.

weapon_description: 14 litres of flammable liquid, a torch, four two-way radios, three gas guns, 3 gas cans, a blank gun, two brass knuckles, two iron chains, a metal cable, three batons, two wooden sticks, ten knives, two daggers, three bayonets, a utility knife, two crowbacks and more.
description: Eleven people aged between 19 and 32 affiliated with Forza Nuova, including a provincial leader, were arrested and charged with attempted arson and kidnapping. The police intervened when the group was organizing an attack on a social center. They planned to kidnap a person inside the building and burn the building down after the raid. The police were monitoring a meeting held in the home of the leader and arrested them when they begun boarding their cars to go to the center. The police seized 14 litres of flammable liquid, a torch, four two-way radios, three gas guns, 3 gas cans, a blank gun, two brass knuckles, two iron chains, a metal cable, three batons, two wooden sticks, ten knives, two daggers, three bayonets, a utility knife, two crowbacks and more. The investigation had been launched following an attack on the social center in February which caused minor damage to the building and arson attack against two cars near the center in July.
A Moroccan immigrant and several unidentified people were severely beaten by neo-Nazis and members of Golden Dawn. One of the victims was hospitalized.

Two men intervened when a Pakistani street vendor was racially insulted and attacked by two people. The two men were both stabbed and were in critical condition. One of the perpetrators was an "Ultras Guerrieri" [football supporters] known to the police.

The victim was together with other members from the Rättvisepartiet socialisterna [Justice Party Socialists], trying to get people to sign a campaign against Nazi violence. He was hit in the back of the head with an iron pipe and knocked to the ground. Three men then started to kick and punch him while he was lying on the ground. He was taken to the hospital for treatment.

Two Indian men were attacked by a group of around twenty teenagers. They chased the men up the street and attacked. One of the victims suffered a broken tooth and the other a broken collarbone. A bypasser intervened and took the victims in their car. When they were dropped off, one of the victims died of a heart attack triggered by the attack. Prior to the incident, some of the perpetrators had said that they wanted to "beat up a Paki." Three of the perpetrators pleaded guilty to manslaughter.

weapon_description: Nail bombs, bullets, swords, axes and knives
description: A 31-year-old man hid four home-made nailbombs underneath his five-year-old son's bed. The perpetrator's activities were uncovered after police conducted a search for child pornography at his flat and found 39,000 indecent images on his computers. Police also discovered an armoury of gun powder, fuses, live bullets, swords, axes, knives and a bayonet along with internet material on how to poison people and make bombs. It is believed he intented to target black and Asian people, European immigrants, Jews, Muslims and anyone he regarded as a political opponent with the bombs. The search of the flat also revealed anti-Semitic literature and photographs showing his admiration for Hitler and the Nazi cause. In addition, he had several notes, including one in which he wrote: 'Be under no illusion, we are at war. And it is a war we are losing badly.' and  'Unless we the British right stop talking of racial war and take steps to make it happen, we will never get back that which has been stolen from us' and 'I'm so sick and tired of hearing Nationalists talk of killing Muslims, of blowing up mosques, of fighting back. Only to see these acts of resistance fail to appear. The time has come to stop the talk and start to act.'  The perpetrator used to post on Blood & Honours webpages and after his arrest, members hailed him and compared him to the perpetrator behind the London bombings. Among the materials found at his residence were copies of Blood & Honour magazine. Also found among his own writings was the ‘14 Words’ slogan, which is popular with B&H and can be found in much of the organisation’s literature.

A group of eight to ten masked Italians armed with sticks and knives attacked three Romanians at a parking lot, known to be a squat place for immigrants. One of the victims was stabbed in the back and hit in the head. The other two victims suffered bruisings. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

The perpetrator, wearing a shirt with neo-Nazi symbol, stabbed an antifascist on the train. Several young antifascists were getting on the train following a counterdemonstration against Democracia Nacional, who were opposing immigration. When the perpetrator saw that several antifascists were going to board, he pulled out his 25 centimeter knife and hid it behind his back. One of the men who got on made remarks to the perpetrator about his shirt. The perpetrator then stabbed the victim, causing fatal injuries. Several young people and a security guard tried to catch the perpetrator. During the struggle, another young man was seriously injured and a third man suffered cuts to his fingers. The perpetrator was sentenced to a total of 26 years in prison: 19 for the crime of murder aggravated by ideological hatred and 7 for attempted murder. The murder was the most high-profile neo-Nazi hate crime of the first decade of the 21st century in Spain. It was also the first time that the Spanish justice applied the aggravating circumstance of ideological motives in a conviction

location: Headquarters of Esquerra Republicana de Catalunya
description: A homemade explosive device was set off outside the doors of the headquarters of Esquerra Republicana de Catalunya. The device (a container loaded with screws and small steel balls) did not cause any injuries but caused material damage to the gate and several cars parked nearby. The attack was only one in a series of attacks against this and other left-wing political parties in the area.

Around 25 people described as right-wing extremists attacked a group of Pakistani migrants in their home. The perpetrators gained entry to the residence by kicking in the door and breaking the windows. They used clubs, crowbars, and knives in the assault, seriously injuring five of the victims. The case is potentially linked to CaseID 2007-12-3.

Eight immigrants were attacked in their rented apartment by a large group of unidentified people, believed to be Greeks. The perpetrators broke into the apartment and beat the victims with batons and knives. All of the victims were injured, including a Pakistani man who was hospitalised in a critical condition. The attack, described as racist, was the fourth on immigrant homes in the past four months. A lawyer representing the Pakistanis said the attack was part of an organized series of hits and not an isolated incident. The case is potentially linked to CaseID 2007-12-1.

Arson attack against a family in an apartment block. The police believed the people were specifically targeted as the family was connected to left-wing movements and worked actively against racism and xenophobia. The names and images of the family had been posted on a right-wing site. Police assumed a right-wing motive and a connection with a previous extreme right attack on "Cyklopen" (a youth center).

The 25-year-old perpetrator attempted to enter the premises of a left-wing associated, but stabbed the victim twice when he was denied entry. The perpetrator was arrested and charged with attempted murder. The perpetrator was known in left-wing circles for belonging to an unnamed far-right political group and his clothes were decorated with neo-fascist symbols.

A 35-year-old man was arrested for being in possession of bomb making materials at his home. He had books and manuals containing 'recipes' to make bombs and detonators using household items such as weedkiller, lighter fluid and sugar. Officers found two tubs of sodium chlorate weedkiller and three bottles of lighter fluid, as well as fireworks, some of which had been tampered with. The police also discovered a significant amount of racist and far-right propaganda, as well as membership cards for groups such as the Ku Klux Klan, the November Ninth Society and the British People's Party. The perpetrator had harassed a mixed-race couple and left stickers on the gate of their home, one of them reading 'Only inferior white women date outside their race. Be proud of your heritage. Don't be a race-mixing slut', while another from the Combat 18 group said: 'It's our country. Let's win it back. Repatriation now.' The police also found a picture of him with another convicted plotter along with his prison address (CaseID: 2007-10-31). He was sentenced to six years in prison for the terror offence and a further 15 months for the harassment, giving him a total sentence of seven years and three months. The perpetrator was again arrested in 2019, accused of stirring up racial hatred by displaying neo-Nazi stickers. During this trial, he described himself as an "ethno-nationalist" and said he did not believe in "diversity or multiculturalism". He also denied the Holocaust took place and said he had been a member of the Ku Klux Klan.

A young Moroccan man was attacked by two Italian men during the Carnival. While playing football in the street, the victim was subjected to racial insults by the perpetrators. They then tripped him and proceeded to beat him. As a result, he sustained multiple injuries, including a broken hand.

A group of skinheads aged between 18 and 20 were arrested for throwing molotov cocktails against an abandoned farmhouse inhabited by immigrants. The bomb caught fire but was extinguished by the rain, causing only minor property damage. The four were described as not being an active part of the skinhead movement and were also involved in shooting towards a Nigerian with an airsoft gun (CaseID: 2018-2-22)

A 19-year-old man racially abused and stabbed two Polish mechanics to death with a screw driver. A 21-year-old man was co-accused but found not guilty. The perpetrator claimed he was “off his head” on alcohol and drugs at the time. The perpetrator was given two life sentences.

weapon_description: Pushing in front of train and beating/kicking
description: A 20-year-old German woman pushed a 19-year-old Angolan man in front of a train. The victim was standing at the train platform in the morning when he was approached and hit by the perpetrator. A couple of minutes later, when the train was entering the platform, the perpetrator pushed he victim onto the tracks while shouting, "shit n****r". With the help of two passer-bys, the victim managed to get of the tracks seconds before the train arrived. The engine driver saw the incident, and operated the emergency brake but said he would not have been able to stop the train in time. The victim was unharmed. The perpetrator was arrested on the station.

weapon_description: Hand grenade, bomb fuses, two automatic weapons, five pistols and revolvers, one rifle, 10 kilos ammunition, military sound bombs and some grenades
description: The police found a large number of weapons in properties belonging to some of the members of the Nordic resistance movement [Swedish at the time]. The police seized a hand grenade, bomb fuses, two automatic weapons, five pistols and revolvers, one rifle, 10 kilos ammunition, military sound bombs and some grenades. The trial resulted in a man being sentenced to two years and six months' imprisonment for, among other things, aggravated weapon crime and preparation for general destruction.

A 40-year-old man was fatally stabbed by his 22-year-old right-wing extremist neighbor following ongoing disputes over the perpetrator’s loud far-right music and political views. On the day of the attack, an argument between the two escalated into a fight, during which the victim fell down the stairs and sustained a head injury. Later that night, after returning from a bar crawl, the intoxicated perpetrator turned his music up loudly, prompting the victim to confront him briefly before returning to his apartment. The perpetrator then went upstairs and stabbed the victim twice in the stomach with a 40-centimeter bayonet, killing him. In court, the perpetrator admitted that their conflict stemmed from his far-right ideology and was sentenced to over eight years in prison for manslaughter.

Following claims that a Roma teenager had attempted to kidnap a baby, mobs targeted Roma communities with arson attacks. In this attack, molotov cocktails were thrown into a Roma settlement. Even though the bombs exploded, they allegedly did not set fire to the settlement as the attack happened just after a rainstorm. The attack happened in a period of several arson attacks on Roma settlements in different suburbs in Italy, and in a context of an increased anti-Roma rhetoric from Italian authorities (see e.g. caseID 2008-5-13-1).

Following claims that a Roma teenager had attempted to kidnap a baby, mobs targeted Roma communities with arson attacks. The perpetrators took to the streets chasing Romas out of three settlements. Molotov cocktails were thrown into the settlements which were largely destroyed by fire and more than 500 victims, half of whom were children, had to flee. The perpetrators burned Roma communities to the ground. There were no reports of human injuries. The attack happened in a period of several arson attacks on Roma settlements in different suburbs in Italy, and in a context of an increased anti-Roma rhetoric from Italian authorities (see e.g. caseID 2008-5-11-1).

The 39-year-old perpetrator was sentenced to 10 months in prison after racially insulting and assaulting a dark-skinned man. The perpetrator first shouted "sieg heil" and made the Hitler salute before he unprovokedly approached a man and said "what are you doing, you black skull, in my country?" Immediately after, perpetrator started beating and kicking the victim until he was unable to move on the ground. During the beating, he continued to make the Hitler salute. In the police car, the perpetrator continued his racist insults with phrases like "SRM [Swedish Resistance Movement], hate, hate, I hate all fucking blackheads."

A group of people tried to place an explosive device outside the entrance of a left-wing social centre. The perpetrators were quickly discovered, who fled the scene. The bomb was detonated some hundred meters away from the centre.

Two members of Nomad 88, aged 19 and 22, went on a shooting spree with the aim of ridding the suburbs of immigrants. They fired 35 submachine gun bullets at a group of young people, but no one was injured or killed in the incident. During the searches, the police seized a large arsenal, including 17 rifles and pistols, more than 9,050 cartridges, 13 magazines, grenades and equipment for explosive devices. Most of the weapons were stored in a van. In 2010, fourteen men between the ages of 18 and 35 belonging to Nomad 88 were tried. Twelve of them were sentenced, from two weeks probation to two and a half years for membership of the violent gang, and for arms possession. Nomad 88 was established in 2007 and by 2010, the group had dissolved. It's objective had been to "bring down the state, buy arms, create an army". The members planned "to control an area of ​​Paris" , "to attack kebab-type restaurants" , "to clean up mosques, synagogues and cities" and "to organize raids against political opponents."

A 30-year-old man, who was French with North-African background, was beaten by two men in a park. The two perpetrators had asked him if he was an Arab and what he thought of "the events in the former Yugoslavia" before beating him. The victim later described that they had attacked him when he told them that he was Muslim. The victim was unable to work for 21 days because of injuries from the attack. Police later arrested two suspects, and the victim recognized both of them. One of them an 18-year-old man who had a large quantity of neo-Nazi literature in his home. The perpetrators were aquitted in court.

An 18-year-old Nazi stabbed a 20-year-old leftist in the shoulder on a regional train. The two were seated near each other when the perpetrator, wearing an SS shirt, engaged in a conversation with the victim. The discussion escalated, and the attacker then stabbed the victim before leaving the train at the next station. The victim was hospitalized.

A 50-year-old lawyer shot towards an asylum seeker center six times with a rifle. A 16-year-old boy was struck and suffered severe injures. The perpetrator was sentenced as psychotic and criminally insane and therefore could not be sentenced. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

Two men tortured, killed and tried to cremate a 55-year-old man. Before the attack, the victim had been drinking with the two perpetrators, aged 18 and 21. The court found that the motive was premised on right-wing beliefs - the perpetrators despised the victim as he was an alcoholic, unemployed and a welfare recipient. On the night of the attack, the youngest perpetrator wore a T-shirt with a picture of Hitler's deputy, Rudolf Hess. The 18-year-old was found guilty of murder and sentenced to ten years juvenile imprisonment. The 21-year-old recieved nine years for aiding and abetting murder. The perpetrators both had prior criminal records. While in custody, the perpetrators continued to send each other 'Germanic greetings.'

A homless person was beaten to death by a neo-nazi. The perpetrator was on his way home from a Nazi demonstration under the motto "Death penalty for child molestors" organized by "Freie Kräfte Leipzig." The perpetrator had marched through the park and found the man sleeping on a bench and then started beating him. He left the scene, but returned later and continued beating the victim. The victim suffered severe head injuries and bruising all over his body and died from the injuries sustained the following month. The perpetrator was sentenced to eight years imprisonment.

The two perpetrators beat a 50-year-old man to death in a park by the train station. The victim was disabled and while he lived in a care facility, at the time he stayed on a park bench. The perpetrators repeatedly beat and kicked the victim and used a 5 kg garbage can to strike the victim in the head and upper body. The coroner testified that he had never seen a more violent act during his 40 years working. The prosecutor claimed that the motive was a 'deep inner disdain and contempt' for the victim who was a 'bum' in their eyes and a 'feeling of superiority.' The police found an extensive collection of right-wing propoganda on their cell phones. The youngest perpetrator, aged 24, was sentenced to life imprisonment. The eldest, aged 34. was sentenced to 12 years imprisonment and mandatory alcohol therapy. He was considered by the court to be less responsible for the murder due to his heavy drinking that day.

The perpetrator racially insulted the victim before slashing his throat with a knife. The victim was chatting with about six friends when a minicab pulled up at traffic lights. The passenger, who was arguing with the driver, exchanged words with the group before being driven away, calling the victim a 'f****** Paki.' The perpetrator returned and walked towards the victim before slashing his throat. The perpetrator was sentenced to life.

weapon_description: Beating/kicking with reinforced gloves and combat boots
description: A 20-year-old neo-nazi attacked an art student at a bus stop after he refused to give him a cigarette becuase he was a "hobby Nazi." The perpetrator punched the victim in the head. When he fell to the ground, the perpetrator kicked his head, stomach and genital area with his combat boots. When the victim stopped moving, the perpetrator stole his valuables. The victim died after choking on his own blood. The perpetrator was sentenced to eight years in yout prison for manslaughter. The perpetrator had a criminal record for racially motivated assault.

A group of three men attacked three foreign students. A fight erupted after a group of young men and women, including the three perpetrators (who had been drinking), began racially abusing the group of foreign students. One of the perpetrators asked a black student from South Africa ‘where are you from?’ before he tried to punch him, but missed. The student managed to run away and the group turned their attention to a student from Qatar, his cousin, and his friend, who had initially tried to hide from the gang inside a takeaway place. The Qatari student was punched in the face, knocking him to the ground. He initially regained consciousness and was held in a police van before being taken to hospital where it was discovered that he had fractured his skull and had suffered a brain haemorrhage. He died three days later in the hospital. His friend was hit over the head with a bottle and needed six stitches. A 22-year-old man was charged with manslaughter, a 19-year-old with wounding with intent to cause grievous bodily harm and a 21-year-old with racially aggravated assault.

A 46-year-old Norwegian-Somalian private taxi driver was killed after being shot at thirteen times. The 26-year-old perpetrator had written that he planned "to kill Muslims if the opportunity presented itself." The court weighted the fact that the perpetrator had "susbtantial activity and used strongly racist sentiments on the internet." The perpetrator was a member of a local shooting range. He claimed that he suffered a black out during the night of the killing. The court concluded that he was criminally insane and sentenced him to forced treatment at a mental health institution. He managed to escape, but was caught the same day.

A 48-year-old man of foreign origin was beaten unconscious by a 16-year-old in a racially motivated attack. While at a gas station with his son, the perpetrator passed by, gave a Nazi salute, and shouted racist slurs like "Heil Hitler" and "I hate people with dark skin." After the victim and his son returned outside, the perpetrator's brother, sitting in a car, made obscene gestures. Provoked, the victim asked for an apology, leading to a confrontation. As they argued, the perpetrator emerged, shouted for the victim not to touch his brother, and punched the victim, knocking him unconscious. Both the perpetrator and his brother joined in the attack before fleeing the scene. The victim suffered a broken nose, a concussion, facial cuts, and damaged teeth, and continued to experience dizziness and pain over a year later. The attacker was sentenced to 270 hours of community service.

A group of six men, aged between 23 and 40, had been out drinking and were driving around the area. When they pulled up outside a pub, the victim approached them and asked them for a light. One of the perpetrators got out of the car and chased the victim to his home nearby while yelling racist abuse at the black victim. The victim went into the house and returned with his brother, armed with a hammer and a machete. One of the other perpetrators then reversed the car into the victim, crushing him against the wall. The victim was taken to the hospital, where he was pronounced dead shortly after. Two of the perpetrators were EDL supporters and sentenced to 18 months imprisonment. The driver, aged 23, was sentenced to six years.

A 36-year-old Chinese man was attacked by a gang of youths, all of them minors. The victim was waiting at a bus stop, when the perpetrators surrounded him, insulting him "Dirty Chinese". The victim was hit in the face by one of the perpetrators. He suffered a broken nose. Two of the perpetrators also had a knife and a hammer although those were not used in the attack.

Members of the Nordic Resistance Movement [Swedish at the time] attacked several left-wing activists in the city center. A person from Rättvisepartiet socialisterna [The Socialist Justice Party] was attacked at the central train station, a person belonging to the group Ingen människa är illegal  [No humans are illegal] was attacked on the train and when a member of Socialist Justice Party attempted to intervene, the perpetrators broke his nose. Another activst from The Socialist Justice Party was attacked on the street. He was knocked to the ground, beaten, and kicked.

A 44-year-old man was arrested at the train station carrying component parts for two, viable, improvised incendiary devices. The perpetrator was on his way to meet a woman when he was arrested, after drinking and behaving agressive in public. In a house search, the police found amassed components and materials, information on how to make devices, a handwritten booklet called: "Waffen SS UK Members Handbook" and far right extremist material. The perpetrator had dated online, but several women had refrained from meeting him due to his racist views. One woman said he told her he had been on National Front marches, and had knowledge of firearms. The perpetrator was a follower of the Blood & Honour network. He was unemployed and lived with his mother. Prosecutors alleged that he wanted to target those he thought "non-British."

Around 60 anti-racists had met at a square to hand our flyers. When they heard that Nazis were arranging a march close to the square, the victim and others headed in their direction. When they were on their way, around 30 Nazis started chasing them and four to five of them caught up with the victim. The victim received several blows to the face and collapsed. He was then kicked in the head and witnesses said the Nazis jumped on his head. The victim and another anti-racist were taken to the hospital. The Nazis belonged to the group  "Salemfonden" who were behind the Info 14 network that handed out flyers before marches. Salemfonden arranged a march every december in commemoration of the death of a young neo-nazi. Every year between 1000 and 2000 people took part in this demonstration, including neo-Nazis from Denmark, Finland, Norway, Estonia, Russia, Poland, England, France, Belgium, Holland, Switzerland, Italy and Germany.

Arson attack on activity house for left-wing youths. The attack was carried out at the same time as a planned event, but which was cancelled. The entire building burnt down, but as the premises were empty at the time, no one was injured in the fire.

The perpetrator stabbed a police officer known for his work against right-wing extremism at his home. According to the victim, the perpetrator shouted 'Du linkes Bullenschwein, du trampelst nicht mehr auf den Gräbern unserer Kameraden herum' [You leftist "bullpig", you are no longer going to step on our comrade's graves] before attacking him. The knife barely missed his heart and the victim survived. The victim repeatedly prevented right-wing extremists from marching in the city of Passau or restricted their public appearance through a large police presence and numerous controls. It was speculated that the phrase related to an earlier incident in which the police director had ordered the grave of a Nazi to be opened after after images that the coffin had been adored with a Reich flag, which was found during the inquiry. The perpetrator was never identified. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

Two skinheads in their thirties stabbed an anti-fascist. They asked him if he was a 'redskin' and to remove anti-fascist patches from his clothes. When he answered 'no', they stabbed him in the thigh and fled the scene. The victim recieved five stitches at the hospital.

A 16-year-old anti-fascist was stabbed in the back following an argument with a group of around 10 individuals, allegedly linked to neo-Nazi ideology. An anti-fascist group reported that the young victim was hospitalized due to the attack inflicted by a person with neo-Nazi beliefs. The confrontation began when the victim and his friends confronted the perpetrators, who were dressed in neo-Nazi aesthetics, leading to an argument that escalated into violence. One of the perpetrators stabbed the victim in the back, causing serious injuries. The anti-fascist group claimed that the attackers were affiliated with a legalized fascist organization, such as "Democracia Nacional."

An asylum seeker from Somalia was attacked by three youths outside a store. One of the youths punched him and thereafter kicked him while he was on the groud. The victim suffered several injuries and recieved surgery on his arm. The court described the incident as 'brutal' and racially motivated. One perpetrator, a 17-year-old boy, said he had been the one who used the physical violence. Due to his age he recieved 30 days imprisonment and 150 hours of community service.
A group of people threw three molotov cocktails and stones against the windows of a former school housing fifty families. They landed on the balcony and did not cause any damage.

weapon_description: Melee weapons, including a wooden club and telescopic baton, and beating/kicking
description: Ten to twelve masked people armed with melee weapons, including a wooden club and a telescopic baton, beat and kicked four people from Revolutionär kommunistisk ungdom [Revolutionary communist Youth] outside their party premises. Two of the victims were hospitalized, one with a broken elbow from being hit with a baton. The police were unable to find the perpetrators. The victims believed that the attack was premeditated.

The 25-year-old victim was walking to a fast food restaurant when the perpetrator slashed his neck open with a knife, leaving a 18cm-long wound. CCTV cameras captured the perpetrator "celebrating" his attack and he later told a friend he had "done a Paki." The perpetrator claimed he was robbing the victim. The court convicted him of racially motivated murder and of attempting to pervert the course of justice after he had burned his clothes after the attack. He was also found guilty of a racially motivated breach of the peace at an Asian takeaway nearby that night, by threatening staff and squirting them with food sauce. The victim, who was due to become a father for the first time, was in Glasgow to sit his captain's exams at the city's Nautical College.

Two men, aged 29 and 32, shot at a mosque and tried to set it on fire with a container filled with petrol and two Molotov cocktails. The arson attack failed because one perpetrator burnt himself while trying to ignite the petrol container. The fire was extinguished by the chairman of the mosque. The police caught the two men, who both confessed. They publicly apologised to the mayor and announced an apology to the local Turkish Community. They explained that they had watched a football game on TV that evening and were frustrated about the defeat of their team; they both got drunk and attacked the mosque to ‘let off steam’. The public prosecutor considered the offence as a ‘spontaneous’ and hence not politically motivated act, arguing that the perpetrators were not affiliated with any extreme right-wing group. While the police, who also found illegal guns in the perpetrators’ homes, did not assume a xenophobic or Islamophobic motivation, the question has been raised as to why the perpetrators picked the mosque for ‘letting off steam’.

A group of five to six men began to insult a Senegalese man and make fun of his car, saying things like, ‘Shitty n*****, look what a crap car you have’. The perpetrators struck him in the face with a beer bottle when he got out of the car and suffered permanent loss to his sight on his left eye. The main perpetrator was sentenced to four years in prison for racially motivated attack.

The victim, a professional dancer, suffered permanent disabilities after a brutal assault by around 30 neo-Nazis near Kiel's town hall. Leaving work with colleagues, he was struck unexpectedly with a wooden baton by one of the perpetrators, a politician from the party "Nationaldemokratische Partei Deutschlands" (NPD), sustaining a double skull base fracture that caused irreversible balance disorders and numbness on one side of their body, ending their career. The attack occurred during the neo-Nazi group "Aktionsgruppe Kiel"’s attempt to disrupt an anti-racism event.

Police officers were attacked in Wittenberge when they tried to take action against an illegal demonstration by the neo-Nazi scene. The officers were attacked with stones and filled plastic bottles from around 65 people at the demonstration. One police officer suffered multiple fractures of his lower jaw.

Four masked people attacked survivors of a concentration camp who had gathered to remember their liberation. The attackers screamed 'Heil Hitler!' and 'This way for the gas!' at ten elderly Italian men and women. They fired shot from airguns at a group of 15 French survivors. One suffered a head wound while another was injured by a shot in the neck. The four perpetrators managed to escape.

weapon_description: 50 improvised explosive devices (IEDs) approximately 40 knives, more than 30 guns, a cross bow and arrows
description: A 39-year-old man was arrested after the police discovered 12 firearms and 54 improvised explosive devices, including nail bombs and a booby-trapped cigarette packet at his home. The forensic searches took several days to complete and led to the recovery of more than 50 improvised explosive devices (IEDs), approximately 40 knives, a cross bow and arrows and more than 30 guns in total. Further explosive material found included weedkiller and hydrogen peroxide. Although the perpetrator did not have a clear target for his weaponry, the police found a list of names, addresses and personal details of four people at his home, including that of a woman who had featured on a documentary on the July 7 bombings as a neighbour of one of the bombers. He had joined the BNP in 2007 and was listed as having "gold" membership of the BNP and a copy of its magazine Hope and Glory were found at his home. The perpetrator was a former soldier who worked as a bus driver.  He had manufactured the explosives at the home where he lived with his mother. He was sentenced to 11-years-imprisonment

Unknown assailants attempted to set fire to a makeshift mosque in Athens, injuring five Bangladeshi migrants. The attackers broke the windows of a basement flat used as a mosque, threw gasoline inside, and ignited it. Four victims suffered respiratory issues, while one sustained burns. All were treated at the hospital. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

A 41-year-old man and his 18-year-old son were arrested after raids in their homes. The police found ricin, said to be 6,000 times more toxic than cyanide. The man had made the ricin and recruited his soon to help run Aryan Strike Force, which idiolised Hitler. He dismissed other extreme groups as weak and gutless. ASF was said to have recruited some 350 people worldwide online. It was believed 'the  purpose ... was the creation of an international Aryan group who would establish white supremacy in white countries.' The group had not drawn up a list of targets but the perpetrator had discussed poisoning Muslims' water supplies with an avowed Nazi in Serbia, as well as emailing other ASF members about posting cockroaches through letterboxes of Asian restaurants and businesses to start infestations and for their closure. Although the hatred was often directed towards Muslims and ethnic minorities, the group's propaganda often attacked 'Zionist governments.' The perpetrator wrote on an internet forum: 'The Jew is the Aryan's sworn enemy above all.'The perpetrator pleaded guilty to producing a chemical weapon, preparing acts of terrorism, three counts of possessing material useful to commit acts of terror and possessing a prohibited weapon and was jailed for 10 years.

Two boys were attacked when leaving the social center "La Strada" after attending a rock concert. Two boys dressed in black attacked them while screaming "comunisti di merda, voi ei vostri centri sociali" [Communists of shit, you and your social centers]. They beat the two boys and stabbed one of them in the thigh. The victims managed to get to the hospital and one of the victims recieved eight stitches.

weapon_description: 300 weapons and 80 bombs, including pipe bombs, rocket launchers, grenades, and firearms
description: 32 people were questioned by the police and at least 22 properties searched after the police uncovered a network of suspected far-right extremists with access to 300 weapons and 80 bombs. The police suspected that the bombs were to be used in a bombing campaign against mosques as detectives seized maps and plans of mosques from the homes of suspected far-right supporters. They found a British National party membership card and right-wing literature in one of the suspects home. The arrests were linked to other arrests in Europe, New Zealand and Australia.

A pregnant Egyptian woman was stabbed to death in a court where the alleged attacker was appealing a conviction for insulting the victim by calling her an “Islamist” and “terrorist”.  Both her and her unborn child died following the attack. Her husband was injured when a police offer shot him, mistaking him for the attacker. The perpetrator was a German with Russian origins.

A 40-year-old Polish man, who was homeless, was murdered by a man and a woman on the street. Unprovoked, the perpetrators had attacked the victim with punches and kicks. He was kicked while lying on the ground, his throat was stamped on, and he was dragged around on the ground. His stomach was "jumped on like a trampoline." After the attack, the perpetrators robbed the victim of a few pence he had in his pockets. The victim suffered brain injuries, a fractured nose and ribs, and inhalation of blood to the lungs, leading to his death about an hour after the attack. Police believed the attack to be racially motivated due to its' unprovoked nature and remarks allegedly shouted at the scene, like: "Go back to your own country, you’re not wanted in Ireland" and “Foreign bastards, you’re going to pay." The court found the perpetrators guilty of murder, and sentenced them to 11 and 14 years in prison.

A 22-year-old man was violently attacked by four Neo-Nazis, aged 20 to 26, due to his political orientation. The incident began with an altercation between the attackers and a group of ten leftist individuals, including the victim. When the victim attempted to flee, he was brutally beaten, including a "curb kick" inspired by the movie American History X, leaving him with a brain damage and several cuts and bruises. The attackers repeatedly called him "Zecke" (a slur for leftists) during the assault. Police intervention stopped the violence. In court, it was revealed the attackers acted out of anger, intending to kill their perceived political opponent. The 26-year-old received a prison sentence of five years and six months for attempted murder and grievous bodily harm, while two accomplices, aged 21 and 23, were sentenced to two years each for grievous bodily harm.

Around three in the morning, a 21-year-old man in a group of five skinheads began to kick a homeless man sleeping in a photo booth in the head. The blows caused a head injury and hemorrhage that left the victim in a coma. He spent 541 days in the hospital and almost four years later, he suffered a 60% disability. During trial, two of the defendants lawyers, a 90-year-old man, said homeless people were 'cancers of society that should be extirpated' and 'parasites.' One of the perpetrators was a member of Alianza Nacional. The people in the group were aged between 20 and 29. Two of the perpetrators were sentenced to 10 years and 12 years, while the others were released.

According to witnesses, two skinheads threw two paper hombs [type of firecrackers] on a street known to be a popular meeting place for the LGBTQ+ community. They threw the paper boms in the middle of a large crowd. One person was slightly injured by splinters. A motorbike caught fire and there was a small crater left in the asphalt.

Two Iranian men were attacked by three individuals—two men, aged 26 and 30, and a 26-year-old woman—at a subway station at night. The incident began when one of the perpetrators sprayed Coca-Cola on the victims, leading to a confrontation. The 26-year-old attacker kneeled and headbutted one of the victims, knocking him unconscious. The other victim was assaulted by all three attackers. As the victims attempted to escape onto an arriving train, the perpetrators followed them, continuing the assault with beating, kicking, and harassment. One victim was hospitalized with facial injuries and shoulder fractures, while the other sustained less serious injuries. The perpetrators were sentenced to prison for insults and bodily harm.

A group of around 15 people belonging to CasaPound attacked a group of anti-fascists tearing down their posters. The perpetrators screamed that 'the neighborhood is ours' and attacked the victims with clubs and sticks. One person was severly injured and needed medical care.

According to investigations and interviews with the perpetrator conducted by a Swedish professor, the perpetrator was out looking for victims when he spotted a parked car with a foreigner and a Swedish woman. He despised women who 'betrayed their own race' by engaging in mixed-race relationships. He fired multiple shots towards the car, killing the woman and seriously injuring the man. The suspected perpetrator, born in 1972, went on a shooting spree between 2003 and 2010  inspired by lone actor no. 54 where he targeted blacks, Muslims and Romas in Malmö. He was arrested in 2010 and sentenced to life imprisonment in 2012 for homicide and attempted murder for other cases. It is believed the perpetrator fired shots against what he believed to be the mans apartment a few months later (CaseID: 2010-3-12). See lone actor no.56 for other cases by the same perpetrator.

The perpetrator fired multiple shots through the bathroom window of an apartment where a 28-year-old man resided. The resident was not home at the time of the attack. The perpetrator, born in 1972, went on a shooting spree between 2003 and 2010 inspired by lone actor no. 54 where he targeted blacks, Muslims and Romas in Malmö. He was arrested in 2010 and sentenced to life imprisonment in 2012 for homicide and attempted murder for other cases. There is limited information about the case. It is believed he shot towards the same apartment a few months later (CaseID: 2010-12-31). See lone actor no.56 for other cases by the same perpetrator.

weapon_description: Iron bars, heavy steel profiles, stones, bottles, wooden slats, fireworks and beating/kicking
description: During a match between the left-wing football club Roter Stern Leipzig (RSL) and FSV Brandis, around 50 neo-Nazis launched a violent attack on RSL players, officials, and fans. The masked perpetrators stormed the field, throwing fireworks, stones, and bottles into the crowd before chasing and beating victims with iron bars, steel profiles, and wooden slats. They shouted slurs like "Shitty Zecken" and "Shitty Reds." Three people were seriously injured, including one with a broken arm and another with a shattered cheekbone. RSL officials believed the attack was premeditated due to the heavy weapons used. One attacker was linked to the right-wing extremist group "Terror Crew Muldental," which was later investigated for criminal activity aimed at using violence against political opponents.

An 18-year-old member of the neo-Nazi group "Freie Kräfte Schwalm-Eder" (FKSE) attacked a police officer on duty, after a fight had broken out. The victim was handcuffing another neo-Nazi when the perpetrator kicked the victim under the chin. The victim suffered a broken jaw and cheekbone during the incident. The perpetrator was sentenced to 15 months in juvenile prison.

A 24-year-old former skinhead attacked and almost killed a 26-year-old man of Kosovar origin at a nightclub. The perpetrator had been in the company of a gang wearing t-shirts with far-right slogans. The perpetrator praised Hitler in front of the victim, and the victim had told him to "forget Hitler, he's dead". The perpetrator was outraged and took out a switchblade, which he slit the throat of the victim with. When the police arrived, the perpetrator was reportedly laughing by the bleeding victim. Before being arrested, he had asked a friend to go to his house and hide books about the Third Reich. The victim was critically injured. His carotid artery and several nerves were severed, and he lost a lot of blood. He survived the attack. The perpetrator was sentenced to 11 years in prison.

The perpetrator shot through the window of an Islamic prayer centre and a person who was praying inside was injured by glass splinters. On the same street, the perpetrator fired multiple shots towards an apartment. The perpetrator, born in 1972, went on a shooting spree between 2003 and 2010 inspired by lone actor no. 54 where he targeted blacks, Muslims and Romas in Malmö. He was arrested in 2010 and sentenced to life imprisonment in 2012 for homicide and attempted murder for other cases. See lone actor no.56 for other cases by the same perpetrator.

A group of punks were severely beaten by leading members of the neo-Nazi clan who unofficially had ruled the small town of Colditz since the early 2000s. The perpetrators kicked the heads of the victims while they were lying on the ground. Two of the attacked suffered traumatic brain injuries. The N. family, consisting of a father and his sons, had transformed Colditz into a neo-Nazi stronghold, for around 20 years committing severe criminal activities, including drug trafficking and violence against political opponents.The N. family created a community network of neo-Nazis who regularly terrorized and beat up political opponents and other people who were viewed as unwanted, according to their right-wing extremist ideology (see CaseID 2015-4-11-1 and 2016-10-0, the other incidents do not meet the inclusion criteria). The N. family was arrested in 2023 after the police found crystal meth worth half a million euro, a cannabis plantation with 2600 plants, seven weapons and 32.000 euro in cash.

weapon_description: One mortar bomb, three submachine guns, one revolver, 10 pistols and one stun gun
description: Three young neo-Nazis, two men and one woman, were arrested following the discovery of an arsenal of weapons. Police found one mortar bomb, three submachine guns, one revolver, 10 pistols, and one stun gun. The perpetrators were suspected members of an extreme right-wing group that primarily disseminated racist and neo-Nazi ideology through social networks on the Internet. Nazi flags, neo-Nazi literature, and clothing were also found in their homes. The arrests came as a result of a routine monitoring operation conducted by units focusing on violent youth gangs.

About eight neo-Nazis disrupted a birthday party at a bar and violently attacked the participants. The perpetrators and the birthday party were at the same bar, but did not know each other. One eyewitness said "When they [the perpetrators] came into the bar, I had the impression of a uniform group - strictly parted hair, waxed. They made a right-wing, if not extremely right-wing, impression on me." The perpetrators shouted "Heil Hitler" among other things, and did the Hitler hand salute. To deafen the music of the birthday party, they loudly chanted Nazi songs. When one victim, the birthday boy, tried to stop the perpetrators from disturbing, he and friends who came to help were beaten and kicked so badly that they had to be hospitalized. One perpetrator stomped violently with one foot on a victim's head, which was lying face down on the ground, causing multiple fractures of the nasal bone and both eye sockets. Three people from the birthday party were injured, as well as a waiter who tried to intervene. Two of the victims were seriously injured. Two of the perpetrators were local RFJ officials (FPÖ youth organization). At least one of the perpetrators was later involved in an attack on a Green Party MP and his body guard (see CaseID 2010-6-23).

On New Year's morning, at around 3 AM, two 16-year-old leftists were insulted as "Scheiß-Zecken [slur for leftists]" by a group of right-wing extremists. One of the perpetrators punched one of the victims in the face. Even when the victim was lying on the ground, several of the perpetrators kicked him so hard that he lost consciousness. Both victims had to be taken to hospital by ambulance and treated as inpatients due to their injuries. One of the victims suffered a broken jaw as a result of the attack.

A 37-year-old Egyptian man was violently attacked by a group of young men near a gay bar. The group of 20-year-olds shouted racial and homophobic insults, including "Dirty Arab, dirty n*****, f*****," as they brutally beat the victim. He was hospitalized with serious injuries, and doctors gave him a 30-day recovery prognosis. This case is linked to caseID 2010-1-1-3.

A 37-year-old Ethiopian man was attacked by a group of young men performing fascist salutes and singing extremist songs, while also throwing firecrackers. When the victim approached them to ask them to stop throwing the firecrackers near his girlfriend, he was brutally beaten, sustaining multiple broken bones. Doctors gave him a 30-day recovery prognosis. This case is linked to caseID 2010-1-1-2.

An attempted arson attack was thwarted when a 30-year-old Black woman returned home with her two children to find her apartment soaked in petrol, the gas line to the stovetop severed, and two used matchsticks on the floor. Fortunately, the fire and explosion the perpetrators had intended did not occur. Had it been successful, the explosion could have destroyed the entire apartment block, which houses multiple families. According to police, the attack had the potential to cause significant harm and is believed to have been motivated by racism and xenophobia.

A 26-year-old left-wing militant was attacked by three men, believed to be affiliated with the neo-fascist movement. The perpetrators recognized the victim as a left-wing activist and followed him onto a bus, where he was accompanied by three women. Shortly after, they began shouting insults at him, before striking him with a brass knuckle on the forehead and punching him in the ear. The bus driver stopped and opened the doors, allowing the attackers to flee. One of the perpetrators wore a hoodie with "skinhead" emblazoned on it, while another wore a baseball cap featuring a stylized double-bitted axe. The victim was hospitalized with a forehead injury.

Three migrants were injured by two young Italian men who shot at them with an air rifle, leaving one of the victims seriously wounded. Such attacks are not uncommon in the area surrounding the town, where thousands of migrants are exploited by the mafia to harvest fruit. In response to the attack, a revolt broke out, with thousands of migrants marching through the town armed with sticks and stones, burning and damaging cars and businesses. This case is linked to caseID 2010-1-9-2.

Throughout the day, residents of the town participated in a "migrant hunt" in the surrounding area, following a revolt by thousands of migrants. The migrants had marched through the town armed with sticks and stones, burning and damaging cars and businesses. The local mafia, the 'Ndrangheta', played a key role in organizing and leading this "counter-revolt." They shot at, beat with sticks, and chased down migrants they encountered, also setting fire to shelters. Notably, two migrants were shot in the legs during the violence. This case is linked to caseID 2010-1-6-1.

Unknown perpetrators shot two 9mm bullets through the window of an anti-fascist housing project and cultural center. The projectiles hit the ceiling of an illuminated room in the living area of the building. The person who was inside the room at time, was unharmed. There had been several right-wing threats and attacks against the housing project, as well as other anti-fascist and alternative institutions, recently (cases do not meet the inclusion criteria). The residents of the housing project suspected that the perpetrators were members of the right-wing extremist group "Aktionsgruppe Kiel", which is closely linked to the “Nationaldemokratische Partei Deutschlands”. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

At around 1 AM, two punks suddenly heard someone shouting "Fucking punks, you're about to get a punch in the face." Then four masked men dressed in black ran towards them from a park and blocked their way. One of the victims was punched in the face. When the other victim intervened, three of the perpetrators attacked him with punches and kicks. One of the perpetrators finally attacked one of the victims with a cutter knife and injured his forearm. The unknown perpetrators then flee. The victim was admitted to the hospital with a severely bleeding cut. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

In the early hours of the morning, a group of alternatives was attacked by seven right-wing extremists. A 23-year-old victim is hit on the head with a beer bottle and fell to the ground. The other victims managed to escape. The perpetrators surround the victim and beat him. The victim was injured in the head and had to seek medical treatment. Among the attackers were active right-wingers from a local neo-Nazi group.

Three masked people from the right-wing extremist scene attacked a 20-year-old man in a bar. The perpetrators got into an argument with the victim and his group. One perpetrator asked whether he was an "enemy of the Nazis." The victim replied "Yes, and you?", and the situation escalated. The group to which the victim belonged then tried to leave to avoid an argument. According to eyewitnesses, the perpetrators chased the group and threw the victim to the ground. Then one of the perpetrators kicked him several times in the face. The victim was taken to the hospital by ambulance. He suffered unspecified facial injuries described as severe, a laceration on the upper eyelid, and several bruises, according to the police.

A gang of youths set fire to lodgings occupied by ten Bangladeshi migrants, who were sleeping inside at the time of the attack. The police drew up charges against twelve youths aged between 14 and 19, and one 23-year-old man, for an arsonist, racially-motivated attack. There is limited information about injuries.

Three young men were attacked by four hooded assailants armed with knives and glass bottles as they were leaving the left-wing social center "La Strada." The perpetrators struck the victims with the bottles and knives, leaving them hospitalized with multiple knife wounds and injuries from the bottles used as blunt instruments. The social center "La Strada" alleges that the attackers are linked to the far right. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

A 41-year-old man of Algerian origins was attacked with a knife by three unknown people, two men and a woman, on a tram in the afternoon. When the victim boarded the tram, the perpetrators immediately insulted the victim with xenophobic remarks. After an argument, the male perpetrators attacked the victim with a knife. The victim was able to take the knife from the perpetrator's hand. While defending himself, the victim suffered a minor injury to his hand.

According to the police, two German citizens were victims of dangerous bodily harm that was directed against the left. Two suspects were identified. No further details are available. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

A 17-year-old walked past a group of about 15 people on his way home in the evening. The victim heard the perpetrators say "There's a Zecke [slur for leftist]!", whereupon he was surrounded by the group. One of the perpetrators took a knuckleduster out of his pocket and hit the victim several times in the face and back. The victim tried to escape, but was caught, pushed to the ground and hit in the face again. The state security police investigated the incident.

A 27-year-old teacher was attacked by two perpetrators while she was entering her car. The perpetrators immobilized her and engraved two swastikas on her arm. The police said they believed the teacher was targeted because she had offered Greek language lessons to the children of immigrants.

A 19-year-old member of the “Antifaschistischen Linken Fürth” (ALF) was beaten up by four members of the neo-Nazi scene, aged 20 to 29. The victim was with fellow ALF members when they encountered the perpetrators. The perpetrators started bullying the leftists and called for reinforcements. The leftists fled, but the victim was caught up by the perpetrators who pulled him to the ground and kicked him ten to twenty times, including in the head. Three of the perpetrators were committed members of the right-wing extremist groups "Freie Netz Süd" and "Bürgerinitiative Soziales Fürth". The main perpetrator was sentenced to prison for dangerous bodily harm.

The house of a 48-year-old anti-fascist activist was subjected to an arson attack during the night. A Molotov cocktail was thrown at the house while the victim’s wife and three children were sleeping inside. The victims managed to escape and put out the fire. Four members of the group "Anti-Antifa Wetzlar", aged 17 to 23, were arrested. Two of them admitted that they had carried out the attack. The perpetrators were charged with serious arson attack and attempted murder.

At around 3:30 AM, two well-known neo-Nazis forced their way into the apartment of a former comrade who had left the right-wing scene and co-founded a punk band. For over an hour and a half, the perpetrators repeatedly maltreated, threatened, beat and kicked the victim. The victim's girlfriend was held down by force and prevented from intervening or getting help. The reason for the attack was an unpublished anti-Nazi song by the victim's band, which had become known in the local neo-Nazi scene. The victim suffered bruises and contusions and had to be treated in hospital as an inpatient. His girlfriend suffered bruises.

Five Kurdish man were attacked by four young Italian men. The victims were playing football. The perpetrators stated that they had no right to play and proceeded to beat them up with metal bars and baseball bats. The victims were severely injured and hospitalised.

The perpetrator shot through the window of the apartment of a person he had targeted earlier (CaseID: 2009-10-23). Shots were also fired against a glass balcony nearby, but the perpetrator was only charged with the first incident. The perpetrator, born in 1972, went on a shooting spree between 2003 and 2010 inspired by lone actor no. 54 where he targeted blacks, Muslims and Romas in Malmö. He was arrested in 2010 and sentenced to life imprisonment in 2012 for homicide and attempted murder. See lone actor no.56 for other cases by the same perpetrator.

A group of 15 to 20 people attacked a bar owned by two Bengali brothers. Four people were injured in the attack, including  one of the owners, who was beaten with wooden bats and had to have stitches in his mouth, head, and arm. One customer’s nose was broken and another suffered a head injury. The Rome juvenile court prosecutor charged three teenagers with crimes, including assault, with a racial aggravation.

The perpetrator shot towards the police station. Two bullets were found in the window, which had bullet-proof glass. There were found 31 cartridge casings from at least five different weapons. However, during trial, it was claimed that the perpetrator had placed the casings on the site to mislead the investigations. The perpetrator, born in 1972, went on a shooting spree between 2003 and 2010 inspired by lone actor no. 54 where he targeted blacks, Muslims and Romas in Malmö. He was arrested in 2010 and sentenced to life imprisonment in 2012 for homicide and attempted murder for other cases. See lone actor no.56 for other cases by the same perpetrator.

weapon_description: Head beat against metal pole and beating/kicking
description: Four alternative youths on their way home at nighttime were suddenly yelled at by a group of around ten right-wing extremists, who shouted, "There are the Zecken [slur for leftists]!" Then the perpetrators ran towards the victims. A 20-year-old was caught up with was repeatedly beaten and kicked by several perpetrators. They also hit his head against a metal pole. One of the perpetrators also asked the victim about an Antifa flag hanging in a window of his apartment: "If it isn't taken down tomorrow, this kind of thing will happen more often!" The victim suffered a bleeding cut on his right temple, a traumatic brain injury, as well as bruises and hematomas.

Before the verdict in a famous neo-Nazi court case was announced, a large group of people from the right-wing extremist milieu attacked people attending the trial and injured several of them. A 21-year-old leftist woman had to be treated in the hospital as an outpatient. The police, who arrived after the attacks, arrested two of the perpetrators and began investigations for dangerous bodily harm.

location: Facoltà di Giurisprudenza, Università Tor Vergata
description: Around forty people attacked a group of students protesting against a CasaPound gathering at the university. Three people were hospitalized and in serious condition. There is limited information about this case.

The perpetrator shot multiple times towards the car which two men of foreign descent were sitting in. The victims had taken a note of the perpetrator as he appeared to walk around in circles around their car while they sat waiting for their friend. He suddenly pulled out his pistol and fired multiple shots towards the car. One of the victims was struck in the arm, but they both survived the attack. The perpetrator, born in 1972, went on a shooting spree between 2003 and 2010 inspired by lone actor no. 54 where he targeted blacks, Muslims and Romas in Malmö. He was arrested in 2010 and sentenced to life imprisonment in 2012 for homicide and attempted murder. See lone actor no.56 for other cases by the same perpetrator.

Around 40 members of CasaPound attacked left-wing militants at the university while they were distributing flyers that criticized the activities of an association linked to CasaPound. The perpetrators beat, kicked, and struck the victims with blunt instruments. Six students and one university employee were hospitalized with various injuries, including broken noses, broken arms, head injuries, and bruising.

According to the police, a German was the victim of dangerous bodily harm that was directed against the left. A suspect had been identified. No further details are available. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

A group of five to six neo-Nazis attacked and injured two women and a man, aged 23 to 25, in a subway station at night. The victims were initially harassed and insulted with anti-Semitic language by one of the perpetrators in the subway. The other perpetrators joined in the altercation. When the victims left the subway, the male victim was hit on the head with a bottle by the perpetrators. The two female victims were hit on the head and shins and had to seek medical treatment. The perpetrators were able to escape undetected. State security took over the investigation.

A 47-year-old Albanian homeless man was attacked by two young men, aged 19 and 21. The perpetrators threatened the victim before beating him, also using a belt. Although the victim refused hospitalization, paramedics treated his injuries at the scene. The carabinieri later located the attackers, who had fled. Both perpetrators had shaved heads, and one of them identified himself as "a true fascist." They were part of a larger group of seven young men, though five had fled before the attack occurred.

Two leftist youths were attacked by several neo-Nazis. After a political argument, the perpetrators beat one of the victims to the ground and blinded the other victim with pepper spray. The attack continued with beating and kicking while the victims were laying on the ground. One of the victims had to be treated in the hospital with a suspected cerebral hemorrhage. Passer-byers and the police had to stop the violence. Five neo-Nazis, among them members of "Kameradschaft Aachener Land" (KAL) and "Nationaldemokratische Partei Deutschlands" (NPD), were taken into custody.

A group of young people threw several Molotov cocktails at the entrance door of a mosque. The attack occurred on a busy day when many people were at the mosque. One of the Molotov cocktails hit the wall and started to burn. Another cocktail, which a young perpetrator was handling, spilled on him, preventing them from throwing it at the door and causing them to flee in fear. One of the perpetrators began to write xenophobic phrases on the wall but only managed to write "out" before running away. The incident took place during the early hours of Saturday.

A Moroccan man was attacked and later drowned in a canal. The main perpetrator had arrived at the store where the victim worked, ten minutes after closing. He became infuriated when he was denied entering the store. When the victim threatened to use tear gas, the perpetrator called four other people to join him. Fighting ensued and the victim was last seen running along the canal, followed by the attackers. The group of attackers are of Jewish faith and the main perpetrator had links to the Jewish Defense League (LDJ). He was sentenced to nine years imprisonment, but the sentence was reduced to eight years in the second trial.

A 19-year-old punk was severely insulted by a right-winger he knew from before, partly because of his political attitudes. The perpetrator finally hit him in the face with a beer bottle. The victim suffered a bleeding cut just below one eye and had to be treated as an outpatient in the hospital. The police investigated the incident.

A 15-year-old boy from Nigeria was stabbed to death. The victim was with 'four black males and five white females' when they crossed by the house of of the main perpetrator. One of the girls asked for a light from the main perpetrator and his younger brother. A row then allegedly ensued with name calling and "racist undertones". A fight subsequently broke out, resulting in the brothers being kicked and punched and the older brother believing one of the black males had taken his mobile phone. The group fled the scene and the brothers decided to pursue the group in a car and retrieve the perpetrators mobile phone. They found the group at a roundabout and the perpetrator got out and approached a member of the group. The victim intervened and was stabbed in the heart by the oldest brother, a 40-year old man. The perpetrator committed suicide the day before the trial. His 26-year-old brother was acquitted as it was the older brother who had inflicted the stab wound. The deceased perpetrator had been involved in another racist attack ten years earlier (CaseID: 2000-6-0)

According to the police, a 17-year-old was insulted by a group of about ten right-wing individuals. The perpetrators called the victim a "f*****g zecke [slur for leftist]", pulled him from the bicycle, and beat him with a telescopic baton. The victim suffered a ruptured eardrum, among other things, and had to be treated as an outpatient in hospital. On the same day, in the same city, a 20-year-old alternative activist was reportedly beaten by two right-wingers (case does not meet inclusion criteria). It was not reported whether these incidents were connected.

Three young men, with skinhead aesthetics, assaulted a gay couple. The perpetrators were jumping on parked cars, and the victims confronted them for their behavior. The perpetrators then responded with insults towards their sexual orientation. The perpetrators then attacked the victims, and one of the victims was hit in the head with a skateboard, causing head trauma that required several stitches. The other victim suffered minor injuries. The victims were beaten while the perpetrators continued shouting insults at them. One of the perpetrators was identified and sentenced to a two-year prison sentence.

weapon_description: Beating/kicking, stones, bricks, pieces of asphalt
description: Two Congolese-Italian men, aged 22 and 28, were insulted and attacked by a group of six perpetrators. At 5 a.m., the victims were returning home from a night out at a nearby club and had just arrived at the door of their apartment building. The attackers, waiting on scooters, verbally assaulted them, shouting, "Dirty n******, go back to your country," before beating them and throwing stones, bricks, and pieces of asphalt at them. The victims were hospitalized due to the severity of the attack.

Two molotov cocktails were thrown on the house of some Romanian immigrants. The victims were those who sheltered a friend of theirs who had been racially insulted and physically attacked by three italian men some days earlier (the case does not meet the RTV severity inclusion criterium). The same perpetrators are suspected to be behind this attack.

An 18-year-old left-wing militant was beaten up and then stabbed by a group of right-wing militants. He was attacked at a pub after he said that he is a leftist. After the attack, the victim ran away and was helped by his father.

A 20-year-old punk was attacked by a group of autonomous nationalists. The perpetrators arrived on the victim's doorstep and shouted "Sieg Heil!". The victim was seriously injured by several blows with baseball bats. He suffered a fractured skull base and a fractured forearm, among other things. The police confiscated neo-Nazi propaganda material and several baseball bats during their investigation.

weapon_description: Metal bars, baseball bats, brass knuckles, and beating/kicking
description: Around 15 to 20 people, who police suspected are right-wing extremists, attacked a group of 14 left-wing youths who were sitting around a campfire. The perpetrators were armed with baseball bats, iron bars and brass knuckles. Several of the victims who did not flee quickly enough were knocked to the ground. The perpetrators deliberately kicked the heads of two victims lying on the ground. Meanwhile, other perpetrators pursued the fleeing victims. During the attack, the perpetrators shouted "Scheiß Zecken [slur for leftists]" and "Merseburg stays German", among other things. The perpetrators fled before the police arrived at the scene. Four victims had to be treated as outpatients for bruises, abrasions and contusions. A 26-year-old also lost a tooth, among other things, and a 22-year-old had to be treated as an inpatient for head injuries.

Militants of the anti-capitalist network were attacked by unknown perpetrators. The victims were distributing leaflets in the city, when they were attacked by a group of unknow perpetrators that they alledge were from the far right. The victims were attacked with bats as well as beaten up. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

A 17-year-old German-Kurdish left-wing activist was subjected to a near lethal attack by a 24-year-old member of the "Freies Netz Süd" network. The incident happened on a train. The victim made a comment about the fanny pack carried by the perpetrator’s girlfriend, because it was from the neo-Nazi brand “Thor Steinar”. The perpetrator reacted by hitting the victim to the ground and kicking him in the face at least once. The victim was injured so badly that he had to be resuscitated two times, underwent four surgeries and was in coma for several days. The perpetrator was on probation from a sentence for politically motivated violence, at the time of the assault. The perpetrator was later accused of bodily harm and attempted murder.
According to the police, two people from Cameroon were victims of dangerous bodily harm for racist reasons. Three suspects were identified. No further details are available.

A 19-year-old man (same perpetrator as in 2009-12-6) was arrested on September 1 in Richterich. His accomplice, a 25-year-old man, was arrested on September 22 in Aachen. The two high ranking members of “Kameradschaft Aachener Land" (KAL) had manufactured and distributed explosive devices and prepared a bomb attack on Labor Day demonstrations in Berlin. The 19-year-old perpetrator brought nine homemade explosive devices to Berlin on May 1, some of these containing glass splinters. When the perpetrator noticed the massive police control in the area, he threw away the explosives and fled. DNA of the 19-year-old was later found on the explosive devices. The 25-year-old helped with the production of the bombs. The police suspected that the perpetrators had manufactured a large number of explosive devices and distributed them. The attack was planned to target both police officers and counter-demonstrators. The perpetrators had planned a second explosive attack on political opponents at an upcoming demonstration in Dortmund (CaseID 2010-9-0). They were arrested shortly before the second planned attack. The perpetrators were charged for the preparations of crimes involving explosives.

A house occupied by Eastern Europeans was subjected to a petrol bomb attack. Two beer bottles containing flammable liquid were lit and thrown at the front of the property just after 4am. Two people who were in the house at the time were not injured. Police treated the attack as a racially motivated hate crime.

A 19-year-old neo-Nazi attacked a 15-year-old well-known left-wing activist. The victim was standing at a petrol station with a friend, when the perpetrator got out of a car and forcefully hit the victim to the head two times.
