The victim sustained a life-threatening fracture to his skull and had to operate a titanium plate into his head. The attack had previously been announced online in a video that called for violence against the victim. A few weeks before the attack, the victim's garage was spray-painted with the inscriptions "Death to the Red Front" and "We'll get you, F****** (victim's name)". According to the Interior Minister, Geithain was a focal point for Saxony's right-wing extremists, with a tightly managed neo-Nazi scene (see e.g. another attack in the same period, caseID 2010-5-8-1).

A 19-year-old punk was attacked by three hooded strangers around 2 AM. The victim was sitting on a park bench, when he was suddenly attacked. The attackers broke his nose and ripped out a piece of his earlobe. They stole his cell phone and destroyed his backpack. The day before the attack, a leftist youth was severely beaten in a premeditated attack by neo-Nazis in the same area of Leipzig, Geithain (CaseID 2010-5-7). According to the Interior Minister, Geithain was a focal point for Saxony's right-wing extremists, with a tightly managed neo-Nazi scene. Motive not explicitly stated but sufficiently evident to be included.

Four young women attacked and racially insulted a Chinese couple who owned a bar. The perpetrators entered the bar, took beers from the fridge, and intended to leave without paying. When the Chinese woman, who owns the bar, kindly confronted them about the theft, the attackers insulted her, saying, "I don't pay anything, you're Chinese! Be thankful I don't send you back to China. Since you're so brave to ask me to pay, I should give you a lesson." They then brutally beat her with kicks and punches, and shattered a beer bottle over her head, taunting, "Here’s your beer, you dirty Chinese." The attackers then proceeded to destroy the bar. The woman's husband, also a bar owner, arrived to find the scene. The perpetrators briefly left but returned with more friends, who continued trashing the bar and assaulted the husband. Both victims were hospitalized due to the severity of the attack.

Inmates at Ranby Prison made a bomb intending to kill fellow Muslim prisoners. The inmates threw the bomb in the room where worshippers were in, but a prison officer removed it from the facility and disabled it before it went off.

A group of Afghan refugees who were waiting for a car to go to work, were attacked by a gang armed with knives and sticks. A 20-year-old was struck in the face and suffered four broken teeth and required stitches to his forehead. He also suffered injuries to his arms, legs and body. A second victim was hit in the face. Two hours later the same perpetrators attacked a Palestinian refugee in a different square (see CaseID 2010-5-11-2). Motive not explicitly stated but sufficiently evident to be included.

A 20-year-old Palestinian refugee was attacked by a gang in a public square. The victim was stabbed in the leg and and suffered multiple injuries, including a disfigured face from receiving blows. Two hours earlier the same perpetrators attacked Afghan refugees in a different square (see CaseID 2010-5-11-1).

Three children, aged four, eight and eleven, who were playing in front of a supermarket, were suddenly subjected to racist abuse by a young woman. The perpetrator then threw a half-full bottle of beer at the 11-year-old and pushed her against a wall. Meanwhile, four male youths appeared, who also began to insult the victims with racist slurs and chant neo-Nazi slogans. Finally, one of the perpetrators headbutted the 11-year-old and punched her in the body. The police managed to catch the perpetrators shortly afterwards. State security investigated the incident. The severity threshold in this case is lowered due to the deliberate targeting of children.

A 38-year-old worker lost an eye in a violent attack at the Birrificio Bruton brewery, carried out by members of the far-right "Bulldog" group, linked to Forza Nuova and CasaPound. The group, armed with a knuckleduster and a knife, stormed the bar, beating patrons and throwing bottles and glasses. The attack appears to have been a targeted raid against a venue frequented by left-wing individuals. One of the victims, who was with his wife at the time, suffered serious eye injuries, requiring 130 stitches and likely losing the eye. Two attackers were arrested and are facing further investigation. This incident is part of a broader pattern of far-right violence in the area, with previous attacks at the same venue.

weapon_description: Metal bars, shovels and other, beating/kicking
description: Eight 16-year-old people were attacked by 15 neo-Nazis in the home of one of the victims. The perpetrators broke into the residence of one of the victims, armed with metal bars, shovels and other weapons, because they were “bothered by the fact that he [the victim living there] seemed like an antifascist”. The perpetrators were thought to be members of the local groups "Nationaler Widerstand Tostedt" and "Gladiator Germania". The perpetrators beat up three of the 16-year-olds. One suffered a broken nose and lost memory, one suffered facial cuts and one tore an arm tendon during the attack.

A group of teenagers were attacked by neo-Nazis because they called the police due to the perpetrator's offensive shirt. The victims were grilling in a park when they noticed a man in another group wearing a Hitler T-shirt with the slogan “Ein Volk, ein Reich, ein Führer”. The victims called the police to report the offensive attire. The police told the perpetrators that they had been called to the place by the victims. When the police left the scene, the perpetrators sang the illegal Horst-Wessel song and attacked the victims with battery and bottles. One of the perpetrators tried to hit the victims with an iron bar. One of the victims suffered facial injuries. The attack was stopped by park guards.

A neo-Nazi attacked several left-wing demonstrators with a knife during a clash between fascists and anti-fascists. After neo-Nazis thought to be members of the local groups "Nationaler Widerstand Tostedt" and "Gladiator Germania", attacked leftists youths in a private residence the day before (see CaseID 2010-5-23-3), a spontaneous anti-fascist demonstration marched towards the neo-Nazi shop “Streetwear-Tostedt”. The perpetrator was the owner of “Streetwear-Tostedt”. The perpetrator was in the shop with fellow neo-Nazis when the left-wing demonstrators approached the building. The perpetrator attacked several members of the demonstration with a knife. The perpetrator was sentenced to nine months in prison for serious disturbance of the peace.

A mother and three daughters were confronted by two 18- and 28-year-old skinheads outside of a shopping mall. They were shouting racial slurs, "Sieg Heil" and threatening to kill their whole family. One of the daughters, a 9-year-old girl, was punched. The severity threshold of this case is lowered due to children being beaten.

A group of people threw two petrol bombs at a house hosting migrants before fleeing on motorbikes. The attack caused material damage, but there were no injuries. The police arrested seven people aged 17-23 for the incidence. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

A 15-year-old Iraqi was attacked in the street by several young people for racist reasons and was seriously injured. The victim had to be hospitalized for several days. No further details are available.
According to the police, a German man of Vietnamese origin was the victim of dangerous bodily harm for racist reasons. A suspect was identified. No further details are available.

weapon_description: Batons, wooden lists, tear gas and vehicle
description: A group of antifascist youths were attack by a group of neo-Nazis. The perpetrators, who were in two cars, tried to hit the victims with the cars. The perpetrators got out of the cars and attacked the victims with batons, wooden lists and tear gas. They were hit repeatedly in the body and head.

A taxi driver of Nigerian background was attacked by a customer. The perpetrator refused to pay for his fare, and called the victim a "bastard n*****" before headbutting him in the mouth, knocking out two front teeth. The victim required stitches and dental work. The attack was described as unprovoked and racist. The perpetrator was sentenced to nine months in prison for the attack.

A 30-year-old man from Pakistan was beaten up by three people as he was walking on the main street of the neighborhood. As the victim was picked up by an ambulance and brought to the hospital, ten people shouted "don't come here again, we will beat you up" in addition to racist abuse.

A leftist youth was attacked by right-wing extremists. The perpetrators approached the victim from a car and beat and kicked him. The victim called a friend, who rushed to the scene, where he found his friend lying in a pool of blood. Due to the serious injuries, including a ruptured eardrum, bruises, cuts and lacerations, the victim had to spend several hours in hospital.

Five neo-Nazis attacked a young leftist on the street in the night. The perpetrators stopped their van next to the victim and insulted him. The victim was initially able to flee, but the perpetrators caught up with him on foot. The victim collapsed after the perpetrators hit him on the head with a beer bottle. While the victim was lying on the ground, the perpetrators continued to kick him. The victim was treated as an outpatient. Glass splinters had to be removed from his head and he suffered a laceration.

Three Roma women, including one who was eight months pregnant, were violently attacked by an Italian man near the open-air market on Via Di Nanni. The women had been asking for alms and rang the intercom of a nearby apartment. The man answered, angrily ordering them to leave. Although the women complied and walked away, the man followed them, brandishing a baton. He assaulted them, shouting, "You’re only here to steal!" The pregnant woman was severely injured, leading to the tragic loss of her baby. All three women were hospitalized for their injuries.
According to the police, a man of Russian origin was the victim of dangerous bodily harm for racist reasons. Three suspects were identified. No further details are available.

The perpetrator shot towards three people in a waterpark. One person suffered burns from a bullet that grazed his leg. The police did not find any cartride cases and it became known later that the perpetrator had purchased a cartride case collector. The perpetrator, born in 1972, went on a shooting spree between 2003 and 2010 inspired by lone actor no. 54 where he targeted blacks, Muslims and Romas in Malmö. He was arrested in 2010 and sentenced to life imprisonment in 2012 for homicide and attempted murder. See lone actor no.56 for other cases by the same perpetrator.

A 37-year-old man, who was the bodyguard of an MP from the Green Party, was injured after the politician got into an argument about racism at a World Cup public viewing. It started at a Germany vs. Ghana match, when a group of four perpetrators repeatedly provoked visitors and said things like "fucking n******". They also used several Nazi slogans. The politician intervened when the group was racist towards another group originating from Ghana, and an argument started. The perpetrators approached the politician and his companion, the victim, saying "Look, the Greens are here too," and then throwing a beer in the politician's face and hitting the victim with an elbow on the cheekbone. The victim followed the perpetrators after being hit with the elbow, and one of the perpetrators turned around, said "I am going to kill you now", and punched the victim in the face. He was taken to the hospital with a broken cheekbone. At least one of the perpetrators had previously been the perpetrator in an attack in a bar (see CaseID 2010-1-0).

A 19-year-old man was attacked by a group of eight men for wearing a T-shirt featuring Che Guevara. While in a square with friends, the victim attempted to find a bathroom when the perpetrators noticed him. They pushed him into a secluded area of the square and assaulted him. The victim suffered injuries to his face and head, was hospitalized, and given a 20-day recovery prognosis. The attackers are suspected to be affiliated with "Azione Giovani," the youth wing of the neo-fascist party Alleanza Nazionale.
According to the police, a German man of Angolan origin was the victim of dangerous bodily harm for racist reasons. Two suspects were identified. No further details are available.

The perpetrator shot a weight-lifter of foreign descent in the back through a 24/7 gym studio window. The police did not find any cartridge cases and it became known later that the perpetrator had purchased a cartride case collector. The perpetrator, born in 1972, went on a shooting spree between 2003 and 2010 inspired by lone actor no. 54 where he targeted blacks, Muslims and Romas in Malmö. He was arrested in 2010 and sentenced to life imprisonment in 2012 for homicide and attempted murder for other cases. See lone actor no.56 for other cases by the same perpetrator.

A 23-year-old man suffered serious head injuries after being attacked by neo-Nazis. The victim was described as a political opponent of the perpetrators. At a tram stop, the perpetrators insulted the victim and his two friends "for no reason," according to the indictment. Then they beat the victim with targeted blows to the head. The perpetrators left the tram, got in their car and followed the injured victim and attacked him again. The victim collapsed and lost all memory of the incident. The perpetrators were arrested a few months after the incident and charged with dangerous bodily harm. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

A young man from southern Norway was assaulted after being subjected to a racial slur. The 25-year-old attacker shouted "you damn n****r" before punching the victim in the face. The victim sustained a facial cut that required five stitches. The prosecution argues that the racist remark aggravates the crime. The case is being heard in Nord-Gudbrandsdal District Court.

The perpetrator was on his way after shooting a foreign weight-lifter (CaseID: 2010-6-26) when he spotted the Turkish truck driver sitting in his car, smoking, and listening to the radio. The perpetrator fired two shots against the driver, one bullet striking him in the shoulder. The victim survived the attack. After the shooting, the suspected perpetrator is believed to have used his mothers computer in the middle of the night to read about the shooting. The perpetrator, born in 1972, went on a shooting spree between 2003 and 2010 inspired by lone actor no. 54 where he targeted blacks, Muslims and Romas in Malmö. He was arrested in 2010 and sentenced to life imprisonment in 2012 for homicide and attempted murder for other cases. See lone actor no.56 for other cases by the same perpetrator.

After shooting a foreign weight-lifter (CaseID: 2010-6-26) and a Turkish truck driver (CaseID: 2010-6-27), the perpetrator was on his way home when he spotted a third victim. While on his bike, the perpetrator shot against the black victim, but the bullet missed. He got off his bike and attempted to fire a second time, but his weapon jammed. He got back on his bike and cycled home to his mother. He went on her computer and read news reports about the shootings. The perpetrator, born in 1972, went on a shooting spree between 2003 and 2010 inspired by lone actor no. 54 where he targeted blacks, Muslims and Romas in Malmö. He was arrested in 2010 and sentenced to life imprisonment in 2012 for homicide and attempted murder for other cases. See lone actor no.56 for other cases by the same perpetrator.

Two 43-year-old and 36-year-old Moroccan men were attacked by an Italian man after the perpetrator's girlfriend, who works at a bar, was the target of inappropriate comments from two Moroccan men. Upon learning of the incident, the perpetrator set out to find the culprits but instead encountered two random Moroccan men who had no involvement. At a bar, the victims were threatened and insulted, and one was struck on the head with a glass ashtray, knocking him unconscious. The other was slapped, punched, and dragged for one kilometer to the bar where the girlfriend worked. She did not recognize him as one of the offenders, so the perpetrator left him there. Throughout the attack, the perpetrator made racist remarks, including, "Dirty Moroccans, I am going to make you pay for it," and "If my girlfriend recognizes you, I'll kill you." One of the victims was hospitalized for head injuries.

A Polish couple was attacked by two men in an unprovoked street attack. The attack happened as the victims made their way home from a barbecue. One perpetrator had "roared like a wild animal" before punching the male victim to the back of his head shouting "******* foreigners... don't mess with the English". The male victim passed out twice during the attack and woke to see two people kicking him. He was also punched more than 10 times during the attack. The female victim tried to stop the attack by getting in between the attacker and her partner., but she was punched and thrown to the ground. Both victims required hospital treatment for their injuries. One perpetrator was sentenced to 27 months in prison. The attack was described as a hate crime.

Two Polish people were attacked by a drunk group "because of their Polish nationality". The victims were walking home in the early hours when they were confronted by the perpetrators. The female victim was punched, stamped on and kicked in the head. One of the men present told them to "leave it because you could kill her". The perpetrator then replied: "I want to see how this Polish b**** dies." In court it was heard that it was a "very one-sided fight," and that the attack was unprovoked.

A building that was the home for 293 immigrants was subjected to an arson attack. During the night, waste paper containers in the hallway of the building were set on fire. Residents of the house told that they had seen skinheads smearing the walls, and a swastika and anti-immigration graffiti were found in the stairwell. There were no reports of any injuries, but the fire department said that there was a risk to life. The leader of the State Office for the Protection of the Constitution and Counterterrorism said he assumed that the perpetrators were right-wing extremists. The same building was attacked again a few days later, see CaseID 2010-7-12.

A 31-year-old well-known leftist was insulted as a "gay pig" by a man described as a right-wing attacker. Before he could escape, the victim was brought down by the perpetrator and attacked while lying on the ground. He was so badly injured that he had to undergo surgery on his elbow.

A 36-year-old man, originally from Maghreb, was attacked by two 20-year-old skinheads. The victim was hit suddenly with a brass knuckle and a baton on the face. He was hospitalized with a broken jaw, he passed out after being hit.

Four Senegalese persons were assaulted by a group of five people, aged between 17-21, as they were leaving work. The perpetrators were waiting for the victims outside the factory where the victims were employed. Two of the perpetrators had been fired from their jobs earlier that same morning by the company's management due to their alleged xenophobic behavior towards their Senegalese colleagues. Company sources revealed that these two individuals had been involved in several incidents characterized by racist behavior towards African workers "due to the color of their skin". The attack began with the perpetrators slashed the car with an iron bar belonging to one of the victims, after which they proceeded to physically assault them. One victim sustained severe head injuries, believed to be caused by an iron bar. All four victims were transported to the hospital, with the seriously injured victim requiring a three-day hospital stay.

A building that was the home for 293 immigrants was subjected to an arson attack, after being subjected to a similar attack days before (see CaseID 2010-7-7). During the night, waste paper containers in the hallway of the building were set on fire. Residents of the house told that they had seen skinheads smearing the walls, and a swastika and anti-immigration graffiti were found in the stairwell. There were no reports of any injuries, but the fire department said that there was a risk to life. The leader of the State Office for the Protection of the Constitution and Counterterrorism said he assumed that the perpetrators were right-wing extremists.

A neighbor attacked the seven-year-old son of a single mother and his friend of the same age, brutally hitting and kicking the two children. The perpetrator had previously repeatedly racially abused and bullied the mother and her children over a long period of time because of their migrant background.

A 41-year-old man from Egypt was suddenly attacked with a baton by an unknown person in the train station around 5 PM. The victim was racially insulted and threatened with a knife. The victim was injured in the arm when protecting himself from the blows.

A 29-year-old man from Niger was attacked while sitting in a bar with his 30-year-old friend. A right-wing extremist suddenly started to harass the 29-year-old. When about a dozen other perpetrators arrived, they beat the 29-year-old severely, shouting insults such as "fucking n****r". The victim was repeatedly kicked while lying on the ground. The 30-year-old tried to help but was pushed out of the bar by the security staff among others. A young woman who tried to intervene was spat on and kicked. Outside, several of the perpetrators surround the 30-year-old and hit him with a wooden stick, injuring his arm. Eventually the perpetrators fled. The 29-year-old was treated as an outpatient in the hospital for a head wound, among other things. The police investigated for incitement and dangerous bodily harm.

During a town festival that took a stand against right-wing tendencies in the region, a visitor was attacked by two drunken right-wing extremists. He received several blows to the face, resulting in a broken nose, among other injuries. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

During a fire brigade camp, a 29-year-old youth supervisor attracted attention by making right-wing remarks to the young people present. When a 20-year-old supervisor from another youth fire brigade confronted him about this, the 29-year-old punched him in the face several times, even after he lost consciousness. The victim suffered a broken nasal septum and hematomas on his head and had to spend several days in the hospital for treatment.

On the sidelines of the local town festival, a group of right-wingers beat a punk with a baseball bat. The victim had to be treated in hospital. There were multiple right-wing extremist attacks on leftist youths during the festival (CaseID 2010-8-8-1, other cases do not meet the inclusion criteria). The night before, several right-wing extremists attacked the local alternative youth club.

weapon_description: Club, quartz sand gloves and beating/kicking
description: At the local town festival, a group of right-wing youths threatened left-wing alternative visitors. The perpetrators chased the victims and beat two of them. One of the victims was slightly injured by blows with quartz sand gloves, another suffered a traumatic brain injury from a blow with a club. There were multiple right-wing extremist attacks on leftist youths during the festival (CaseID 2010-8-8, other cases do not meet the inclusion criteria). The night before, several right-wing extremists attacked the local alternative youth club.

location: Yong Hua Garden takeaway, Lochend Road
description: A group of three youths ambushed a Chinese delivery driver outside his family's takeaway. The perpetrators surrounded his car and began rocking it back and forth. The victim phoned police and got out of the car. The group then forced the victim towards a wall and a 16-year-old punched him in the face. The victim hit his head on the pavement and suffered fatal brain injuries. Despite evidence, including witnesses who said the gang called the victim a "Chinky" after the attack, the police did not treat it as racially motivated. The family had previously been racially harassed prior to the incident. The police later issued an apology for their handling of the case. The 16-year-old was imprisoned for five years.

weapon_description: Baseball bats, stones, bottles, dragging through broken glass, and beating/kicking
description: Around 30 neo-Nazis and football fans attacked a party at an alternative housing and cultural project after a soccer match between Chemnitzer FC and the left-wing anarchist FC St. Pauli. Around 150 guests, including fans of both teams, were celebrating after the match. The party was held in solidarity with alternative housing projects that were repeatedly attacked and shut down. The perpetrators, who were dressed in black and masked, entered the premises around 11:30 PM. They used stones and baseballs to attack the victims who were outside on the street. One of the victims was dragged through the broken glass that was lying on the street. Another victim was hit in the head with a bottle. Several people were injured. One or two victims were taken to the hospital. The perpetrators were prevented from entering the building and were chased away. Two well-known right-wing extremists were among the perpetrators. The attack on the housing project had been announced in advance in neo-Nazi and hooligan chat forums.

Unknown perpetrators set fire to the well-known left-wing housing project "Praxis". The perpetrator(s) set fire to a window on the ground floor around 3 AM, which spread to the room. The fire brigade evacuated the building and spent 30 minutes extinguishing the fire. No one was injured. However, the room on the ground floor burned out completely. It was only by chance that no one had slept in the room at the night of the attack. The “Praxis” building had been subjected to several attacks by right-wing extremists during the past months, including smashed windows and anti-1ntifa graffiti. Five days after the attack, a second left-wing alternative housing project in Dresden was subjected to an arson attack by a right-wing extremist (CaseID 2010-8-24-1). The building had a solidarity banner for “Praxis” at their façade. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

weapon_description: Bottles, wooden pallets, beer crates and beating/kicking
description: Around 30 right-wing extremists attacked a private party held by 15 leftists. The victims celebrated the birth of a child, and the party was held in a factory hall. Suddenly, the perpetrators, many of them wearing clothes from the right-wing extremist “Thor Steinar” brand, stormed the party. Without saying anything they beat the guests with wooden pallets, beer crates and bottles. There were also severe beating and kicking. Three of the victims were treated as outpatients on site. Four of the victims were taken to the hospital. Among the injuries were lacerations, broken ribs, bruises and hematomas. There was no previous conflict between the perpetrators and the victims, nor did the parties know each other. Four of the perpetrators, aged between 20 and 29, were arrested. Motive not explicitly stated but sufficiently evident to be included.

A left-wing housing project was subjected to an arson attack by a 21-year-old neo-Nazi during the night. The perpetrator admitted to having thrown a bottle filled with flammable liquid into the apartment. Seven adults and three children were in the apartment at the time of the attack. The residents managed to put out the fire and nobody was injured. The perpetrator was a former active member of the right-wing extremist group “Assipöbel Dynamo”, which was responsible for several former attacks on the alternative housing project (cases do not meet the inclusion criteria). The perpetrator was sentenced to seven years and ten months in youth prison for ten murder attempts and particularly serious arson. Five days earlier, unknown perpetrators set fire to the well-known left-wing housing project "Praxis" (caseID 2010-8-19).

The perpetrator shot at an employee working at a fast food restaurant. The perpetrator was directly inspired by lone actor no.54, targeting kebab workers and using a laser sight on his pistol. Prior to the attack, the perpetrator disguised himself with a wig and glasses and observed the fast food place. He returned at night and waited until the employees went outside for a smoke. When they went inside they left the backdoor wide open due to the warm weather. The perpetrator then pointed his lasergun at one of the employees through the backdoor. He fired, but the bullet missed, went through the window in the front and hit a nearby car instead. The perpetrator returned home and followed the news from him phone. The perpetrator, born in 1972, went on a shooting spree between 2003 and 2010 inspired by lone actor no. 54 where he targeted blacks, Muslims and Romas in Malmö. He was arrested in 2010 and sentenced to life imprisonment in 2012 for homicide and attempted. See lone actor no.56 for other cases by the same perpetrator.
An alternative youth was insulted with anti-Semitic slurs by an unknown person in front of his house. The victim was then beaten and stabbed in the torso with an object. The victim suffered injuries.

Neo-Nazis attacked guests at the left-wing alternative bar "Hirsch-Q". The approximately 20 masked perpetrators threw stones and bottles at the guests, shouted "Sieg Heil" and anti-Semitic slogans. According to the police, two victims were slightly injured, and one was seriously injured. Five of the perpetrators, who were known as members of the right-wing extremist scene, were caught and arrested by the police. They were investigated on suspicion of breach of the peace and dangerous bodily harm. "Hirch Q" was subjected to repeated attacks by neo-Nazis (e.g. CaseID 2010-12-12, other cases do not meet the inclusion criteria).

A 27-year-old member of Antifa was attacked on the street by 10 to 20 young neo-Nazis. The victim was on his way home when the perpetrators appeared and shouted insults, including "Antifa ass" and "He's Antifa, it's his turn". The victim was kicked and beaten with fists, batons and bottles. The victim suffered lacerations and bruises. The perpetrators belong to the local right-wing extremist group "Aktionsgruppe Bückeburg" (now "Autonome Nationalisten Bückeburg"). The victim was treated in the hospital.

A 16-year-old man stabbed a 24-year-old man of Turkish origins in the stomach with a knife while shouting "Sieg Heil" and "Heil Hitler". The victim suffered life-threatening injuries from two stab wounds. The perpetrator was charged with attempted murder. The incident was assumed to have a right-wing extremist background due to the slogans shouted by the perpetrator during the attack. The trial took place behind closed doors.

A 19-year-old man (same perpetrator as in 2009-12-6) was arrested on September 1 in Richterich. His accomplice, a 25-year-old man, was arrested on September 22 in Aachen. The two high ranking members of “Kameradschaft Aachener Land" (KAL) had manufactured and distributed explosive devices and prepared a bomb attack on political opponents on an upcoming demonstration. They were arrested shortly before the planned attack. A few months before, the perpetrators failed to carry out an explosive attack on a May 1 demonstration in Berlin (CaseID 2010-5-1). The detection of the September plot was assumingly part of the investigation of the attempted May attack. The perpetrators were charged for the preparations of crimes involving explosives.

A leftist youth was insulted by two masked right-wingers as a "fucking Zecke [slur for leftist]". The perpetrators then beat and kicked him. The victim suffered a complicated fracture in his hand, numerous hematomas and bruises on his head and face. The victim was hospitalized for two weeks.

At around 2 AM, a 22-year-old Syrian man and his companions were harassed by a drunk man in front of a nightclub. Shortly afterwards, other men joined the perpetrator. After insults such as "fucking foreigners" and shouts of "Sieg Heil", the perpetrators attacked the victims. The 22-year-old was stabbed by a knife in the neck and seriously injured. The unconscious victim was taken to the hospital, where he had to undergo emergency surgery. The victim's life was in danger for more than a week and he was in an artificial coma. The police arrested a 21-year-old man who was investigated for attempted manslaughter.

Two 15-year-olds and a 19-year-old were suspected of having detonated a self-made explosive device in the entrance area of ​​an asylum shelter. The perpetrators had compacted black powder in an aluminum container and detonated it. Despite the unpredictable effects of the explosive device, no one was injured directly. One resident, however, startled as a result of the detonation, fell out of bed, and sustained a head injury. One of the 15-year-olds was accused of being the main perpetrator and detonating the bomb. He had an SS rune tattoo tattooed on his hand in 2020. Another perpetrator had hung a Nazi flag in his parents' house for others to see, and (in 2010) published numerous postings glorifying National Socialism and Hitler on Facebook. The perpetrators were unknown for a long time, but eleven years after the attack video recordings led to a then 15-year-old, who led to other suspects. One perpetrator confessed to the crimes, but retracted the confession on the first day of the trial in 2023. However, he became entangled in contradictions when questioned by the judge.

A group of young punks were subjected to an unprovoked attack by around 20 masked neo-Nazis. The perpetrators arrived in cars and began kicking and punching the victims while shouting, "Hasta la vista Antifascista". Four of the victims, aged between 18 and 22, suffered hematomas. One 20-year-old lost consciousness and had to be treated as a outpatient with a suspected traumatic brain injury. One 16-year-old suffered an asthma attack while fleeing from the perpetrators. The perpetrators chanted political slogans during the attack.

An Afghan translator working for MDM (Doctors of the World) was beaten unconscious by a mob of 20 people, of which some were armed with crowbars. The victim was wearing his uniform at the time of the attack. He was struck on the head and the body and they tried to strangle him. The victim was brought to the hospital with a bleeding gash on the head. MDM identified the attack as part of a growing trend of attacks on immigrants. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

A 34-year-old Ecuadorian man died after being assaulted by three Spaniards in a park. The victim, who did not know the attackers, was reportedly targeted for urinating in a park where children were present. Witnesses emphasized the racist nature of the attack, noting that the perpetrators repeatedly shouted the slur "dirty sudaca" (a derogatory term for South American migrants). The attackers struck the victim multiple times, causing him to lose consciousness. While unconscious, one perpetrator kicked him in the head. The assault was witnessed by one of the victim's children. The victim was rushed to the hospital but died hours later. The perpetrators were charged only with assault, not homicide, as judicial sources argued that the victim’s death resulted from an aneurysm rather than the injuries inflicted.

A resident of a refugee home was attacked by two right-wing extremists on his way to the home. They hit him with a bottle and knocked him to the ground. While he was lying on the ground, they kicked him. The victim had to spend four days in hospital due to his injuries.

A 27-year-old Eritrean man was attacked by a group of neo-Nazis while returning home by train. Midway through the journey, the perpetrators boarded, and one sat directly across from the victim, directing racial slurs at him, including, "What the f*** are you looking at, you dirty n*****?" Shortly after, a 19-year-old assailant struck the victim violently in the face. As the victim attempted to stand and leave the train, he was pursued and further assaulted, resulting in a broken cheekbone that required surgery.

The perpetrator fired at a Roma man standing outside the hospital smoking. The perpetrator aimed at the victims heart, but the bullet grazed his head instead, leading to a 3 cm wound. The perpetrator had just purchased a new laser sight for his pistol and went home and adjusted it. The perpetrator, born in 1972, went on a shooting spree between 2003 and 2010 inspired by lone actor no. 54 where he targeted blacks, Muslims and Romas in Malmö. He was arrested in 2010 and sentenced to life imprisonment in 2012 for homicide and attempted murder. See lone actor no.56 for other cases by the same perpetrator.

A group of 20 hooded men attacked a Pakistani immigrant at dawn in a public square. They beat the victim, and when he tried to flee, one of the perpetrators threw two Molotov cocktails at him. The victim was not injured from the latter. The police suggested the attack was racist.

A 28-year-old man was sentenced for repeatedly starting fires outside homes belonging to immigrants, endangering the residents. On three occasions (see also caseID 2010-11-0-1 and 2010-11-0-2), the perpetrator placed burning rubbish bins near homes, prompting families to evacuate urgently in the middle of the night. None of the families were physically injured. In one instance, swastikas were found drawn on a nearby wall. The prosecutor argued for a minimum 10-year sentence, emphasizing that while the accused did not intend to kill, he knowingly put lives at serious risk. The perpetrator had kept statistics on foreigners living in Alsace, he supported the regionalist far right party "Alsace d`abord", and he recognised his acts were xenophobic.

A group of Greeks locked the door of a basement prayer site for Muslims, where there were 40 migrants from Bangladesh. Then they broke the windows and hurled firebombs into the premises. The perpetrators also shouted right-wing slogans, such as "foreigners out of Greece". The victims managed to extinguish the fire before the fire brigade arrived, but two migrants were injured and transported to the hospital. It can be suspected that the perpetrators belonged to the Golden Dawn, as the walls of the building had been covered with stickers of the neo-Nazi organization.

Three polish men, two of them aged 25 and the third 43, killed a taxi driver in his cab. One of the young men shot the taxi driver after he had been driving them for fiteen minutes. The shooter then handed the gun to the olde man, who also shot the victim. In total, seven shots were fired against the victim. The main plotter 'wanted to feel what it would be like to murder someone and chose [the victim] because of his dark complexion.' One of the men had a tattooo of a swastika on his arm. The three men were given prison terms of up to eighteen years.

Five Bangladeshi men were attacked by three men reportedly linked to a far-right movement. The victims were playing cards in a bar when the perpetrators approached and assaulted them with punches, kicks, and a baton, all while shouting racial slurs. Police later apprehended the assailants and confiscated the baton, which was inscribed with the fascist slogan "Boia chi molla" and "Dux Mussolini." Three of the victims required hospitalization due to their injuries.

The perpetrator shot a Somali-Swedish man at a bus-stop. The bullet went through his stomach and out through his back. The perpetrator, born in 1972, went on a shooting spree between 2003 and 2010 inspired by lone actor no. 54 where he targeted blacks, Muslims and Romas in Malmö. He was arrested in 2010 and sentenced to life imprisonment in 2012 for homicide and attempted murder for other cases. See lone actor no.56 for other cases by the same perpetrator.

A 14-year-old boy from the punk scene was harassed and insulted by a well-known right-wing extremist at the local fairground. A short time later, another member of the group of perpetrators punched the victim several times in the head. The victim suffered a fractured nose, a slight concussion, a bruised eye and injuries to his arm. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

weapon_description: Climbing carabinier used as a knuckle duster, beating/kicking
description: Two 30-year-old men were attacked by a group of eight skinheads as they left a club. The assailants targeted the victims, perceiving them as "leftists" based on their appearance. During the assault, one of the attackers used a climbing carabiner as brass knuckles, severely injuring one of the victims on the head. Subsequent police raids on the perpetrators' homes uncovered Nazi memorabilia and a cache of weapons, including a katana, knives, brass knuckles, baseball bats, and clubs.

The perpetrator shot a Nigerian-Swedish man in the back at a bus-stop. The perpetrator, born in 1972, went on a shooting spree between 2003 and 2010 inspired by lone actor no. 54 where he targeted blacks, Muslims and Romas in Malmö. He was arrested in 2010 and sentenced to life imprisonment in 2012 for homicide and attempted murder for other cases. See lone actor no.56 for other cases by the same perpetrator.

The perpetrator shot through the kitchen window of three Roma women baking cakes with their children. The bullet barely missed the baby the first woman held in her arms, passed through the loins of the second, and pierced the arm of the third. The perpetrator, born in 1972, went on a shooting spree between 2003 and 2010 inspired by lone actor no. 54 where he targeted blacks, Muslims and Romas in Malmö. He was arrested in 2010 and sentenced to life imprisonment in 2012 for homicide and attempted murder for other cases. See lone actor no.56 for other cases by the same perpetrator.
According to the police, one person was the victim of a dangerous bodily harm directed "against left-wing groups." Six suspects were identified. No further details are available.

A militant of the student union Unef was attacked by a group of skinheads, the "Autonomes lorrains". The victim, who is disabled and uses a wheelchair, was smoking a cigarette in front of her student residence, when the perpetrators threw her on the ground, gassed with tear gas and beat her up. They told her: "We recognised you dirty leftie, we don't want to see you protesting anymore!". This comes in a context of frequent attacks by this group against left-wing militants in the city.

The perpetrator fired two shots into the victims tailor shop, missing the target both times. The victim ran outside and confronted the perpetrator, believing him to have thrown rocks into the building. The perpetrator headbutted him to the ground.  The perpetrator, born in 1972, went on a shooting spree between 2003 and 2010 inspired by lone actor no. 54 where he targeted blacks, Muslims and Romas in Malmö. He was arrested in 2010 and sentenced to life imprisonment in 2012 for homicide and attempted murder for other cases. See lone actor no.56 for other cases by the same perpetrator.

Two men, aged 28 and 32, killed a 19-year-old Iraqi near the train station. They punched the victim, sprayed him with pepper spray and stabbed him in the stomach with a jackknife. The victim died in the hospital from the injuries sustained. The main perpetrator was sentenced to 13 years imprisonment for murder motivated by xenophobia. He had previous criminal convictions and the court ruled that after prison he should be placed in preventive detention. The other perpetrator was sentenced to three years in prison for dangerous bodily harm and was sent to a rehab factility for alcohol problems. Both perpetrator had tattooes of right-wing symbols and letters. The 29-year-old perpetrator was active for a long time in Kameradschaft Aachener Land, a group developed in 2001 and banned in 2012.

A grocery store belonging to Pakistanis was attacked by four people from the far right. The perpetrators stormed the store, injuring two migrants. They were taken to hospital, and one of them was treated in a serious condition. One of the perpetrators was arrested.

weapon_description: Kalashnikovs, rifles, ammunition, knives, brass knuckles
description: Police searched 18 houses in Vienna, Lower Austria, Styria, Carinthia and Tyrol, in connection to an investigation by the Counterterrorism authorities into the right-wing radical webpage "Alpen-Donau.info" and the forum site "alinfodo.com". They seized Kalashnikovs, rifles, ammunition, knives, brass knuckles, as well as Nazi memorabilia. The operation was called "the largest police operation against the local neo-Nazi scene since the 1990s".

A group of three people threw an explosive device at the tent of Iranian hunger strikers. The attack occurred during the night when five Iranians were inside. The roof of the tent was set on fire, but the victims managed to throw the device on the pavement where it exploded.

On his way home from a Halloween party that had become the target of an organized right-wing attack, a 22-year-old leftist encountered a group of 15 to 20 right-wing extremists. The victim tried to flee, but was caught and punched in the head and kicked in the body several times. He fell through a glass door. The victim suffered a broken nose, cuts and abrasions on his face, and a bruised back, and had to be treated as an outpatient in the hospital. Two of the victims friends, who had heard the glass door breaking and rushed to help, were also attacked. The Halloween party had been targeted because it was organized and attended by leftists. Earlier in the evening, three other guests were slightly injured by right-wing attackers who broke into the venue.

A group of people had been harassing an anti-fascist social center earlier that evening, before they returned more numerous in numbers.When the anti-fascists went outside to tell thegroup to get away, one person pulled out a knife and stabbed one of the anti-fascists in the back.

A 28-year-old man was sentenced for repeatedly starting fires outside homes belonging to immigrants, endangering the residents. On three occasions (see also caseID 2010-10-0-1 and 2010-11-0-2), the perpetrator placed burning rubbish bins near homes, prompting families to evacuate urgently in the middle of the night. None of the families were physically injured. In one instance, swastikas were found drawn on a nearby wall. The prosecutor argued for a minimum 10-year sentence, emphasizing that while the accused did not intend to kill, he knowingly put lives at serious risk. The perpetrator had kept statistics on foreigners living in Alsace, he supported the regionalist far right party "Alsace d`abord", and he recognised his acts were xenophobic.

The perpetrator had kept statistics on foreigners living in Alsace, he supported the regionalist far right party "Alsace d`abord", and he recognised his acts were xenophobic.

An Iranian refugee who was on a hunger strike to be granted political asylum, was attacked outside her house. The perpetrators were two unidentified people on a motorcycle who had waited for the victim outside the house. They hit the victim all over her body with a bat. She was brought to the hospital, where she was given first aid.
According to the police, two people of Turkish origins were victims of dangerous bodily harm for racist reasons. A suspect was identified. No further details are available.

A 31-year-old Moroccan man was assaulted by a waiter while spending the evening at the "Q" Club. Around 4 a.m., the man lit a cigarette inside the club. Despite several other people also smoking, the waiter singled him out, shouting, "Dirty Moroccan," and struck him, knocking out four of his teeth. No action was taken against the other 7-8 patrons who were also smoking. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

A young leftist man was attacked by a 22-year-old right-winger. According to the victim, four individuals approached him and assaulted him with a knife. The victim managed to escape and reported the incident. He received medical treatment for cuts and bruises. Witnesses and security camera footage indicate that the altercation occurred following a confrontation between an extreme right-wing group and an ultra-left group. Both groups were characterized by typical clothing and symbols. Allegedly, the perpetrator said to the victim, "Say hello to Carlos on my behalf," referring to Carlos Palomino, a teenager who was murdered by a military officer with ultra-right-wing views at the same metro station where this incident occurred (see caseID 2007-11-11).

A group of alternative youths was attacked by five well-known neo-Nazis, when they were out on the street in the evening. The perpetrators began intimidating the victims and asked them about the whereabouts of people affiliated with the left-wing organization “Soziale und Politische Bildungsvereinigung Limbach-Oberfrohna e.V”. The victims tried to flee and avoid a confrontation. However, when they happened to encounter other leftist youths, the situation escalated. The perpetrators randomly grabbed a 14-year-old victim, kicked him and beat him with brass knuckles. When other victims tried to help, they were also attacked. Several of the victims suffered injuries that had to be treated in the hospital. Later the same night, at least one neo-Nazi set fire to the occupied house and headquarter of Soziale und Politische Bildungsvereinigung Limbach-Oberfrohna e.V (case does not meet the inclusion criteria). 13 suspects were arrested and a 19-year-old ringleader from the neo-Nazi scene was sentenced to two and a half years in prison for committing the arson attack.

Two Palestinian immigrants were approached by four men holding rifles on a beach during the night. The perpetrators beat the victims and left them covered in blood. They managed to crawl to a nearby shop, and were transported by ambulance to the hospital. One of the victims received 24 stitches on his head and the other suffered a broken arm and leg. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

A 33-year-old Paraguayan woman was racially assaulted by a couple inside a crowded metro train after an argument ensued between her and the perpetrators. The attack began when the victim entered the packed metro and came close the perpetrators, resulting in them immediately insulting her. The victim was speaking in Guaraní, a language used in some parts of Latin America. The perpetrators insulted her, calling her derogatory names such as "whore", making fun of her accent, and stating "you immigrants are starving, get out of here, you're coming to take our jobs!". The situation escalated physically as the perpetrators pulled her hair, kicked, and punched her in the face, and delivered several kicks to her stomach. No one intervened to assist the victim during the attack. After the assault, the victim received initial treatment at an outpatient clinic. The following day, due to persistent pain and visible injuries including marks on her face and neck, she sought further medical attention at the hospital. She required a neck brace and was unable to work due to her injuries.

weapon_description: Arson and a propane gas bottle
description: A 30-year-old German man tried to launch a fire explosion outside a mosque. The incident happened around 6:30 AM. The perpetrator had transported an 11kg propane gas bottle to the mosque before setting fire to the outer wall. The propane gas bottle did not explode. An employee discovered the fire and managed to put out the flames. The façade and a window were damaged. Two months after the attack, the perpetrator was arrested. He had carried out six arson attacks on Islamic targets between June 2010 and January 2011 (CaseID 2010-12-9, other cases do not meet the inclusion criteria). He admitted his serious intentions to the police by stating that, “something really should happen”. He also explained that he carried out the attacks because he had been beaten by immigrants in his childhood. However, he denied being a racist. The court heard that perpetrator was mentally ill and thus had diminished responsibility for his actions.

A Black man was on the tram on his way home from work in the early evening, when he was attacked by a group of five people. They insulted him as "a criminal foreigner" and spilled beer on him. One perpetrator punched him three times in the face as the victim attempted to get off the tram. The perpetrators then left the tram. The victim had to be taken to the emergency room with serious facial injuries. The police were able to catch the suspected main perpetrator, who was a well-known member of a right-wing extremist group.

A group of young Greeks attacked, for no apparent reason, an immigrant who was selling items in the city center. The perpetrators punched and kicked the victim many times, before the locals intervened. The victim was brought to the hospital in an ambulance. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

A 30-year-old German man threw a glass container with flammable liquid at an Islamic cultural center that housed Iranians. The incident happened around 5 AM. The façade of the building caught fire. The fire went out on its own but there were minor damages to the building. The two people who were inside the cultural center at the time of the attack were uninjured. One and a half month after the attack, the perpetrator was arrested. He had carried out six arson attacks on Islamic targets between June 2010 and January 2011 (CaseID 2010-11-19, other cases do not meet the inclusion criteria). He admitted his serious intentions to the police by stating that, “something really should happen”. He also explained that he carried out the attacks because he had been beaten by immigrants in his childhood. However, he denied being a racist. The court heard that perpetrator was mentally ill and thus had diminished responsibility for his actions.

Three young men, two from Peru and one from Ecuador, aged 17 and 18, were attacked by three Italian men. The perpetrators assaulted the victims using a bottle and a wooden stick, while also subjecting them to racial abuse, shouting, "Go away, dirty n******." The victims sustained injuries and were hospitalized.

weapon_description: Knives, metal chairs, bar stools, and bottles
description: Ten to fifteen people form the neo-Nazi group “Skinhead Front Dortmund-Dorstfeld” attacked visitors at the left-wing alternative bar "Hirsch-Q". The perpetrators suddenly appeared late in the evening. They vandalized the bar with clubs and used knives, metal chairs, bar stools, and bottles to attack the victims. Four of the victims were taken to the emergency room. One of them suffered stab wounds to his arm and hip. One of the perpetrators, a 23-year-old man, had been convicted of manslaughter after killing a punk in 2005 (CaseID 2005-3-28). He was released from prison a few months prior to the attack on the bar. "Hirch Q" was subjected to repeated attacks by neo-Nazis (e.g. CaseID 2010-8-26, other cases do not meet the inclusion criteria).

A young man was stabbed by two individuals, aged 27 and 25, associated with the extreme right group Ultras Marcia. The incident occurred when the perpetrators, accompanied by a group of young people, entered a bar, and assaulted the victim by stabbing him. The victim sustained a stab wound to the chest along with various bruises. Police suspect that the attack may have been motivated by the victim's affiliation with groups holding ideological views opposite to those of the perpetrators. The perpetrators are familiar figures in the neighborhood surrounding the bar, described by residents as members of Nazi groups. They are recognized by their shaved heads and tattoos bearing fascist symbols.

Three neo-Nazis, aged 18 to 23, attacked a 24-year-old man from Ecuador and his two female friends, from Mexico and Germany respectively. The perpetrators insulted the Ecuadorian with xenophobic slurs before punching him to the ground. The perpetrators continued with kicking the victim repeatedly. When the female victims tried to defend their friend, they were attacked. Both female victims suffered abrasions and bruises. The Ecuadorian victim was hospitalized for traumatic brain injury and a broken nose, among other things.

The victim was stabbed with a kitchen knife when he showed up on the doorstep of the perpetrator's home, mistaking it for his friend's house. Police found a BNP flyer displayed in the defendant’s flat and seized a t-shirt, with the words: ‘F*** off. We’re full,’ depicting a boat called SS Asylum heading for the white cliff of Dover. Officers also seized three crossbows - one with a telescopic sight - a 17’ ‘Bad To The Bone’ folding knife, a swastika-embossed dagger and a variety of other weapons, including baseball bats, swords and a rifle. The perpetrator confirmed his BNP sympathies in court, saying ‘I believe you should put British people first.’ The perpetrator was sentenced to life imprisonment.

weapon_description: Baseball bats, iron bars, stones, bottles, and beating/kicking
description: The right-wing extremist group “Freundeskreis Rade,” formed in January 2011, organized multiple violent attacks targeting foreigners and leftists. Eight members were tried for forming a criminal organization and multiple counts of dangerous bodily harm. Victims were attacked with baseball bats, stones, bottles, and iron bars, resulting in severe injuries, including facial fractures requiring surgery. The attacks included incidents described in CaseID 2011-5-1 and CaseID 2011-2-0. On April 25, 2012, police raided 17 locations, including the group’s homes and offices of the far-right party “ProNRW,” seizing weapons and arresting members. In January 2014, seven members were convicted, with the ringleader sentenced to two-1nd-1-half years in prison.

A 20-year-old man launched an unprovoked attack against a man from Afghanistan. The perpetrator punched and kicked him multiple times in the face because he allegedly had befriended the perpetrator's sister. The perpetrator was convicted of racially motivated violence and sentenced to six months in prison. The victim suffered a broken cheekbone.

weapon_description: Muskets, brass knuckles, knives, chains, handcuffs, martial arts clubs, and a parabellum bullet
description: Three members of the neo-Nazi group "White Rebels Barcelona" were sentenced for plotting attacks on immigrants and individuals with opposing ideologies, spreading Nazi propaganda, and assaulting a young deserter (see caseID 2011-4-7-2). The attacks were prepared around the same time as the attack on the deserter. Therefore it is assumed that the arrest happened in 2011, even if an exact date is missing. Evidence of their plans was discovered through internet chats monitored by the Mossos d'Esquadra. The group was well-organized, with members assigned specific tasks such as acquiring materials, creating templates, designing graffiti, scouting locations, and purchasing spray cans. A document seized by the police detailed plans for "hunting nights" to target immigrants or individuals with opposing ideologies, such as redskins. During the investigation, police also confiscated prohibited weapons, including brass knuckles, muskets, knives, chains, handcuffs, martial arts clubs, and a parabellum bullet, which were found in the possession of two perpetrators. Additionally, the seized document outlined instructions for forming "action groups" and suggested graffiti attacks on the Barcelona mosque when the "Muslim issue is more heated and more effective." Plans also included targeting immigrant shops and places of worship, like the Barcelona synagogue. The perpetrators were sentenced for both plotting attacks on immigrants and people with opposing ideologies, as well as for the assault on the deserter. They received five-year sentences for the attack and plotting. The leader of the group had previously been convicted of murdering an anti-fascist on a train (CaseID 2007-11-11).

The 43-year-old spokesman of the far-right group Danmarks Nationale Front (DNF) was arrested after the police found bomb manuals and chemicals in his basement. During a search of his house the police found a number of chemicals that could be used to make explosives. He was charged with attempting to manufacture one or more bombs or explosives. The police ended up not prosecuting him for bomb-making due to lack of evidence, and instead he was found guilty for theft of chemicals, as well as for violating the Fireworks Act and the Weapons Act.

A left-wing 24-year-old man was attacked by two men, aged 20 and 23. The perpetrators belonged to the right-wing extremist milieu. The perpetrators were arrested and accused of brutally beating the victim due to his political views. The police investigated the case as an incident of dangerous bodily harm.

Early on New Year's morning, a group of about seven right-wing extremists entered a kebab restaurant. Among them were the main perpetrator from CaseID 2006-1-9 and CaseID 2013-9-21. After making right-wing and racist remarks, including shouting "You are not German", the perpetrators attacked the Turkish owner of the restaurant with batons and chair legs. Two guests who tried to help the victim were also attacked. One of them had a tooth knocked out. The perpetrators finally left the shop. The owner of the restaurant had to be treated as an outpatient for lacerations and a hematoma on his head, as well as an injury to his arm. Both interveners were also injured.

A 30-year-old man of Afghan origin was attacked on the street by two men in their 40s. The perpetrators shouted “Heil Hitler” several times while following the victim. One of the perpetrators tried to stab the victim in the upper body with a pocket knife. The victim defended himself with the arm and had to undergo surgery for cut injuries after the incident.

Unknow perpetrators tried to burn down the office of a Turkish association and of Royal Air Maroc. They started the fires, but people present were alerted by the smoke and managed to stop the fire from spreading. Racist tags and a swastika were also found at the scene.

weapon_description: Iron bar, baseball bat and beating/kicking
description: A young couple returned from a concert located in a small venue frequently visited by supporters of the far left. To get to the metro more quickly, the two young people decided to go through a gas station and a parking lot. They then came across a group of people gathered around two cars, allegedly skinheads. Two people in the group, armed with an iron bar and a baseball bat, suddenly rushed towards them. They started beating the couple until the baseball bat broke in two. The two victims were taken to hospital in serious condition. The two main perpetrators received prison sentences of five years, while six other received minor sentences. The court held that the sole reason for the attack was the left-wing stance of the victims.

A 25-year-old Black man was attacked and stabbed by two white brothers at a tram stop. The perpetrators first asked the victim if he "had any problems" before hitting him in the face with a beer can, stomping on his chest, and stabbing him, causing a deep wound that perforated his lung. The victim was left in critical condition. The attackers were identified 11 years later through DNA evidence. One of the brothers, a known neo-Nazi, was sentenced to four years in prison for attempted murder. The court rejected his claim that the victim had fallen on the knife.

A 22-year-old man who was jailed for a robbery slashed a fellow inmate with a machete in a reported racist attack. He armed himself with a blade and waited near a shower block attacking a group of Kurdish inmates. He sliced the cheek of one of them while shouting: "Go back to your own country."

Unknown perpetrators attempted to set fire to the homes of two Turkish-origin families, drawing swastikas on the houses and a resident's vehicle. Around 4:30 a.m., firefighters contained a fire that had ignited the front door of one home, spreading to the ground floor. Woken by crackling sounds, the family of four narrowly escaped by climbing through a window as the stairwell burned. A second fire across the street was then discovered at the neighboring home, also occupied by a Turkish family, who managed to escape unharmed. Though no physical injuries occurred, one house sustained significant damage, requiring its occupants to be rehoused.

An 18-year-old man racially abused and violently attacked foreign-born staff at a city restaurant. Accompanied by a male friend who attempted to calm him, the perpetrator began by shouting at a worker disposing of trash outside. The worker retreated inside, but the attacker followed, hurling racist abuse, attempting to punch two staff members, and accidentally smashing a fish tank. He then punched and choked one victim in a headlock, struck another, and hurled chairs. After leaving, still shouting racist slurs, he returned to assault another individual, biting their finger and punching a third victim in the face. One person required stitches and weeks off work. Police found the attacker on the floor, bleeding from the fish tank injury. At the hospital, he continued his racist outbursts and assaulted a doctor and a woman by kicking her in the jaw.

A man from Cameroon was racially insulted and attacked by two men while working as a pavement vendor. After finishing his shift in the early morning, he visited a gas station restroom where he encountered the attackers smoking. One of them dropped ash on his head and shouted racial slurs like "fucking n*****" before they punched him, pushed him to the ground, and kicked him. Despite calling for help, a staff member failed to alert the police, allowing the assault to continue. The victim eventually managed to call the police himself after dragging himself outside. He was hospitalized with multiple injuries, including a broken leg and several injured ribs. The two attackers received 13-month sentences, with 11 months on probation, and the judge cited the racist motive as an aggravating factor.

Members of “Freundeskreis Rade” attacked the owner of a kiosk of foreign background. The perpetrators broke into the kiosk, pulled the owner to the ground, and kicked him repeatedly. When the victim's father intervened, he was attacked with a baseball bat. The masked attackers fled but were arrested during a raid in April 2012 (CaseID 2011-0-0-3). This incident was part of a pattern of violent attacks committed by the group between February 2011 and March 2012. The group was later tried for forming a criminal organization (CaseID 2011-0-0-3).

A 22-year-old student was attacked by three men while waiting at a bus stop and talking on the phone with his girlfriend. The victim, who was wearing a kefiah, was approached by the perpetrators, who asked if he was an anti-fascist. When he replied, "Well, yes," they brutally assaulted him, attacking him with a scratch awl and punching him in the face. After he fell to the ground bloodied, they kicked him before fleeing the scene. The victim was rushed to the hospital, where he was treated for head trauma.

A 48-year-old man carried out an unprovoked racist attack against a woman. The victim was on a night out at the city centre and on her way home, the perpetrator followed her onto a car park, where he pushed, shouted racial abuse and assaulted the victim. The victim suffered fracures to her hand. The perpetrator was arrested on suspicion of racially aggravated assault.

A group of 40 people, armed with iron bars, broke into temporary accommodations for immigrants and beat three people during the night. The attack came after a Greek woman had been attacked and robbed by Moroccan immigrants and a local church was subjected to theft. At least three people were injured, one of whom was in danger of losing his eye, while another suffered a broken leg. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

A group of leftists who were waiting for the tram was attacked by a large group of right-wing extremists. The incident happened at nighttime.  Two of the perpetrators went straight up to one of the victims and immediately punch him in the face. Another victim who pushed the perpetrators away was hit in the face with a beer glass. When a third victim intervened verbally, she was insulted as a "Sophie Scholl slut" and punched in the face. She fell to her knees, and one of the perpetrators hit her again. Two of those affected lost consciousness. The police were able to arrest six suspects near the crime scene. State security investigated for dangerous bodily harm.

Three left-wing activists and three bystanders were attacked by a group of fascists during a commemoration march for the victims of the foibe massacres, organized by far-right groups including Forza Nuova, Fiamma Tricolore, CasaPound, and Brescia Identitaria. The attackers, armed with batons and brass knuckles, targeted a young woman, beating and kicking her while she was on the ground. When three passersby and two leftists intervened, one of them was struck on the head and another beaten while on the ground. Undercover police officers present did not stop the assault. Two victims were hospitalized, one with a broken nose.

A 22-year-old man was attacked outside a gym by two young men dressed in 1970s fascist-style attire, including Ray-Bans and pointed boots, with their faces covered. After calling him by name, they struck him repeatedly in the face and kicked him, leaving him with a broken ankle and four cracked ribs. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

weapon_description: Telescope batons, brass knuckles, and beating/kicking
description: Two punks, aged 23 and 24, were attacked by a group of 15 to 20 masked right-wing extremists. The 23-year-old wore a sweater with the slogan "Love Music - Hate Fascism." As the pair tried to walk past, they were asked if they knew what fascism meant. When the 23-year-old answered affirmatively and continued walking, he was struck in the back of the head with a telescopic baton and punched in the temple with a brass knuckle, causing him to collapse. When the victims attempted to flee, the 24-year-old was kicked in the back and called a "Zecke [slur for leftist] whore." The attackers eventually let them go. The 23-year-old sustained head wounds, while the 24-year-old suffered significant back pain. The perpetrators were charged with dangerous bodily harm. This incident is connected to ongoing politically motivated violence in the region, including CaseID 2012-6-15-1.

A group tried to storm a mosque and hit an imam with bricks after taunting worshippers arriving for evening prayers with racist chants. The front window of the mosque was smashed before two from the group ran inside. A man inside was injured by broken glass. When the imam and the victim injured by the glass came out of the mosque, the group was still throwing bricks and shouting abuse, and the imam was hit by a brick. Five nearby parked cars and a number of homes were also damaged before the gang arrived at the mosque. The perpetrators were aged 16 to 23, and four from the group were facing jail.

An Italian man attacked a 28-year-old pregnant woman from Burkina Faso, who lived in the same apartment building. During a heated argument, the perpetrator insulted her, saying, "N*****, you’re a b****, be careful or I’ll punch you, I’ll kill you." He then physically assaulted her, grabbing the 8-month-pregnant woman and pushing her down the stairs. She was hospitalized with injuries, but fortunately, her child was not in danger.

weapon_description: Hitting and stabbing with broken glass and beating/kicking
description: A doorman was injured after two brothers attacked and stabbed the victim with a glass and a sharp object for racist reasons. The incident occurred at the entrance of a club when the victim, who was working as a doorman, denied entry to the perpetrators. Just before the attack, one of the perpetrators threatened, "I'll kill black people like you". First, the perpetrators struck the victim in the face with a glass bottle, then they attacked the victim with a sharp object and stabbed him up to three times. After, the perpetrators threw the victim to the ground, where they continued to beat and kick him while uttering threats like "kill him, kill him." The attackers then fled the scene. The victim suffered serious injuries. The perpetrators were sentenced to prison for the crime of attempted murder aggravated by racism. They received two years and nine months in prison.

A 32-year-old man was attacked by members of the right-wing extremist party "Nationaldemokratische Partei Deutschlands" (NPD). The victim was cycling and saw the perpetrators putting up NPD election posters shortly after midnight, and criticized them as they drove past. He was then followed by the perpetrators who were driving an NPD election workers' van. The vehicle stopped in front of the victim, and the perpetrators jumped out and ran towards him. One hit the victim with an iron bar, the other with his fist on the head and body. The victim suffered a bruised shoulder, abrasions, hematomas and a split upper lip.

A 31-year-old Turkish man was subjected to a racially motivated attack on a train by five skinheads. The perpetrators xenophobically insulted the victim, before hitting him in the face with a glass bottle. The victim had to be treated in the hospital for facial injuries.

A 36-year-old French tourist of Greek descent, accompanied by two Spanish friends, was brutally attacked by a group of young individuals with nazi/skinhead aesthetics. The attack, which occurred during a festival when the streets were crowded with young people, left the French victim severely injured. He was beaten with brass knuckles, resulting in the loss of vision in one eye, a fractured skull, cheekbone, and nasal septum. According to the victim, the aggression was racially motivated and unprovoked, as the perpetrators attacked him without uttering a word. The victim describes that he has some physical traits that are similar to Arabs, because of his Greek roots. The victim described the attackers as a group of individuals aged between 20 and 25 years old, with short or shaved hair, and dressed in sports clothing. The assault took place around four in the morning, and the presence of many people in the streets made it challenging for the police to apprehend the perpetrators. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

A 17-year-old leftist was shot in the eye with a gas pistol by a 22-year-old neo-Nazi. The perpetrator was out with two friends. He had a shaved head and was wearing bomber jackets with red lettering on the back, camouflage pants and combat boots. A fight broke out between the victim and two leftist friends and the right-wingers. The perpetrator shot the victim, who was a spokesperson for "Antifaschistische Initiative Leonberg" in the eye from close range. The victim received serious eye injuries and required multiple surgeries. The perpetrator was sentenced to two years in prison for dangerous bodily harm. One of the perpetrators was involved in the manhunt and arson attack on young migrants one month after the incident (see CaseID 2011-4-11).

A group of about fifteen neo-Nazis attacked a place of religious worship where Pakistani and Bangladeshi immigrants were praying. The perpetrators were wearing hoods and holding bats, and started beating the six immigrants that were there. One of the victims was hit on the head and required four stitches. Two other victims were hit on the head and different places on their bodies.

A 21-year-old leftist woman was attacked from behind on her way home at nighttime. The two masked perpetrators, who were described as apparent right-wing extremists, repeatedly punched the victim in the head and face until she fell to the ground. She was then kicked several times in the body. Before the perpetrators fled, they snatched a bag with personal belongings from her. The victim was recognizable as a leftist by her appearance. The victim had to be hospitalized for three days for concussion, among other things.

An Albanian man was assaulted by 15 supporters of Treviso FC at a highway rest stop. The attackers began by insulting the victim, shouting: "Go back home, you dirty Slav." They then pushed him, kicked him in the face, and finally smashed a beer bottle over his forehead. The victim was hospitalized following the attack.

A 29-year-old was insulted by three right-wing extremists at the train station. The perpetrators called the victim a "zecke [slur for leftist]" and proceeded to beat and kick him. The police investigated the incident for dangerous bodily harm and conducted house searches within the right-wing scene.

Two Pakistanis, aged 22 and 28, were stabbed with a knife by two Greeks. The police arrested the perpetrators, aged 19 and 22, who pleaded guilty to the assault. Allegedly, the perpetrators were linked to so-called attack battalions that targeted immigrants and had formed in Nikaia and Kolonos.

Three leftists were attacked by a group of 25 mostly masked right-wing extremists. The incident happened in the evening. The victims were on their way back from a rally against the entry into the state parliament by the “Nationaldemokratische Partei Deutschlands” (NPD). They noticed the perpetrators and escaped behind the next street corner. The perpetrators ran after the victims and attacked them. One of the victims was kicked in the head and fell to the ground. Two others were hit in the head. One of the victims fell onto the street with his bicycle and blocked traffic. Shortly after the perpetrators had fled, the police arrived on the scene. One of the victims suffered a concussion, two others suffered bruises.

Rags soaked in accelerant were pushed through the door of a house while the family was inside. A neighbor managed to extinguish the fire before it could spread. Police are treating the incident as racially motivated.
According to the police, a Greek citizen was the victim of dangerous bodily harm for racist reasons. No suspect could be identified. No further details are available.

During a march carried out by 100-150 members of Golden Dawn, there was recorded dozens of attacks and beatings of immigrants in various locations. The participants also attacked an Afghan political refugee camp in Propylaia with crowbars and beatings, injuring two people.

weapon_description: Bottle, quartz sand gloves, pepper spray, and beating/kicking
description: Three masked men described as neo-Nazis attacked four leftists in front of a pizzeria around midnight. The victims were sprayed with pepper spray, kicked and beaten, with two of the perpetrators wearing quartz sand gloves. The perpetrators hit a 28-year-old victim in the head with a beer bottle, causing him to suffer a laceration that required outpatient treatment in the hospital.
