One of the perpetrators had a previous sentence for physically injuring a 15-year-old left-wing activist (CaseID 2010-5-7). According to the Interior Minister, Geithain was a focal point for Saxony's right-wing extremists, with a tightly managed neo-Nazi scene.

A man was violently attacked by a 20-year-old neo-Nazi and his 17-year-old accomplice while buying cigarettes at a gas station in Västerås. The attempted aggravated assault, captured on surveillance cameras and described as brutal, involved repeated punches and kicks, with both attackers stomping on the victim's face while shouting racist slurs. The 20-year-old was sentenced to one year and nine months in prison, and the 17-year-old received eight months of youth care. Both attackers were known to police, with the 20-year-old having prior neo-Nazi ties, e.g. to "Svenskernas parti" (Party of the Swedes), and a criminal history.

Two suspected neo-Nazis attacked a 38-year-old political opponent. The incident happened at around 1:30 PM. The perpetrators shouted "Sieg Heil" several times. When the victim intervened, he was hit several times by one of the perpetrators. The victim suffered a broken nose. When the police, who was alerted by passers-by, took down the perpetrators' personal details, one of them gave the Hitler salute.

Four members of the neo-Nazi group White Rebels Barcelona—two adults and two minors—attacked a former member who had left their group to join an opposing faction. The victim was ambushed at a bar, where the perpetrators beat and kicked him, striking his head with an iron chain. Despite escaping inside, the attackers followed, damaging furniture with chains and threatening, "This is a warning; next time we’ll kill you." The victim sustained a scalp wound requiring stitches. Days earlier, the perpetrators had sent intimidating YouTube messages. Police searches of their homes uncovered Nazi paraphernalia, iron chains, knives, brass knuckles, military boots, and handcuffs. One adult was jailed, and one minor placed in a closed regime. The perpetrators were also sentenced for plotting more attacks on immigrants and individuals with opposing ideologies (see caseID 2011-0-0-2).

A group of citizens coupled with members of the Golden Dawn carried out a series of attacks against immigrants and refugees in the afternoon. They trapped and beat immigrants and refugees in at least three places. They broke windows and threw bottles of petrol at a Somali Community building, shouting racist slogans and writing neo-Nazi Golden Dawn slogans on the walls. In a place next door that also functioned as a religious place, 10 Afghan refugees were trapped inside. The perpetrators threw stones and broke the windows of the building. When members of the Afghan Committee came to the scene to free the refugees, they were attacked by the perpetrators with kicks and punches.

A group of around 20 neo-Nazis set fire to a garden hut where five young men of Italian and Turkish origin were hiding after a fight. The incident was described as motivated by right-wing extremist believes. 20 neo-Nazis were having a garden party, at the residence of a 35-year-old well-known neo-Nazi, close to where a group of three Italians and six Turks were having a party. An argument broke out between the two groups because one of the neo-Nazis drove into one of the victims with his car on the slim road between the residents. The argument escalated into a fight, after which the victims called the police and tried to flee. Five of the victims tried to hide in the garden hut, where they barricaded the door. Some of the perpetrators followed the victims and set fire to the hut. All five victims managed to escape, but they suffered from smoke inhalation. One of the victims, an 18-year-old, suffered a broken rib and injuries to his knee as he was attacked by the perpetrators when he fled the burning hut. The perpetrators shouted racist slurs while kicking the 18-year-old. The hut was burned to the ground. 14 perpetrators, aged 18 to 35, were arrested. A 21-year-old and a 22-year-old were charged with attempted murder. One of the perpetrators had been involved in the attack on leftist youths one month earlier (see CaseID 2011-3-12).

Two 29 and 24 year-olds were arrested after shouting racist abuse and physically attacking a man of West-Indian origin. When the victim left a store, the two perpetrators shouted among other things "Monkey!" after him. An argument erupted, in which one of the perpetrators grabbed a beer bottle and smashed it over the victim's face, before giving a Nazi salute. A witness claims she heard the perpetrators shout "Heil Hitler". The victim was left bloodied on the ground with an open wound on his head. The perpetrators were sentenced to 10 months in prison each.

A drunken 22-year-old man made racist comments to a black woman while she was waiting for a bus in the city centre. A passerby intervened and told the perpetrator that his language and behavior was unjustified. When the intervener backed away, the perpetrator followed him. He carried two plastic bags, one of which contained a pint glass, and swung the bag, smashing the glass over the victim's head. The perpetrator also headbutted the victim on the mouth and nose. The perpetrator was sentenced to 21 months in prison.

A group of ten beat up six Indian students as they played cricket in a park. The perpetrators told their victims not to play at the spot because they "didn't belong there". They screamed racial abuse at the group before attacking them in front of families. They pushed victims to the ground and started beating and kicking them. Three had bottles of alcohol that the perpetrators were drinking from smashed over their heads. One victim, who feared he had been blinded, had to have shards of glass removed from his eye after he was hit with a bottle. The attack was described as completely unprovoked.

The house of a 28-year-old man of Lebanese origins was subjected to an arson attack during the night, by what appeared to be neo-Nazis. The wooden stairs of the house were set on fire, presumably by a molotov cocktail. The owner, who was sleeping in the annex, was waken up by his dog and called emergency workers who put out the fire. One of the walls of the hallway was smeared with NPD graffiti. The victim was a reality celebrity who had previously publicly criticized the “Nationaldemokratische Partei Deutschlands” (NPD). He had been threatened online several times before the arson attack and had discovered similar NDP graffiti one week before the attack.

A 27-year-old Polish man was beaten unconscious in an unprovoked attack. He was walking home with two others after having a couple of drinks in the city centre, when three men stopped him and asked where he was from. He told them he was from Poland. They then said they were going to kill him and punched him to the ground, before continuing to punch him and stamp on his head. He was left with severe facial injuries, which needed surgery and he got a metal plate inserted in his face. Motive not explicitly stated but sufficiently evident to be included.

A 21-year-old man from Sudan was racially abused and hit on the head with a rock, punched, kicked, stamped on and attacked with a stick by a gang. The victim was walking home late at night when two men asked for a cigarette. When he offered them one, they hurled racist insults and punched him in the stomach. He tried to run away but was chased by the pair, who were joined by up to four others. One managed to catch up to him and attacked him again. When he escaped, he was caught up and attacked for a third time. He was repeatedly kicked, punched and stamped on. He was also struck with a wooden stick and hit with a large rock, leaving him with a deep cut that needed stitches. The attack stopped when a member of the public saw what was happening and shouted, causing the perpetrators to flee. The perpetrators were described as white and between 19 and 20 years old. Police described the attack as racially motivated.

After a protest against a house occupied by CasaPound, a group of around 15 people armed with sticks and wooden clubs arrived by cars and attacked leftists on the street. Three people were taken to the hospital with head injuries, one of which required several stitches. The group of perpetrators included members from Blocco Studentesco and CasaPound.

A Polish man was beaten with baseball bats by a group of three masked men. The perpetrators entered the victim's home in the evening, where the attack happened. A woman was also in the house when the attack happened. He received treatment at hospital for injuries to his body and hand. Police described the attack as a hate crime. It is understood the victim was one of a small number of foreign nationals living in the area.

Five perpetrators, aged 21 to 28, were charged with dangerous bodily harm, incitement to hatred, and violations of the Weapons Act following a violent altercation after the May Day celebrations in Radevormwald. A man of Turkish origin sustained serious facial injuries, and xenophobic slogans were shouted during the attack. The perpetrators were suspected members of the right-wing extremist group “Freundeskreis Rade.” This group had coordinated physical attacks on foreigners and leftists to emphasize their xenophobic agenda. Despite a raid in April 2012, the public prosecutor could not definitively prove their membership in Freundeskreis Rade. This case is connected to CaseID 2011-2-0 and CaseID 2011-0-0-3.

A 57-year-old Nigerian man was bitten by a Rottweiler before its' owner screamed racist abuse at him and lunged at him with a machete. The victim was yards from his home when the dog bit him. He told the dog’s owner, a 41-year-old male, that the animal should be on a leash. The perpetrator responded by screamed racist abuse like "Shut up you ******** African, do you want me to show you what I have got?" before pulling the machete from his backpack and lunging at him. The victim grabbed the perpetrator's wrist to try to get the machete away from him and managed to wrestle it from him. Police arrested the perpetrator who claimed "his dog did not like black people because a previous owner, a black man, had mistreated the animal." Later the court heard how the perpetrator's police interview was "peppered with racist rants" and he was sentenced to 18-months in prison.

weapon_description: Three bottles containing a flammable liquid
description: Three bottles containing a flammable liquid were thrown at the facade of a left-wing autonomous center at around 1 AM. Several people were in the building at the time of the attack, and it was visible from the street that the lights were on inside. The NGO "Mobile Beratung für Opfer rechter Gewalt" thus concluded that the perpetrators accepted that people's lives were at risk. The fire burned out by itself, and the facade was charred. The incident happened two days before a planned neo-Nazi march in the town. Around 300 members of the right-wing scene were expected to attend the march. Autonomous leftists had called for counteractions. The police suspect that the attack was connected to the upcoming demonstrations. The autonomous center had been attacked by right-wing extremists four times in the past 15 months (cases do not meet the inclusion criteria). Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

Three days of anti-immigrant violence occurred in the aftermath of the murder of  a 44-year-old Greek man, who died after a stabbing in what appeared to be a street robbery. Residents blamed the killing on the institutional neglect of their neighbourhood and an "immigrant crime wave". Two days after the murder, on May 11-12, protests were organized by Golden Dawn party members and supporters against migrants in downtown Athens, attended by thousands, and riot police were called in as far-right youths rampaged through immigrant neighbourhoods, allegedly "clubbing and pummelling victims to the ground." Pakistani community representatives said more than 100 Asian and African immigrants were attacked by several hundred youths dressed in black, some armed with bats. Records from the ambulance service (Ekas) show that eight foreigners with fractured heads were admitted to hospital in the space of three hours. Overall, at least 120 people were injured in the attacks, 25 of them seriously - 12 of whom sustained severe stab wounds. Earlier the same day, a 21-year-old Bangladeshi national was fatally stabbed by a group of four individuals, presumably Golden Dawn members, wearing black clothing who arrived on motorbikes. The group thereafter fled.

In the evening, a 17-year-old anti-fascist was on his way home when he was grabbed from behind, hit in the face and thrown to the ground by four apparent right-wing extremists. The perpetrators kicked the victim in the head, stomach and legs. Some of them were wearing boots. When the victim stopped moving, the perpetrators let him go. The victim had to spend two days in the hospital with bruises, among other things. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

Two Albanians were beaten by locals at dawn in the port of Rethymno. One of them was seriously injured and transported to the hospital. Authorities considered it to be a racist act. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

A man was beaten with iron bars by a gang in what police called a racially motivated attack. The victim was walking in the street when he was attacked by three men. Two of them struck the man repeatedly with iron bars while the third took out a knife and cut the victim in the arm with it. The man was later treated in hospital for cuts and bruising. The perpetrators were described as white and in their early 20s.

A 28-year-old man, described as belonging to the left-wing scene, were repeatedly insulted by a group of ten neo-Nazis on the tram at around 2:30 AM. When the victim and the perpetrators got off at the same station, the victim was kicked in the back and strangled. A 28-year-old man who intervened, was beaten until he briefly lost consciousness. The police searched for the perpetrators for weeks after the attack. Local “Antifa” activists recognized the main perpetrator as a well-known neo-Nazi who had participated in marches organized by "Nationaldemokratische Partei Deutschlands" in the past.

weapon_description: Stick, beating/kicking with steel-toed boots, and knuckle duster
description: Three young people were sentenced to three years in prison each for attacking a black man "solely because of his skin color". The events occurred early in the morning when the three perpetrators approached the victim, who was on his bicycle. Two of the defendants, who where in a car with two minors, knocked down the victim with a stick from the vehicle. The four of them got out of the car wearing masks, neo-Nazi clothing and steel-toed boots, and began to kick the victim. The third defendant, who was in a second vehicle, also stopped the car and joined the attack by pouncing on and repeatedly kicking the victim. The perpetrators also attacked the victim using brass knuckles. The victim suffered multiple injuries to the neck, arm and chest as well as concussion injuries that took fourteen days to heal.

A 12-year-old boy was racially abused and attacked by a man. The boy was running on a path beside a stream when he was approached by a man near a footbridge. The man punched him, threw him to the floor and then kicked him. During the assault he racially abused his victim and tried to throw him into the stream. The victim was taken by ambulance to the hospital with cuts and bruising. The perpetrator was a white man, about 30-years-old.

A group of about 20 people attacked a meeting on multiculturalism organized by Labour councillors, shouting "E-E-EDL" as they stormed the venue. The attackers smashed a glass door by head-butting, kicking, and throwing concrete pillars, glass, and rocks. Trapped inside, the victims were pelted with chunks of glass and rocks through the broken door. A 48-year-old woman suffered a severe hand injury from a rock, requiring surgery and a three-day hospital stay. Witnesses described the attack as well-organized and targeted.

According to the police, a 70-year-old man was beaten with a club for racist reasons. When the perpetrator was arrested, the police discovered a baseball bat, a Reich war flag, a blank-firing pistol, and balaclavas in his possession.

A 34-year-old woman and a 46-year-old woman were racially abused and spat on by a 46-year-old man on the street in the evening. The 46-year-old victim, who was wearing a burka, was injured when she was hit on the head with a glass bottle and kicked. Passer-bys held the attacker until the police arrived.

A group of five young men attacked a homeless person. They kicked him repeatedly and the victim died of the injuries sustained six days later. The main perpetrator had tattooed "skin" on his right hand and "88" on his left arm. The police found several photos, one that shows him with NPD members, one under the a Reich war flag and another wearing a jacket with the text "Odin instead of Jesus." He was sentenced to 13 years in prison for manslaughter." A witness testified during the trial that another perpetrator wanted to attack the victim because he smelled bad and had no home. He recieved 10 years in prison. The other defendents recieved ten months to three years.

A 33-year-old taxi driver, with foreign background, suffered a broken nose after being attacked by two drunken passengers and racially abused by a third. The victim drove the three perpetrators to their destination, and the perpetrators said they weren’t paying and got out of the car. They also left the doors open, forcing the victim out of the vehicle. Two of them kicked and punched the victim while the third hurled racist abuse at him. The victim pressed his emergency alert button to let other drivers know his location. The victim's brother arrived and all three men kicked and punched his Vauxhall Vectra taxi. He then drove at one perpetrator who ended up on the bonnet but was unharmed. The perpetrators then spotted the victim trying to hide inside a shop and punched and kicked him again, giving him a broken nose.

During a Champions League final celebration, a 34-year-old Senegalese man was stabbed twice by a group of 6–8 individuals wearing Nazi and Hell's Angels symbols. The attack began after the victim, out drinking with a friend, asked a girl not to step on his foot. Shortly after, two assailants approached and began beating him, joined by others. One attacker then stabbed the victim in the arm and chest, leaving him unconscious. The victim was hospitalized, and police arrested two suspects. Authorities investigated a potential racial motive, as the attackers displayed Nazi symbols. The victim later described the assault as racially motivated. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

A gang of "white thugs" attacked two Muslim men during an English Defence League rally. They were protesting about an empty butcher's shop being turned into an Islamic centre. The victims, who were brothers, were walking along the street when they were attacked. They were punched and kicked to the ground. The assaults were captured on film by members of an anti-fascist group. One victim broke his jaw as a result of the attack. A skinhead was later jailed for three months for his part in the attack.

Three men, aged 15, 21 and 23, were attacked by four racists, aged 21 to 25. The incident happened in the evening and all those involved were drunk at the time. The 23-year-old victim was attacked because of his dark skin, according to the police. The victim was headbutted several times. When the two other victims intervened, they were hit with a bottle. The 23-year-old was injured in the head and the 21-year-old suffered cuts. Both were treated as outpatients in the hospital. The perpetrators were investigated for dangerous bodily harm.

A Turkish student was beaten up by a group of men in a bar because he was speaking Turkish with a friend. The perpetrators told the victim that only German was allowed to be spoken in the bar and in Germany. The victim refused and was subsequently beaten up. He suffered a broken nose.

A group of Nazis attacked the M15 (citizen movement promoting a more participatory democracy) camp in Plaza de Fuente Dorada. During the attack, the perpetrators insulted, threatened and attacked the people camping outside. As a consequence, three of the campers suffered injuries of varying magnitude, one of them requiring several stitches to the face.

Two Indians who were employees of a multinational company, were attacked from behind by five men as they were leaving the office. The perpetrators hit one of the victims, who fell unconscious to the sidewalk, while the other managed to escape. The victim was taken to the hospital, where he was diagnosed with a concussion, hematoma in one eye and minor injuries to the elbow. Allegedly, the attack had occurred at the same time as a rally by the neo-Nazi organization Golden Dawn in the area. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

Along Viale Trento, an area recently marked by neo-fascist graffiti, including Celtic crosses and swastikas, a group of eight Italian individuals attacked two young workers of Somali origin. After leaving a bar, the two victims were first subjected to a barrage of racist insults, then chased and ultimately struck on the head with a bottle. The attack caused traumatic injuries, deep lacerations, and significant blood loss.

A group of eight people attacked two Somali men leaving a bar. The victims were racially insulted and chased before one was hit in the head with a bottle, causing lacerations and loss of blood. The attack is preceded by a series of incidents in the city.

A young man was attacked by three neo-Nazis. The perpetrators had been putting up stickers that read "Für Familie, Volk und Heimat – Nationale Sozialisten Mecklenburg und Pommern" and tagged the letters "NS". The victim removed the stickers with right-wing content. The perpetrators, who were waiting on a corner, attacked the victim with beatings and hit him in the head with telescope batons several times. The victim was seriously injured and had to spend several days in hospital.

A left-wing housing project was set on fire during the night by suspected neo-Nazis. The front door of the building was set on fire with paper. The residents woke up when they heard the fire alarm and managed to put out the fire. Nobody was injured. The incident happened in the aftermath of a series of left-wing attacks on officials from the “Nationaldemokratische Partei Deutschlands” (NPD). The housing project was listed on the website of the right-wing extremist organization “Nationaler Widerstand Berlin” (NW-2erlin) in an overview of potential targets for arson attacks. Furthermore, an explicit request for action against left-wing projects were distributed through an internal email list by NW-2erlin. Several other left-wing targets were subjected to arson attacks during the night, including a children’s and youth club of the “Sozialistischen Jugend Deutschlands” (SJD) and an Antifa shop. The police assumed that the arson attacks were acts of revenge for the violence against neo-Nazi representatives. The case is connected to CaseID 2011-6-27b and case ID 2011-6-27c.

A left-wing housing project was set on fire during the night by suspected neo-Nazis. The front door of the building was set on fire with paper. The residents woke up when they heard the fire alarm and managed to put out the fire. Nobody was injured. The incident happened in the aftermath of a series of left-wing attacks on officials from the “Nationaldemokratische Partei Deutschlands” (NPD). The housing project was listed on the website of the right-wing extremist organization “Nationaler Widerstand Berlin” (NW-2erlin) in an overview of potential targets for arson attacks. Furthermore, an explicit request for action against left-wing projects were distributed through an internal email list by NW-2erlin. Several other left-wing targets were subjected to arson attacks during the night, including a children’s and youth club of the “Sozialistischen Jugend Deutschlands” (SJD) and an Antifa shop. The police assumed that the arson attacks were acts of revenge for the violence against neo-Nazi representatives. The case is connected to CaseID 2011-6-27a and case ID 2011-6-27c.

A left-wing housing project was subjected to an arson attack by suspected neo-Nazis. Two cars that were parked in front of the residential building was set on fire. The flames reached up to the first floor. A resident suffered smoke inhalation while trying to put out the fire. The victim was treated in the hospital. The incident happed in the aftermath of a series of left-wing attacks on officials from the “Nationaldemokratische Partei Deutschlands” (NPD). The housing project were listed on the website of the right-wing extremist organization “Nationaler Widerstand Berlin” (NW-2erlin) in an overview of potential targets for arson attacks. Furthermore, an explicit request for action against left-wing projects were distributed through an internal email list by NW-2erlin. Several other left-wing targets were subjected to arson attacks during the night, including a children’s and youth club of the “Sozialistischen Jugend Deutschlands” (SJD) and an Antifa shop. The police assumed that the arson attacks were acts of revenge for the violence against neo-Nazi representatives. The case is connected to CaseID 2011-6-27a and case ID 2011-6-27b.

A 41-year-old German man set fire to a Turkish cultural center where around 20 men of Turkish origins were sitting in the bar area. The perpetrator, who was known as a neo-Nazi in the local community, lived in the house next door to the cultural center. He stormed into the bar armed with a knife and an axe. He shouted, "I've had enough. I'm going to burn you all now. I hate you" and poured out a flammable liquid and set it on fire. The victims were able to escape through the back exit. The tenants from the upper floors managed to escape uninjured. The cultural center was completely burned out. The perpetrator was known to many of the victims. They described him as a Nazi because of his skinned head and combat boots. According to the victims, the perpetrator often watched the guests at the cultural center and took pictures of them. The previous owner of the bar told the media that the perpetrator had previously stormed into the bar armed with a knife and threatened people who were present while shouting “You kanakas, you can’t be stabbed you can only be burned”. The perpetrator was charged with serious arson and attempted murder. Motive not explicitly stated but sufficiently evident to be included.

weapon_description: Knife and belts with metal buckles
description: Three far-right activists attacked and stabbed a young leftist at night. The incident occurred after the perpetrators entered a bar. One of the perpetrators called the victim a "fucking red," leading to a confrontation that continued in the street. The perpetrators then began to attack the victim with belts featuring metal buckles, targeting his head and other parts of his body. The victim managed to escape, but was later caught by two of the perpetrators that surrounded him and stabbed him in the abdomen with a knife. The victim spent 10 days in hospital and needed 448 days to recover from his injuries. The perpetrators were sentenced to three years in prison. One of the perpetrators had previously been convicted for another stabbing incident involving a young man in January 2008 (case does not meet inclusion criteria).
Three neo-Nazis attacked two immigrants in Chania from behind and hit them with a knuckle duster. One of the migrants was taken to hospital.

A 19-year-old woman of mixed race was attacked by two unknow perpetrators. The victim was attacked in the entrance hall of her apartment complex after she walked her dog.  The perpetrators used a utility knife or box cutter to draw two swastikas on her arms and injure her on the face and legs. The victim was hospitalized.

A taxi driver of foreign background was attacked by a 27-year-old passenger, who punched and kicked him while he lay on the ground. After dropping off two passengers, the remaining two men requested a ride to another address. When the driver asked who would pay the fare, an argument ensued. The driver pressed the emergency button for help and exited the taxi, where he was verbally abused by one of the men, who threatened to kill him and used racial slurs. A scuffle broke out, and the driver fell. He was then beaten and kicked into unconsciousness, later hospitalized with bruises and grazes.

A group of between five and ten skinheads attacked a Moroccan boy first inside, then outside, a pub. When the victim went to the bathroom, he was followed by three skinheads who began attacking him. The victim fled outside but was attacked and racially insulted on the street. Staff of the pub  called the police and the perpetrators fled the scene. The police later found two 23-year-olds with brass knuckles and knives in their car suspected of being the main protagonists of the attack. The victim was hospitalized with several injuries.

Upon leaving a cafe owned by an Iraqi, four immigrants of Armenian, Syrian and Iraqi backgrounds were attacked by a group of around 40 people with covered faces. The perpetrators, aged 17-25, shouted "foreigners will die" before beating and stabbing the victims with knives and bats. The victims were hit on their heads, faces and bodies. They were later transported to the hospital.

A 71-year-old man of foreign background was attacked by a 16-year-old as he was opening a mosque for early morning prayers. The perpetrator approached him calling him a “Paki b******.” He then pushed him to the ground before kicking him and stamping on his head and body for about 10 minutes. Witnesses said that the perpetrator continued the attack as the victim laid unconscious on the ground. The victim was rushed to hospital where he stayed for several days with severe face injuries. The perpetrator had sent a text message after the attack which said "I have just left a Paki in a puddle of blood." He was sentenced to three years in prison.

A Romanian family was attacked outside their home, resulting in one death and two serious injuries. Around 10 PM, their 48-year-old Austrian neighbor shot at them with a small-3aliber rifle from five meters away, killing a 65-year-old man with a bullet to the heart and seriously injuring his wife. The couple's son managed to disarm the attacker, who then stabbed him in the stomach, causing severe injuries. Police arrested the perpetrator shortly after. Initially described in the media as a neighborhood conflict, the attack occurred on the same day as Anders Behring Breivik’s massacre in Norway (caseID 2011-7-22), which may have contributed to its limited coverage in Austria. Although authorities initially denied a racist motive, investigation files later revealed the attacker’s far-right affiliations, racist remarks, and preparations for what he described as a planned mass killing to "liberate Austria from foreigners." He carried extensive weaponry, cash, and notes with nationalist slogans including "for a NEW Austria", some allegedly intended as signs for victims. The attacker, a former soldier and truck driver, hanged himself in his cell months later, halting further investigation. Media and NGOs criticized the authorities for downplaying the racist and extremist elements of the crime.

weapon_description: Fertilizer bomb, Ruger Mini 14 (semi-automatic rifle) and a 9mm Glock 17 (semi-automatic pistol)
description: The 2011 Norway attacks, referred to in Norway as 22 July [22. juli], were two sequential domestic terrorist attacks by a 32-year-old man against the government, the civilian population, and a Labour' Youth League (AUF) summer camp, in which 77 people were killed and 262 people were injured (number based on people who sought medical care). The first attack was a car bomb explosion in Oslo within Regjeringskvartalet, the executive government quarter of Norway. The bomb was placed inside a van next to the tower block housing the office of the then Prime Minister. The explosion killed eight people and injured around 200 people. The second attack occurred less than two hours later at a summer camp on the island of Utøya. The camp was organized by the AUF, the youth division of the ruling Norwegian Labour Party (AP). The perpetrator, dressed in a homemade police uniform and showing false identification, took a ferry to the island and opened fire at the participants, killing 69 and injuring several people severly. The attack was the deadliest in Norway since World War II and a survey found that one in four Norwegians knew someone affected. The perpetrator had sent his lengthy manifesto to more than 1,000 people before the bomb exploded. In 2012, the perpetrator was sentenced to 21 years of preventive detention in prison, the maximum sentence allowed in Norway. The sentence can be extended indefinitely as long as the prisoner is deemed a threat to society.

Between two and four unknown perpetrators threw several Molotov cocktails into the ground floor apartment of a building mainly occupied by Roma and Sinti residents, during the night. The nine victims that were in the apartment and 40 to 50 other residents were able to get out in time. Nobody was injured by the flames, but a woman was taken to the hospital after having a nervous breakdown. The building was burned to the ground. The police investigated the crime as a xenophobic attack and attempted murder. According to witnesses, two of the perpetrators were bald and dressed in black clothes. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

At least one punk was beaten to the point of hospitalization by around twelve members of “Nationaldemokratische Partei Deutschlands” (NPD). A total of 25 right-wing extremists raided the streets in the night, traveling in several vehicles and putting up NPD election posters across town. A witness described how the group of perpetrators suddenly chased two punks. They were carrying batons and pepper spray.

A man of Asian origin was unprovokedly attacked and stabbed by two men. The victim had visible scars of at least ten knife jabs. Police found extreme right propaganda on the the attackers' computers, indicating they wanted to get rid of immigrants and "outcasts". Prior to the attack, the two perpetrators sent messages to each other to celebrate the terror attack in Norway (CaseID 2011-7-22) and sending pictures of themselves doing the Nazi-salute. The attackers were charged with attempted murder. The perpetrators also carried out another attack (see CaseID 2011-7-30).
According to the police, a Polish citizen was the victim of dangerous bodily harm for racist reasons. A suspect has been identified. No further details are available.

A 40 year-old homeless person was stabbed by two men while laying asleep in a park. The victim would reportedly have died had he not received urgent medical care. Police suspected the attackers assumed the homeless man to be an immigrant. Police found extreme right propaganda on the the attackers' computers, indicating they wanted to get rid of immigrants and "outcasts". The two perpetrators sent messages to each other to celebrate the terror attack in Norway (CaseID 2011-7-22) and sending pictures of themselves doing the Nazi-salute. The attackers were charged with attempted murder. The perpetrators also carried out another attack only days before (see CaseID 2011-7-28).

Two men on motorcycles attacked the Afghani victim with a wooden club with iron spikes. The victims hand was slashed as they drove by him.  Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.
According to the police, a person from Kosovo was the victim of a dangerous bodily harm for racist reasons. A suspect was identified. No further details are available.

A Romanian man working in the fields was brutally attacked by two Italian men, one of whom is the son of a notorious local mafia boss. The victim was struck repeatedly with a brick to the head and face before being violently beaten while on the ground, leaving him close to death. The attack followed months of racist insults from the perpetrators, highlighting the racial hatred behind the assault. The victim narrowly survived the attack, which left him with severe injuries.

A 40-year-old man was blinded after being attacked by two men. The victim was walking on the street with a friend when he was subjected to xenophobic bullying by the perpetrators. The two parties started arguing. One of the perpetrators shoved his umbrella in the victim’s face causing serious eye injuries. The victim was treated in the hospital. It was uncertain if the victim’s eye would be functional again.

Two leftists, aged 24 and 25, were attacked by five men, aged 18 to 24, while they were sitting in a park in the evening. The victim had earlier the same day taken part in a counterdemonstration against a rally for the "Nationaldemokratische Partei Deutschlands" (NPD). The victims were approached by the perpetrators, and both were attacked with beatings. One of the victims managed to escape and alerted the police, who arrested the perpetrators. They were investigated for dangerous bodily harm. The police believed that the attack had a political background. According to the Interior Minister, Geithain was a focal point for Saxony's right-wing extremists, with a tightly managed neo-Nazi scene. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

An Afghan immigrant was attacked by unidentified individuals, who hit him with a metal object to the head and body, near the main railway station. The victim was found unconscious by passers-by and transported to the hospital with multiple injuries that required stiches. The Afghan Community in Greece linked the event to the neo-Nazi organization Golden Dawn. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

Around 40 partly masked neo-Nazis beat up seven punks at a city festival. The victims were making themselves comfortable on the outskirts of the festival at around 10 PM, when they noticed the perpetrators who were moving in their direction. The victims realized that the perpetrators were neo-Nazis when they insulted the group of punks with "Scheiß Zecken [slur for leftist]”. The victims were severely beaten. One of the victims had his nose broken and was treated in the hospital.

A group of 15 to 20 young men beat up two young women at a city festival at nighttime. They insulted the victims, calling them "Scheiß Zecken [slur for leftist]” among other things. Then then beat the victims. One of them briefly lost consciousness. The victims were severely injured and had to be treated in the hospital. A second suspected motive for the crime was apparently the black skin of one of the victims. At least one of the perpetrators had previously been convicted for committing politically motivated attacks (cases do not meet inclusion criteria) and was back in court at the time of the attack on suspicion of forming a criminal organization.

A 40-year-old Algerian man was left with serious facial injuries moments after a group of youths had asked him for the time. The victim had been walking past a bus stop where the group of 15 people in their mid-teens were gathered. He checked his watch to give them the time, but was then pounced on by a number of them, who hurled racist abuse during the brutal assault. The victim managed to flee with injuries including a broken nose and damaged shoulder after being repeatedly punched. He alerted police and was treated in hospital.
Four Moroccan men were racially abused and attacked with brass knuckles. One of the victims had to be treated as an outpatient in hospital. The police arrested the perpetrators.

A group of 30-40 Golden Dawn members were provoking local residents in the metro station and shouting slogans against immigrants and the left. When several young anti-fascists arrived in the area, the neo-Nazis attacked them with beatings, crowbars and knives. One of the victims was hospitalised with multiple stab wounds.

A man was knocked unconscious in what the police believed was a racially motivated attack. The victim required medical attention. Police did not release any details about the attack, but they arrested two men aged 22 and 33.

In the evening, two men attacked a 50-year-old Egyptian man in front of the train station, insulting him with racist slurs. The group then proceeded to hit him on the head with a beer bottle. The victim was injured. The police arrested the perpetrators.

A group of reported fascists attacked several Pakistani immigrants in the area around a local park. Then they entered a bus, forcibly removed several Pakistani immigrants from the bus and hit them on the head and all over their bodies. The perpetrators broke the teeth of a 60-year-old victim and left him covered in blood. Another younger victim was severely beaten and injured.

weapon_description: Wooden bars, iron bars and screwdrivers
description: Over a two-day period, there was a spate of attacks against Pakistani immigrants after allegations that a Pakistani man had harassed a Greek girl. It is unclear how many separate incidents occurred and how many people were attacked.  The grass-roots organization United Against Racism and the Fascist Threat reported that 25 people were injured in a series of attacks on the first day. A witness testified that the attackers entered a house where Pakistanis were residing and beat all 20 inhabitants using wooden and iron bars as well as screwdrivers. At another house, five people were beaten and had to be hospitalized.

Groups of 40 Golden Dawn members carried out an organized progrom against immigrants. They gathered near a suburban train station where they started beating passing Pakistani immigrants. The perpetrators also stopped a bus, entered it and beat four immigrants. In Agios Panteleimon Square the Golden Dawn members attacked and wounded ten Afghan immigrants. In addition to these attacks, the perpetrators invaded and looted 35 homes of immigrants, targeting Pakistani immigrants. Armed with bats, knives and revolvers they raided the houses and attacked immigrants, injuring 15-17 people. In one of the houses, the perpetrators fired bullets that barely missed the shoulder of one of the victims. In total, around 30 people were injured during the attacks. Four victims were hospitalised.

A 20-year-old man was racially abused and attacked by a white, drunk man. The perpetrator approached the victim with racial insults when the victim was walking in the street. He then hit him in the face which resulted in the victim breaking his nose.

A 32-year-old Asian man was beaten up by a gang who racially abused him. He was having a cigarette in the street when a group of about six people walked by him. One of the group shouted racial abuse at the victim. The victim ignored the abuse, but was then subjected to further insults before being assaulted. He was knocked unconscious and received a serious cut to his eye, as well as significant bruising.

A group of twelve men belonging to Golden Dawn approached the victim and two other Afghans, swearing at them and telling them to leave Greece before attacking. The victim was hit in the head with a bottle and stabbed five times in the chest and back, suffering a lung puncture close to his heart. The other two Afghan men managed to escape. One of the two Afghans identified two of the alleged suspects to the police. In court, the main victim recognized two of the perpetrators in an image of Golden Dawns raid battilion. Two men and one woman were arrested and charged with the attack. Six years later, after posponing the trial 18 times, the two men were found guilty of grievous bodily harm, while the woman was convicted of orchestrating and instigating the attack.
According to the police, a Brazilian citizen was the victim of dangerous bodily harm for racist reasons. A suspect was identified. No further details are available.

A group of fifteen people carried out a raid on a mosque. They broke the windows and threw trash into the area before they attacked an immigrant with a brass knuckles. The victim was wounded in the head.

A 38-year-old man, who could not swim, was pushed into a canal in what police believed was a racially-motivated attack. He was walking in the street when he was approached by three men who became abusive, and after an altercation they pushed him into the canal. The police stated: "We believe the offenders knew the victim could not swim and subjected him to a frightening ordeal." The perpetrators were described as white males in their 30s.

A group of 20 neo-Nazis who were headed towards an anti-fascist protest, came across a forty-year-old Pakistani immigrant. The victim was leaving a place of religious worship when the perpetrators attacked him with a stick, causing an open head wound. He was consequently hospitalized.

A 48-year-old man was severely injured by four members of the neo-Nazi group “Kameradschaft Aachener Land” (KAL), aged 16, 18, 24 and 26. The perpetrators were outside a popular youth club, trying to recruit more members for KAL. They shouted Nazi salutes several times. The victim was a witness to the scene. Ann argument broke out between the victim and the perpetrators. The perpetrators then attacked the victim by hitting him over the head with a bottle. All four perpetrators brutally punched and kicked the victim, who was lying unconscious on the ground. The victim suffered a laceration, cuts and several bruises and swelling. The injuries suggested that the victim was beaten with the broken bottle. The perpetrators were charged with attempted murder. The prosecutor stated that the background for the argument that led up to the attack was the attempted recruitment of young people to KAL. North Rhine-Westphalia banned KAL because of its members´ extreme and violent actions in August 2012.

A 31-year-old Algerian man was attacked by a group of young men, aged 20 to 25, while sitting on a bench. The attackers struck him with bats and bottles, beating him severely. The victim, unable to escape in time, was hospitalized and required stitches for his injuries. The perpetrators admitted their intent was to target Africans, and this incident is part of a broader pattern of violence against migrants in the area in recent months.

A 29-year-old known neo-Nazi drove into a group of three Antifa activists. The victims were gathered at a parking lot, wearing black clothes and balaclavas, together with five other leftist youths. The perpetrator was sitting in a car close by. Three of the victims approached the perpetrator with a can of tear gas and a baton. As a response, the perpetrator raced towards the victims at full speed. One of the victims, a 21-year-old man, was hit by the car, hit his head on the windshield and was thrown over the roof. The victim suffered a brain hemorrhage, attended hospital for several days and had to go to rehabilitation for weeks. The prosecutors did not assume that the perpetrator was in a compelling self-defense situation and stated that "He could easily have fled. Instead he drove his car into his opponents [the victims]". The perpetrator was charged with three counts of attempted manslaughter.

Several right-wing extremists appeared at a school party, first deliberately insulting guests whom they considered to be alternative young people, thereafter attacking a young man by hitting him. The victim suffered a broken nose.

A group of people began racially insulting the Moroccan victim before attacking him with punches and kicks. The victim suffered head injuries,  a fracture of his left orbit, and was consequently hospitalized. Two people belonging to Forza Nuova, aged 26 and 37, were arrested. The group had tried to beat another Moroccan as well that evening, who was sleeping in an abandoned building. The man managed to escape and take refuge in a bar while the perpetrators set fire to the bed  which he slept on.

Two young men of North African origin were attacked by three men, serving in the 2nd infantry batallion of the French Foreign Legion, and injured with a knife. One of the perpetrators was imprisoned. The court has retained the racist motive.

A 24-year-old neo-Nazi (the same perpetrator as in CaseID 2012-2-24-1) attacked the chef at a pizzeria with a knife. The victim was at work when the perpetrator stabbed him several times. According to the indictment, the incident was motivated by the perpetrator’s “deep dislike for fellow citizens of non-German origin”. The victim suffered life-threatening injuries and had to undergo emergency surgery. The perpetrator later referred to the victim as a Jew, because of his dark hair and eye color. When searching the perpetrators apartment, the police found a wall painting of a Reich war flag, Hitler DVDs and swastikas. The perpetrator was charged with two attempted murders motivated by xenophobia.

A pipe bomb was left on the windowsill of a Polish couple's home. A loyalist group called The Real Ulster Freedom Fighters (Real UFF) claimed they were behind the attack. The attempted attack happened after graffiti was painted in the area about a week earlier, saying that foreigners were not welcome. The victims lived near young families, elderly and aprimary school, and police said the bomb could have killed anyone in the area. A Councillor said "There is an obvious racist motive behind this attack".

A 15-year-old of Cameroonian origin was attacked by a group of three men, two siblings and their dad. The victim was leaving a friend's house by bike when, not far from there, the perpetrators were walking. The perpetrators insulted him as a "n*****, dirty black", hindered the victim from passing, and brutally beat him up. The victim was taken to the emergency room of the Calais hospital.

Two soldiers harassed two Turkish men, shouting 'Death to all Muslims', and 'fuck Islam.' A fight ensued and when one of the victim tried to get away, one of the perpetrators, a 23-year-old man, hit one of the victims with a car. The victim suffered 21 fractures. The incident was speculated to be a result of the 9/11 attacks. It is unclear whether the perpetrator were on-duty or off-duty at the time of the attack.

A 25-year-old and a 30-year-old man from Sri Lanka were attacked by a group of 15 people while having a beer after work. The attackers beat the victims severely and spat on them. One of the victims was hospitalized with multiple bruises, especially on his face, while the other was left in a coma for a month and required facial reconstructive surgery. One of the perpetrators, the son of a mafia boss, was sentenced to 14 years in prison for "attempted murder aggravated by racist motives." Following the attack, both victims left the city. A few days later, another racist attack targeting Sri Lankan nationals occurred in the same neighborhood (see caseID 2011-10-28-3).

Members of two far-right groups received prison sentences for terrorism after police discovered weapons and a far-right propaganda film. Members of a splinter group of Blood & Honour called "Bloed, Bodem, Eer en Trouw" (BBET) (meaning "Blood, Soil, Honour and Loyalty") and members of the Dutch neo-Nazi group "Ulfhednar" (also a splinter group of Blood & Honour, local to the Alkmaar area) were first arrested for illegal weapon possession. The police watched members of the groups after being tipped off by the Dutch General Intelligence and Security Service (AIVD). Four perpetrators were arrested after they had gathered at the home of one of the Ulfhednar members and attempted to leave carrying a large bag. Police found several firearms in the bag. One of the arrested perpetrators was the leader of BBET. During a raid on one perpetrator's home following the arrest, more weapons and ammunition were found. They also found a video where a Black person's face were used as a target in a shooting exercise. At the trial, 16 perpetrators were tried for racism and for terrorism (the four initial perpetrators as well as several other members of BBET). The court found it proven that BBET was a terrorist group that wanted to install a national-socialist regime by committing attacks against people and buildings. The combination of the ideological pamphlets, the dissemination of the ideology, a propaganda film, the arsenal of weapons and shooting exercises showed their "readiness for action" according to the judge. The court was convinced that the groups intended to "hit democracy in its heart" and to "instill serious fear in the population by planning attacks - which could cost the lives of countless people [...]" All perpetrators were found guilty and received sentenced to up to 5 years in prison.

A 27-year-old punk and a 31-year-old alternative artist were on their way to an anti-fascist concert that was held at a socio-cultural center, when two masked men suddenly ran towards them from a bush. The 27-year-old was knocked to the ground from behind. He lost unconsciousness. The 31-year-old was hit on the back of the head from behind by the other perpetrator and fell to the ground. Then, several other perpetrators hit and kicked his head several times before fleeing. A passing driver called the emergency services. The 27-year-old only regained consciousness when an ambulance arrives at the scene. Both victims had to be treated as outpatients in the hospital. The 31-year-old suffered a concussion, a laceration on his head and ear. The 27-year-old suffered a hematoma on his eye and lacerations on his head. A wound on his forearm required stitches. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

A group of at least ten people, armed with chains, metal objects and wooden bats, surrounded two women from Albania of Greek origin and asked for their IDs. When the victims refused to show them, the perpetrators slapped, spat on them and threw one of the victims to the ground. Then they hit the victim with a club on the head and beat both of them with fists, kicks and crowbars. The beating continued despite one of them losing consciousness. The victims were transported to the hospital with multiple injuries. The police arrested five Golden Dawn members, including a former secretary of the organization, for the attack.

A 27-year-old Tamil man was racially attacked by unknown perpetrators, who beat him severely. He was hospitalized in the ICU following the assault. This attack occurred just days after another racist incident targeting Sri Lankan nationals in the same neighborhood (see caseID 2011-10-18-3).

A group of 20 to 25 people attacked a 25-year-old Somali man. They beat him until he was unconscious. The victim was taken to the hospital with a fractured eye socket. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

A 15-year-old suffered severe brain damaged after being attacked by a 20-year-old in an unprovoked and racially-motivated attack. The victim was approached and punched as he walked home from a beach party. During the attack the victim hit his head on a car as he fell to the ground which had "devastating consequences". He was later recorded making racist comments about the victim, which according to the judge in court proved that the attack was racially motivated. The perpetrator pleaded guilty to racially motivated grievous bodily harm and was sentenced to six years in prison.

A teenage gang attaked an Indian takeaway which left one man in hospital with a serious head injury. The gang targeted workers at the takeaway after they were ejected from the shop for racially abusing staff. They then smashed up a car parked outside, before attacking a 53-year-old worker at the takeaway with a lump of masonry. The incident was treated as a racially motivated attack by police. The injured victim was treated in hospital for a serious head injury. Seven men was arrested, aged between 16 and 18.

A group dressed in black armed with sticks and clubs attacked five people from the Partito Democratico [Democratic Party] who were putting up posters. The victims suffered head trauma, wounds and one suffered a broken arm. One of the perpetrators was recognized as a member of CasaPound.

A 16-year-old boy was slashed across the face during a reported racially-motivated and unprovoked gang attack. The four perpetrators approached two 16-year-old Asian boys. One of them struck the victim with a piece of wood before another slashed him across the face with a knife. The group fled but were caught after one perpetrator texted a friend admitting his involvement in the attack. It was reported that it was an “absolute miracle” that he didn’t lose his eye. The incident happened amid racial tensions in the area between white and Asian gangs. The perpetrators were angry after three of them had been targeted by Asian gangs in different ways prior to the attack, but neither of the two 16-years-old boys had any connection to any of the incidents. The perpetrators, aged 18-21, got jail sentences ranging from 15 months to 5 years.

A 20-year-old man of Moroccan origin was subjected to a knife attack by a 25-year-old man. The victim was walking on the street with a friend when they encountered a group of six men. One of the men insulted the victim. The perpetrator then stabbed the victim, who suffered a serious wound. The perpetrator was a skinhead and wore a Pitbull jacket and an Iron Cross earring. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

The police found explosive devices in the homes of members of the neo-Nazi organization “Autonome Nationalisten Bückeburg”. The residents of 30 suspects, aged 17 to 19, were searched. Large quantities of illegal firecrackers produced in Eastern Europe were detected and confiscated. The police described the explosive devices as extremely dangerous. The possession of the weapons violated the Explosives Act.  Autonome Nationalisten Bückeburg was known for their serious commitment to violent action, and had carried out a number of unprovoked attacks before the house search.

A 38-year-old Congolese-Norwegian woman was attacked by two perpetrators, a male and a female, at 04.00 AM. On her way to the bus she was confronted by the perpetrators, who blocked her way. The woman pushed the victim and spat at her, saying she should "return to where she came from, there are already too many of you here." The woman then urged her partner to attack, which he did. He punched the victim in the stomach and hit her head against the ground multiple times before people who were passing by removed him. Unconscious, the victim was driven to the emergency room by an ambulance.

A 27-year-old neo-Nazi shot at the windows of a Turkish grocery store. The perpetrator shot randomly around and at the targeted store with two carabines. He also had several packages of explosives on his body that could have been detonated with fire. A witness suffered blast trauma from the shots fired. The perpetrator announced the crime to the police and asked not to be shot. He was known to have psychological problems and had been in treatment for a long time preceding the incident. The shooting was investigated as a crime motivated by political believes because the perpetrator was wearing a Swastika armband at the time of the attack. The police also found the perpetrator’s backpack that contained a Waffen SS helmet in a river. A caretaker had previously found an incendiary device and leaflets with right-wing extremist slogans in the perpetrator's possession. The perpetrator denied being a right-wing extremist and said that he wore the Nazi arm band to draw attention. The shooting happened a few days after the detection of the neo-Nazi group “Nationalsozialistischer Untergrund” (NSU) who killed ten people between 2000 and 2007. Nine of them were small business owners with a migration background.

weapon_description: Knuckle dusters, quartz sand gloves and beating/kicking
description: Two brothers of foreign origin were suddenly harassed by four men on the tram. The perpetrators said, "Shitty foreigners, what are you doing here?" Then one of the perpetrators took the bag from one of the victims and threw it across the tram. When the victim got off the tram, they were followed and attacked. One of the victims was hit on the side of his head with brass knuckles. The other victim was hit with quartz sand gloves and injured in the stomach area and on his right upper arm.

A 19-year-old black male lost two teeth after he was punched by a woman as he walked along a street. He was racially abused by the woman and two men before she assaulted him. The female perpetrator was said to be white and in her 40s.

weapon_description: Clubs, knuckle dusters, quartz sand gloves and beating/kicking
description: Five right-wing extremists, aged between 22 and 32, targeted a youth center where a punk concert was held. The perpetrators, some of them armed with clubs, knuckle dusters, quartz sand gloves and combat boots, entered the premises of the youth club and attacked people who were attending the concert. The perpetrators knocked the victims to the ground, beat and kicked them. Seven of the victims were injured, some of them seriously. One of the victims suffered multiple nasal fractures. The court saw it proven that the perpetrators had entered the concert with the aim to beat up punks [leftists]. The perpetrators received prison sentences between three years and three months, and 18 months.

A man was stabbed in his stomach, chest and head by a 17- and 18-year-old hooded men after he intervened in an unprovoked racist attack. The victim and his girlfriend were talking to two men with foreign appearance late at night when one of the foreign looking men was suddenly attacked from behind by the perpetrators. The victim intervened and stopped the attack. The perpetrators claimed they wanted to "cleanse Norway". The victim continued to observe the two perpetrators. After a short time, the two perpetrators launched a new attack, and the victim intervened again. This time, he held them on the ground until police arrived. Immediately after the incident, the victim discovered that he was stabbed multiple times, he was rushed to the hospital where he underwent surgery and received 30 stitches. The perpetrators were charged with racially motivated violence.

A 46-year-old man of Turkish origins were attacked by four young men. The victim was approached by the perpetrators while he was walking in a park. The perpetrators wore dark clothes, had short hair and three of them were wearing combat boots. The perpetrators insulted the victim by calling him a “Turkish pig” before stabbing him two times in the stomach with a knife. The victim was severely injured by bruising and stab wounds. He was admitted to a hospital. The incident was investigated as an attempted murder.

Two boys of Turkish origin, aged 16 and 17, were beaten up by at least three known neo-Nazis. The victims were attending a Christmas market when they were chased by the perpetrators who shouted “Don't look so stupid, you bastards” before being beaten and kicked with combat boots. One of the victims suffered a laceration to the back of his head and a broken nose. One of the perpetrators, a 24-year-old member of the neo-Nazi scene (same perpetrator as in CaseID 2005-3-28), was sentenced to two years in prison for dangerous bodily harm. The perpetrators were suspected of being members of the neo-Nazi group "Skinhead Front Dortmund-Dorstfeld". Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

A 21-year-old Jewish student was subjected to anti-Semitic abuse and physically assaulted by another student during a ski trip organized by the London School of Economics (LSE) athletics student club. The group began playing a Nazi-themed version of the drinking game "Ring of Fire," where playing cards were arranged in the shape of a swastika, and players made "Führer" salutes while praising the blitzkrieg offensive. When the victim could no longer tolerate the anti-Semitic insults directed at both Jews in general and him personally, he confronted the players. In response, one of the players assaulted him, leading to a fight in which the victim suffered a broken nose.

At around 2 a.m, six or seven men on motorcycles began harassing the victim, saying "Come on, come on, Africa, Africa", before hitting him in the head with a beer bottle. The bottle broke and when he tried to defend himself by covering his face, his wrists were slashed. They punched him in the face, breaking his nose and cracking a tooth. They fled the scene on their motorcycles when the police arrived at the scene. Due to the timeframe, location and Modus Operandi, it may be suspected that Golden Dawn was behind the attack.
According to the police, two Turkish citizens were victims of dangerous bodily harm for racist reasons. No suspect was identified. No further details are available.

A man in his 30s was pelted with bricks and bottles by a gang of up to seven men in what the police called a racially motivated attack. The perpetrators also shouted verbal abuse at him. The man suffered grazes to his hand and knee during the assault. The perpetrators were described as white men, aged between 14 and 26.

The Continassa nomad camp, by large inhabited by Romas, was set on fire during a demonstration by residents of the area after a 16-year-old reported to have been raped by two Romas living in the camp. As a response to the rape accusation, inhabitants of the neighborhood organized a demonstration with the aim to "Clean up the Continassa". A group of Bravi Ragazzi ultras (later disbanded) also joined. Racist slogans were shouted which demonstrated explicit ethnic hatred towards Romas. Participants were encouraged to "burn them all". Huts, camps and caravans were set on fire, and flames could be seen from outside the camp. However, the 16-year-old girl later admitted to have lied about the rape accuse, as she was from a conservative family and had only tried to cover up her first sexual relationship. Two of the perpetrators were sentenced to four years in prison each for arson aggravated by ethnic hatred. Two others was sentenced to three and two years for among other things incitement to racial hatred. It is unknown whether anyone in the camp was injured.

An individual of Cameroonian origin was racially insulted and attacked with a glass bottle by two individuals. The perpetrators had first insulted guests at a café and were thrown out of the premises. Outside the café, the perpetrators racially insulted the victim and hit him in the head with a glass bottle. The same victim had also been a victim of another right-wing attack in March the same year, where he was racially abused and threatened with his life with a broken bottle (case does not meet inclusion criteria).

Around 15 men attacked three immigrants, including a man from Afghanistan, with wooden and metal sticks. The Afghan man had to be treated at the hospital for injuries to his head and nose. When they got to the hospital, there were three other injured migrants there. Due to the timeframe, location and Modus Operandi, it may be suspected that Golden Dawn was behind the attack. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

Two men were killed and three injured when the perpetrator went on a shooting spree. The perpetrator first killed two people in Piazza Dalmazia before shooting the three others in a central market. He the proceeded by shooting himself. He was described as a fantasist, an author of cult essays and books inspired by Tolkien and Evola, who dreamed of a return to the pagan roots of a Europe reigned over by Norse kings. The motivation for the killings was tied to the perpetrators affiliation with CasaPound. Casapound distanced themselves from the perpetrator, claiming that he was not a key activist. However, after the attack, it was reported that Casapound started removing the perpetrators articles from their website. The perpetrator was already known to the police for unauthorized demonstrations, threats, outrage and resistance to public officials. He was described as an introverted, withdrawn and depressed.
According to the police, two Polish citizens were victims of dangerous bodily harm for racist reasons. Two suspects were identified. No further details are available.

A man of Senegalese origin was brutally attacked at his workplace as a transporter. Three days after visiting the family of one of the victims of the Florence massacre, the victim was fixing packages when a colleague began insulting him, saying, "They should have killed you all in Florence" (caseID 2011-12-13). Another colleague joined in, threatening to kill him and using racial slurs. The two then physically attacked him, hitting him in the face and causing him to fall, losing consciousness. The assault, witnessed by other colleagues who did not intervene, left the victim with serious injuries, as confirmed by an emergency room report.

A 59-year-old man was attacked by three men on a train. The perpetrators had talked loudly and derogatory about dark-skinned passengers who were in the carriage. The victim asked the perpetrators to stop. Consequently, the 24-year-old perpetrator hit the victim in the head with a full beer bottle. The victim suffered a laceration. The perpetrator was arrested.

Two leftist teenagers were attacked with an iron bar by three neo-Nazi minors, aged between 14 and 16. The victims and the perpetrators had an ongoing ideological conflict for some time, beginning a few months before the attack. The perpetrators had told the victims online that they were not welcome in the city, as well as supporting the extermination of Jews, and displaying neo-Nazi symbols. Earlier on the day of the incident, the perpetrators had met the victims and asked if they were communists. The victims responded that they were leftists. A few hours later, the perpetrators followed the victims. Before the attack, the perpetrators were hiding behind some bushes before attacking the victims. They surrounded the victims, insulted their clothing, and one of the perpetrators then pulled out an iron bar about 30 cm long and struck one of the victims in the face, causing bleeding from his eye, bruises, and a cut that required six stitches. The second victim received a blow to the neck, but it did not cause visible injuries. During court proceedings, the perpetrators admitted their sympathy for far-right ideas.

weapon_description: Beating, tear gas, two rifles with rubber bullets, baton
description: A group of seven young men attacked three Moroccan men living in an isolated bungalow with other undocumented immigrants from Morocco and Tunisia. Armed with two rifles, a baton, and two tear gas canisters, the perpetrators knocked on the bungalow door, pretending to be police officers. Once inside, they tear-gassed the victims, threw them to the ground, beat and kicked them, and pressed a rifle barrel to one victim's head. The attackers then dragged them outside, forced them to kneel, and shot rubber bullets at them as they tried to flee. The assault was motivated by a series of local crimes, which the perpetrators attributed to illegal immigrants. One assailant told a victim, "If it’s not you, it’s your brother; if it’s not your brother, it’s your cousin; if it’s not your cousin, it’s someone of your race." The group later bragged in private messages about planning a "lynching" and a "hunt for illegals."

Two men described as right-wing radicals attacked five men of foreign origin in the street for racist reasons, injuring some of them seriously. The perpetrators had also shouted "Sieg Heil" and "Heil Hitler" in the streets. One Filipino victim suffered a brain hemorrhage after being kicked with combat boots. Four other people, with various foreign backgrounds, were also attacked, but no further information about these attacks were reported. The perpetrators got six and four years in prison.

An asylum seeker of Iraqi origin was attacked by an unknown man in the evening, leaving him with facial injuries. One evening, the victim was on his way back to the asylum home where he lived. He was approached by the perpetrator, who asked what he was doing there. The victim explained that he lived in accommodation close by. The perpetrator told the victim to leave Austria, among other things, and grabbed the victim by his arm. Two young women intervened and told the perpetrator that he should stop. As the victim then backed off the perpetrator punched him twice in the face. The victim fell to the floor and remained there for a few minutes. Once he could stand up again he went to the police. A medical examination established that his cheek bone and maxillary sinus were fractured.

An Asian taxi driver was attacked by two "tattooed skinheads", leaving him too injured to work for two months. The perpetrators were among a group of friends who missed the last train home after a night out and then argued with taxi drivers about the cost of a fare. They racially abused their victim as they punched and kicked him, leaving him with a shattered thumb, a broken nose, and dislodged teeth. The victim said he was punched so hard he felt as if he had been hit by a car. Witnesses said they thought the attackers were so violent they looked like professional fighters. In court the perpetrators got 8 and 11 months in jail.

A 16-year-old boy of mixed race and his mother's boyfriend, who was black, was beaten up by a group of white men. The victims were walking to a garage when the perpetrators shouted racist abuse at them. The 16-year-old victim called a friend to ask them to pick them up because he was getting worried about the group, but they were then set upon. The adult victim was hurt and the 16-year-old victim was left with a fractured eye socket which needed treatment at the hospital. The police said that the assault appears to have been unprovoked.

A Kurdish doner kebab shop was subjected to an arson attack. The shop was set on fire and burned to the ground. Four Kurds were injured. The letters “MHP” were written to places on the façade of the shop. MHP stands for the Turkish far-right “Partei der Nationalistischen Bewegung”. The police did not rule out a political background for the attack. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

A journalist was assaulted by a far-right protester during the celebration of "Día de la Toma". The perpetrator repeatedly struck the victim in the head, resulting in a deep cut on his nose and numerous bruises. The journalist stated that the attack took place while he was performing his reporting duties and was clearly identified as a journalist by the perpetrator.

A 32-year-old Bangladeshi street vendor selling roses was assaulted by a 30-year-old former soldier. The assailant initially approached the vendor to ask for a cigarette but quickly escalated to insults and threats before physically attacking him. Nearby street vendors intervened, striking the assailant, who then fled the scene. The victim sustained a broken leg in the attack. Before the assault, the perpetrator reportedly told two witnesses, "Remember that we are Sardinians, we are different from them." Afterward, additional witnesses reported hearing him declare, "If I see an Indian outside, I will kill him. I am bad, I am from Sant'Elia [a neighborhood in Cagliari]." Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

A young left-wing activist was violently assaulted by four suspected members of the far-right movement CasaPound. The assailants reportedly followed the victim by car, subjected him to verbal threats and insults, and then launched a physical attack, during which he was headbutted and repeatedly punched in the face. The assault resulted in the victim sustaining a broken jaw.

A Roma father and a son were sentenced to 10 and 14 years in prison respectively for the murder of a 32-year-old Senegalese man. The incident started when a group of Senegalese men were playing football in the streets, which the perpetrators father did not approve of. The perpetrator insulted them with slurs like "sons of bitches, black shit, go back to your own country." As the group refused to stop playing, the father called his sons, who came to the scene - the first with a cane and the second with a knife, starting a fight in which the victims did not want to enter. Then, another brother arrived, whom his father incited to end the lives of the Senegalese: "these n****** have disrespected me, we must kill them all!" Following his father's instructions, the third brother went to get a handgun, returned, and fired a first shot in the air and another at the 32-year-old victim, who died. One of the other brothers attacked another Senegalese with a cane and threatened the others with a knife.

A 23-year-old Moroccan man was brutally beaten by three men. The victim had asked a blonde woman on the street for road instructions and invited her out for a coffee. The perpetrators, who had been standing close by, commented on the conversation and insulted the victim with xenophobic slogans. The victim became aggressive and approached the perpetrators. The perpetrators hit the victim in the face and kicked him in the head while he was laying on the ground. The victim suffered a broken nose and severe injuries to a cervical vertebra. The victims' condition was life-threatening and he had to undergo surgery in the hospital. The state security police responsible for political crimes took over the investigation because of the right-wing extremist appearance of the perpetrators.

A group of EDL members attacked two Muslim men during an un-policed English Defence League (EDL) march against an Islamic Centre in Dagenham. The victims were walking near the EDL march without realizing what it was when they were attacked. The victims were punched and kicked to the ground and one suffered a broken jaw. Passersby tried to intervene and help the victims and were also abused by the perpetrators. The interveners were members of the Hope Not Hate NGO who were taking photographs of the march and were previously attacked by EDL members (excluded because of limited information). One of the perpetrators, a 23-year-old man, was convicted for the attack.

An apartment building occupied by non-German as well as German residents, was subjected to an arson attack by a 21-year-old right-wing extremist. The entrance and the stairwell of the building were set on fire and burned. Seven people had to be rescued by fire fighters. A swastika was scratched into a car that was parked in front of the building. The perpetrator partially confessed to the accusation of setting fire to the building with the intention to kill at least one of the Polish residents. The perpetrator was sentenced to four years in prison for attempted murder motivated by xenophobia.

A 21-year-old punk was attacked by 20 neo-Nazis after a right-wing concert. The victim and his girlfriend were passing by the pub where the concert was held.
