The perpetrators, eight of them armed with aluminum baseball bats, attacked the victim who fell to the ground where he was kicked in the head several times. The victim went to the doctor the next morning because he was throwing up constantly after the attack. He was diagnosed with serious head injuries and had to be treated in the hospital as an inpatient.

A dozen members of Nordic resistance movement [Swedish at the time] stormed an anti-racist meeting. The left-wing municipal politician in Falun was hit in the head with a bottle. Around 40 anti-racists locked themselves in the room for two hours before the police could guarantee their safety. Three people were arrested. A 27-year-old who is the local leader of the organization in Stockholm and responsible publisher of SMR's online magazine was suspected of abuse. A 33-year-old local leader in Dalarna and a 24-year-old were suspected of inciting fear.

A 36-year-old Senegalese street vendor was attacked and stabbed by two unidentified assailants. The incident began when the victim noticed the perpetrators approaching him on a scooter. They shouted racial slurs, including "You are a dirty n*****." The victim attempted to defend himself, but the assailants escalated the attack, wielding a knife. He was stabbed multiple times in the arms and later hospitalized for his injuries.

A 17-year-old was attacked unprovoked by a leader of the far-right group "Jóvenes Inconformistas." The victim, who had anti-fascist aesthetics, was brutally beaten. Witnesses reported that the attack was so brutal that one of the neo-Nazis had to intervene to stop the blows due to the severity of the situation. The victim ended up in the emergency room. This incident occurred during a period of heightened neo-Nazi violence in Salamanca, Toledo, and Zaragoza (see e.g. caseID 2012-2-19-1, 2012-2-19-2 and 2012-4-0). The incident sparked protests in Salamanca against fascist violence.

Five to six people in two cars arrived at an abandoned railway station where about 50 migrants had taken refuge. According to four foreign journalists documenting the poor living conditions, two or three assailants began beating some migrants. In response, the migrants chased them, forcing most to flee in one car. One perpetrator, however, remained behind, and as the migrants surrounded him, he suddenly drove off, running over one person. As he fled, migrants threw sticks at him, but he sharply reversed, sped towards the group, and hit a 35-year-old Algerian, causing serious injuries. Two others were also hurt—one beaten and another struck by the car. The attack was allegedly linked to accusations of theft in a public market earlier that day, though migrants claim the perpetrators frequently returned to the site to assault them with clubs and sticks.

location: Calle Real del Arrabal de Toledo,
description: A member of a neo-Nazi group, accompanied by about 20 others, stabbed a foreign immigrant with a punk aesthetic and anti-fascist ideological views during a Carnival celebration. The incident occurred when the perpetrator, walking with his neo-Nazi group, encountered a group of six boys, some of whom were known to the perpetrator from being neighbors in the same neighborhood. One of the perpetrators knew that the victim and his group held opposing political views. A confrontation ensued, and the perpetrator drew a knife. As the victims tried to escape, they were chased by the perpetrator and others from the neo-Nazi group. The perpetrator managed to stab the victim several times, inflicting a six-centimeter-deep wound in his lower back. It was stated in the judgment that the perpetrator acted out of discrimination against the victim as a foreign immigrant with punk aesthetic and anti-fascist ideological views. The perpetrator received 7 years in prison for attempted homicide. About an hour later, the same neo-Nazi group attacked two victims because of their anti-fascist ideology (CaseID 2012-2-19-2).  This incident occurred during a period of heightened neo-Nazi violence in Salamanca, Toledo, and Zaragoza (see e.g. caseID 2012-2-10-1 and 2012-4-0)

A member of a neo-Nazi group, accompanied by about 10 others, stabbed two anti-fascists during a Carnival celebration. This incident occurred an hour after a similar attack by the same neo-Nazi group, in which they stabbed a foreign immigrant with a punk aesthetic and anti-fascist ideological views (CaseID 2012-2-19-1). The perpetrator, along with his neo-Nazi group, went to a bar where the victim was, someone the perpetrator had a strong hatred for due to his anti-fascist views. Members of the neo-Nazi group then threw a glass at the victim's head and began to beat him. The perpetrator stabbed the victim with a twelve-centimeter knife, injuring his left kidney. During the same brawl, the perpetrator also inflicted a knife wound on a second victim's forearm. The perpetrator was sentenced to 10 years in prison for attempted homicide. This incident occurred during a period of heightened neo-Nazi violence in Salamanca, Toledo, and Zaragoza (see e.g. caseID 2012-2-10-1 and 2012-4-0)
A group of Golden Dawn members broke into an immigrant house and attacked the inhabitants with bats and stun guns. Two people were severely injured.

A man of Asian background was beaten unprovoked before being pushed in front of a train by a stranger. The victim was first punched twice in the head and then pushed forcefully. The victim tumbled over the edge of the platform and landed on the tracks in front of a train which was about to start moving. The police arrested a 24-year-old man. The perpetrator made racist remarks against an officer of a different ethnic origin than Danish. Police said that it appeared that it was a completely random victim and suspected a racist motive. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

A 26-year-old Iraqi man was attacked by two men. The perpetrators followed the victim and racially abused him before beating and kicking him to the ground. Members of the public intervened and called paramedics and police to the scene. He suffered a cut to his head and broken tibia and was taken to the hospital where he underwent surgery. The police treated this as a racially motivated attack.

A 21-year-old Vietnamese man was subjected to a knife attack by a 24-year-old neo-Nazi (the same perpetrator as in CaseID 2011-10-9) in prison. The victim was stabbed in the chest and had to undergo emergency surgery. According to the indictment, the attack was unprovoked and happened “out of sheer xenophobia”. The victim had allegedly been selling illegal cigarettes in prison. The perpetrator stated that he believed that Vietnamese cigarette sellers only sells cigarettes to pregnant women and children. The incident was investigated as an attempted murder. The perpetrator was sentenced to prison in 2011 for stabbing an immigrant in a pizzeria because of his “deep dislike for fellow citizens of non-German origin”. When searching the perpetrators apartment, the police found a wall painting of a Reich war flag, Hitler DVDs and swastikas. The perpetrator was charged for two attempted murders motivated by xenophobia.

A group of CasaPound activists armed with sticks and helmets attacked anti-fascists taking down right-wing posters advertising a march the next day. Three anti-fascists were injured, one of which had to undergo surgery, and others required stitches to the head and several contusions.

A house inhabited by Turkish migrants was set on fire. Eight people suffered smoke inhalation, four of them children. In the same area around the same time, the memorial of a migrant worker that died after a neo-Nazi arson attack in 1997 (see CaseID 1997-5-0) was defaced with a Hitler portrait and the building where the integration office was located burned down. The series of attacks made several organizations suspect a right-wing motive. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

The police confiscated 237 explosive devices from a group of young people belonging to the “Autonome Nationalisten”. Most of the objects were not permitted and illegally owned. Autonome Nationalisten Bückeburg was known for their serious commitment to violent action, and had carried out a number of unprovoked attacks before the incident. The case is connected to CaseID 2011-11-8.

Three left-wing students were attacked by over ten right-wing militants from ControTempo in front of a high school. The students were preparing to join a protest organized by Fiom when they unrolled a banner and handed out flyers. The assailants, who were distributing their own flyers, demanded they leave, then began beating them with helmets and a megaphone. Some teachers and the vice-principal were also pushed and hit. The three students were hospitalized, one with a broken nose, and a teacher sustained a broken wrist.

A man was attacked by two drunk men, aged 26 and 28, after protecting a woman from Togo and her six-year-old daughter. The woman and her daughter were in a grocery store when the perpetrators approached them and insulted them, including shouting “Heil Hitler” and doing the Hitler salute. When the victim intervened to protect the woman, he was beaten and kicked. The perpetrators left after the store manager got involved, but shortly returned to attack the victim again. The victim suffered injuries to his hand and abrasions to his head, shoulders, and arms. The perpetrators were sentenced to one and two years in prison for dangerous bodily harm and incitement to hatred.

An Asian taxi driver was attacked by a 25-year-old man who was dressed in camouflage gear. The victim was waiting for a fare when the perpetrator approached. He pulled out a torch and shone it at the driver's identity badge, challenged him over who he was and yelled racial abuse. He ordered him to wind down the window of his car and punched him in the face, which fractured his nose. He also threatened to kill him. When other cabbies arrived after the driver sent out a distress call message, the perpetrator threw bricks and rubble at them. The perpetrator was sentenced to two-and-a-half years in prison after admitting racially aggravated assault causing actual bodily harm.

A group of six neo-Nazis attacked a group of concertgoers on their way home after a performance by a left-wing band. One of the victims was hit in the eye and head by one of the perpetrators with a brass knuckle, which left him with a permanent eye damage and 95% loss of sight on one eye.

After a concert, four people were insulted by around ten suspected right-wing extremists in front of a youth club and attacked. The perpetrators shouted slogans such as "Shit Antifa" before attacking. The victims were beaten and kicked and were injured so badly that they had to be treated by a doctor. One of the victims had to stay in hospital for several days because of a broken eye socket.

A group of 10-15 men in black with shaved heads and skulls on their shirts attacked two migrants from Syria with iron bars and knives. They beat them until one of the Syrians was lying unconscious, close to death in a pool of blood while the other one was severely injured and heavily bleeding. Shortly after two police cars and a police motorcycle arrived and searched the area for the perpetrators while the two injured were taken to the hospital in an ambulance. The perpetrators managed to flee.

A 19-year-old man from Ecuador was the victim of a racist attack by three young sympathizers of the neo-Nazi skinhead movement. Two of the perpetrators were minors, and one was 18 years old. The incident started with racist comments directed at the victim by the perpetrators, followed by a physical assault. Witnesses intervened to stop the attack, which made the perpetrators to flee the scene. The victim lost consciousness during the assault and was hospitalized with multiple and severe bruises on his head. The perpetrators were later arrested by the police, who confirmed their affiliation with the neo-Nazi skinhead ideology.

A 29-year-old woman, originally from Cameroon, and her six-month-old baby were attacked with corrosive liquid by a man, aged around 40. The victim was pushing a pram though an underpass when he began shouting racist and sexual comments at her. She then felt liquid being thrown on her back. When she turned around the perpetrator hurled more corrosive liquid on her, which badly burned her back and chest. Passer-bys found the woman and raised the alarm. She was treatment at the hospital for her injuries and needed skin grafts. The baby was unharmed. He was unfamiliar to the victim and the police treated this as a potentially hate-motivated attack (2012).

Three young men were attacked after an argument with several neo-Nazis about their political beliefs. The perpetrators eventually attacked the victims with telescopic batons. Two of the victims were seriously injured.

weapon_description: Iron bars, brass knuckles and flares
description: A group of fifteen masked attackers armed with iron bars, brass knuckles and flares attacked a group of people shortly before an anti-fascist concert. Three people were injured, one of them seriously. The 16-year-old victim was struck to the head and suffered an open wound to his skull and bruising all over his body. The attackers threw flares into a car. When two people get out of the car they were beaten and slightly injured. They also required medical care. The attackers wore Martens boots and bomber jackets, and covered their faces with ski masks. One of the men had two tattoos on his neck: the number 88 and the Wehrmacht eagle. Two months after the attack, 12 of the 15 alleged perpetrators were arrested for attempted murder, injuries, arson and public disorder. Nine were sentenced to prison, two were released and the last one was a minor. The attack was believed to be a retaliation for an attack by anti-fascists on October 12 the previous year. The young skinheads were linked to several far-right parties and football clubs. The political parties were Alianza Nacional [National Alliance], Movimiento Social Republicano [Republican Social Movement], Plataforma per Catalunya and the football clubs were Espanyol (Brigadas Blanquiazules [Blue and White Brigades]) and Real Madrid (Cusos, facción catalana de los Ultra Sur). The 18-year-old who led the attack  was sentenced to 18 years in prison. He was a member of Alianza Nacional.

A 27-year-old man was arrested after racially insulting and attacking a 24-year-old man of Turkish origins. The assault happened in a bar. Witnesses heard that the perpetrator shouted that he was proud to be German and hated all foreigners. The perpetrator choked the victim before hitting him over the head several times with a bottle that broke. The perpetrator then stabbed the victim in the neck with the broken bottle. The victim was rushed to intensive care with potentially life-threatening injuries. The perpetrator, who had a “Blood and Honour” tattoo, was arrested in May and charged with attempted manslaughter.

A group of 15 people wearing motorcycle helmets, black jackets and armed with iron bars and sticks, broke into the Departments of Mathematics and Physics at the University of Athens. There, they attacked members of student associations at the faculty and anarchist students. Three students were injured, one of whom was taken to the hospital with serious head injuries. Eyewitnesses suggested the perpetrators were members of the neo-Nazi organization Golden Dawn.

The office of socialist youth organizations was subjected to an arson attack by several people, described as right-wing extremists. The building was the office for the organizations Young Socialists (JUSOS), Action of Critical Students (AKS) and Association of Socialist Students (VSStÖ). Over some time, the perpetrators had repeatedly gained access to the office unnoticed, and left right-wing symbols like swastikas on the walls. On the day of the attack, the perpetrators had vandalized furniture and left swastikas on the walls, as they had done before. The perpetrators then left and returned hours later. They set fire to a sofa that was right next to two sleeping teenagers. The two victims were hospitalized with smoke inhalation and burns.

A young anti-fascist minor was stabbed in a fascist attack, sustaining a two-centimeter-deep wound in the abdomen.  This incident occurred during a period of heightened neo-Nazi violence in Salamanca, Toledo, and Zaragoza (see e.g. caseID 2012-2-10-1, 2012-2-19-1 and 2012-2-19-2).

Three people, aged between 23 and 26, attacked two boys of African origin. The perpetrators beat the victims with betls and a char and stabbed them, leading one to be hospitalized in critical condition while the other was less seriously injured. The perpetrators were later arrested by the police and identified as ultras. In the home searches, the police found photos of Hitler and Mussolini, leaflets from Forza Nuova and other right-wing literature.

A 30-year-old man was beaten by a neo-Nazi couple known for their adherence to the organized right-wing extremist scene, aged 30 and 23, after confronting them. The victim got off the train in the evening. He was drunk at the time of the incident. On the platform, the victim noticed that the perpetrators were putting up large scale posters with right-wing extremist propaganda. The victim, who disagreed with the perpetrators’ ideology, approached them and tried to stick one of the stickers to the 23-year-old’s face. A scuffle broke out, resulting in the victim laying on the ground and being kicked repeatedly by the perpetrators. The attack ended after the victim begged for his life, reminding the perpetrators that he was human. In the hospital, the victim was diagnosed with a lumbar fracture, a broken rib, and a broken nose.

A 50-year-old Indian English professor was attacked by a 19-year-old man on the metro. While the victim was sitting, the perpetrator began racially abusing him, shouting insults like "Dirty foreigner, go back to your country." The attacker then physically assaulted the victim, striking him and headbutting him. As the victim attempted to leave the train, the perpetrator followed and continued the assault until a plainclothes police officer intervened. The victim sustained a broken nose, requiring surgery, and multiple bruises.

Late in the evening, a gang of youths threw an incendiary device onto the balcony of a house inhabited by several families of Albanian origin. The residents of the house, who were alerted by a witness, were able to put out the fire. Six young people aged between 16 and 22 were identified as perpetrators, and suspected of building the incendiary device together. Four of these were directly involved in the arson. They confessed to the crime. According to the police and public prosecutor, some of the perpetrators expressed racist reasons for the crime during questioning.

After a visit to a disco, a guest was racially abused by four people. When the victim tried to confront the perpetrators, he was hit in the face with a beer bottle. The victim suffered several facial injuries as a result, including a severe fracture of the nasal bone. The police were called and were able to identify the perpetrators on the spot.

Two people were attacked by a well-known neo-Nazi. The victims were hanging up posters for an event organized by the party "Die Linke". The perpetrator first attacked one of the victims with several punches to the face. When the victim tried to flee, he was knocked to the ground again by blows to the back of the head. The second victim intervened and was also attacked by the perpetrator, who then armed himself with a baseball bat. As a result of the blows to the head, one of the victims suffered a severe traumatic brain injury, which required hospital treatment.

An 18-year-old neo-Nazi, who was said to be a member of the group "National Socialists Wuppertal", attacked two men from the Antifa scene, aged 25 and 31, with a broken bottle neck. Both victims suffered serious head injuries. The 31-year-old victim was treated in intensive care with deep cuts to his face. Witnesses alerted a police patrol, which arrested the perpetrator near the crime scene.

A 22-year old man was attacked by two men with motorcycle helmets for tearing down a poster by the Gruppo unione difesa. The victim suffered amongst other injuries a cranial-facial trauma, multiple contusions, abrasions to his face, left knee and elbow, bruises, and an edema to his right orbit.

Two pensioners, aged 67 and 69, handing out anti-fascist leaflets, were injured in an unprovoked attack. They were helping at a Socialist Worker stall when a group knocked over the men's table before coming back a short while later in a group of around 10 men and one woman. One victim was headbutted in the face, while his colleague was punched to the floor. A victim said: "I think these were hardcore Nazis." One victim needed laser surgery for a torn retina and was "hopeful his sight would be okay". Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

weapon_description: Telescope batons, brass knuckles, beer glass, and beating/kicking
description: A Syrian family was ambushed and brutally beaten by four neo-Nazis, aged 19, 24 and 32, when attending a spring festival in their hometown. The drunk perpetrators shouted xenophobic slogans while beating the victims with telescope batons, brass knuckles, feet and fists. One of the victims fell unconscious to the ground. The attack lasted for about twenty minutes. Many people stood paralyzed and watched. Seven of the victims were injured. Broken facial bones, sprains, bleeding that penetrated the brain, and reduced respiratory function were among the injuries listed by the court. One of the victims had to undergo emergency surgery. The perpetrators had been active in the right-wing extremist scene for several years. The perpetrators were sentenced to prison sentences of up to four years for politically motivated violence.

A man was injured after being pushed downstairs by four people, aged between 21 and 30. The perpetrators had approached the victim and demanded that he salute 'Hitler' while they performed the Nazi salute. When the victim refused, the perpetrators pushed him down the stairs, which had a height of about two and a half meters. When the police arrived, the victim was lying in a semi-conscious state with three witnesses nearby. The victim was taken to a health center for treatment. Three of the perpetrators were of Guinean nationality and one was Spanish.

A neo-Nazi attacked an alternative youth at a town festival. The perpetrator brutally beat the victim. When other right-wing perpetrators intervened and tried to beat the victim, he was able to escape. The victims were taken to the hospital, where he was diagnosed with a broken nose. He was in need of an operation. Charges were filed against the perpetrators.

The victim, a driver from Iran, was attacked by a man and seriously injured by a blow to the throat and a broken hand. When the driver was on the ground, the attacker continued to kick him while shouting "Go back to your country, you Arab." The perpetrator was sentenced to 11 months in prison for the attack of an xenophobic background.

A 30-year-old Egyptian immigrant was attacked near a police station after having delivered identification papers to his nephew. When the victim delivered them, the police photographed him and warned him not to return through the main square. The victim ignored the advice because alternate routes were too long, and minutes after he left the station he was surrounded and beaten by twelve men, some of whom were wearing shirts with the Golden Dawn insignia. The victim was hospitalized with a concussion.

In the evening, a group of more than twelve masked people from the right-wing scene attacked a group of eight people, described as non-right-wing youths. The perpetrators pursued the victims because of their outfits and chased them through the streets. A 24-year-old was caught and beaten. He suffered a bleeding head injury and was temporarily unconscious. He had to be treated as an inpatient at the hospital. Another victim was injured by punches and kicks. On the same evening, there were other attacks reportedly motivated by right-wing extremism in different parts of the town (cases do not meet the inclusion criteria due to lack of information). Brass knuckles and clubs were allegedly used in the attacks. In the weeks preceding the attack, neo-Nazis were said to have patrolled the town and visited apartments where they suspected that punks were living. The violent incidents described in this case was the culmination of right-wing extremist activity in the town.

weapon_description: Three machine guns, a submachine gun, three carbines, a grenade launcher and live ammunition
description: The police found a collection of illegal weapons in the possession of a 37-year-old man. During a search of the perpetrators house, the police secured three machine guns, a submachine gun, three carbines, a grenade launcher and live ammunition. The police also found “Mein Kampf” and other banned right-wing literature and Nazi memorabilia. The prosecutor’s office did not confirm that the perpetrator had a connection to any right-wing terrorist group.

Three migrants walking down Laskaridou were attacked by a group of people on seven or eight motorcycles with chains and crowbars. When a large group of migrants gathered the motorcyclists fled. The three victims were taken to the hospital where they were treated for head injuries. The victims brother suspected that Golden Dawn was behind the attack. Due to the timeframe, location and Modus Operandi, it may be suspected that Golden Dawn was behind the attack.

Following Nationaldemokratische Partei Deutschlands (NPD) demonstrations, five young leftists were attacked by masked right-wing individuals outside a youth club after a punk concert. As the victims were about to get into their car, the perpetrators began smashing it with batons, baseball bats, and kicks. One of the victims suffered a broken hand from a baton strike. All the victims sustained injuries, including cuts and bruises from the shattered glass.

A student known for his actions as a member of the Socialist Workers Party, ANTARSYA and an anti-racist organization was approached by two unidentified men. The victim, who was wearing a Che Guevara T-shirt at the time, was called "traitor" by the two men before they hit him in the face repeatedly. The victim was left covered in blood and was brought to the hospital to receive stitches.

Shortly after midnight, a man was racially abused, beaten, and dragged into a basement entrance by three unknown men. At around 4 AM, he was found unconscious by residents of the building and taken to hospital with injuries. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

The 34-year-old perpetrator was angry after he had ordered a cab to wait but then drove off, and attacked a random Asian man on the street. He racially insulted the victim before stabbing him with a kitchen knife he had stolen from the party he had been at. The victim died of injuries sustained to his heart. The perpetrator was high on cocaine during the attack. He was sentended to a minimum of 20 years for racially-motivated murder.

Three refugees were insulted and attacked by several perpetrators. At around 7 p.m., the victims encountered the perpetrators who said, "what are you doing in Germany, you bum," and attacked with punches and kicks. One of the victims, a 22-year-old Afghan, was struck in the head with a bottle and injured. The victim was taken to the hospital by emergency services. One of the perpetrators had previously been expelled from the grounds of the refugee shelter.

A Syrian man was attacked by a 33-year-old racist. A German man who intervened was severely injured. The Syrian victim was encountered by the perpetrator at a gas station. The perpetrator acted threateningly and shouted xenophobic slurs. The intervening victim asked the perpetrator why he was racially attacking the Syrian. The perpetrator responded by harassing the intervening victim and his family. The police were alerted. When the perpetrator tried to escape on his bike, he was hindered by the intervener. The perpetrator attacked the intervener by beating and kicking him with great force, also while he was laying on the ground. The intervener had to be admitted to intensive care and almost lost a leg as a result of the attack. The court did not see any evidence that the perpetrator had been acting in self-defense and sentenced him to one year in prison.

A Senegalese street vendor and two bystanders were attacked by a group of young men. The vendor had just closed his stand and was heading home when the intoxicated perpetrators began racially insulting him. As he attempted to escape, he was surrounded and shoved. Two men in their twenties—one working in a shop and the other a soldier with the Brigata "Sassari"—witnessed the scene and intervened, asking the attackers to leave the vendor alone. In response, the group became even more aggressive, beating and kicking both the vendor and the bystanders, even stabbing them with a broken bottle. The victims managed to flee, and the perpetrators also ran off. A passerby later found the vendor and bystanders, covered in blood, and called an ambulance. One bystander needed stitches to his head and face, while the other sustained unspecified injuries to his head and arms. At least eight young men, all in their twenties, were under investigation for the attack.

During a violent anti-migrant protest after the fatal stabbing of a 30-year-old Greek during a dispute with three men believed to be Afghan nationals, clashes arose between protesters and the police. The police fired tear gas to disperse the crowd, consisting of mainly Golden Dawn supporters, who were trying to storm an abandoned factory where homeless migrants had taken shelter. In return, the protesters threw stones, flares and firebombs at the police, causing material damages and injuring eight policemen. Five protesters were arrested.

A 30-year-old Asian man had his jaw broken when he was attacked by two men. The victim was out with his girlfriend when the assault took place outside a nightclub. Police treated this as a racially motivated attack. The suspects were described as white men in their late 20s.

A mosque was subjected to an arson attack by two unknown perpetrators. A neighbor of the mosque observed the perpetrators while they were setting fire to a curtain on the ground floor through an open window. The congregation had just gathered for evening prayer inside the mosque. The witness alerted members of the Muslim community, and they managed to extinguish the flames. Nobody was hurt. The perpetrators fled.

A 33-year-old man from Bangladesh was stabbed by an unknown man, who also shouted racist abuse, on the train. The victim was taken to the hospital with minor injuries. There is limited information about this case.
According to the police, a citizen of Bosnia-Herzegovina was the victim of dangerous bodily harm for racist reasons. No suspect was identified. No further details are available.

Two-three people on motorcycles approached an immigrant from Albania in front of a primary school at midnight and attacked him with what was believed to be a sword. The blade penetrated the victim from the back to the chest. The perpetrators immediately fled. The victim was hospitalised in a critical condition and treated in the intensive care unit. The attack was likely related to another stabbing that occurred twenty minutes later, in another location closeby, in which two immigrants from Poland were attacked with knives (see CaseID 2012-5-31b). Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

Two immigrants from Poland were attacked with knives by unidentified perpetrators on motorcycles. Eyewitnesses suggested it was a racist attack. The two victims were hospitalized. The attack occurred only twenty minutes after a similar attack in another location closeby, in which an immigrant from Albania was stabbed by two-three people on motorcycles (see CaseID 2012-5-31a). Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

An immigrant was beaten by a group of young people on motorcycles. The intervention of citizens prevented a further escalation of the attack. The victim was transported to the hospital in an unconscious state, and remained in a coma. Allegedly, the leader of the group behind the attack was a person well known for his "political action" in the area and the perpetrators had close ties with Golden Dawn.

A Tunisian man was violently attacked with a metal pole by his neighbor after enduring months of racist abuse. The 21-year-old perpetrator had long harassed him with threats and monkey chants outside his home. One day, while the victim was washing his car, the perpetrator resumed his taunts. After being called a "prat," the perpetrator threatened to kill the victim's wife and daughter. The situation escalated when the perpetrator returned with two accomplices and a metal pole, striking the victim on the leg, arm, and back before hitting his head multiple times. As the victim tried to defend himself, the accomplices restrained him, punching him repeatedly. Covered in blood, the victim struggled to call for help. The attacker also vandalized the victim's car. The victim sustained a deep scalp wound, swelling to his forehead, and bruising to his arms and legs. The perpetrator received a six-and-a-half-year prison sentence.

Approximately 15–20 members of Golden Dawn, wearing T-shirts that read ‘Golden Dawn Saturday Night’, attacked five people from Pakistan. Two of the victims were badly beaten and suffered severe injuries. When the police arrived, the perpetrators continued their attack and the polcie arrested the victims.

A 24-year-old man was arrested and sentenced to several years in prison for multiple crimes, including a racially aggravated assault on a dark-skinned girl and her friend during a Pride festival. At the Pride festival, the perpetrator randomly targeted a mix-race woman and racially insulted her. This woman ended up with a broken jaw from a punch that knocked her unconscious. When the victim's white friend intervened, he assaulted her too and referred to her as a "n***** lover" and was repeatedly kicked and punched.

An English Defence League supporter lit and then threw firework at peaceful anti-jubilee protesters as they gathered for a rally. It landed in the hood of a 19-year-old, exploded on his shoulder and set fire to his hair and hoodie. The victim's friends patted down his body to stop the fire from spreading, and the force of the blast burned a hole in his jumper. A "Stuff the Jubilee party" EDL protest was organized at the same time, and the EDL and anti-jubilee protesters clashed. Members of the anti-jubilee group criticised the clashes and an organiser said: “We had planned a pro-republican demonstration but the EDL and the National Front and the Infidels charged at the Monument and ripped our banners down.” The victim was in pain, he perforated his ear drum and suffered a burn mark to his right shoulder.

A journalist from the Jerusalem Post was attacked by a group of about twenty people, with covered faces, while they were beating immigrants and homeless people in the street. The journalist had tried to take pictures of the attack before he was severely beaten for about 15 minutes. The perpetrators also removed his camera. The victim was rushed to the hospital after having received blows to the head and chest. There is limited information about injuries concerning the other victims.

Two well-known neo-nazis were arrested on the suspicion of preparing a 'serious act of violence that could endanger the state.' They allegedly planned an attack on a vehicle belonging to the left-wing state parliament member from Jena. The police had first arrested a former NPD member who is said to have supported the Nationalist Socialist Underground (NSU) and provided them with weapon and ammunition. His arrest started another preliminary investigation, which led to a large-scale raid in which two men, aged 28 and 34, were arrested. The police had intercepted text messages with references to explosives, specifically how modelig clay had to be kept away rom 'electrical sources.' Two weeks later, one of the members sent a text message reading 'I've got your toy with me, you can now herald the Last Judgment.' The message ended with: 'Heil Beate!', appearing to be a twin reference to 'Heil Hitler!' and one of the NSU members, who was in pretrial detention at the time. 'Beate will be proud of us,' the other replied. The 34-year-old was believed to have had connections to people close to the NSU cell. The 28-year-old was regarded as a senior figure in the far-right scene. He had run as a candidate for the NPD party in state elections in 2009. He was also the leader of Freies Nets Saalfield [Free Network Saalfeld] of Thüringen Aktionsbüro.

A group of people broke into the house of the victim with knives and threatened him and the other immigrants there that they had to get out and leave the area or face the consequences. When they returned a third time, the perpetrators wore Golden Dawn uniforms and badly beat the people there, injuring more than ten people.

weapon_description: Brass knuckles, pepper spray, belts, beating/kicking
description: A group of 50 CasaPound members shouted fascist slogans and attacked concert-goers. The perpetrators, who entered the venue with tickets, gathered under the stage, chanting "Duce, duce" and waving a CasaPound flag. The crowd responded with whistles, prompting the attackers to start beating and kicking them, using belts and brass knuckles, and spraying pepper spray, which made the air inside the venue unbreathable. At least five people were injured, including facial trauma and bruising, and required medical attention.

A group of 10–20 Golden Dawn members attacked the house of five Egyptian fishermen. They damaged two cars outside the house before entering the house. Four of the Egyptians managed to escape. However a 28-year-old man sleeping in the attic was unable to get away and ended up severly beaten. He suffered amongst other injuries a fractured jaw and a broken nose. He was taken to the hospital for treatment and the police shortly after detained five men and a woman who were identified as taking part in the attack.

Two men with a pitbull on a leash approached an elections' stand of the Greek communist party (KKE). Without a reason they threw water and orange juice at the microphones chanting “Communists, you will die”. When a member of the party demanded an explanation for the attack, the men immediately started beating him on the face and the head. An eye-witness suggested the perpetrators attacked the victim with an iron fist. The victim was injured and fell to the ground bleeding while the men fled. He was later taken to the hospital. Allegedly, the perpetrators were from the extreme-right Golden Dawn party.

weapon_description: Baseball bats, fence slats, power cables, and tear gas
description: A group of 14 leftists, aged 16 to 23, was ambushed by ten suspected neo-Nazis during a party on a riverbank in Bad Dürrenberg. The masked perpetrators, armed with baseball bats, fence slats, power cables, and tear gas, attacked the group, injuring six people. Five attackers, aged 21 to 24, were arrested. The state security police, responsible for investigating political crimes, handled the case. This assault was one of a series of attacks targeting political opponents in the area, including CaseID 2011-2-23.

Two motorbikes with four people surrounded an immigrant from Pakistan on his bike and forced him to stop. They beat him severly, breaking his neck, severly injuring his head, cutting his hand and more. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

A 79-year-old man attacked several women and injured three girls from Belarus. The incident happened on a playground. The perpetrator insulted the victims with xenophobic slurs. According to police, the man grabbed two of the girls by the neck and arm and pushed them to the ground. He hit a third girl with a stick. The man was investigated for dangerous bodily harm. The police suspected that the attack was motivated by xenophobia. The severity threshold of this case is lowered due to the deliberate targeting of children.

A group of people attacked and injured two homeless migrants of Algerian origin. They were hospitalized. The incident was followed by an attack on an Egyptian migrant a few days later in the same town (see CaseID 2012-6-19). Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

A 25-year-old Pakistani immigrant was attacked by a group of neo-Nazis while on his way to work. The perpetrators hit him with a brass knuckles on the back of the head and on the face. The victim passed out and was brought to the hospital by passers-by. This was one of several attacks in Nikaia against Pakistani immigrants by groups of perpetrators on motorbikes during a period of two weeks. Allegedly, the attacks occurred after the Golden Dawn opened offices in the area.

Two homeless migrants of Algerian origin were attacked by four people with iron bars and knives when they were sleeping at the beach. The perpetrators arrived at the location on two motorbikes, and upon realizing the two victims were immigrants, the perpetrators attacked them. After the attack, the perpetrators stole the victims' clothing, mobile phones and money. The victims were brought to the hospital and treated for head injuries, abrasions and fractures. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

A group of youths stabbed a migrant from Pakistan at a metro station. The attack was captured in a video that was uploaded on the internet. In the video, one of the perpetrators asked "Did you stab him?" and another answered "The knife went right through him." The perpetrators were suggested to be Golden Dawn members.

A 34-year-old black man was attacked by six strangers in the evening. As he tried to walk past the perpetrators, he was jostled and insulted with racist language. The perpetrators then beat the victim with sticks. One of the perpetrators also pulled out a knife. The victim managed to snatch the stick from one of the perpetrators, five of the perpetrators fled. The remaining perpetrator attacked the victim with the knife. The victim managed to hold onto the perpetrator's hand, but suffered a bleeding cut on his hand. The attack stopped when the police arrived. Apart from the cut wounds, the victim suffered multiple bruises all over his body.

A 25-year-old Egyptian man was beaten by two men wielding a crowbar and a club in what was described as a racist incidence. The victim was hospitalised in a serious condition and required a kidney operation as a result of the attack. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

A 25-year-old migrant from Egypt was attacked by two people who beat the man with wooden objects and iron sticks. The attackers fled, while the victim was taken to the hospital. The doctors had to remove one of his kidneys due to severe damage. The incident followed an attack against two Algerian migrants in Chania a few days earlier (see CaseID 2012-6-16). Eyewitnesses suggested the attack was carried out by members of the neo-Nazi Golden Dawn organization. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

A 38-year-old Roma woman in a wheelchair was attacked by two 55- and 42-year-old men of Nordic apperance. She was punched and kicked multiple times. When the victim fell out of her wheelchair unconcious, the men continued kicking her. The woman had an amputated leg, and the men also kicked her legstump multiple times according to witnesses. The victim was hospitalized for several days after the attack. The police stated that the attack seemed to be racially motivated. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

The 32-year-old singer of a punk band was stabbed during a music festival. There was an altercation after the concerts between two gangs, one from the far left, the other from the far-right. It was reported that a person from the far-right group had started the fight before fleeing. The victim was stabbed in the abdomen, arm and under the shoulder during the fight. He was critically injured, but survived the attack. According to the victim's father, the main perpetrator was a member of the Artam Brotherhood, a neo-Nazi group. According to the victim himself, he "was attacked by a fascist who was not there by chance." The victim also got charges against him, as he was believed to have beaten the perpetrator. The attack sparked anti-fascist demonstrations in Geneva.

Unknown people started throwing rocks against the facade of an occupied house used to house political refugees before they threw three powerful paper bombs at the windows of the ground floor. One of the bombs hit a Sudanese man sleeping in the face, causing severe injuries to his right eye. Anti-fascists suspected that CasaPound were behind the attack.

A Black wheelchair user was brutally attacked by three unidentified men while with a group of friends. The assailants hurled racial insults at the victim, prompting a companion to intervene in an attempt to defuse the situation. However, the attackers knocked the victim to the ground and continued their assault before fleeing the scene. Two passers-by rushed to provide first aid, but the victim sustained significant facial injuries as a result of the attack.

A Pakistani immigrant was riding his bike to work when he was attacked by four people on motorbikes in a public square. They threw him under the bike, punched him in the face, and beat and kicked him all over his body. The victim suffered a broken nose. This was one of several attacks in Nikaia against Pakistani immigrants by groups of perpetrators on motorbikes during a period of two weeks. Allegedly, the attacks occurred after the Golden Dawn opened offices in the area.

Two Asian brothers were attacked in an unprovoked, racially aggravated assault by a 21-year-old and a 17-year-old. One victim was repeatedly kicked in the face while on the ground, as the attackers hurled racist abuse. An eyewitness, fearing for his own safety, refrained from intervening but later described the severity of the attack, believing one victim could die from the kicks. After finishing the assault, the attackers, visibly intoxicated, congratulated each other. The 21-year-old was sentenced to 12 months in prison, while the 17-year-old received a 12-month detention and training order.

weapon_description: Beating/kicking, throwing of heavy objects and cigarette butts
description: Three men, aged between 17 and 23, broke into the apartment of a 59-year-old man and demanded money from him for alcohol. He gave them two euros, but when they found his wallet contained 25 euros, they began attacking the man - punching him repeatedly, smashing a chair on his head and even throwing his television at him. The perpetrators briefly left to buy alcohol and returned to further show their contempt for the victim. They urinated on him and put lit cigarette butts into his nostrils. The victim died the following day from the injuries sustained and was found four days later by a social worker. One of the perpetrators recieved eleven years imprisonment, another a nine year youth sentence. while the trial of the third was postponed due to his cancer diagnosis. The motive was allegedly a Darwinist outlook on life and they consided the victim as worthless. One of the perpetrators owned swastikas and had arranged or attended a party on Hitler’s birthday.

After the Italy-Germany football match, four Italian men racially abused and brutally attacked a 38-year-old Bangladeshi man. While the victim was waiting at a bus stop, the perpetrators shouted racial slurs at him, including "Go away n*****! You can't wait here, you're a n*****... I'll send you to your country." The attack escalated when one of the men hit the victim on the head with a glass bottle, then proceeded to beat and kick him while he was on the ground. The victim was hospitalized and required delicate surgery on his nose, among other medical treatments.

During a celebration of Spain's victory in the European Football Championship, a group of approximately 30 far-right football fans associated with neo-Nazi groups launched racist attacks targeting migrants and minorities. The perpetrators actively sought out victims based on the color of their skin. One victim, a street seller wearing a Barcelona t-shirt, received a blow to the head that caused a large cut which bled heavily. While the victim was searching for his lost glasses, several neo-Nazis kicked him until he was unconscious. The perpetrators attacked multiple street sellers, though the exact number of victims remains unknown. Throughout the incident, they hurled racial insults at others based on their ethnicity. The Mossos d'Esquadra arrested three individuals, including two minors, in connection with the racist attacks during the celebration. The perpetrators, identified as a group of young individuals carrying Spanish flags, neo-Nazi symbols, and Celtic motifs, also burned a Catalan flag during the incident. In addition to the racist assaults, the perpetrators engaged in violent acts against the police, throwing blunt objects and setting fire to 14 containers. While three individuals were arrested, further arrests were not ruled out.

weapon_description: P38 pistols, 7.65 Beretta handguns, SS knives, a mortar, war bombs
description: A 34-year-old man was arrested after police discovered "an authentic supermarket of weapons, ammunition, and bombs" at his home in the mountains. Authorities seized a vast array of weapons, including war relics, a mortar, P38 pistols, 7.65 Beretta handguns, SS knives, and war bombs that required examination by bomb squads. Some of the weapons were operational, while others, originally intended for collectors, had been repaired for use. Four additional individuals are under investigation for assisting the perpetrator. The man was also in contact with a well-known neo-fascist figure, the founder of Ordine Nuovo, who is under investigation for involvement in the 1969 Piazza Fontana bombing. Police suspect that the perpetrator acted as a custodian of arms for anti-democratic far-right groups.

A group of seven far-right sympathisers attacked a heavily outnumbered group of anti-fascists heading to a benefit event at News From Nowhere radical & community bookshop. The perpetrators, some of whom were wearing masks, punched and kicked their victims. The victims were pursued into a restaurant where the they were beaten to the ground. One of the victims suffered a lump to his head in the size of a golf ball. Six men, allegedly members or sympathisers of far-right groups, including the British National Party (BNP), the English Defence League and the North West Infidels, were jailed for between nine and 17 months. The attack was allegedly planned.

Three people set fire to a home for asylum seekers. The attack happened during the night. A window was set on fire in the building where around 100 people were inside. A guard managed to put out the fire before anyone got hurt. A right-wing extremist motive was confirmed after two of the perpetrators confessed to the crime.

A group of eight right-wing extremists, six men and two women, attacked functionaries and visitors of a leftist art center. The perpetrators arrived at the opening of an exhibition while shouting Nazi slogans. The organizers of the event informed the police about the disturbances, and expelled the perpetrators from the site. Shortly after, the curator of the exhibition was beaten up and suffered a broken nose. The director of the facility was hit over the head with a full beer bottle. A visitor got her head smashed into the hood of a car on her way home. A police officer was attacked and seriously injured. Other visitors were hit with bottles and injured. Five of the victims were treated in the hospital. The perpetrators were arrested and investigated for dangerous bodily harm.

Two men smashed the window of a house where a Polish man lived, chasing him into the street and brutally beating him in the head and face. They left him lying semi-conscious in the road. The victim sustained lacerations to his nose and mouth, suspected fractures, and multiple bruises to his head and body, requiring hospitalization. When the perpetrators were arrested, several weapons, including knives and a brush shaft, were found, although they denied using them during the assault. Both men were sentenced to 18 and 21 months in prison after admitting to grievous bodily harm. The judge noted that the attack had strong racist overtones.
40 people with helmets, hoods, bats and knives severely injured an Armenian, Iraqi and two Syrian immigrants. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

Five Indian and Pakistani immigrants were injured after being attacked in their homes by around 20 masked men. Allegedly, the victims were beaten with clubs and metal bars. One of the victims suffered a broken arm, while another had cuts and bruises all over his body. The perpetrators, who were suggested to be Golden Dawn members, looted a total of seven houses that day.

During a discussion led by organisers of an upcoming pride parade, an openly gay member of Finnish parliament was attacked with pepper spray by activists from the Finnish Resistance Movement. The victim was hospitalised. The police quickly identified the motive as political aimed at disrupting the discussion event which focused on the threat posed by the extreme right and the perpetrators. One of the perpetrators was also involved in CaseID: 2013-1-30.

A 17-year-old boy suffered face injuries and a suspected broken jaw after racist abuse and attack by a gang of boys. The victim was riding his bike through the park when he was attacked and racist abuse was shouted at him by the perpetrators. Police went to the scene and three youths, two aged 15 and one aged 17, were arrested on suspicion of racially aggravated wounding. He was treated for his injuries at the hospital.
According to the police, a Pakistani citizen was the victim of dangerous bodily harm for racist reasons. A suspect was identified. No further details are available.

A 41-year-old journalist narrowly escaped injury when a firecracker exploded near his office, tearing a hole in a neighboring building's roof. The incident occurred months after his reporting on a neo-Nazi gathering in Brandenburg. Following the article's publication, his office was targeted with posters reading "Lying press, shut up," and animal innards were smeared on its entrance. Police linked the attacks to his coverage of right-wing extremists. Over the months, the journalist faced ongoing threats and intimidation. A respected journalist with awards for his reporting on neo-Nazism, his case drew national attention as part of a series of right-wing attacks in Spremberg. This ultimately led to the ban of the neo-Nazi group "Widerstand Südbrandenburg." The perpetrators remain unidentified.

The apartment of a family of Turkish immigrants was subjected to an arson attack by three men and a woman, aged 25 to 43, during the night. The perpetrators were drunk when they broke the glass of the front door window and shouted xenophobic slurs and "Sieg Heil". The perpetrators then threw a burning rag at the front door. One of the victims managed to put out the fire in the entrance hall. Eight people were in the apartment at the time of the attack, but nobody was injured. The perpetrators were arrested and the crime was investigated as an attempt at serious arson. The police did not confirm that the perpetrators had any connection to the right-wing extremist scene.

In the evening, the employees of a kebab shop were initially racially abused by two men. When the perpetrators began to riot, two of the victims stood in the doorway. A physical altercation ensued. One of the perpetrators pulled out a knife and cut one of the victims. The perpetrators continued to chase and beat the already injured victim when he tried to flee. The other employees were able to prevent further attacks until the police arrived.

Five immigrants from India were waiting at a bus stop when five young people, aged 15-19, drove by. At the sight of the immigrants, the perpetrators stopped the car, got out and started beating one of them. When the other immigrants intervened, they were also attacked, including with a knife. The perpetrators were charged with attempted murder and causing dangerous bodily harm. The incident was part of a series of attacks on immigrants, after a Pakistani was arrested for having severely injured and sexually abused a 15-year-old girl on the island of Paros a week earlier. In one attack, a group of Pakistanis were attacked by several young men. In another attack, two people on motorcycles hurled smoke bombs at the home of a Bangladeshi man. These incidents did not meet the requirements for inclusion in the dataset. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

A 44-year-old man, accompanied by his partner, shot at a group of young Muslims celebrating the breaking of the Ramadan fast. The attack occurred in a supermarket parking lot and lasted around forty minutes, during which the man fired at least eight shots, injuring one person. The couple also targeted a car containing a mother and her child of Maghrebi origin. The man and his partner, both intoxicated, made racist remarks during the assault. The couple was immediately arrested, with the man sentenced to four years in prison and the woman to two years. Both were convicted of violence with aggravating circumstances, including premeditation, alcohol use, weapon possession, and targeting victims based on ethnicity or religion.

An 18-year-old woman and her mother were attacked on the street. The two victims, both wearing headscarves, had just exited the emergency room after the mother had had a seizure when a screaming man ran towards them and started hitting her with his shoe, kicking her and pounding her head against the wall until she fainted. When the daughter intervened, he also attacked her. The attacker shouted insults like "You are destroying the country" and "It's all your fault". Nurses intervened and held the attacker until police arrived. The perpetrator was reportedly active in "Tryckfrihetssällskapet" [Society for Freedom of the Press].

A Roma man and his son were out walking when they were attacked and beaten with shovels and spades by a group of men. The father was kicked in the face, and they were both beaten with shovels and spades. One victim said: "We had a few drinks and we were singing, but we weren't doing anyone any harm, next thing it's 'dirty gypsy this, dirty gypsy that'." The victim claims the responsible for the attack were the same who set his wife's home on fire earlier. Nobody was home when the arson attack happened (and therefore excluded from the RTV dataset). A week after the attack a boot mark from the kick to the father's face was still clearly visible. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

After a match between the football club "Alemannia Aachen" and "FC Saarbrücken", around 100 right-wing fans of Alemannia Aachen attacked left-wing fans of the same team. The perpetrators were members of "Karlsbande Ultras" (KBU), among them were neo-Nazis from the "Kameradschaft Aachener Land", and the victims were members of the anti-racist "Aachen Ultras" (ACU). When the victims left the stadium, the perpetrators were waiting for them. They were attacked with flagpoles, bottles and belts. One victim was brought to the ground by around 15 perpetrators and beaten and kicked for several minutes. One victim was kicked repeatedly in the head. Between 10 and twenty victims were injured. The ACU are committed to the fight against fascism, racism, violence and homophobia. Despite claiming to be apolitical, the KBU has the goal of driving the ACU out of the stadiums. The case is connected to CaseID 2013-1-12. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

A 26-year-old mixed-race woman was attacked by a mother and her teenage daughter in an unprovoked racist assault while walking to a shop. The victim had just left home with a friend to buy baby wipes when the teenage girl began staring at them from across the road. The girl then struck the victim from behind, followed by a barrage of punches. The girl’s mother joined in, grabbing the victim by the throat while another individual restrained the victim’s friend. The pair beat the woman on the ground for several minutes before she managed to escape, suffering a black eye, broken rib, mild concussion, and other injuries. A 39-year-old woman and a 15-year-old were arrested on suspicion of actual bodily harm.

weapon_description: Knife, bottles, pepper spray and beating/kicking
description: A group of anti-fascists were attacked by at least six members of the right-wing extremist group “Besseres Hannover”. The victims were standing at an information stand for the “Kampagne Nazis die Räume nehmen”. The police, who had been protecting the event, had just left when the perpetrators appeared. A scuffle broke out between the parties. The perpetrators threw bottles, took out one of the victims and began beating and kicking him while spraying with pepper spray. One of the perpetrators stabbed one of the victims with a knife. The perpetrators continued the violence in a nearby town (CaseID 2012-8-10-2).

After attacking the information stand of an anti-fascist campaign (CaseID 2012-8-10-1), members of the right-wing extremist group “Besseres Hannover” attacked a left-wing youth club. The same perpetrator who had stabbed a victim on the information stand in CaseID 2012-8-10-1, stabbed an anti-fascist who was attending the youth club. The victim suffered injuries to his face and back.

According to the police, during an Nationaldemokratische Partei Deutschlands (NPD) rally, two left-wing individuals were victims of dangerous bodily harm. An additional incident involved attempted dangerous bodily harm against another left-wing individual. Two suspects were identified, but limited information is available.

Three men wearing traditional Islamic clothes were referred to as “terrorists” and racially insulted by a group of five men and one woman as they walked on the street. The group then attacked the victims with punches and kicks. One of the victims was knocked unconscious while another suffered injuries to his eye and ear after having his head stamped on.

The victim, who was from Iraq, was found covered in blood, with a broken leg, and bruises covering his body. He had been detained in Athens and taken to Xanthi by the police. The police, upon realizing he had legal papers allowing him to stay in the country, released him but did not transport him back to his residence in Athens. He was therefore in Xanthi without money to get back to the city. He decided to hitch hike and was then attacked by a group of people in black uniforms on motorcycles. They beat him until a witness arrived, after which the perpetrators left and he was taken to the hospital. The witness raised money for him to travel back to Athens. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

Early in the morning, five dark-clad people on four motorcycles rode through the neighborhood of Omonia Square in central Athens, hunting down immigrants. Upon encountering a 19-year-old Iraqi, they beat him with their fists and stones and stabbed him several times with a knife. The young man died the same day in a hospital. Earlier that night, in the same area, the five men had tried to attack another two migrant males (citizens of Romania and Morocco), who managed to escape.  Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

A group of unidentified individuals carried out attacks early in the morning with stones, sticks, knives and bats, attempting to break the doors and windows of houses where immigrants lived. Several Pakistanis were attacked. One of the victims was stabbed with a knife and required hospital treatment, while another victim was hit on the head with a bat. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

A 24-year-old man and his accomplices terrorised a Eastern European family by putting a lit firework through the door of their home as they slept. The Kosovan father woke up by a noise, he went downstairs and saw the hall carpet was on fire. He managed to stamp the flames out before one of the perpetrators threw another two at the house. Some firework was pushed through their letterbox. The father went outside and saw three youths who used an offensive racist word. The family was so traumatised that they planned on leaving the country. One of the perpetrators, who was later arrested, bragged in police interview: "EPNW, English Pride, Nation Wide." He was later sentenced to prison for 3 years and 11 months.

Two Pakistanis were attacked and injured in the home they were living in. An unknown number of people broke into the house where the Pakistanis were staying and started beating them with fists, kicks and wooden beams. The victims were hospitalized with blows to their heads and other parts of the body. The incident was part of a series of attacks on immigrants by assailants on motorcycles, after a Pakistani was arrested for having severely injured and sexually abused a 15-year-old girl on the island of Paros a week earlier.

Seven perpetrators wearing helmets and black clothes, holding Greek flags, attacked a 32-year-old Sudanese migrant. They got off the motorcycles and started to kick the victim to the ground. His friend injured his hand and managed to run off. The victim was repeatedly beaten with a club and stabbed with a knife and was left bleeding and unconscious. When he came around, about 20 minutes later, his red t-shirt was ripped the perpetrators had carved a large 'X' on his back. Images of the victims scarred back reached international media. The victim suspected that members of Golden Dawn were involved in the attack. Due to the timeframe, location and Modus Operandi, it may be suspected that Golden Dawn was behind the attack.

A taxi driver of Nigerian origins was attacked by three passengers - a married couple and their friend. The perpetrators got into the victim’s taxi and began insulting him for the color of his skin. The victim stopped briefly and asked them to stop making such comments. As he drove on, the perpetrator continued the racist abuse. One of the perpetrators, a 33-year-old man, grabbed the driver by the neck from behind and spat on him. The other male perpetrator hit the victim from behind, slightly injuring him. The attack caused the victim to lose control of the car and crash into a parked Mercedes. The couple were caught by the police, but their friend managed to escape. The property damage amounted to around 40,000 euros.

At around 10:30 AM, a woman and her two sons were racially abused by an unknown woman in the train station. The perpetrator sprayed tear gas in the face of the  six-year-old son and injured him. The severity threshold of this case is lowered due to the deliberate targeting of children.

A group of people with their faces covered attacked two street vendors of African descent. The victims were severely beaten and left "covered in blood". Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

Two Turkish sisters, aged 45 and 52, were victims of a violent, racially motivated attack in a parking lot during the early evening. The assailants, a man and a woman, verbally abused and racially insulted the sisters before severely beating and kicking them. The attack, reportedly triggered by one of the victims wearing a headscarf, left both sisters hospitalized. The 52-year-old sustained serious head injuries requiring intensive care. A few days later, police identified the attackers as a 23-year-old woman and her 33-year-old male companion, both with prior records for assault and drug offenses.

A 17-year-old leftist man was attacked by neo-Nazis while taking action against right-wing symbols in public. The victim, who was a member of the SPD-affiliated youth organization “Die Falken”, was covering right-wing stickers when he was ambushed by the masked perpetrators. The perpetrators hit the victim in the face and head while shouting political slurs. The victim was taken to the hospital with a concussion, bruises on his cheekbones and nose, and impaired vision.

A group of around 15 young men organized a punitive attack on a migrant welcome center, intending to "teach a foreigner a lesson." They threw several rocks at the center, and one of the rocks struck the head of the person in charge. The victim was hospitalized and required stitches for a head wound.

A 26-year-old Turk and a 46-year-old Iranian were attacked and, according to the police, seriously injured by a group of six to ten German men. The incident happened in front of a discotheque at nighttime. The perpetrators shouted racist slogans and attacked the victims before fleeing in a minibus. Both victims suffered injuries that had to be treated in the hospital. The 24-year-old was still in the hospital two days after the attack. Based on the nature of the crime and the statements made by the perpetrators, the police assumed that the crime was motivated by xenophobia.

Leftist activists were subjected to a near-fatal knife attack by masked perpetrators suspected of ties to the right-wing extremist scene. After a peaceful festival at the left-wing occupied house "Rote Flora," the attackers, dressed in black, arrived and set a fire that spread to a nearby tree, threatening the building. When the victims attempted to extinguish the flames, the perpetrators used iron bars and knives to attack them, injuring several. Two victims, aged 27 and 29, were stabbed, with the 29-year-old sustaining life-threatening injuries and rushed to the hospital. The 27-year-old stated he was trying to mediate a dispute when attacked. The perpetrators remain unidentified, but the victims attributed the attack to right-wing extremists. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

A group of people on motorcycles drove pas the house of a Pakistani immigrant and threw an explosive device into his yard. The victim suffered severe burns on his back and arms and had to be hospitalized. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

Three neo-Nazis placed a molotov cocktail inside the home of two Pakistani immigrants while they were sleeping. The device exploded on the mattress of one of the victims. He was hospitalised in the intensive care unit with severe burns on his back and hand.

A 25-year-old man was stabbed in the neck after challenging a 27-year-old woman about racist remarks. The victim and friends had just left a bar when the attack happened. Once outside they overheard a woman making alleged racist comments about a black passer-by and challenged her. The group then left to walk away when they heard glass smashing behind them. Two women shouted after them: "We are going to kill you. Do you know who you are walking away from?" The victim then claimed to see a woman moving a knife in front of his face, before he realised he had been stabbed. The victim needed stiches and hospital treatment, and the wound inflicted was just millimetres away from severing a main artery.

Four Golden Dawn members threw two molotov cocktails at some apartment buildings where many Syrian refugees were staying. Two victims were injured, one of whom was hit in the head and the other in the back.

A young Bangladeshi suffered extensive injuries after being set upon by a group of men. The perpetrators drew up on motorcycles before beating, kicking and stabbing the victim. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included. Modus operandi similar to that of Golden Dawn.

A 41-year-old anti-fascist was subjected to a knife attack by two suspected neo-Nazis. The victim was one of the most prominent opponents of fascism in the local community, and a member of the union “Antifaschistischen Aktion Lüneburg / Uelzen”. The victim was closing the doors to the union house for the evening when the perpetrators approached him and addressed him by name. The perpetrators attacked him with a knife. The victim suffered injuries to his arm and had to be treated in the hospital. Shortly before the incident, the victim had spotted four neo-Nazis pointing at him from a car. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

Five young people were harassed and racially insulted by an unknown man while walking home from a market in the evening. Ignoring the perpetrator, they were followed and continued to be insulted. Soon, other men, apparently part of the same group, joined the pursuit. The victims attempted to flee but were chased through the streets, some by car. A 16-year-old was caught, attacked from behind, and kicked in the face, resulting in the loss of an incisor, a broken nose, and a bleeding lip laceration. He managed to escape to a nearby police station and was taken to the hospital, where he underwent surgery .

A 23-year-old man was hospitalized after being brutally beaten and kicked by three members of the right-wing extremist group "Weiße Wölfe Terrorcrew." The attackers, who had been drinking at the neo-Nazi bar “Zum Henker,” targeted the victim on the street, believing him to be a left-wing activist. The assault forced the victim to flee into a kebab shop, where employees defended him with a kebab skewer. The perpetrators followed, hurling racial insults at the employees before a plainclothes police officer intervened and arrested them. They were charged with dangerous bodily harm and insult.
Two Golden Dawn members on motorbikes stabbed a migrant in the back. The victim was hospitalized. There is limited information about this attack.

Eight hooded men in black approached the refugee camps in Dourgouti and started insulting an immigrant who was outside an apartment building. Then they threw three molotov cocktails at him and at the window of the building. No one was directly hit, but one immigrant was slightly injured. The antifascist organization KEERFA suggested the neo-Nazi organization Golden Dawn was behind the attack.

Nine people dressed in black entered a barbershop run by a Pakistani man. First, they verbally attacked a Greek customer, asking him why he was having a haircut in a shop owned by Pakistanis. When he reacted, the perpetrators stabbed him. They also stabbed one of the Pakistani employees. Then the perpetrators began to destroy the shop and throw molotov cocktails, one of which came so close to one of the employees' head that part of his hair was burned. According to the victims, the perpetrators, around 18 to 20 years old, passed by the barber shop almost every week and threatened to shut down the shop. A week before the attack they had thrown rocks and broken the shop windows. A 20-year-old Greek man was arrested on suspicion of belonging to a racist gang. A police statement said the suspect is believed to have taken part in the attack on the barber shop, as well as two other stabbings (see CaseID 2012-9-22a and CaseID 2012-9-22b) and one road attack that did not fit the criterias for inclusion in the dataset.

Around twenty people from CasaPound and Blocco Studentesco attacked anti-fascists at a party using helmets and sticks . Four people were hospitalized with injuries to their head and other parts of the body.

A 45-year-old Chinese man needed hospital treatment after being beaten by four men and a woman outside his home. The attack happended after the victim heard the glass in his front door being smashed and went to investigate. He was racially abused by the perpetrators before they punched him in the face and kicked him to the floor. His wife found him and took him to hospital, where he remained for several days after the attack. Police believed it was a racially motivated assault. One man was charged of assault causing actual bodily harm.

Two individuals, aged 31 and 24, assaulted a young man with a baseball bat and threatened him with a gun. One of the perpetrators, who was hiding his face with a hood, struck the victim with a baseball bat, while the other perpetrator threatened the victim with a pistol. The victim required medical attention for his injuries. A xenophobic motive was suspected, as the victim was a foreigner and the perpetrators were suspected of belonging to a skinhead cell with a history of targeting people they perceived as 'different.' As the perpetrators fled the scene, one of them dropped the gun's magazine, which contained three cartridges and was later found by witnesses. During a search of the perpetrators' rooms, police seized a detonator pistol, three knives, and items bearing neo-Nazi symbols. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

At around 1:30 AM, after an alternative concert had ended, a 34-year-old punk was still talking to two women near the venue when he was suddenly pushed to the ground from behind. He was then called a "fucking tick" by one of the five perpetrators. The victim was kicked in the chest and head. The violence stopped when a passerby intervened. The victim was taken to the hospital in an ambulance and was treated for a concussion and traumatic brain injury.

An anti-fascist was attacked by four neo-Nazis after a night out. The victim was at a club with a friend when they first encountered the perpetrators, who had been staring at him throughout the evening, which the victim chose to ignore. The perpetrators were dressed in neo-Nazi clothing, including t-shirts with the initials "ACAB" and the symbol of the far-right MSR party. As the victim and his friend left the club, they were followed by the perpetrators in a car. The perpetrators began to harass the victim and threw large beer bottles at their heads, resulting in the victim requiring stitches to the scalp.

A group of 7 to 8 people approached a father from Afghanistan and his 14-year-old son. They asked them what they were doing there, before grabbing the boy, punching and kicking him. When the father pulled his son away and ushered him to run, they started beating the father with a chain and broken bottle and stabbed him with a knife. The boy saw a police car drive past slowly, without intervening. After the group had left he helped get his father to a hospital where he had stitches and was unable to move for two days. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

A group of eight people attacked four people who were putting up anti-racist posters. One of the victims, who had a Muslim background and was a known anti-racist, was seriously injured. A few days later, a 30-year-old security guard and known member of Golden Dawn was arrested for the attack.
