A 50-year-old Bangladeshi man was attacked with a bottle when he was walking home. The victim was beaten repeatedly over the head with the bottle, completely unprovoked, before the attacker ran off. He managed to reach home after being offered help by a passer-by. He called police himself and was rushed to hospital with serious face injuries. He needed surgery for a severe gash to the left side of his head and he also had injuries to his hand. Police said it appeared he was targeted for no other reason than the colour of his skin and treated the attack as a racially motivated attack. Motive not explicitly stated but sufficiently evident to be included.

Three men randomly attacked and killed the victim. The perpetrators had been at a party where a girl had said she felt threatened by immigrant boys. The story was made up, but the perpetrators decided to go for a "run", interpreted by another at the party that they went looking for the boys. Around the same time, the victim was kicked out of a pub for drunk behavior. The victim was not of immigrant background and it is unclear why he was targeted. However, according to The Nordic Resistance Movements own account of the events, the victim was trying to push drugs on the perpetrators. He met the three perpetrators by an ATM. The victim talked to one of the perpetrators, before another one put him in a chokehold. The third perpetrator started punching the victim before they stabbed him eight times and began kicking him in the head. The victim died a few days later from the injuries sustained. The day before the attack, the three perpetrator had attended a meeting for one of the combat groups of the Swedish Resistance Movement [later known as the Nordic Resistance Movement], who was more violent at the time. On November 1, an article was published on the Nordic Resistance Movements pages about the incident, describing the perpetrator as an activist who "is known for always standing up and helping and never giving up in confrontations". Two of the perpetrators were arrested but the third withdrew a large amount of money and disappeared without a trace after a TV series titled Efterlyst [Wanted] showed CCTV images from the attack. A previous member of NRM has said that the organization donated money to the perpetrator after he fled. As of 2021, the third suspect is still at large and is on Interpols wanted list.

Three Pakistani men walking on the street behind the FAGE factory in Metamorfosi were stopped by a car with four people and one on motorcycle who asked where they were from. When they answered, the men attacked them with knives, one was stabbed in the hand, the other in the chest. The two injured men managed to get treated in a nearby hospital while the third went to file a complaint at the police station. Due to the timeframe, location and Modus Operandi, it may be suspected that Golden Dawn was behind the attack. In April 2024, one of the perpetrators was arrested again after organizing an attack on police officers, fatally injuring one victim (caseID 2023-12-7). The police reported that the perpetrator was known as a member of the Golden Dawn who had carried out four racist attacks in 2012, including this specific case (the other caseIDs were not identifiable).

Three people attacked two immigrants from Pakistan with a knife at a bus stop. One of them was seriously injured in the chest. The police later arrested one of the perpetrators of the attack, a 20-year-old man, who was accused of being a member of a racist group. The group was behind several attacks on immigrants that occurred in September 2012 (see CaseID 2012-9-10 and CaseID 2012-9-22b) and a road attack that did not fit the criterias for inclusion in the dataset.

Two Nigerians had just left Omonia metro station when six young Greeks on motorbikes began chasing them. The perpetrators eventually caught up with the victims and started to beat them. Then they pulled out knives and other sharp objects from their motorbikes and stabbed the victims. One of them suffered serious injuries and was admitted to the hospital for four days. The other victim stated that he had identified the attackers as members of the neo-Nazi Golden Dawn organization, based on their clothing.

A Moroccan immigrant was attacked by four largely unknown perpetrators. One of them approached the victim, saying, "Stop, police!" while showing a police badge. The other three assailants surrounded the victim, pinned him against a wall, and beat him with metal bars. In addition to the assault, the victim had 170€ stolen from his wallet. One of the perpetrators was recognized as a police officer and the son of the city's mayor. The attackers are the same group involved in caseID 2012-11-9-1, who organized patrols to "hunt down immigrants."

A 30-year-old Greek man was attacked by around ten suspected neo-Nazis, aged 18 to 25. The perpetrators rioted in front of the victim’s restaurant. When the victim stepped outside he was attacked by the group, who shouted xenophobic slurs and hate speech. The victim suffered head injuries and was taken to the hospital where he was treated as an inpatient. The perpetrators were investigated for  dangerous bodily harm and incitement to hatred.

On his way home from an anti-racist demonstration through a folk festival, an 18-year-old was suddenly attacked by a group of about 10 people, described as obvious right-wing extremists. The victim was identified as an anti-fascist by a slogan on his sweater. The perpetrators hit him in the face several times. When the victim fell to the ground, they continued to kick him. Only when a group of leftists intervened, who were also on their way back from the demonstration,  did the perpetrators let go of the victim. The victim had to spend a week in hospital. He suffered whiplash and an open facial injury. The root of one of his teeth was also broken.

A group of ten-twelve men shouting fascist slogans attacked the home of the Imam of the Pakistani Community in Greece. At the time of the attack, the Imam was not home, but two of his housemates were sleeping in the house. The perpetrators broke down the main door and a window, before attacking the housemates with a bat. One of them was seriously injured. When the police arrived, they arrested the victims to check their papers, while the perpetrators fled.

Unidentified perpetrators placed an improvised incendiary device, consisting of a plastic bag with gasoline and a canister, at the entrance of the apartment of three immigrants from Bangladesh. The arson caused damage to the entrance of the apartment and to the walls.

Two Pakistani immigrants riding on a motorcycle, were attacked by around five people. One of the perpetrators were driving a car when he approached the victims, telling them to "go to your country". He then blocked the road with his car, at which point four other people appeared. The five perpetrators, including the driver of the car, beat one of the victims with a knuckle duster on the head and face. The victim was treated in the hospital.

The sister-in-law of a local Roma leader was identified and pointed out by a man sitting at a café, before six or seven local men ran out of the premises and attacked her and her nephew. The victims were punched, kicked and beaten with logs. The attack took place amongst a series of vicious racist raids on Roma families in the same town between August 2012 and January 2013 (not all cases meet the inclusion criteria for the dataset).

Staff at a takeaway shop was racially abused, punched in the face and attempted stabbed with a knife by a white male. The victims were of foreign background. The perpetrator entered a takeaway shop and began hurling racist abuse. He then lifted a large blade from a counter and attempted to stab the takeaway manager. During the incident the man is also punched another member of staff in the face. The victim was treated at hospital because he was struck so hard he almost lost an eye and could not work. The perpetrator then fled and police were called. The Italian-born 37-year-old man who started the business said he was contemplating leaving Northern Ireland due to a number of racist incidents directed towards him and his staff.

About twenty Golden Dawn members attacked a 45-year-old member of ANTARSYA (Anticapitalist Left Cooperation for the Overthrow). The incident occurred in a cafe, when the victim made derogatory remarks towards the perpetrators. As a result, the victim received a strong blow to the head and was allegedly also pepper sprayed by the group. The victim was taken to the hospital with serious head injuries. Two members of the Golden Dawn were sentenced to twelve months of imprisonment.

Two Lebanese men were attacked by two men. The victims were on their way home to the residence for asylum seekers when the perpetrators, who were German, approached them. An argument broke out before the perpetrators attacked the victims with a knife and a baton. One of the victims were injured and had to be taken to the hospital. The police assumed that the crime was motivated by xenophobia.

A group of Golden Dawn patrolling with a car around the area stopped outside the house of a 20-year-old man from Pakistan. He was on the balcony when suddenly a guy came out of the car and shot at him with a carbine hunting rifle. The victim was injured on his hand. There were six other migrants inside but they were not injured.

Ten people wearing black T-shirts with the Golden Dawn logo stopped in front of a car wash where two Pakistani immigrants worked. Armed with clubs and crowbars they immediately began to beat the immigrants. One of the victims was taken to the hospital with a serious head injury.

A 21-year-old man attempted to set fire to a communal home housing a Turkish family of nine, including five children, at 2:30 AM. Intoxicated after a wine festival, he ignited bulky waste near a shed containing a heating oil tank and used a mattress to spread the fire. Trash bins were placed to block the family’s escape. Residents extinguished the flames before they spread. The police arrested the man shortly afterward, finding a swastika flag and right-wing extremist music in his apartment. The court identified xenophobia as his motive. The family had moved to the home after their previous residence was targeted in another arson attack. Initially charged with attempted murder, he was convicted of aggravated arson and sentenced to three years in prison.

Ten people threw smoke bombs into the house of Pakistani immigrants while they were sleeping and beat three of them. Two of the victims were transferred to the hospital, one of whom was unconscious. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

weapon_description: Chains, dogs and objects with nails in them
description: Four members of Golden dawn attacked a 21-year-old Egyptian man while shouting racist abuse. The victim was on his way to post a parcel to his father when he was approached and beaten repeatedly with chains in the face, bitten by dogs and hit by an object with nails in it.  He was severely injured and blinded by the incident.
According to the police, an Iranian citizen was the victim of a dangerous bodily harm for racist reasons. No suspect was identified. No further details are available.

17 young people affiliated with a gang of far-right skinheads were arrested following an attack on a homeless person. The victim suffered numerous insults and humiliations before being thrown into a bonfire. There is no reported information about the injuries from this attack. According to the Civil Guard of Madrid, the attack on the victim may have had xenophobic overtones. The Civil Guard of Madrid also stated that the perpetrators did not form a gang but acted in a coordinated manner. The perpetrators used a park as their meeting point to plan their actions. The 20-year-old leader of the group was sentenced to prison after this attack. During the investigation, police discovered that the same group had previously attacked two leftist brothers earlier in the month (case does not meet inclusion criteria). Additionally, the perpetrators were allegedly involved in two other assaults on August 2 and 4, one outside a local bar and another in front of a 24-hour shop (these cases do not meet inclusion criteria).

At around 3:30 AM, a 20-year-old employee at a kebab shop from Thailand was attacked by three men on his way home from work. The victim had been inside the shop when one of the perpetrators looked through the window and threw a full cup at the window. A few minutes later, the perpetrator returned, turned to the victim in front of the window and made "slit-eyed" faces and gave the Hitler salute twice. 15 minutes later, when the 20-year-old was on his way home, the perpetrator reappeared together with two friends. The victim was punched in the face and put in a headlock. The other perpetrators also hit him in the head. The victim managed to free himself. In hospital, he was diagnosed with a concussion and swelling on his cheek.

A 44-year-old woman was stabbed to death by a 25-year-old right-wing extremist. The victim was visiting the perpetrator's apartment as a prostitute. She made fun of the political sentiments of the perpetrator and described "Mein Kampf" as "shit". The perpetrator stabbed the victim in the heart with a machete, killing her instantly. He then dismembered the body and hid it in a close-by lake. The perpetrator was a rapper who made right-wing extremist, violence glorifying and misogynistic lyrics and videos. His ex-girlfriend, who testified in court, confirmed that the victim was murdered because she had made fun of the perpetrator's political views. He was sentenced to 12 years in prison for manslaughter.

Two left-wing alternative youths were attacked with bottles, punches and kicks by three neo-Nazis. One of the victims was so badly injured that he had to be taken to hospital by ambulance for treatment.

Some 150 people, including an unknown number of Golden Dawn members, attacked several migrants and damaged migrants' shops in the Aghios Panteleimonas neighborhood of Athens. The attacks came hours after an unidentified immigrant allegedly stabbed a hairdresser in the area before stealing cash from his shop. It remains unknown how many people were injured, but at least one person had to be transported to hospital with non-life-threatening injuries.

Fireworks were hurled into a shop run by Sri Lankans after someone shouted racist slurs. A couple and their two-year-old daughter had popped into the newsagent after going trick-or-treating. The door was then opened and a firework hurled in. To direct the firework away from his daughter, the male customer put his foot on it. It then exploded and lodged in the shoe of his girlfriend - piercing the leather and burning her foot, which she needed hospital treatment for. She said: "I heard someone shout 'Paki *****' at the shop owners and the firework landed right by our daughter." The shop owners said they have had issues with racist youths previously.

A 28-year-old Bangladeshi man was digging around trash bins for scrap metal when two women and a man set upon him with a knife. The victim was rushed to the hospital, where he was treated for a gash to the back of his thigh. Police are investigating the assault as a right-wing racist crime. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

Violent protests against increasing crime in the area broke out among residents two days after a robber of African origin had broken into a hair salon and attacked the hairdresser with a knife. During the protests, an angry mob of around 100 people started to smash the windows of shops belonging to migrants. Soon the situation escalated and almost every shop with name and signboard in foreign letters was targeted. During the incidence, a migrant of Algerian origin was found stabbed and was rushed to the hospital. Eye-witnesses also reported the mob to have chased migrants, while some were threatened with knives. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

During an anti-fascist rally, participants entered a shop in Koulori Square to distribute leaflets. A group of young people got up from a table and started shouting and punching the anti-fascists, and proclaimed themselves as supporters of the neo-Nazi organization Golden Dawn. When the victims tried to leave, a group of 15 people waited for them outside the shop and began to punch, kick and threaten them. One of the perpetrators pulled out a knife and began to chase the victims around the area. One of the victims suffered a dislocated shoulder and was brought to the hospital. A second victim suffered a wound on the face after having been hit with a metal object, and was brought to an outpatient clinic.

At a traffic light, a car approached the two victims who were on their motorcycle. They began racially insulting the victims and when the traffic light turned green, the car sped up and hit the motorcycle from behind. The two victims fell to the ground and were seriously injured. Both were taken to the hospital for treatment, and one of the victims suffered a severe leg fracture.

A group of six people attacked an Afghani immigrant. The victim was on his way home from a cafe when one of the perpetrators hit him with and iron bar. The victim fell to the ground and the six perpetrators started beating him. The victim had to be treated at the hospital.

Two Golden Dawn members, armed with knives and wooden and iron bats, attacked members of the Communist Youth of Greece (KNE). The KNE members were visiting a vocational high school to invite students and teachers to participate in a strike, when they were severely attacked. Striking workers guarding a factory nearby were also attacked when they intervened to help the KNE members. A worker and a young member of KNE were injured in the attack and hospitalized with head injuries.

A group of Golden Dawn members attacked two 24-year-old immigrants from Syria and Algeria on a pedestrian street. Three people threatened the victims with a knife and beat them with a bat, while five others were present at the location of the incident. After the attack, the immigrants went to a clinic at the local immigrant shelter to receive first aid.

A 30-year-old Senegalese man was attacked and then robbed by members of Golden Dawn. He was found severely beaten, with injuries to his face, including his lower teeth missing. Passers-by found the victim and helped him to get treatment.

Two Moroccan men were attacked by three largely unknown perpetrators. The victims, who work on nearby farms, were in the city center to buy cigarettes and find a ride to their shelter. The perpetrators surrounded them, beating one of the men, while the other managed to flee. The beaten victim lost consciousness and later woke up in the hospital. Along with the assault, 210€ was stolen from his wallet. One of the attackers was identified as a police officer and the son of the city's mayor. These perpetrators are the same group involved in caseID 2012-9-25-1, responsible for organizing patrols to "hunt down immigrants."

weapon_description: Knives, brass knuckles, belts with large buckles and sticks.
description: Four young men, aged 16, 17, and 18, with links to far-right groups, were arrested following several attacks, including at least one targeting Romani individuals. In one of the incidents, two boys were attacked by a group of about 20 people. Several of the perpetrators were armed with knives, brass knuckles, belts with large buckles, and sticks. The perpetrators chased the victims, who tried to escape. One of the victims was caught and brutally beaten while the perpetrators shouted insults like "fucking Gypsy, we've split your head open, fuck you." Due to the severity of his injuries, the victim was hospitalized. The police were investigating whether the perpetrators were members of a skinhead group. The perpetrators were suspected of carrying out several attacks motivated by far-right beliefs on the same night (cases do not meet inclusion criteria).

A 22-year-old Senegalese man living in Belgium died after being attacked while out at a cafe with his younger brother, who was also injured. While at a cafe late in the evening, the perpetrators, who did not know the victims, started throwing ice cubes at the victim's heads. When the victims then decided to leave, they were pursued by the perpetrators. They were attacked with glasses, bottles, punches and kicks. The 22-year-old victim fell into a coma and died in hospital five days later. The victims' family and friends described them as "not in the nature to provoke a fight", and believed there was a racist motive. Two perpetrators were charged with fatally beating one victim with the aggravating circumstance of racism, and beatings that incapacitated the other victim, and "inciting racial hatred against the two young men of Senegalese origin." The two perpetrators were finally given a 5-year prison sentence, but suspended for the entire sentence. They had to pay 30,000 euros to the victim's mother and each of her brothers as moral compensation.

A man was approached by an unknown older individual who began threatening him, stating he would kill the victim's son and calling him a "f****g Turk," among other insults. The perpetrator then struck the victim several times in the head. After the victim fell to the ground, the perpetrator continued by kicking him in the head. The victim sustained serious facial injuries as a result of the attack.

Police arrested four individuals and raided the homes of 17 others, all associated with the online forum "Stormfront Italia." Access to the website was subsequently blocked. The forum hosted a large volume of extremist content, including racist, anti-Semitic, anti-Roma material, Nazi and fascist symbols, an Italian translation of the white supremacist book The Turner Diaries, and a blacklist naming Italian Jews and pro-immigrant activists. Authorities had been monitoring the forum since 2011 and found evidence that the group was transitioning from online activity to offline organizing. This included attempts to collaborate with established far-right organizations such as Forza Nuova and CasaPound to expand their membership. Investigators also suspected the group was planning attacks on Roma encampments in northern Italy, though it remains unclear if weapons were being procured. The Italian group maintained close ties with its American parent organization, "Stormfront."

Three Golden Dawn members attacked a group of anti-fascists using wooden sticks. One of the victims was hit with five sticks at the same time, and suffered broken arms while trying to protect his head from the blows. All perpetrators were sentenced to two years in prison with a three-year suspension for the attack.

weapon_description: Brass knuckles, metal bars, chairs, glasses, beating/kicking
description: A group of 20 to 30 members of the far-right group Blocco Studentesco attacked several left-wing militants. The victims were patrolling outside a bar where the perpetrators had planned to hold an electoral event for the upcoming university elections. After informing the bar owner about the event, he decided not to host it, as the perpetrators had misled him. When the perpetrators arrived, the owner asked them to leave. They returned later, hooded, marching in formation and wearing CasaPound armbands, and began attacking both the victims and random passersby. They used chairs, glasses, metal bars, and brass knuckles. One victim was repeatedly kicked in the face while on the ground, and another was struck in the head with brass knuckles. Both victims were hospitalized.

Around 50 people armed with knives, brass knuckles, and wrenches chanted antisemtic slogans while attacking Tottenham fans drinking at a pub. The attack occurred before the Europa League game between Lazi and Tottenham. Tottenham holds a strong Jewish fan base, with slogans including 'Yid Army'. During the game, Lazio fans reportedly chanted 'Juden Tottenham' and held up the pro-Palestinian banner. A senator in Italy’s centre-left Democratic Party, said the attack was laced with: 'antisemitic, racist and Fascist connotations'. Nine people were injured in the attack which was believed to be racially motivated. Two ultras, aged 26 and 27, were charged with attempted murder.

Five people who were on their way back form a concert was attacked by around 15 neo-Nazis. The incident happened on a train station. The perpetrators first shouted slogans such as "Anti-Antifa" and "We are Germany" before brutally attacking the victims. A 31-year-old victim had to undergo surgery in hospital for a broken cheekbone and eye injuries as a result of the attack.

A group of six people, wearing signs of extreme right-wing Golden Dawn, attacked an Egyptian vendor in a market in Kallithea. The perpetrators were dressed in black and arrived at the market on motorcycles. They went directly to the victim's stand and, without a reason, began to beat him in the face and body. The victim collapsed on the asphalt, covered in blood. He was transported to the hospital with injuries.

weapon_description: Hand grenades, submachine guns, pump guns and thousands of rounds of ammunition
description: The chairman of the right-wing extremist group "Witikobund", who was also a Freedom Party (FPÖ) politician, was arrested for arms smuggling and keeping military equipment. The initial investigation was about arms smuggling, and during a house search connected to this, investigators found three hand grenades, three submachine guns, pump guns and thousands of rounds of ammunition.

A group of seven people attacked a man of Colombian nationality in a park. The victim was stabbed with a razor. Two people were identified and charged for the attack, although they acted within a group. One of the perpetrators was sentenced to two years and two months in prison for a crime of injuries with dangerous means and the aggravation of racist and xenophobic motives. The same person was in 2014 arrested and accused of stabbing five immigrants on the street in Lleida (CaseID 2014-9-22). A second perpetrator was sentenced to one year and nine months in prison for participating in the attack against the Colombian citizen. Both perpetrators belonged to the far-right association Nueva Época.

Two men suspected of belonging to Hammerskins (based on their clothing and appearance) surrounded an anti-fascist at the central station and began stabbing him in the stomach, arms and shoulders. The victim was hospitalized.

A group of eight people attacked two young immigrants from Algeria in a city square. The perpetrators, who were riding motorcycles and wearing hoods (modus operandi similar to that of Golden Dawn), greeted the victims in Arabic before hitting them with glass bottles. One of the victims suffered a head injury and ended up with twenty stiches, while the other suffered a minor injury to his arm. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

Five young women, who belonged to the leftist milieu, were attacked by a group of six neo-Nazis while they were waiting for the bus. The perpetrators, who were wearing combat boots and bomber jackets, ambushed the victims and beat them with bats and batons. Two of the victims required hospital treatment for their injuries.

A trio of 18-year-olds exited an apartment and threw a bottle at a 33-year-old man and attacked another. All three then began punching and kicking another man, also aged 33, before striking him to the head with a bottle. As a result of this attack, the victim suffered serious injury to his eye and face and was taken to hospital for treatment. The other victim sustained minor injury after he had been struck by the thrown bottle. Police arrested the three perpetrators who pled guilty to the assaults. All three perpetrators were sentenced to prison. A detective stated that the attack was unprovoked and "purely motivated by the color of their [the victims] skin."

The victim was attacked by a group of six neo-Nazis at a bus stop. The perpetrators screamed racist insults at the victim, before chasing and beating him. When the victim escaped and entered a souvlaki restaurant, he was chased outside again by the owner. There, the perpetrators continued beating him and broke his arm.

A 23-year-old Slovakian man was injured after being jumped by a gang as he stood outside an address in a reported racist attack. He was making sure his girlfriend walked home safely when he noticed a group of men standing nearby. He was approached by the men who made a racist comment before launching the attack. The perpetrators were white with English accents. Police stated that "This was an unprovoked attack on an innocent man for what appears to be no other reason than he was Slovakian." The victim was left with a broken wrist after the attack.

An Iraqi immigrant was attacked by four people on motorbikes at midnight. The perpetrators first asked the victim where he was from, before beating him and stabbing him multiple times in the shoulder, back and neck. The victim was taken to the hospital. Due to the timeframe, location and Modus Operandi, it may be suspected that Golden Dawn was behind the attack.

Two hooded men wearing jackets with the Golden Dawn logo attacked a 23-year-old Egyptian man and his cousin with iron bars. The cousin managed to escape while the victim received blows to the head and face, and lost consciousness. The perpetrators fled the scene.

A group of locals peacefully protested outside the Golden Dawn offices in the city after hearing about an attack on two minors. The protesters were attacked with stones thrown from the Golden Dawn office windows, before three Golden Dawn members emerged from the building, armed with helmets and knives. One protester was slashed with a knife. Earlier, six members of the Golden Dawn had assaulted the two minors in front of a café without provocation, punching one of the victims, pepper-spraying both, and attacking several bystanders who intervened.

A 40-year-old Kenyan was attacked by three men at a discotheque where he was working as a cleaner. The victim was cleaning the bathrooms when the perpetrators approached him. The perpetrator first said something to the victim that he could not hear because of the loud music. The perpetrators then kicked the victim to the ground, smashed a bottle over his head so it broke, and stabbed him in the eye with the broken bottle. The perpetrators also called him a dirty foreigner. The perpetrators fled. The victim was seriously injured in the eye and face and had to undergo two operations.

Two Asian men were leaving a pub speaking in their mother tongue when three people, including the owner of the pub, overheard them. One of the perpetrators, a 20-year-old woman, complained about the two men not speaking English and said they should "go back to their country". Suddenly, the perpetrators carried out an unprovoked attack on the two victims, with punches and kicks. The female perpetrator also struck one of the victims over the head with a shoe. One of the victims was knocked unconscious and the two were picked up by the emergency services. The owner of the pub was sentenced to four and a half years for wounding with intent and nine months for assault causing actual bodily harm. The two other perpetrators were also convicted of racially aggravated actual bodily harm, and were sentenced to 18 months of youth' custody and 18 months imprisonment.

Three people attacked an Afghani man. One of them hit him with a beer bottle while another punched him with knuckledusters. The perpetrators got into their car and fled the scene. The victim suffered severe eye injury and eventually became blind in one eye. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

A man poured petrol over his Polish neighbor from a jerry can and lit a match, while setting off fireworks outside as the victim and his wife watched from a window. Although none of the fireworks hit the victim, he suffered burns to his eye from the petrol. The perpetrator initially denied the incident but later admitted to a racially aggravated assault. He was sentenced to 16 months in prison and issued a 10-year restraining order preventing contact with the couple. The perpetrator allegedly harbored animosity toward his neighbors since they moved in.

weapon_description: Ten kilos of explosives, assault rifles, submachine guns, brass knuckles and sawed-off shotguns
description: During a second house search in 2013, the police found assault rifles, submachine guns, brass knuckles, sawed-off shotguns and ten kilos of explosives during a search of Objekt 21s meeting place. Supporters of Blood & Honour had founded the "cultural association" Objekt 21 in March 2010. While the association was offically dissolved in 2011, it continued to exist after no charges were brought after a house search. At its peak, the association had 30 hardcore members and around 200 sympathisers. One of the members was a well-known neo-nazi from Thuringia who secured good relations between Objekt 21 and neo-nazis from Thuringia. The public prosecutor's office charged seven people with belonging to the association and having committed crimes. They were sentenced in 2013 for various offenses to prison terms of between 18 months and six years. According to the jury, some of them had violated the Prohibition Act of 1947 by glorifying National Socialist ideology.

A Kurd living in Nordhausen was attacked by neo-Nazis, who used an electric shock device and struck him repeatedly in the head, causing serious injuries. Nordhausen, a small town in Thüringen, is known for its strong neo-Nazi presence. Motive not explicitly stated but sufficiently evident to be included.

During police sweeps for illegal immigrants in Athens (Operation Xenios Zeus), a Nigerian-born US citizen was detained and handcuffed by the police in the context of an immigration stop. When the vicim tried to take a photo of his handcuffs, Greek police officers beat him unconcious. Between August 2012, when Operation Xenios Zeus began, and February 2013, the police forcibly took almost 85,000 foreigners to police stations to verify their immigration status. No more than 6 percent were found to be in Greece unlawfully.

Two men, aged 19 and 20, were arrested on the suspicion of plotting to damage mosques after a police inquiry into racist graffiti attacks the past year. Racist slogans had been daubed in red paint on an Islamic Centre and threatening notes were sent to mosques elsewhere in Britain. The family home of the youngest was searched and material including ingredients used in making explosives were seized. At the time police said these ingredients could cause a "substantial explosion". During the police raid the bomb squad was also called in and the area around the perpetrators home was evacuated. Slogans daubed in the area included "Die Ragheads", "Pakis go home" and "BNP for life - KT". Police also found references to body armour and how to manage a terror organisation including dealing with surveillance and counter surveillance. Officers also found magazines and papers with letters missing which had been used to write five notes in envelopes sent to mosques threatening them to "leave town or there will be hell to pay". After the 22 July attacks, both men performed an initiation ceremony during which they branded each other on the arm with a cross. The two men referred to themselves as Knights Templar and demonstrated an extreme right ideology with a particular hatred of Islam but were not part of a wider more organised group. On the computer of the youngest, the police found an al-Qaeda training manual and Anders Behring Breiviks manifesto. They pleaded guilty to conspiracy to cause criminal damage and to send articles containing threates which were intended to cause distress. The lawyer of the youngest hoped to present medical evidence showing his client suffered from Asperger's syndrome or autism.

A 33-year-old Indian man was subjected to a racial attack by three to four men on New Year’s Eve. The victim was out in the street together with friends around midnight. He was standing in a crowd of people when he was insulted by the perpetrators for his skin color. The victim did not know the perpetrators from before. The perpetrators proceeded to beat and kick the victim, also while on the ground. The perpetrators fled. The victim suffered a broken nose among other injuries, and had to be treated in the hospital.

On New Year's morning, a 35-year-old man was racially abused by an unknown person at a New Year's Eve party in an apartment. The victim tried to defend himself verbally, but the insults continued. As the victim tried to leave, he was suddenly attacked by several perpetrators, some of them masked. They used tear gas. The victim tried to flee, but was beaten and kicked so violently that he briefly lost consciousness. Bleeding heavily from the head, the victim finally managed to reach a nearby police station. He suffered a head wound and facial injuries, among other things, and had to be treated in the hospital. He also lost several teeth as a result of the attack. The state security police investigated for dangerous bodily harm and insult.

Three people on motorcycles approached an Egyptian worker and attacked him. He was severly beaten and suffered several fractures. The victim sated that the perpetrators had Golden Dawn badges on their jackets.

Two women of Kenyan and Ghanaian origin were racially insulted by a couple while waiting for the metro. One of the women was on her phone, which seemed to irritate the attackers. The female perpetrator began shouting racial slurs, including referring to her by the n-word, leading to an argument. During the altercation, the male perpetrator pushed one of the women onto the tracks, causing her to break her heel bone. A bystander activated the emergency stop, preventing the metro from arriving. The victim required surgery for her injuries. The male attacker, 51, was sentenced to one year on probation for grievous bodily harm, while the female attacker was acquitted. The sentence was criticized for being too lenient and not accounting for the racist motive.

Three men, two of Pakistani origin and one of Indian descent, were rescued after an arson attack targeted their  home. Unknown attackers poured a flammable substance over the front door, setting it ablaze, which filled the property with thick smoke. Emergency responders, equipped with breathing masks, had to enter the home to carry out the rescue. Police classified the incident as a racially motivated hate crime. The victims escaped without physical injuries.

A 39-year-old member of the Reichsbürger movement was arrested after the police found a bunker filled with illegal explosives in his garden. The perpetrator had officially run a technology store and fireworks wholesaler from his home, but the perpetrator’s permit for storing and selling explosives had not been renewed. Following this, the perpetrator did not respond to the police's request to enter his premises to confiscate the explosives. When the police gained access to the premises, which was secured with barbered wire, the perpetrator refused to give them the keys to the bunker where he stored his weapons. The bunker contained large quantities of fireworks and pyrotechnics. Almost a year before the ride, the police had discovered around 1.8 tons of explosive chemicals in the possession of the perpetrator. The raid was carried out with caution because the perpetrator had announced that he would use all available means to defend himself against the raid, and threatened to put high voltage on the barbered wire. The perpetrator did not recognize the Federal Republic of Germany as a state, and considered his property to be exempt from the German sovereign territory.

location: Kurdistan Information Centre, 147 Rue La Fayette
description: A 30-year-old Turkish man, suspected of right-wing affiliations, shot three Kurdish women at the Kurdistan Information Center. The victims, aged 24, 28, and 54, included two members of the Kurdish Workers' Party (PKK), with the 54-year-old being a co-founder of the PKK. The third victim was the manager of the center. The perpetrator, who worked as a driver and translator for two of the victims, shot two of them three times in the head and the third victim four times. There was no sign of struggle, and reports suggest the use of a silencer as no one heard the shots. Unverified claims linked the attack to the Gray Wolves and Turkish intelligence services. The perpetrator died before the trial.

Three men associated with the group White Pride attacked a 34-year-old taxi driver of South Sudanese origin. The victim had heard one perpetrator say that "a N**** like him should not be allowed to drive a car." Then they lifted him out of the car and proceeded to punch and kick him. The victim suffered a severe concussion and remained on sick leave more than a week later. The perpetrators were arrested.

A 27-year-old migrant worker from Pakistan was killed by two members of Golden Dawn on motorcycles, aged 25 and 29. The victim was on his way to work when the two perpetrators attacked him, stabbing him seven times. The victim died from the injuries sustained. The perpetrators were arrested after a couple of hours and immediately confessed. The police found material from Golden Dawn in their homes. During Golden Dawns trial in 2020, it became known that the two perpetrators belonged to the organization.  The two men were convicted and sentenced to life imprisonment in 2014.

An Asian family accidentally hit another car's mirror while parking, leading to an argument with the car owner. A 24-year-old man and his wife intervened, making racist remarks toward the family. The man pulled the end of a family member's headscarf. When the family tried to drive away, he blocked their car, punched the father through the open window, leaving him unconscious with facial injuries that required surgery. The man pleaded guilty to racially aggravated bodily harm, while his wife admitted to causing racially aggravated harassment.

A group of immigrants from Pakistan were attacked by a group of people with batons who were shouting racist slogans, while they were sitting in a mini market. One of the victims was injured and transported to the hospital. The police charged eight people with causing grievous bodily harm, of which seven were between 16 and 17 years old.

Italian authorities dismantled a far-right extremist network in Naples linked to Casapound, arresting ten individuals accused of subversive association, armed gang activity, and incitement to racial hatred. The group had plotted to rape a Jewish university student and burn down a Jewish-owned jewelry store, plans revealed through wiretapped conversations. Investigators documented systematic indoctrination of young militants in ethnic hatred and anti-Semitism, often centered on discussions of Hitler’s Mein Kampf. The group was also implicated in violent clashes, including stabbings, arson attacks, and organized street assaults on left-wing activists (see, for instance, CaseID 2011-4-27). Their base, the "Berta" club in Naples, was used to plan violent actions. Among those arrested was a Casapound leader and parliamentary candidate.

A 56-year-old Indian-born was attacked by two men on the tram. The victim was travelling home with his 21-year-old daughter after watching a football match when he was beaten up. The perpetrators made racist comments to which the victim responded "please behave", which resulted in the men beating him more than 18 times in the head and face. This left him with black eyes, a swollen face and a concussion. The daugther witnessed the attack and tried to stop the beatings without success, and without help from bystanders.

The victim was racially abused by a white 20-year-old male, before the perpetrator hit him with an axe on the head, causing a gash. The perpetrator also tried to set his dog on the victim. He then tried to strike the victim's brother with the axe, but missed. The victim was taken to the hospital for treatment. The perpetrator was sentenced to 18 months in prison.

An asylum home was subjected to an attempted arson attack, which happened on Auschwitz's Holocaust Remembrance Day. According to witnesses, the perpetrators drove up in a dark car and ignited an incendiary device on the wall of the asylum home. No one was injured. A 21-year-old man turned himself in after the attack. He had been driving the car while another perpetrator, a 24-year-old man, threw the incendiary device. The 24-year-old perpetrator was believed to have right-wing extremist views, but the police spoke about a "spontaneous action under the influence of alcohol." The attack led to a lot of discussion about the right wing milieu in the area.

location: 3rd General High School of Paleo Faliro
description: A 17-year-old student was attacked and stabbed by a 20-year-old and his companion outside a high school. In the days before the attack, the victim had seen a classmate hang out with one of the perpetrators and warned against it, because he belonged to an extreme right-wing organization. Allegedly, the classmate had informed the 20-year-old about the warning, and together with a friend, he attacked the student with a knife to the head, neck and face. The victim was taken to hospital and had to undergo surgery. During the trial, it became known that the perpetrators were members of the neo-Nazi organization Golden Dawn and that they had organized the attack through text messages in advance. It also became clear that one of the motives behind the attack was that the victim had written an anti-fascist message on his classmate's desk.

During a book launch of a book on the far right organized by Jyväskylä Social College and Left Youth, an organizer of the event was stabbed in the neck. Three men armed with knives and bottles attempted to enter the premises, but were denied acces and began attacking. One of the suspects was described as carrying a bag of bottles and wearing goggles, protective gloves and a bulletproof vest. At least one of the perpetrators was a member of the Nordic Resistance Movement at the time of the attack. One of the suspects was also involved in CaseID: 2012-7-19.

Two 16- and a 27-year-old men faced charges for making potentially lethal weapons, specifically a nailbomb. The police found a pipe packed with nails and screws, charged with gunpowder, in the bedroom of the 16-year-old. The device had been made with chemicals bought off the Internet and right wing literature from the BNP and the English Defence League were found in the inspection, as well as Nazi emblems. As the house search entered its third day, another explosive device was found under a waste oil tank at a Garage in Glascote Road. The device had the appearance of a home-made sawn-off shotgun. In one of the “barrels” was a firework with the fuse extending out of it. The device was taken to Sutton Coldfield police station, which later had to be evacuated while experts assessed how dangerous it was. Some tape holding the barrels together had human hair and fingerprints which belonged to the 27-year-old co-accused, who said he had put the device under the oil tank to hide it from the police. The 27-year-old tried to take the blame for making the device, saying he wanted to show the younger boy how to do it.

A young woman was attacked by two men in their 30s for wearing a Republican badge, which in Spain is commonly associated with the political left. The perpetrators insulted the victim, calling her "red" and shouted "Viva España". The perpetrators pushed the victim, threw her to the ground, punched her in the face and kicked her in the stomach. As a result of the attack, the victim was unable to walk for three days.

A group of eight people attacked a Moroccan immigrant with kicks and crowbars. However, locals were quick to intervene and the perpetrators fled. Later that night, the perpetrators attempted to attack three more immigrants, who were able to chase them away. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

A 38-year-old of Turkish origins working at a pub was attacked by a drunk 22-year-old man. The perpetrator entered the bar where the victim worked and immediately began to shout xenophobic and National Socialist slogans. The perpetrator went up to the victim and headbutted him in the face. Other guests had to hold the perpetrator to prevent further attacks. The victim suffered a broken nose and had to receive medical treatment. The perpetrator was arrested and faced charges for dangerous bodily harm, xenophobic insults and the use of unconstitutional symbols.

An incendiary device was placed at the entrance of a left-wing squatting place. The attempted arson attack did not cause damages except for paint being removed. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

weapon_description: Fence slats and laser pointer and beating/kicking
description: Six police officers were injured on the yearly commemoration of the bombing of Dresden in February 1945. 10,000 people were holding hands around the city center like a human chain to prevent neo-Nazi demonstrators from entering the streets. A neo-Nazis rally with around 700 participants was announced on short notice. 3,500 police officers were deployed to prevent clashes between demonstrators and counterdemonstrators. Two police officers were seriously injured by masked men from the right-wing camp. The victims were hit over the head with fence slats and had to be treated in the hospital for head injuries. One police officer was blinded and injured with a laser pointer and was treated in the hospital. Three other police officers suffered minor injuries when some of the perpetrators tried to break through the barriers. Five of the perpetrators, aged 21, 22, 25, 27 and 29, were arrested.

Three 20-year-old men were sentenced over an arson attack on Sussex mosque. The mosque was occupied at the time the fire was started. According to the sources "it could have had devastating consequences if it hadn’t been put out quickly". Nevertheless, the only damage was caused to the building. The police described the incident as a religiously-aggravated hate crime in the context of increased far-right attacks as revenge for the killing of Lee Rigby. The perpetrators were sentenced to three years at a young offenders institute.

Seven Golden Dawn members attacked three workers from Pakistan. The victims were beaten and hit with batons, leading to serious injuries. One of the perpetrators was identified as a teacher in a Greek public school.

weapon_description: Homemade bombs, bomb-making materials, air rifles, a machete, a high-powered crossbow and catapult, airguns, small gas cylinders, adapted plastic pipes and tubes and an envelope containing fuse wire
description: A 16-year-old with Aspergers was arrested after planning to attack his former school and other areas, including a cinema and a mosque. The perpetrator was inspired by the Columbine High School shootings and allegedly drew up tactics for what he called "Operation: The New Columbine" in a notebook with a Nazi swastika and the face of Che Guevara on the cover. The notebook allegedly contained a "hit list" which included his former school, a mosque, a cinema and other buildings among his targets. He detailed his plans in a notebook and stockpiled homemade bombs, bomb-making materials, and various weapons including air rifles. Behind his Liverpool football club curtains, detectives found a machete, a high-powered crossbow and catapult, airguns, a gas mask, flak jacket, small gas cylinders, adapted plastic pipes and tubes and an envelope containing fuse wire. The police also found videos of the suspect and two other boys making and testing homemade explosives - including throwing a petrol bomb against a building with children inside. The perpetrator admitted he had a "strong interest in mass killings" but denied planning to carry out an attack, saying it was only a fantasy to help him cope with bullying. The perpetrator came to the attention of police by chance in February 2012, when he was arrested over a schoolboy skirmish and officers carried out a routine search of his bedroom.

A 15-year-old was standing at the bus stop when two young men started to insult him and called him a "Zecke [slang for leftist]". Shortly after the two perpetrator had moved on, a third man came along, hit the victim on the head with a bottle, pulled him to the ground by his hair and continued to kick and hit him.

Anti-fascist protestors were approaching a restaurant in which members of Golden Dawn where having an event, when they were attacked by members of the organization and the police. The police launched tear gas at the protesters, while two people were injured from being beaten on the head with batons. The victims were taken to a health center.

The perpetrator, a well-known local fascist, recognized the anti-fascist inside a takeaway shop and attacked him. When the perpetrator saw the victim, he started shouting his name, followed by 'Viva il Duce' [long live the Duce] while making the fascist salute. The victim said he didn't want any trouble and the perpetrator replied 'if you don't have problems, I'll create them for you' while he pulled out a knife and pointed it at the victims throat. Employees intervened and the victim headed outside. The perpetrator followed him and punched him with a brass knuckle in the face, striking his left eye and causing a fracture of the cheekbone . The perpetrator fled the scene when the police arrived.

A 42-year-old Jordanian man who had lived in Italy for 21 years was cleaning up outside the café where he worked in when a group of about 15 youths, aged 18 to 22, began throwing bottles at him. When he approached them, they hurled racist insults, pushed him, and, as he tried to defend himself, beat him with brooms taken from the café. One attacker struck him on the head from behind with a metal object, leaving him bleeding. The group then followed him into the café, throwing tables at him. The victim was hospitalized and treated for a head injury, scalp wounds, and multiple contusions.

A group of anti-fascists attending the "Festival gegen Rassismus" were ambushed by right-wing extremists as they left the event. The perpetrators, who had been waiting by the train station, used bottles, pepper spray, and physical violence in the attack. Around 30 people were involved in the clash, with eight victims requiring hospitalization, including at least ten injured. The attack had been planned and announced online in advance. The perpetrators gathered at a known neo-Nazi bar before targeting festival-goers. Ten individuals were arrested in connection with the assault.

During a dance event at a bar, a 28-year-old leftist was attacked by right-wing extremists after expressing concern about their presence. One of the right-wingers punched the victim in the face, causing a nosebleed. The situation was briefly de-escalated, but the victim was later attacked again outside the bar. A second perpetrator threw a beer bottle at him, and the victim suffered a bleeding head injury and a fractured hand, requiring hospitalization. The bar owner was also racially abused when attempting to intervene. One of the perpetrators later shouted "Sieg Heil" and gave the Hitler salute. The state's security department is investigating the incident.

A 63-year-old woman insulted a 29-year-old mother with a Turkish migrant background, who was out with her three children, with xenophobic remarks. The perpetrator then grabbed the four-year-old child and threw him onto the street. Oncoming cars managed to swerve in time. The severity threshold in this case is lowered due to the deliberate targeting of children.

During the night, five anti-fascists were attacked and injured with pepper spray and punches by members of the right-wing hooligan group "Karlsbande Ultras" (KBU) and people from their circle. In the hospital emergency room, there were further insults and threats from neo-Nazis.

Six people in black clothes with knuckle-dusters attacked three migrants causing injuries to the head. The perpetrators asked "where are you from" before the attack. When they went to the police to report the attack, the victims were detained despite their injuries. They were sent to the hospital the next day. Due to the timeframe, location and Modus Operandi, it may be suspected that Golden Dawn was behind the attack.

An immigrant was dragged out of a public market by a stall holder and handed over to a group of Golden Dawn members in a nearby street. There, the victim was beaten and left unconscious, covered in blood. Allegedly, the victim used to sell pretzels at the market and the stall holder had previously threatened him, saying "I am Golden Dawn and we will expel all dirty immigrants from the country".

A 22-year-old security guard at a homeless shelter, of Pakistani background, was hit over the head with a concrete block by a man who made references to the victim's ethnicity. The perpetrator pleaded guilty to one count of committing a racially aggravated assault causing actually bodily harm.

A group of at least three masked neo-Nazis attacked young leftists in their shared flat. The perpetrators broke into the apartment in the middle of the night. They were armed with wooden slats and knives. The perpetrators hit a victim who was lying on the ground with the wooden slats. The victims suffered a concussion. The perpetrators were eventually forced out of the apartment by the victims. The following night, right-wing extremists tried to break into the victims apartment again. Two days later, two of the perpetrators beat a 14-year-old Turkish boy and his 18-year-old companion to hospitalization (CaseID 2013-4-8).

A 44-year-old owner of an Arab bistro was attacked by to right-wing extremists while he was at work in the afternoon. The perpetrators entered the bistro and asked for beer. The perpetrators suddenly shouted racist slogans and "Sieg Heil", before leaving. A short time later, the perpetrators enter the bistro again and attacked the victim. They kicked and beat the victim with bottles, also while he was laying on the ground. When a friend of the victim tried to calm down the perpetrators, he was hit on the ear. Only when a second friend of the victim intervened did the perpetrators leave the victim alone. The right-wing extremists gave so-3alled Hitler salute and threatened to come back. The victim suffered, among other things, numerous bruises and a bleeding injury in the mouth. One of the perpetrators reappeared and attacked the victim again the following day (CaseID 2013-4-8).

At least four neo-Nazis, aged 18 to 30, attacked a 14-year-old Turkish boy and his 18-year-old German friend. The victims were on the street in the evening. The perpetrators beat the victims with batons. The 18-year-old was repeatedly kicked while he was lying on the ground. The victims were treated in the hospital for their injuries. The perpetrators fled to a nearby apartment but were soon arrested. According to initial police findings, two of the perpetrators were also involved in an attack where at least three masked neo-Nazis kicked in the door of a shared flat at night, and attacked the leftist residents (CaseID 2013-4-6). Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

A 33-year-old student from Cameroon was attacked by a drunk man on his way home from a party. The perpetrator insulted the victim by using the n-word and calling him an idiot. The perpetrator then struck the victim, causing him to fall to the ground. The perpetrator only let go of the victim when bystanders intervened. The victim had to be treated in the hospital for a broken leg sustained during the attack.

A 12-year-old boy was racially abused by an unknown man while crossing the parking lot in front of a supermarket. The perpetrator then threw a liquor bottle at the victim, which hit him on the head. The victim suffered a laceration that required outpatient treatment in the hospital. The severity threshold is lowered in this case due to the deliberate targeting of children.

A 33-year-old was arrested for at least eight attacks during two months against a 44-year-old Bangladeshi for racist motives. The victim was a peddler at a traffic light in the area. In one of the attacks, the suspect and two accomplices allegedly used an improvised metal club to repeatedly hit the victim, while telling him to leave the country. There is limited information about the other incidents. A case was filed against the perpetrator for the offenses of unprovoked and dangerous bodily harm, threatening, insulting and violating the provisions on weapons and on actions aimed at racial discrimination.

A young bassist of a punk-rock group was stabbed twice by two neo-Nazis around 1:30 am. The attack occurred without any prior exchange of words or insults. The victim tried to flee but tripped and fell, which the perpetrators took in advantage to stab the victim in the arm and leg. The victim was later hospitalized. The victim knew who the perpetrators were from before. Hours before the attack, one of the perpetrators had posted on Twitter: "A filthy person who can be seen is a filthy person who can be beaten." According to the police, the perpetrator had a long criminal record for similar offenses and was identified by the victim. This perpetrator, known by a nickname, was an active member of a far-right group. One of the perpetrators stabbed a young man from an anti-fascist group two years later (see caseID 2015-5-19).

The attack was one in a series against Muslims by the same perpetrator. A Ukrainian white supremacist stabbed an 82-year-old Pakistani migrant to death. The victim was walking near his home when the perpetrator spotted him. The perpetrator stabbed the victim three times in the back, leading to fatal injuries. The perpetrator had arrived in the United Kingdom five days before the attack. He told investigators that he attacked the victim because he "was a Muslim and there were no witnesses." Initial rumours speculated that EDL was behind the attack, as six Muslims had been convicted of attempting to bomb one of their rallies and the victim had recieved threatening letters from EDL. The letters were dated before the perpetrators arrival in the UK. The perpetrator was given a life sentence for the murder and three attempted bombings of mosques [CaseID: 2013-6-21, 2013-6-28 and 2013-7-12]. He confessed to police that his motivation was to kill and harm non-whites.

weapon_description: Unknown, but in possession of a non-live hand grenade, a flammable substance, and several butterfly knives.
description: The police searched the home of a 23-year-old neo-Nazi after he called for acts of terrorism in online forums. The perpetrator had posted a video where he incited violence by stating that, “History has taught us one thing: the spoken word will not bring about change. This can only be brought about through armed struggle.» In a second video, the perpetrator made detailed descriptions on how to make bombs. In the videos, he greeted the viewer with a Hitler salute in front of a swastika flag. The perpetrator had also published wanted posters with pictures, addresses and phone numbers of political opponents, as well as death threats to these victims. The perpetrator’s deeply anti-Semitic online activity could be traced back to 2011. When the police searched his home, they found a non-live hand grenade, a flammable substance, a decorative rifle, several butterfly knives, and a decorative rifle.

A 30-year-old Italian man attacked a Romanian man in a call centre, using a hammer. After the attack, the perpetrator photographed himself with the weapon and posted the image on Facebook, commenting on it as an act of "ethnic cleansing". The victim sustained head injuries and was on sick leave for a week.

A 12-year-old boy was racially attacked by two skinheads. The victim was on the street in the afternoon, when he was insulted by the perpetrators because of his southern appearance. The perpetrators beat and kicked the victim in the stomach several times. The victim was taken to the hospital after the incident. The state security police investigated the incident. The severity threshold in this case is lowered due to the deliberate targeting of children.

A 30-year-old seasonal laborer of foreign origin was subjected to a racist attack as he walked on the main street. The man was first insulted, then kicked and punched. Some passer-bys called the police and rescue workers. The victim was admitted to the hospital.

A 14-year-old boy from Afghanistan was attacked by a group of men dressed in black outside the metro station of Attiki square after the group had asked him for his documents.  As the Afghan teen declared he did not have any, he was kicked and fell on the ground. The attackers reportedly smashed a bottle of beer and injured him on the forehead. The group fled, while the boy collapsed in the middle of the street. A passerby took him to the hospital, where doctors closed the wounds with some 30 stitches.

A 47-year-old Black man was attacked by three men during his vacation in the French countryside. While parked in his car and studying a map, a man approached and asked if he needed assistance. A woman then approached and told him to leave, threatening to call her husband, who would force him to leave. The victim decided to exit the car and go for a walk. Upon returning, he was confronted by two men, one holding a stick, and a third man appeared. As he attempted to re-enter his car, the three men attacked and beat him, hurling racial slurs such as "dirty n*****," "dirty Caribbean," and "You have always been our slaves, you will always be our slaves." Injured and unable to drive, the victim called his family, who were also vacationing with him, and was taken to a hospital where he remained for two days.

Around 20 members of the right-wing extremist group "Terror Crew Muldental" attacked a group of people on a day trip, injuring seven victims. The attack, which occurred on a forest path, involved beatings, kicks, and strangulation, resulting in injuries like a broken nose. Several victims required hospital treatment. Months later, police raided three group members, suspecting them of forming a criminal organization and committing dangerous bodily harm. Investigations against Terror Crew Muldental had started in 2011 due to their violent actions against leftists (CaseID 2011-7-27). In trials in 2016-2017, the perpetrators were acquitted after victims claimed to have forgotten the incident and not known the attackers. The judge suggested witness fear might have influenced the testimonies, and investigations into false testimony were initiated.

Three Moroccan immigrants were stopped by a police patrol car to be checked. As soon as the police released the immigrants, ten people came out of a nearby bar, of which one of them had allegedly had a conversation with the police before. They asked where the immigrants were from, before they started beating them. When one of the victims fell to the ground, semi-unconcious, the perpetrators continued to kick him in the body and head. The victims later went to the police station to file a complaint, but instead the police arrested two of the victims for lacking papers. According to the victims, they were allegedly punched in the face during their arrest.

A group of men dressed in black attacked a 15-year-old boy from Afghanistan. When he was getting out of the subway station, the perpetrators began punching him in the shoulder. When he turned around, they asked him where he was from and to see his papers. When he said he was from Afghanistan, one of the perpetrators kicked him, causing him to fall to the ground. They broke a bottle of beer on his face and stabbed him with it. He went to the hospital and recieved 30 stitches. The victim described that the men were wearing black shirts that had 'two laurel trees that joined at the bottom, with a different shape inside.' It is therefore suspected that Golden Dawn was behind the attack.

A left-wing student was assaulted by a group of unidentified attackers, believed to be affiliated with Forza Nuova. The victim had participated in a protest a week earlier against the Minister of Education's visit, during which Forza Nuova members reportedly threw a helmet at the demonstrators (excluded incident). On the day of the attack, the victim was walking through the Quartieri Spagnoli neighborhood when the perpetrators recognized him from the protest. They violently beat him and struck him in the mouth with a stone. The victim required medical treatment, including five stitches to his mouth.
A fascist stabbed an anti-fascist, causing a perforated liver and various other injuries. Two people were arrested a month later. There is limited information about this case.

A group of ten young men, affiliated with the far-right group Groupe Union Défense (GUD), brutally attacked two couples. The couples were cycling home when they were stopped by the group, who had set up an illegal checkpoint in the street. One of the attackers asked one of the victims, "Are you white? Are you French? You’re dating an Asian, you’re discrediting France!" The attackers then proceeded to beat and kick the two men, and assaulted the woman they referred to as "Asian." The victims were hospitalized, with injuries including a broken wrist, and one victim had to wear a neck brace.

A Bangladeshi minor was violently assaulted by two Forza Nuova affiliates, aged 16 and 19, who knocked him down, beat him severely while shouting racial slurs, and discarded his phone after stealing it. Witnesses alerted the police and the ambulance, leading to their arrest. The attack was linked to a broader pattern of racially motivated violence organized by Forza Nuova, where minors were indoctrinated into hate and encouraged to participate in assaults known as "Bangla tours." Investigators documented 59 assaults on Bangladeshi citizens near the group's headquarters between 2011 and 2014, all of which were treated for physical attacks at the emergency room, highlighting the group’s focus on using violence and racism to radicalize young recruits.

Around 1 AM, a group of six to ten men attacked a group of foreigners outside a dance bar. The assault began when one perpetrator pressed a lit cigarette into the face of a 22-year-old Kurdish victim. When the victim and a 46-year-old Iranian approached the attacker, the 46-year-old was struck in the head with a beer bottle. Several others then attacked the victims, beating and kicking them. The 46-year-old and a 26-year-old Turkish victim suffered serious injuries and were hospitalized. The perpetrators fled in a minibus. The police suspect the attack was motivated by xenophobia, based on the nature of the assault and the perpetrators' statements.

A Chinese woman and her 14-month-old daughter were targeted in a pipe bomb attack on their home. The device was thrown into her garden, forcing the evacuation of nearby homes while army experts conducted searches. Police described the device as potentially deadly and suggested a racist motive. The attack occurred shortly after a similar racially motivated paint attack on the Belfast Islamic Centre, reportedly linked to the neo-Nazi group Combat 18. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

A taxi driver responded to a job at a bar when a man approached him. After confirming he was the taxi driver, the man punched him in the head and face, using racial slurs. The victim fled outside, where two other men questioned if he would call the police. When he replied no and moved toward his car, they began to punch and kick him, joined by the initial attacker. The assailants continued their racial abuse, threatened to kill him, and ultimately drove their vehicle into the front of his taxi while he was inside. The victim was taken to hospital.

Two individuals on a motorcycle approached a man from Rwanda and one of them tried to stab him in the throat. The victim evaded the knife and only got slightly injured. There was another knife attack against an immigrant a few hours later (CaseID: 2013-5-25-1). Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

location: Theological School of the Aristotle University
description: A group of people attacked an Iraqi immigrant outside the University. They first asked him where he was from, before saying racist things such as 'go back to your country.' One of the perpetrators slit him with a knife across the chest, causing a large diagonal wound. The victim managed to escape and was hospitalized. It was the second attack that day against immigrant (CaseID: 2013-5-25)

Two former soldiers, aged 33 and 37, petrol bombed a mosque. A number of worshippers were inside the mosque at the time of the attack for a meeting, but no one was injured. They managed to extinguish the fire and the perpetrators were soon arrested.  The attack occurred four days after a brutal Islamist murder of a soldier. A third man was sentenced for aiding and abetting arson by driving the two other men to the mosque. All three men were sentenced to six years imprisonment.

A 16-year-old was knocked unconscious and left with injuries to his face. The victim, who is a black male, stopped his bicycle to change the music on his MP3 player when the offender referred to him with a racial slur. The victim challenged the offender who then used the term twice more before punching the teenager to the ground and then kicking him until he was unconscious. Police and paramedics arrived at the scene and the victim was taken to the hospital for treatment. One man was arrrested at the scene and the police treated the incident as a racially motivated assault.

A 33-year-old previously convicted right-wing extremist was arrested for possession of a fully functional nailbomb. The police were unable to uncover any specific attack plans. The perpetratror was unemployed, alcoholic and had a criminal record. He had previously been a member of groups such as Kameradschaft Süd.

A taxi driver was racially abused and attacked. The driver picked up a group of four men and drove them to a store, before they returned to the taxi and drove back to the same address. During the journey back, the one of the men became aggressive, telling the taxi driver that Muslims should go back to their own country. The perpetrator then called the driver a “black Muslim bastard" and also made a remark about Muslims killing one person and threatening to retaliate for the act (a probable reference to the murder of Lee Rigby). When the driver arrived at the address, the perpetrator threatened to kill him and struck him thrice down the side of his face with a bottle. The driver was left covered in blood and the four men ran away. The perpetrator admitted racially aggravated assault and was sentenced to 12 months imprisonment.

A 23-year-old refugee from Mali was found outside an asylum seekers' accommodation with serious facial injuries. He was taken to the hospital where he received intensive care and had to stay for at least one day. The witness who found the victim had a short time earlier observed a car with several people in it, who shouted racist slogans. The witness saw that two people were running from the grounds of the asylum seekers' accommodation and into the car, before it drove away. There had been multiple right-wing extremist attacks on asylum seekers in the small town district of Vockerode in the weeks leading up to the attack (cases do not meet the inclusion criteria). The state security investigated the incident. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

Three skinheads, including one woman, recognized and attacked a 19-year-old left-wing activist and student. After a heated quarrel, one of the skinheads punched the victim with a brassknuckle, causing him to fall and hit his head on the concrete. The victim was pronounced brain dead at the hospital and died the following day. Seven people, including a woman, were taken into custody. Several are close to the small group of jeunesses nationalistes révolutionnaires (JNR) [Revolutionary Nationalist Youth]and the affiliated movement of the Troisième Voie [Third Way]. 15,000 people gathered in tribute to the victim and to demonstrate.

A 42-year-old man was arrested for plotting to blow up mosques with home-made gunpowder. The police found more than a kilogram of gunpowder and a home-made explosive device in a briefcase hidden in his bedroom cupboard at his parents' home. Under his bed they found containers of sulphur, potassium nitrate and charcoal – the three components of gunpowder. The perpetrator had an obsession with Hitler and extreme right-wing ideology and was nicknamed ‘Adolf’ by colleagues. In a text message to a friend he said he was making an explosive with ball bearings and nails, and added: ‘It might be destined for the Muslim centre in Birkenhead.’ In another, he said Norwegian mass murderer Anders Behring Breivik was his ‘hero’ and added: ‘Time to start blowing them up.’ The perpetrator, a receptionist at a recycling factory, had made a file of mosques near his home which he referred to as his ‘dreck ziel’ – a German phrase meaning ‘dirt target’. A former friend told: ‘He was a very friendly, well-liked person. But he was a bit vulnerable and could be easily influenced by others.’ He was married but lived apart from his wife at the time of the offences. Police was alerted by the perpetrator's colleagues. He was jailed for ten years for terror offences.

Four skinheads attacked a Senegalese man, hurling insults at him. When the victim responded, the situation escalated into a physical altercation. A fellow Senegalese man attempted to intervene, but the victim was stabbed with a knife, sustaining a punctured lung. The attackers are believed to be members of, or associated with, the far-right group "Hammerskins."

A 48-year-old Sri Lankan shopkeeper suffered a racist attack in his store. Two men, in hooded tracksuits, entered the shop and shouted racist abuse at him. They began to pour fuel over the shop floor before igniting it with a flicked cigarette. The shopkeeper had run from behind the counter to confront them, when he slipped on the fuel and fell forwards. When on the floor, the victim's clothes caught on fire. He managed to put out the flames quickly, but suffered serious burns to his arms and damage to his throat from smoke inhalation. The police treated the attack as a racist hate crime.

A 21-year-old Muslim woman, who was four months pregnant, was physically attacked by two men. The attackers first tried taking her headscarf off and later cut off her hair and tore part of her clothing. After she screamed out that she was pregnant, one of the attackers started kicking her in the stomach. She described the perpetrators as "skinheads", but the police found inconsistencies in her reporting. The woman suffered a miscarriage as a result of the attack. The attack came three week after another young Muslim woman was attacked by two men described as "skinheads" in the same city (CaseID 2013-5-20)
