weapon_description: Fence post, pool cues, beating/kicking, fire
description: A 48-year-old man from the traveling community was killed after being beaten with a pool cue and a large fence post. He was then dragged to a field and set on fire. A week earlier, the victim and his partner visited a bar where a bartender called him a derogatory slur, "pikey." After the woman was fired for this, the victim returned to the bar a week later with a friend, who left at 1:30 a.m. The victim remained, with relatives of the fired woman also present. It’s unclear where the attack began, but the victim was eventually dragged to a field, beaten further, and set alight. Three people—the woman's husband, daughter, and the daughter's partner—are accused of the murder, believed to be a revenge attack for the woman being fired a week before. The former bartender is charged with assisting them.

A 31-year-old man from Burkina Faso was assaulted by two Italian men while biking home from work. The attackers approached him on a scooter, forced him off his bike, and proceeded to beat him severely. During the attack, they shouted racial slurs, including "Get out of the way, you dirty n*****." The victim sustained head and eye injuries, along with bruises and fractures across his body, and was hospitalized.

location: Aisha Mosque and Islamic Centre of Walsall
description: The attack was one in a series against Muslims by the same perpetrator. A Ukrainian white supremacist placed a homemade explosive device outside a mosque during prayers on a Friday. He had taken the device with him on a bus and left the device with a timer before taking the bus back to Birmingham and buying a bottle of wine. About 150 people were evacuated from homes around the mosque, after bomb disposal experts were called to the scene. The device was packed in a children's lunchbox with a picture of a shark on it. The perpetrator was given a life sentence for murder and three attempted bombings of mosques [CaseID: 2013-4-29, 2013-6-28 and 2013-7-12]. He confessed to police that his motivation was to kill and harm non-whites.

A group of seven youths, linked to extreme right-wing groups, attacked two young immigrant men after an anarcho-libertarian rock festival. The victims, both of Maghreb descent, were brutally beaten with weapons such as brass knuckles and a baton. During the assault, they were subjected to racial abuse. The victims sustained facial and back injuries. The perpetrators, suspected members of skinhead factions and with possible ties to the far-right group Troisième Voie, carried out the attack.

A 51-year-old Turkish man was attacked by a 20-year-old drunk right-wing extremist. The victim was walking down the street when the perpetrator ambushed him and struck him in the head with a baseball bat. After the victim fell to the ground, the perpetrator hit him in the face again. The victim suffered a head laceration but declined hospital treatment, receiving on-site care from emergency workers. The perpetrator was arrested, making xenophobic statements to the police, complaining about immigrants and referring to his victim as a "Southerner, Turkish." One month earlier, the perpetrator had been involved in another violent incident on a tram, though this case did not meet inclusion criteria.

An Asian teenager was racially abused,  beaten and stabbed whilst he was walking in a park with two friends. His friends managed to escape, but the victim says he was surrounded by 15 people who punched and kicked him to the ground before he was stabbed. Due to the verbal abuse he recieved, he believes he was targeted after the murder of soldier Lee Rigby who was mudered previous month. The victim was taken to the hospital.

While visiting a fair, two men associated with the local anti-fascist movement were attacked by four youths. The perpetrators were part of a group of about ten individuals wearing black t-shirts with the Golden Dawn party logo. The perpetrators assaulted the victims using iron chains and brass knuckles, inflicting serious injuries that required hospitalisation. The police arrested four Greek youths - three brothers aged 20, 19, and 18 years old, and a teenage boy aged 17 -  on charges of serious assault.

The attack was one in a series against Muslims by the same perpetrator. A Ukrainian white supremacist placed a second homemade explosive device outside a mosque during prayers on a Friday. Officers were called to the scene after it had detonated, but they were not specialists and did not realise the significance of the type of debris. It was therefore not reported until after the other two bombings because police failed to recognise that a bomb had caused the debris. The perpetrator was given a life sentence for murder and three attempted bombings of mosques [CaseID: 2013-4-29, 2013-6-21 and 2013-7-12]. He confessed to police that his motivation was to kill and harm non-whites.

An Asian man was violently assaulted by a 38-year-old member of an alleged "white pride" group, at a pub in Blackwood in July 2013. The perpetrator, who had been drinking alone on the day of soldier Lee Rigby’s funeral, became enraged upon seeing the victim with a group that included white women. He verbally abused the victim and the women, calling them "stupid" for associating with "terrorists" and making racist remarks. When the pub manager, intervened, the perpetrator grabbed him, then struck him over the head with a glass bottle, almost severing his ear. Following the assault, police found racist images on the perpetrator's phone. He was convicted of racially aggravated wounding after denying the charges and claiming self-defense and was sentenced to five years in prison, with the judge condemning his actions as racially motivated and violent.

A teenager assaulted a 79-year-old pensioner in a brutal  attack that left the victim with serious wounds. The 17-year-old punched and kicked the elderly Muslim man who was wearing traditional Muslim dress and on his way to Cowley Mill Road mosque.  The teenager first confronted the man, who suffers from a condition affecting the pigmentation of his skin, asking him: “Are you a white Muslim?”. The attack left the victim in hospital for 12 days. The man suffered a skull fracture and bruising to the brain which have affected his cognitive abilities and speech. The perpetrator was given eight years’ detention in a young offenders’ institution for inflicting grievous bodily harm with intent, at Isleworth Crown Court in December 2013.
Unknown perpetrators threw a smoke bomb and a molotov cocktail into a left-wing center. The people in the room managed to extinguish the fire and no one was injured.

The dark-skinned victim was sitting on a park bench when two men began insulting him because of his Portuguese passport. They then brutally attacked the victim with beatings and kicking. In court, both perpetrators were first sentenced to 3 years and 9 months in prison for dangerous bodily harm with a racist motive, but the Federal Court partially overturned the decision and wanted to hold them for attempted murder.

A group of about twenty people wearing Golden Dawn insignia arrived on motorcycles to the Free Social Space "SYNERGIO", shouting slogans of the organization and throwing T-shirts. They went directly towards the building, where a free English lesson for children was taking place. Armed with iron objects and sticks, they attacked the area, causing serious material damage. The English teacher and some students locked themselves in the bathroom to protect themselves. However, the founder of the social space, who was at the entrance of the building, was attacked by ten-fifteen people who hit him with sticks and irons, causing injuries and bruises that lasted for three months.

An 18-year-old Muslim woman was attacked by an unknown assailant while walking through a park. The perpetrator shouted Islamophobic and racist insults before approaching her from behind. He removed her veil, struck her on the head, and stabbed her in the shoulder and thigh. The victim was left unconscious in the park. This attack is part of a broader pattern of assaults against veiled women in the city, which includes both verbal abuse and physical violence, though many of these incidents do not meet the criteria for RTV inclusion.

A man attacked the Asian victim for chatting to "attractive white women" on the day of Fusilier Lee Rigby's funeral (who was killed by Muslim extremists). The perpetrator became enraged after spotting his victim on a work trip chatting with women and shouted at them: "What are you doing drinking with terrorists?". He then told the victim: "You are all animals. This is not your country". Subsequently, he grabbed the victim by the testicles and smashed a full beer bottle over his head - leaving his left ear nearly severed from his scalp and knocking him unconscious. The victim was left with hearing problems and severe cuts to his left ear and neck. The court heard the perpetrator claimed "Hitler's views are common sense on a lot of things", he had Swastika tattoos, pictures of Hitler on his living room wall and was a member of a fascist "white pride" British Movement.

The attack was one in a series against Muslims by the same perpetrator. A Ukrainian white supremacist placed a third bomb, this time a nail bomb, outside a mosque. He had studied the mosque’s website and timed his device to explode at 1pm during Friday prayers, which usually attracted the biggest crowd of the week. The device was packed with 600g of 25-mm nails, which dispersed in a 70-metre radius with such force that nails were left embedded in tree trunks. Main prayers were delayed one hour to 2pm that day, meaning the area was almost empty when the bomb exploded and no one were injured. The perpetrator was given a life sentence for murder and three attempted bombings of mosques [CaseID: 2013-4-29, 2013-6-21  and 2013-6-28]. He confessed to police that his motivation was to kill and harm non-whites.

A group of around 20 masked men on motorcycles and in cars attacked two Pakistani immigrants. They asked the victims where they were from and then proceeded to stab them and throwing them to the ground while kicking them. One of the victims was cut in the arm, trying to defend himself, and the other recieved a cut on his neck. The perpetrators were members of Golden Dawn and had met earlier at the office for GD.

The police conducted a raid of 11 homes, offices and prison cells in Germany, the  Netherlands and Switzerland, targeting a suspected international cell. Six people, together with an unknown number of accomplices, were suspected of planning bomb attacks to overthrow the German political system. The plot was named 'Werwolf,' in memory of the Nazi 'Werwolf' plan for a commando force to launch attacks behind enemy lines in the final stages of World War II. Prosecutors suspected two Swiss right-wing extremists, a 25-year-old and a 54-year-old, of leading the group. The youngest is alleged to have shot a another right-wing extremist in Zurich in May 2012. In Germany, the police searched the home of a 29-year-old and a 32-year-old in the northern states of Lower Saxony and Mecklenburg Western-Pomerania. No terrorism plans could be proved in court.

Seven drunk neo-Nazis from Thüringen, aged 22 to 53, beat a 34-year-old man from Kazakhstan to death. The incident happened in the night at a town festival. It started when the perpetrators began to racially insult three late repatriates from Kazakhstan. The situation escalated into a fight. Some of those involved suffered minor injuries. Security guards arrived at the scene and were followed by five other men from Kazakhstan, including the later victim. It was reported that the victim followed the guards out of curiosity and that he was attacked without taking part in the fight. One of the perpetrators suddenly struck the victim over the head. The victim suffered a serious brain injury and died in the hospital hours later. At least two of the perpetrators were known to be part of the right-wing extremist scene. A 36-year-old was taken into custody for manslaughter. The police investigated the right-wing extremist motive because the attack was preceded by the unprovoked argument where racist remarks were made.

Several alternative youths were attacked by four neo-Nazis during the night after one of the victims wore an anti-Nazi button. The attackers, including two individuals linked to the neo-Nazi "Patriots MG" and the Borussia Mönchengladbach hooligan group, initiated the assault by hitting one victim, knocking a female victim to the ground, and causing her head to strike the cobblestones. Another victim was knocked unconscious. However, the victims managed to escape without even more serious injury when one of them intervened and stopped the main perpetrator, who fled with his accomplices.

Two soldiers of the Bundeswehr threw fireworks and other pyrotechnic devices at a home for asylum seekers and in the back yard of the facility. The perpetrators also shouted racist insults and repeatedly showed the Hitler salute. No one was injured, but property damage was caused.

Three young men were attacked by a group of men claiming to be members of the far-right English Defence League (EDL). The victims, who were celebrating a 21st birthday, encountered the attackers earlier in a pub, where one of them mentioned his friend was a journalist, which reportedly irritated the group. Later, as the victims were walking home near the Regal cinema, one of the attackers jumped from a car, punched the journalist, and began assaulting his friend. Another attacker struck a third victim with a glass bottle over the head. The assailants fled when another car arrived to assist, shouting, "You've just been ****** by the EDL." Police and ambulance services attended to the injured men.

A 23-year-old military serviceman was arrested for planning a gun attack on a mosque. The perpetrator planned the attack to coincide with the end of the Muslim holy month of Ramadan. He was arrested the day before the planned attack was to take place. The perpetrator was found in possession of category B (handgun/rifle) bullets. Relatives of the perpetrator tipped the police about his plan after they found some alarming documents at his house. The perpetrator had attacked a mosque in the Bordeaux region the previous year, although little damage was caused.

A 65-year-old man of mixed Jewish and Arab descent was verbally attacked by a 29-year-old woman on a bus after attempting to pass by a stroller. The woman called him a "dirty Arab" and later contacted her partner, who joined her in confronting the victim. After the victim exited the bus, the woman's partner struck him with a closed fist and stole the victim’s Star of David pendant. The attacker admitted to using a knuckle-duster during the assault, which he claimed was a "decorative object." The incident was eventually stopped by other passengers.

Uniformed members of the Nordic Resistance Movement handed out leaflets in the street when the victim passed by and questioned their message. After a quick exchange of opinions, he was surrounded by more NRM members who pushed him into a store entrance, where he was then kicked and beaten with the shafts of the SMR activists' flags. The victim bled profusely from four deep cuts in the head. He suffered a concussion and had to be treated in hospital. Three NRM members were convicted and jailed.

During a "Nationaldemokratische Partei Deutschlands" (NPD) rally, six protesters opposing the NPD were injured by approximately 20 neo-Nazis attending the event. The victims had peacefully expressed their anti-racist views when they were attacked by the perpetrators, who used pepper spray and flagpoles. One victim was injured so severely that he required hospitalization for several days.

After an event at the "Self-Managed Hangout of Karditsa", three people encountered a member of Golden Dawn. Allegedly, he was well known in the city for his attempts to attack anti-fascists in the past. This time, the perpetrator attacked the three anti-fascists with a baton. One of the victims suffered a head injury and was transported to the hospital. The perpetrator was sentenced to 11 months in prison with a suspension for the attack.

Unknown perpetrators attempted to set fire to a small Muslim prayer room while people were still inside. The individuals smelled smoke and discovered a piece of paper soaked in flammable liquid, which had been thrown into the room through a gap in the door. They quickly extinguished the fire. Upon the arrival of the police, a swastika was found tagged in orange on the wall.

Unknown perpetrators attacked a 16-year-old Muslim girl. Two men approached her, hurling Islamophobic insults such as "Dirty black, dirty Muslim, go back to your country, take that off (the veil)." They violently removed her veil, forced her to the ground, and beat her. One of the perpetrators held her down while the other cut her face and neck with a sharp object. Both perpetrators were described as being of European descent, with one having a shaved head. The victim attempted suicide twice shortly after the incident.

Two immigrants from Pakistan were attacked in the morning on a main street by a group of 20 men dressed in black. The perpetrators first surrounded the victims with cars and motorbikes. After asking the victims where they were from, the perpetrators stabbed them in the hands and face, threw them to the ground and and kicked them. The victims sought assistance from Amnesty International after the attack, from whom they received medical help. According to the organization, the attack occurred only two hours after the neo-Nazi party Golden Dawn held a rally in the same town.

Unknown perpetrators threw molotov cocktails towards the Luckenwalder refugee accommodation. 168 residents from 24 nationalities, including 23 children, lived in the accommodation at the time. The molotov cocktails ignited but went out by itself and no one was injured. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

Two 20-year-old men from Afghanistan were attacked by a group of six men. The victims were on the street when they were approached and racially insulted. The victims ignored the perpetrators. Two of the perpetrators then attacked one of the victims. He was taken to the hospital with serious injuries to his face and arm, according to the police. The perpetrators escaped.

During a march held by the English Defence League (EDL), six to eight members of the group United Against Fascism protested against the EDL. Two men broke away from the EDL group and one of them tried to push away a banner of the anti-fascist protesters and pushed a female who approached him. The second punched one of the victims repeatedly in the face, even while he was on the ground. The victim suffered a cut to his forehead, and requited ten stitches. One of the perpetrators was sentenced to 18 months of community order and 100 hours of unpaid work.

A 29-year-old man from Southampton was arrested on suspicion of assault after a firework was thrown at a police officer during an English Defence League (EDL) rally in Hampshire. The rally, which was held in protest against the opening of the Madani Academy Muslim school in Portsmouth, was described as otherwise peaceful by Hampshire Police.

Two immigrants from Bangladesh were attacked upon returning from work on a motorcycle. Two perpetrators moved towards them holding wooden beams in their hands, threw them from the motorcycle onto the asphalt and started beating them. They also tried to steal one of the victims' computer. When residents of the neighborhood noticed the incidence, they rescued the victims and the perpetrators fled. One of the victims was transported to the hospital, where he received first aid. According to the Hellenic-Bangladesh Chamber of Commerce and the Movement Against Racism, the attack had a racist motive. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

A Pakistani man was seriously injured in an attack by unknown assailants while walking from a supermarket to the asylum seekers' home. A car, occupied by several individuals, stopped near the victim, and the driver approached from behind and struck him. Other perpetrators then got out and beat and kicked the victim, using a club-like object. The victim lost consciousness and suffered serious injuries. While the police could not confirm the exact motive, a spokesperson stated that a right-wing extremist background could not be ruled out, noting that the attack resembled behaviors commonly associated with such groups. Reports also suggested that the victim had been racially abused during the assault.

The 19 -year-old victim was in a park with his cousin and a friend when they were approached by two men that were both known to their female friend. The two men acted normal until the arrival of a larger group of about 12 others. They then began to call the victim and his cousin "Pakis" and shouted further racial abuse. The two cousins were then physically assaulted with punches, kicks, and beaten with a stick. One of the victims suffered a broken jaw while the other suffered severe blood trauma and optic nerve damage to his eye, effectively blinding him in that eye. His vision was not expected to recover. One of the perpetrators was sentenced for 2 years.

A man from Gabon was pushed of his bicycle by a group of unknown men. The victim was cycling on the street in a new housing development when he was approached by the perpetrators. As the victim was listening to music, he did not understand much, only the word "N*****". As he wished to avoid an argument, he paid no attention to the perpetrators. A few meters further on, one of the perpetrators pushed him off his bike. The victim fell and  lost consciousness. He was later diagnosed with a broken cheekbone, which required surgery. Racist activities, directed primarily against Africans, had been taking place in the area around the crime scene for some time. Case is possibly connected to CaseID 2013-9-20-1.

A Pakistani immigrant was attacked by ten people when he was on his way to work. The perpetrators immobilized him and started to punch and kick him all over his body. The victim suffered a broken nose and was taken to the hospital.

An unidentified group of far-right militants attacked several members of the left-wing association "Torpedo," severely injuring a 22-year-old man. The left-wing militants were socializing at a bar when the assailants began punching and kicking them. During the attack, one perpetrator smashed a glass bottle and used it to slash the victim's face, resulting in a deep cut on his left cheek that caused significant blood loss and required hospitalization, narrowly missing his eye. The attackers fled the scene, with one throwing a bicycle at the left-wing militants who attempted to follow. The left-wing militants refused to cooperate with police, who suspected this reluctance stemmed from plans for retaliatory actions. The bar owner believed the attack was premeditated, noting that four or five of the assailants had scouted the location the previous evening. "Torpedo" members also suspected premeditation, as far-right militants were reportedly waiting outside the homes of two other left-wing members later that night, though both managed to evade attack.

weapon_description: Two Uzi submachine guns, one Russian assault rifle, a Colt, brass knuckles, switchblades and cartridges.
description: The police seized numerous weapons during a raid on the Thüringen right-wing extremist scene. The private homes of three suspects in Crawinkel, Ballstädt and Erfurt were searched. The residence in Crawinkel was a well-known meeting place for the right-wing scene. The police found two Uzi submachine guns, one Russian assault rifle, a Colt handgun, brass knuckles, switchblades and cartridges. The proceedings for violating the War Weapons Control Act had been ongoing since July against four men aged between 27 and 37. A 36-year-old were already in prison at the time and a 27-year-old was arrested during the raid. The perpetrators were closely linked to the Austrian right-wing extremist group "Objekt 21", and the raids were preceded by extensive investigations in both Austira and Germany.

Three men dressed in black on motorcycles attacked a Pakistani immigrant. They threw a bottle of beer in his face, causing lacerations that needed stitches. Based on reporting of the incident, it appears that Golden Dawn was suspected of being behind the attack.

A 27-year-old man was delivering food when he was attacked by two men on bicycles. They racially abused him and one of them struck him in the face. The victim suffered a large, deep cut to his eyebrow, which required stitches, and heavy bruising and swelling to his face.

During a fundraiser at a club for Lee Rigby, a British army soldier who was killed by two muslim perpetrators earlier the same year, eight white men attacked three Asian people. A 39-year-old Asian man was knocked unconscious and repeatedly kicked in the head. His jaw was broken in two places. Two friends of the victim were also attacked, but they suffered less severe injuries. The attack continued until  the bouncers intervened. The victims suggested they were attacked due to their ethnicity, as they were the only Asian people there. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

The police arrested four right-wing extremists plotting to use model planes to fly a bomb into a left-wing rally. A 23-year-old homeless person was believed the be the mastermind behind the plot. He is said to have belonged to the right-wing extremist scene and to have instigated a 42-year-old man to build the explosive device. A functioning explosive device and several model airplanes were confiscated from the home of the alleged bomb maker.

Three Muslim men were walking on the street when two men in a car attacked them unprovokedly. The perpetrators threatened to kill the victims and told them to go back to their country. One of the men got out of the car and said he wanted a fight, before punching one of the victims. Then the driver got out with an iron rod and tried to hit one of the victims over the head with it. However, the victim managed to duck.

A group of at least three neo-Nazis, led by a member of the fascist organization National Action of Ilia, attacked a student known for his anti-fascist activities. The perpetrators hit the victim from behind, while the leader attacked him, seriously injuring him in the face and body. Allegedly, the leader of the group had been involved in several attacks on anti-fascist militants. He was sentenced to one year imprisonment for the attack.

Two men, aged 20 and 26, started yelling 'Sieg Heil' and 'landssvikere' [traitors] outside Blitz, a radical left-wing social center. They then approached the center with a knife and stabbed a 16-year-old boy who was standing by the door. Around ten people from Blitz started chasing the men with sticks, planks and cobblestone. One of the perpetrators was hit in the head and they were both taken to the hospital for their injuries. The oldest one, a 26 year old man, kept threatening the police as they held guard by his room. He was sentenced to 7 months imprisonment.

A 15-year-old boy of Taiwanese descent was severely beaten by three suspected right-wing extremists, aged 18 to 26, during a school trip to Bad Schandau, a small town in Sachsen known for its right-wing extremist presence, particularly the influence of the "Nationaldemokratische Partei Deutschlands" (NPD). After a conflict at a local festival where two Muslim and one Black schoolgirl were insulted, the victim and his group returned to their hostel. Around 3 AM, the perpetrators attacked him in the hallway, causing a broken jaw and serious eye injuries that required surgery. Although the attackers were not part of an organized neo-Nazi group, the crime was considered racially motivated. The victim’s lawyer highlighted racism as a key factor, and the Leipzig Operational Defense Center noted a "clear xenophobic background." The perpetrators received prison sentences of 8 to 15 months for dangerous bodily harm.

After having marked several doors with the celtic cross in an apartment building where several immigrants lived, members of the neo-Nazi organization Golden Dawn attacked a man from Afghanistan. Three perpetrators waited for him outside his apartment as he was about to leave, and first told him they were from the police and asked for papers and money. One of them, a female candidate of the Golden Dawn in Athens, then blocked the entrance of the apartment while two men began to hit the victim on the back of the head. The perpetrators also told the victim to leave the apartment building, or they would "cut off his head". The attack lasted for fifteen minutes. There is limited information about injuries.

Four individuals of various nationalities were attacked by a group of young Italians after attending a boat party on Lake Garda. The incident began when the victims boarded a bus and were immediately subjected to racial insults from the attackers. In response, the victims decided to leave the bus, but the perpetrators followed and assaulted them, beating them severely. One victim, a 24-year-old Iraqi man, suffered a broken jaw, fractured vertebra, broken ribs, and a liver injury. Another victim, a Moroccan man, sustained facial injuries from being punched.

Two men, originally from Iran, were eating at McDonald's when a man approached them. The two men were unable to understand him, and instead told him he could eat with them if he wanted to. Suddenly, the perpetrator leaned over one of the victims, strangled him, and pushed him to the floor before he punched him in the face. When the other victim tried to intervene, he was punched to the face until his nose broke. Meanwhile, the perpetrator shouted "Din perker! I kommer til Danmark og ødelægger det hele" [You perker (derogatory word for immigrants of Arabic origin)! You come to Denmark and ruin everything]. McDonald's employees held the perpetrator until the police arrived.

A Gambian native was assaulted when he, together with his 18-month-old son, was walking to a playground and almost thrown off a bridge in Malmö. Around 10 perpetrators shouted racist slurs during the incident such as "black bastard", and threatened to kill his son. The victim received several punches and kicks to the head, in addition to being lifted and attempted thrown over a bridge. A 21-year-old man is being prosecuted for aggravated assault. The victim was brought to hospital.

Twenty members of the Communist Party-1ligned PAME trade union were painting wall slogans and putting up flyers for a concert in the district. An "assault battalion" made up of around 50 Golden Dawn members from Nikea, Perama and Salamina then launched an organised attack on the PAME members, trapping them and beating them with sticks, batons and axes. The Golden Dawners shouted "F*** your houses, your families, your sisters; you’re going to die here, you commie c****." Nine PAME members were seriously injured. Four Golden Dawn members were convicted for attempted murder of the communist activists. The case was one of several from which a court on October 7 2020 delivered a historical judgement convicting 68 members of the Golden Dawn, after a trial that lasted over five years starting with the murder of an anti-fascist musician in 2013 (CaseID 2013-9-18).

A 15-year-old boy was beaten and seriously injured by an assumed right-wing extremist. The victim had to undergo emergency surgery as a result of the attack due to among other injuries a broken jaw. The police stated that they had information about a perpetrator with right-wing extremist views, and assume the attack to be motivated by xenophobia.

After a football match between the club "Verein für Leibesübungen Halle" (VfL) and "Halleschen Fußballclub", a group of four VFL fans were insulted and attacked by around 20 men near the stadium. The perpetrators shouted “Scheiß Zecken [slur for leftists]”, “I’d love to kill all of you Zecken”, and “dirty Jews”. Two of the victims were caught up by the perpetrators. The other two managed to escape. The 24-year-old victim received two blows to the head and face. The 18-year-old victim received at least two punches to the face. He began bleeding heavily from his nose and mouth, but was also punched and kicked in his body. A driver who noticed the attack ordered the victims to get in quickly, and drove them to a hospital. In addition to damaging three teeth, the 18-year-old suffered a broken nose, which required an operation and a four-day hospital stay. The state security police investigated for dangerous bodily harm, threats and insults. Halleschen Fußballclub was known to have right-wing extremists among their supporters.

A Greek anarchist rapper was killed by members of Golden Dawn. The victim and his friends were at a cafe watching a football game when tensions arose between another group at the cafe. A member of the second group, a security officer of Golden Dawn, called his superior, responsible for political action and informed him about the presence of the rapper and his company in the cafeteria. The superior then called the person who was later accused of stabbing the victim. The police recieved a call that a group of 50 people were on their way to the cafe with baseball bats. When they arrived, the police found the victim injured with stab wounds and while still conscious, the victim identified the perpetrator who was still on site. He died of the injuries sustained. The perpetrator who stabbed the victim worked in the cafeteria of the offices of Golden Dawn. Following the incident, protests against Golden Dawn and the associated rise of the far right took place throughout Greece. This included a protest in Athens, attended by 2,500–10,000 people, which marched towards Golden Dawn's central offices a week after the death. On October 7, 2020, the perpetrator was found guilty, along with 15 other leaders and  members of Golden Dawn, which was unanimously declared a criminal organization by the court.

A 20-year-old Albanian was approached by a 35-year-old Greek who asked him if he was Albanian. When the victim answered yes, the perpetrator headbutted the victim and broke his nose. According to the victim, the perpetrator also did the Nazi salute. After the attack, the perpetrator went to the local offices of the neo-Nazi organization Golden Dawn to seek refuge. A video had also placed him outside the offices a few nights before the attack.

A man from Syria was attacked by three people on the street in a new housing development. He was first punched in the face and then hit repeatedly with a baton. During the attack, the victim was racially abused. Due to serious injuries, he had to be hospitalized for five days. The case is possibly connected to CaseID 2013-8-23.

weapon_description: Hit with beer bottle and kicked with a steel-capped boot
description: Three men dressed in black attacked a Somalian man. They shouted racist comments, before striking him in the head with a beer bottle and kicking him with steel-capped boots. The victim was treated for injuries sustained at the hospital.  Based on reporting of the incident, it appears that Golden Dawn was suspected of being behind the attack.

A 34-year-old Turkish fast-food shop owner was severely beaten by nine intoxicated neo-Nazis, aged 24 to 29, while closing his shop with his girlfriend. The perpetrators, who shouted racist slurs and right-wing extremist slogans, initially verbally attacked the girlfriend, calling her a "Turkish slut." When the victim intervened, he was brutally assaulted, resulting in a skull fracture and permanent brain damage. The victim had to be placed in a coma and undergo emergency surgery. The girlfriend and an employee were also injured. Two of the perpetrators had prior criminal records for right-wing extremism, and one was linked to the far-right group "Kameradschaft Schönebeck," identified through photos from 2012. The main perpetrator had a history of violent attacks, including involvement in a 2006 brutal assault on a 12-year-old Ethiopian boy (CaseID 2006-1-9) and a 2011 attack on a kebab shop owner (CaseID 2011-1-1). Four perpetrators were sentenced to five to eight years in prison for attempted manslaughter.

A man and his family was attacked on the street by a group of nine young men. One of the victims was talking to one of the perpetrators when he was suddenly punched in the face. The victim's father intervened, and a group of people surrounded them and began to beat them. Another victim had his turban ripped from his head. Three of the victims were taken to the hospital. One of them suffered a fractured wrist and a severed ear that required plastic surgery. The police treated the attack as a racially motivated incident.

Two minors were arrested after police discovered Nazi materials and explosive substances at their homes. The investigation began following the appearance of swastikas and anti-Semitic graffiti in the city around the time of the funeral of former SS commander and war criminal Erich Priebke. During the search, police seized explosive and flammable materials at one of the perpetrators' homes. The minors' affiliation with (neo)Nazism was confirmed through the materials found, as well as their online activities, including posing with Mein Kampf and engaging with Nazi groups.

A 27-year-old Libyan student was standing at a bus stop when he was approached by two men. The perpetrators insulted him before one of them stabbed him in the face. The perpetrators then ran off. The victim had to receive stitches to his face. The police treated the incident as a racially motivated assault.

Six hooligans and presumed right-wing extremists attacked a supporter of the leftist football club "BSG Chemie Leipzig". The perpetrators were wearing merchandise from the right-wing football club "Lokomotive Leipzig". The perpetrator identified the victim as a supporter of the opposite team, called him a "Jew" and a "Zeckenschwein [leftist pig]" and shouted that they would kill him. They then beat him up. The victim suffered a fracture in his head, for which he had to be treated in hospital.

Two brothers were sentenced to prison for carrying out a racially motivated attack on a vulnerable 20-year-old man. The victim, who has a medical condition that results in a mental age of a young child, was approached by the brothers, who subjected him to racial abuse. One of the brothers then threatened, "I'm going to bang you," before repeatedly striking the victim in the face with a hammer and hitting him with a plank of wood. Earlier that day, the brothers had been involved in a confrontation with a group the victim was part of. Another man is believed to have joined the brothers in the attack. Both brothers pleaded guilty to racially aggravated assault causing actual bodily harm and possession of an offensive weapon. The judge stated that the victim was targeted not only because of his vulnerability but also due to his skin color.

Unknown perpetrators threw fireworks into the basement of an asylum seekers’ home. The attack happened in the early morning. The perpetrators entered the guarded and fenced area and hurled the fireworks through an open basement window. Heavy smoke aroused in the laundry room and a laundry basket melted. The fire did not spread, and no one was injured. The asylum seekers’ home had previously been subjected to xenophobic attacks several times (the cases do not meet the inclusion criteria), including damage to the exterior and parked cars. Neo-Nazis had put up hundreds of racist stickers in the area.

Two married men were attacked and assaulted in a homophobic manner by two men in their 40s. The perpetrators approached the victims and grabbed them by the arm. When the victims attempted to push them away, the perpetrators began shouting derogatory slurs such as "you're faggots, faggots, sons of bitches." The assault escalated as the perpetrators punched and kicked the victims. Although the victims initially managed to escape, the attackers caught up with them, grabbed one of the victims, and continued to punch him in the face, head, and stomach. One of the perpetrators also raised his arm and shouted, "long live Spain!" The victims sought medical treatment, with one requiring a neck brace for a cervical spine injury sustained during the attack.

A 23-year-old Dutch man was arrested in a pub in Belgium, suspected of plotting terror attacks. He was apparently planning to announce his plans live at the Flemish state television before targeting political institutions. He was also suspected of plotting attacks against 'certain people' on November 15, King's Feast Day [Belgian holiday in honour of the country's royal family]. It was therefore speculated that Belgian royals could have been intended targets. He had allegedly attempted to recruit others in the pub. It was reported that “a mental problem plays a role”, without further details. Prosecutors said the threat of attack appears to have been “very concrete, serious and giving rise to concern.” The perpetrator had written a 80-page manifesto, leading local news media to draw comparisons to the 22 July terrorist and some media even called the suspect “the Dutch Breivik.” In the manifesto, the suspect had called for the overthrow of the Belgian state, which he reportedly denounced as an American puppet regime, and for the creation an independent Flemish Republic. There was also a reference to a phrase interpreted as criticism of the American bugging scandal in Europe.

A Roma woman and her two-year-old child were the victims of an acid attack in the Fuorigrotta neighborhood of Naples, Italy, while standing on the street outside a residential building on Via Andrea Doria 22. The acid, thrown from a balcony, directly struck the child, who was treated at a pharmacy before being taken by ambulance to the hospital. Witnesses reported a history of harassment from the building's residents, who allegedly threw water and toilet paper at Roma individuals to drive them away. Police have opened an investigation, with some neighbors accusing a specific woman of intentionally committing the attack.

A young student, member of the student union Unef, was attacked and stabbed by an unknown far-right perpetrator. The victim was exiting her house, when a person stabbed her with a utility knife on the face and on the neck, resulting in her hospitalization. She received threat calls days before the attack. This attack comes in a context of increased threats and violence from far-right militant groups towards left-wing, student unions members. Another connected case was excluded because it did not fulfill the RTV severity criteria. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

Two asylum seekers were injured in an arson attack on a home for refugees. A witness saw two young, darkly dressed men at the entrance at around 11PM who set fire to the accommodation. Three weeks before the arson attack,  two men had repeatedly shouted “Fucking foreigners!” from a car. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

weapon_description: Slingshot and steel balls and other iron parts
description: Unknown perpetrators shot metal objects at an emergency accommodation for refugees. Several windows were broken, but there were no injuries. This was the first in a series of similar attacks on the emergency accommodation in a few months (CaseID 2013-10-21 and 2014-3-20). After the third attack in March 2014, the state security police investigated for attempted dangerous bodily harm and stated that if someone had been hit, they would have been seriously injured. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

Three men dressed in black (modus operandi similar to that of Golden Dawn) attacked a man from Iran. One of them put him in a headlock and bit his ear off, which the doctos were unable to reattach. He was hospitalized for a week. The victim contacted an NGO who filed a complaint to the police on his behalf, as he was without papers. After three months, the police found the victim and deported him. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

The right-wing fraction of the fan base of the football club MSV Duisburg attacked members of the left-wing ultra group, who were supporting the same team. The incident happened during a football match between MSV Duisburg and a Saarbrucken club. The right-wing fraction of MSV Duisburg, led by the extremist group “Division Duisburg”, were physically superior to the leftist fans. At a club meeting that was held just one month before the incident, the left-wing ultras had to promise to refrain from anti-fascist commitment during matches. The violence begun when some of the victims showed support for the left-wing supporter groups of the football club Eitracht Braunschweig, who had been banned from making group appearances by right-wing actors within the Braunschweig club. Around 30 members of the right-wing extremist group “Nationaler Widerstand” from Duisburg and Dortmund then attacked the victims with beatings and kicks. A woman was kicked while lying on the ground. Among the injuries were a cracked rib, lung problems, and knocked out teeth. Several victims, including women and minors, lay bleeding on the ground. The police intervened and stopped the attack with massive use of pepper spray and batons. There had been confrontations between fractions of the politically fragmented supporter base of MSV Duisburg for several years before the incident. This included violent actions towards left-wing ultras (cases do not meet inclusion criteria). The official leadership of MSV Duisburg later denied the presence of neo-Nazis among the fans and stated that “political motivation does not seem to be the primary factor in this case.” Motive not explicitly stated but sufficiently evident to be included.

weapon_description: Slingshot and steel balls and other iron parts
description: Unknown perpetrators shot metal objects at an emergency accommodation for refugees. This was the second in a series of similar attacks on the emergency accommodation in a few months (CaseID 2013-10-18-2 and 2014-3-20). Only three days before this second attack, unknown perpetrators had broken several windows by shooting metal objects. After the third attack in March 2014, the state security police investigated for attempted dangerous bodily harm and stated that if someone had been hit, they would have been seriously injured. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

weapon_description: Wooden clubs, glass bottles and slingshots
description: A group of 30–40 men, reportedly members of the far-right Vienna football fan group Unsterblich Wien, stormed the Ernst Kirchweger House (EKH), a club house used by left-wing and migrant organizations.Their target was a left-wing Turkish cultural association gathered at the venue before a football match. Armed with wooden clubs, glass bottles, and slingshots, the attackers injured a man affiliated with the communist trade union initiative International, leaving him with a concussion, facial injuries, and a skull laceration requiring hospital treatment. Nine men, aged 23 to 28, were arrested. Some of the perpetrators had posted tributes to Hitler and far-right symbols, including a "Blood and Honor" tattoo, on social media.

A 41-year-old Pakistani man was attacked by a group of individuals aged 30 to 35. The perpetrators initially asked the victim for a cigarette before violently assaulting him, kicking him, and throwing him into the sea, attempting to drown him. The victim, unable to swim, was rescued by three women who intervened and helped him out of the water. He suffered a broken nose and other injuries. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

The victim, a 40-year-old Polish man, was fueling his car after work when he was recognized as a foreigner by two other men and a woman at the gas station. When the victim drove away from the gas station, the perpetrators followed and caught up with him on the road. They then drove in front of the victim and forced him to stop. The two men got out of the car, walked towards the victim, and suddenly began beating him. They also tore him out of the car and kicked him, causing him to suffer serious injuries. One of the perpetrators was a neo-Nazi with a relevant criminal background, which he openly displayed with tattoos and clothing in court. He was sentenced to 1 year and 6 months in prison.

A taxi driver in Höör was brutally assaulted by two men who beat him up to 120 times while shouting racist insults. The attack caused severe physical and psychological injuries, forcing the driver to close his business and relocate. He reported that the assailants attempted to carve a racist symbol into his forehead. The violence began in the taxi and continued in a driveway, but the driver’s life was saved when a woman heard the commotion and called the police. The attackers, both in their twenties, were sentenced to one year and one year and two months in prison, respectively, and ordered to pay 45,800 kr in damages.

Three men of Turkish origins were attacked and injured by three right-wing extremists, aged 21 to 26. The incident began outside a restaurant in the night when the perpetrators racially insulted the victims. The victims called their friends and asked for help. The group of perpetrators and the victims moved to another bar, where a fight broke out between the parties. The perpetrators used batons and quartz sand gloves during the fight. The victims suffered injuries, including a dislocated shoulder, bruises and a laceration on the lip. They received medical treatment. One of the perpetrators were wearing a belt with a swastika emblem. The perpetrators were shouting “Heil Hitler” during the attack. The perpetrators were charged with dangerous bodily harm in conjunction with the distribution of propaganda material from unconstitutional organizations.

When the victim got off the bus he was approached by five skinheads belonging to Portugal Hammerskins. They began to verbally insult the victim on the basis of his black skin colour. As the victim tried to flee, he was punched, kicked and stabbed with a knife on his legs, stomach, and chest. The incident was an initiation ritual for new members to Hammerskins.

Unknown persons threw fireworks at the wooden barracks that housed refugees. The shelter did not catch fire, but one Roma child suffered shock and had to be taken to hospital. The police investigated for attempted arson. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

Three members of the left-wing Partito Comunista dei Lavoratori (Communist Party of Labourers) were attacked by a group of around ten individuals affiliated with neofascist movements. The victims were walking peacefully when they were suddenly assaulted. The perpetrators fled when the police arrived. Two of the victims were injured, with one suffering a broken nose and the others reporting various traumas.

A 39-year-old was with a group of British Indian friends and family when he saw three men damaging his car. When the victim challenged them, the three men punched him to the ground. The victim lost consciousness and was later treated in the hospital for head injuries. A friend of the victim attempted to intervene and was repeatedly kicked by the group, resulting in a fractured arm and nose. He was taken to the hospital along with a second companion of the victim who was also assaulted. The police treated the attack as a racially motivated assault.

A group of five minors attacked a 10-year-old Roma boy in an unprovoked assault. The victim was punched and kicked in the stomach. A passerby intervened, stopping the attack. The perpetrators justified their actions by calling the victim a "dirty g*psy." The severity threshold is lowered in this case due to the deliberate targeting of children.

Three members of an extreme right-wing group were sentenced to three years and six months in prison for a crime of aggravated injuries of abuse of superiority and xenophobia, after beating a dark-skinned young man of Israeli origin. The attack occurred during a student demonstration in the center of Córdoba, in which the defendants were part of a group of 17 extreme right-wing individuals carrying Spanish flags. As the march was ending, the victim who was on his way home accompanied by some friends, passed by the group. When the perpetrators saw him, they began to yell at him, calling him "fat black man". The victim responded by blowing kisses in the air, or by waving his hand, which led the perpetrators to attack him. The three defendants punched the victim in the face , and one of them hit him in the face with a flagstick, breaking one of the victim's teeth.
A 24-year-old woman was racially abused and punched in the face by a white woman in her twenties. The victim suffered a broken nose. The police referred to the incident as a racist attack.

A small group of people who had been trying to seize control of the loyalist Ulster Defence Association, threw a petrol bomb at the house of an immigrant family. The weapon failed to ignite. The perpetrators also carried out attacks on two other properties of immigrant families, that did not meet the requirements for inclusion in the RTV dataset. In both cases, windows of the properties were smashed. Police treated the attacks as hate crimes.

A 19-year-old serving UK soldier was arrested for making a nail bomb at his family's property in Manchester. At the time, he was serving at a UK base in Germany when the police discovered the bomb on another person property while conducting a raid following a tip-off about images of abuse on a computer. The solider admitted making the device, which consisted of 181 metal screws and shards of glass. He had links on his computer to far-right groups in Europe and watched a video of two men being executed under a swastika flag. He also had a "keen interest in the English Defence League" and had attended one of their marches but was not a member of the group. He said he was interested in right wing politics because he did not like mass immigration. He said he made the bomb while on leave "out of boredom". He documented his thoughts in a journal entitled [name]'s Story Book. It featured drawings of guns and knives, images of paramilitary soldiers and references to groups including the National Front, Klu Klux Klan and British National Party.

Four men, three from the Nordic Resistance Movement, approached a 36-year-old man from Nigeria and stabbed him in the stomach without provocation.  According to the police, the men had gotten into a quarrel with a black man, who managed to flee. When they spotted the victim, they mistook him for the man they had previously chased and stabbed the victim instead. According to witnesses, the perpetrators shouted Sieg Heil. The case was reopened after a TV programme interviewed the victim. Three men, aged 18, 22 and 23, were charged but not sentenced for the crime. According to the indictment, the motive for the attack was the victims skin color.

Around 30 people attacked a protest against the Nordic Resistance Movement [Swedish at the time]. The perpetrators threw bottles and firecrackers against the protestors, including prams and families with children. They also attacked the police, striking one officer with a ladder, and two people were stabbed.The perpetrators wrote on their site that one of their activists had been stabbed as well. The police arrested 28 people.

Four members of Golden Dawn stopped a 56-year-old Roma man who was carrying a suitcase with small goods he was selling. The perpetrators first asked the victim to open the suitcase to see what was inside. When the victim told them to wait for him to open it, he was punched in the face. Two of his teeth were broken. Then the perpetrators threw the victim to the ground and kicked him in the body. One of his legs was broken which later required the victim to undergo surgery in the hospital.

A Chinese man in his twenties was attacked by four youths while walking from his home to a store. The man was subjected to racist insults, knocked to the ground, and scratched on the face with a knife. Police described the incident as one of the most severe cases of racially motivated violence they have encountered recently. The attack was deemed unprovoked, as the victim did not know the assailants. The attackers blocked his path, forced him against a wall, and beat him, causing multiple facial injuries. Following the assault, the victim received medical treatment, and the youths allegedly stole his bank card.

A 12-year-old girl was assaulted by a 40-year-old woman in Malmö after refusing to lend her phone. When the girl said no, the woman struck her in the face and shouted racist insults. Witnesses reported that the woman pressed the girl against a wall, hit her, and spat on her. The girl sustained visible marks and experienced pain for several days afterward. A nearby witness confirmed the incident, stating they intervened to protect the girls when they heard the commotion. The woman has been charged with assault, classified as a hate crime due to the racist nature of her remarks. The severity threshold of this case is lowered due to children being assaulted.

Around 20 racists, led by a former Danish Defence League spokesperson , gathered at Korsør Station with plans to violently storm the Motalavej housing area and attack ethnic minorities. The group, including masked men from "Rightwings", had organized the event online, calling for violence against local immigrant youth. Despite the former DDF-leader's claims of 150 participants, the turnout was much smaller, and police heavily monitored the station and Motalavej, preventing the attack. The group dissolved after a brief gathering, with some driving past Motalavej but not entering. The former DDF-leader was later arrested for violating public order regulations.
According to the police, an individual of Turkish origin was the victim of dangerous bodily harm for racist reasons. A suspect was identified. No further details are available.

An unknown man set fire to a home for asylum seekers early in the morning. The roof and façade of the building was burning when one of the residents, who was returning home around 4:45, managed to wake up the ten people who were sleeping inside. Parts of the building burned completely but no one was injured. One of the victims had seen a man "tampering" with the façade at 2:45 AM. The police assumed that the perpetrator was disturbed by the witness, but that he returned and continued the attack a few hours later. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

A 21-year-old member of the far-right skinhead movement injured two people during a concert in Clermont-Ferrand in support of illegal immigrants. The perpetrator fired eight shots from a sawed-off shotgun, injuring one victim seriously in the hands and head. The man admitted to the attack, stating that he intended to intimidate the concertgoers. He was sentenced to two years in prison.

A 22 year old Kuwaiti asylum seeker was walking home when a group of drunken friends engaged the victim in a conversation and began to racially abuse him. Two of the friends in the group then started to punch the victim in the face and body, as well as kicking the victim while on the ground, according to the judge in trial. The victim required surgery to fix a broken nose. One of the perpetrators admitted to the attack and said it was entirely unprovoked and the victim did not deserve it. The two men were jailed for the attack.

A group of people approached the Afghani victim, asking where he was from. When he answered, they broke a beer bottle on his head and the victim lost consciousness. It was the second time the victim had been attacked.

weapon_description: Chains, baseball bats, stools, glasses and bottles
description: A man from an unspecified right-wing group, wearing boots and a bomber jacket, entered a pub where he recognized two people belonging to the left. He then went outside to get the rest of the group (between 20 and 25 and armed with sticks and chains) who began beating the two victims and throwing chairs and glasses. One of the victims was hit with a baseball bat, causing a head injury that he received hospital treatment for. The other victim suffered contusions to his head, arms, and leg. Two of the perpetrators were sentenced to two years in prison for the attack. During trial it was confirmed that they belonged to right-wing groups, and that they had a police record for similar incidents.

Right-wing extremists stormed a celebration at a community center and injured eleven people, some of them seriously. According to the public prosecutor's office, the perpetrators wanted revenge after a stone had been thrown into a house they lived in. They suspected that the person behind the attack was at the party. A 39-year-old masked man entered the hall alone and punched three victims in the head wearing some kind of gloves, making them fall to the ground. Then a group of other masked people entered the center and begun punching and kicking the guests with quartz sand gloves. Charges were brought against 15 suspects. Some of the perpetrators had been active in the right-wing scene for many years and had connections to militant neo-Nazi structures. More than half of the perpetrators had previosly been convicted. Four of them had links to Thuringian right-wing rock bands.

Two left-wing, anti-fascist activists, aged 16 and 17, were stabbed by far-right militants in a violent attack. The victims, celebrating a birthday, were targeted by six men who recognized them as anti-fascist militants. The altercation escalated, resulting in one victim being stabbed in the leg and the other in the stomach. The attack took place in a neighborhood with a strong far-right presence, and the perpetrators were reportedly attempting to assert control over the area.

Two men were jailed for 90 days after an assault. The victim, originally from Liberia, was followed by a car and attacked with punches and kicking from a group of men shouting "We do not like immigrants in Verdal. We hate you and are gonna get you". The victim explains that the violence was unprovoked and random, and that he was hospitalized for his injuries.

Two police officers chased a severely autistic man in a car because they thought "it was funny". The policemen were heard laughing as they were driving after the man walking in the streets outside his home. The victim has a mental age of a three-year-old. One of the officers described the victim as a "f****** P***" [fucking paki], before he got out of the car and ran after the victim, and then beat him. The officer allegedly rugby tackled the victim, threw him into some bins and punched him in the face. The victim cried out for help, and his sister and brother arrived at the scene. As the two officers returned to their car there were heated exchanges between them and neighbours, with one accusing them of being racist. Driving off, one of the officers is heard saying  "[He/The victim] F***ing doesn't interact with people, don't f***ing let him out". The victim was left with cuts and bruises. The officers are also accused on covering up why they chased the 33 year-old man, saying they were concerned for him.

A 30 year-old Asian man was assaulted by a man who approached him and started shouting racist comments. The episode happened outside a supermaket a bit before midnight. The victim was taken to the hospital for urgent treatment of the injuries he sustained.

A young man with a Lebanese background was attacked by a group in the parking lot of a nightclub. First, one of the perpetrators from the group approached the victim and punched him in the face. Then the other perpetrators joined in, insulting the victim with racist slurs, hitting, and kicking him. The victim suffered a double fracture of the jaw and had to be treated in the hospital for several days.

A group of four left-wing militants, affiliated with the French Socialist Party (PS), were attacked by three men while pasting electoral posters. The perpetrators racially insulted the victims, using slurs such as "dirty n*****" and "dirty Arab" (sale nègre, sale arabe), before physically assaulting them. The attackers also used a stone and tear gas during the assault. One of the victims was hospitalized due to the injuries sustained.

A shopkeeper in Aylesbury was left with a broken nose after being repeatedly punched and racially abused. The victim heard a football hit the shop window around 7 p.m., and when he stepped outside to investigate, two men verbally abused him before punching him multiple times, causing a broken nose and facial injuries.

After a demonstration against men's violence against women, a group of men belonging to Svenskarnas party [the Swedes' party] attacked a group of protestors. The group had spread Nazi propoganda for the party in the area before the attack. Six people, four men and two women, had to seek medical care. Five of them were slightly injured, while the sixth suffered life-threatening injuries after being stabbed. A 24-year-old was  arrested on suspicion of attempted murder. A  27-year-old was arrested on suspicion of involvement in attempted murder. A 20-year-old was set free when the district court ruled that the evidence against him did not hold. Finally, a 30-year-old key figure from the party involved in the incident fled, but was later apprehended in Ukraine.

This is the first of two incidents during the same day in which pipe bombs, packed with nails, were detonted outside two houses occupied by Romanian families (see also 2014-3-8-4). A total of nine people, including a child, escaped injuries from the explosions. Police believe the attacks are linked and are treating them as hate crimes. A letterbox had earlier been blown off the door of one of the properties. Two men were arrested for the crimes.

This is the second incident during the same day in which pipe bombs, packed with nails, were detonted outside two houses occupied by Romanian families (see also 2014-3-8-c). A total of nine people, including a child, escaped injuries from the explosions. Police believe the attacks are linked and are treating them as hate crimes. A letterbox had earlier been blown off the door of one of the properties. Two men were arrested for the crimes.

A 57-year-old German man stabbed a 28-year-old man of Angolan descent in the neck with a knife after an argument on a bus, critically injuring him. The victim and the perpetrator first argued on the bus. Several witnesses describe that the perpetrator called the victim racist terms and other insults as he got off the bus, which led to a physical altercation. The perpetrator pulled out a knife and stabbed the victim in the upper body and in the carotid artery. Another witness reports that the perpetrator shouted, "I hate foreigners!" after his arrest. The perpetrator was also injured and had to be hospitalized. There were major demonstrations against the trivialization of racist violence following the attack.

According to information from the Sächsisches Staatsministerium des Inneren (Ministry of the Interior), a young man was beaten up twice because of his ethnicity. The incident happened in a discotheque. Due to the injuries, that included a broken cheekbone, the victim had to spend three days in the hospital.

Two individuals, one of them the father of a young soccer player, assaulted a 16-year-old referee of Algerian origin after a soccer match at the Don Bosco Center. The perpetrators had been yelling at the referee during the match, and at the end of the game, they approached him in one of the corners of the field by the dressing room areas was located. After saying «N*****, you have stolen our game», one of the perpetrators grabbed the victim by the neck and punched him in the right eye. The victim tried to run, but the two perpetrators caught up with him. The second perpetrator grabbed the victim from behind, held his arms back and assaulted him on the back, while the other hit him in the ribs and abdomen. After the attack, the victim was transferred to the hospital by ambulance. He required observation in the hospital for 24 hours and had injuries that required thirteen days to heal, of which he was disabled for three and hospitalized for one.

Around 1.45am, a man and his friends were standing next to their car before a couple approached them. The man in the couple made a racist comment to the victim before punching him in the head. The victim fell and, according to the police, recieved serious head injuries.

A 19-year-old from Chechnya was abducted and stabbed 57 times with a screw driver by a group of people. The victim was travelling to work early in the morning with his stepdad, when they were pulled over by the perpetrators. The perpetrators had claimed to be police and threatened to arrest the victim and his stepdad. When the victims realized that they weren’t officers they tried to run away. The stepdad managed to get away but they managed to grab the victim. The perpetrator had said "Where are you from?", to which the victim replied that he was from Chechnya. The victim said that they then asked if he was Muslim and stabbed him in the genitals. He was also stabbed in the face, stomach, back, legs and shoulders. One perpetrator "we will put him in the river after we finish and break his f****** teeth." When the victim's mother called, the perpetrator picked up the phone and said "he’s f**king dead". Neither the victim or his stepdad were involved in criminality and police believed it was a "random attack carried out by a crazed gang."

weapon_description: Slingshot and steel balls and other iron parts
description: Unknown perpetrators shot metal objects at an emergency accommodation for refugees in a reportedly xenophobic attack. The steel balls and other iron parts were probably shot with the use of a slingshot. Several windows were broken, but there were no reported injuries. When the police arrived to examine the scene, they were almost hit by a metal screw. The state security police investigated for attempted dangerous bodily harm and stated that if someone had been hit, they would have been seriously injured. This was the third in a series of similar attacks on the emergency accommodation in a few months (CaseID 2013-10-21 and 2013-10-18-2). Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

Two Polish men were targeted in a racial verbal and physical attack from a group of youths, leading to one of the victims spending three days in hospital suffering from a fractured skull and bleeding on his brain. The victims were approached by a group shouting "you are f****** Polish, this is our town, we are locals". One in the group thereafter knocked one of them men to the ground, causing him to lose consciousness. When police arrived, the perpetrator continued shouting racist abuse now towards the officers, like "f*** off to Pakistan, you terrorist bastard and 9/11 bastard".

According to the police, a 17-year-old Algerian was racially abused by two perpetrators. The incident occurred in a youth residential facility where the victim lived. The perpetrators had been visiting another resident in the same facility. One of the perpetrators, an 18-year-old man from Bernau, threw a knife at the victim, which struck him in the head with the handle. The perpetrator shouted "Sieg Heil." The 18-year-old was known to the police, and an arrest warrant was issued against him.

Three alleged neo-Nazis received sentences of three to five years in prison for an attempted murder of a 40-year-old man. Two of the perpetrators were also charged for belonging to a criminal group. The events occurred early in the morning, when the three defendants had just left an establishment on Alfonso XIII street, frequented by people of the far-right and with neo-Nazi ideology. At one point, two men passed through the street, and the perpetrators recognized one of them for being a collaborator of a refugee aid agency. Immediately, they began to shout "traitors to Spain, perroflautas, we are going to kill you." The two men rushed to Alfaros Street, but the perpetrators followed them. There, they blocked the road of the two men and one of the perpetrators, using a knife of about nine centimeters, stabbed the collaborator of the NGO in the side. Immediately after, the perpetrators fled the scene of the attack. The victim's companion notified health emergencies, which rushed the victim to the hospital.

A 21-year-old intoxicated man suddenly attacked two Romanian men with an iron bar. The perpetrators shouted at the victims, "Foreigners, what do you want here?" When a witness intervened, the perpetrator threatened him with a knife. The victims managed to flee. Police officers who arrived at the scene arrested the perpetrator, who was known to the police from before. State security investigated for dangerous bodily harm, insults and violation of the weapons law.

Twelve far-right members of Liga Joven, the youth organization of Movimiento Social Republicano (MSR), aged between 19 and 30, were arrested after attacking several members of Sindicato de Estudiantes, an anti-fascist student association. The victims had attended an event organized by the student association when the perpetrators interrupted, throwing bottles, furniture, and other objects at them, resulting in serious physical injuries, according to the police. The perpetrators were described as having shaved heads, wearing bomber jackets, and carrying a Spanish flag.

A 27-year-old man was hospitalized after being attacked by two neo-Nazis. The victim was on a subway station with two friends around 5 AM. They were insulted by one of the perpetrators, who was wearing clothes from a right-wing extremist brand. The victim made it clear to the perpetrator that he wound not have a discussion. He identified himself as a member of the right-wing scene and asked whether the victim had a problem with that. The second perpetrator joined in the following scuffle. The victim was kicked in the face and suffered serious eye injuries. He was treated as an inpatient at the hospital. The perpetrators fled. The state security police investigated for dangerous bodily harm.

A man from the United Arab Emirates suffered serious head injuries after being struck repeatedly with a metal baton and a broken bottle by three men. The three men, all from Edinburgh, admitted running at the victim, pushing him to the ground and repeatedly punching and kicking him on the head and attacking him with the baton and bottle. It was also accepted that the attack was racially motivated. The victim suffered life-threatening bleeding to the brain.

A woman was stabbed by a man in Älta in April after confronting him about his Nazi salutes at a bar. The incident escalated into a violent altercation, resulting in her being knifed. The 26-year-old assailant was arrested the following day on suspicion of attempted murder.

A Zimbabwean man in his car was followed by a group of men in their vehicle shouting racist abuse. The perpetrators followed the man untill a stop and then attacked him in the street, leaving him with what the police describe were serious facial injuries. The perpetrators were alle white in their late teens to mid-twenties. They fled the scene and witnesses called an ambulance for the victim.

weapon_description: Explosives, firearms, machetes, knives, combat gear and ammunition
description: Presumably inspired by the 22 July attacks in 2011, a 32-year-old man gathered an extensive collection of weapons, explosives, and combat gear closely resembling the equipment used by Breivik. When the police tried to enter his apartment, he unsuccessfully tried to detonate several improvised explosive devices and then shot himself. Authorities later reported that they had found copies of Hitler’s Mein Kampf and extensive literature about the Oklahoma bombing in 1995. However, no connections to other right-wing extremists or organizations could be found, nor specific attack plans.

A 22-year-old was attacked by three right-wing extremists. The incident began when the perpetrators called  the victim a "fucking Zecke [slur for leftist]". The perpetrators then demanded that he take off his jacket with the word "Antifa" on it. When the victim did not comply, he was knocked to the ground, where the perpetrators kicked him and jumped on his upper body, among other things. When the perpetrators let go of the victim and walked away, he managed to alert his friends, who picked him up and took him to the hospital. There, he was diagnosed with a hand fracture and several rib fractures.

A man of Somali origin was beaten in the street by two unknown men. The police suspected a racist motive. The state security police were investigating the incident as dangerous bodily harm. No further details are available.

Two men in their early 20s and a woman aged 19, all orinially from Eastern Europe, were attacked by a group of 15 people with golf clubs. One of the men lost two teeth and all three suffered bruises and cuts. The police are treating the attack as a hate crime.  This attack is one of several racial incidents targeting Eastern Europeans and Africans in Belfast (see e.g. caseID 2014-4-23-2 and 2014-4-24-2).

Unknown perpetrators shot at a house where a Roma family of seven lived. The family escaped injuries. Police are treating the incident as a hate crime. This attack is one of several racial incidents targeting Eastern Europeans and Africans in Belfast (see e.g. caseID 2014-4-22-2 and 2014-4-24-2).

An 18-year-old of Turkish background was on his way home at around 8:30 PM when he was verbally abused with racist slurs by four or five people. The perpetrators suddenly attacked the victim, hitting and kicking him - including in the head and neck. The perpetrators fled. The victim was taken to the hospital with severe facial injuries and underwent surgery for more than four hours. He had suffered a double jaw fracture. The leader of the attack had been wearing a pin with a red swastika on a white background.

A 23-year-old man was stabbed in a racist attack after he was confronted by two men. Police said both men shouted racist comments and one of them stabbed the man in the right leg with a small knife. He required hospital treatment for his injury. Police are treating the incident as a hate crime.  This attack is one of several racial incidents targeting Eastern Europeans and Africans in Belfast (see e.g. caseID 2014-4-22-2 and 2014-4-23-2).

Two individuals, one of Turkish origin and one of German origin, were racially insulted and physically attacked. The police were investigating the incident as dangerous bodily harm. No further details are available.

Two right-wing extremists, aged 20 and 21, carried out an arson attack on a refugee home during the night. 240 refugees lived in the building at the time. The perpetrators sprayed a door with petrol and set it on fire. One of them gave the Hitler salute. Because the door was made of steel, the fire went out on its own.
