The perpetrators, who were filmed by a surveillance camera, were arrested close to the crime scene. The state security police investigated the perpetrators for attempted serious arson.

A pensioner of Serbian origin was attacked by two men, in what was reported as a racially motivated attack. The victim entered the elevator on a metro station, where the perpetrators were already standing. What was described as "a foreign looking woman" with a pram also tried to enter into the elevator. The victim asked the perpetrators to squeeze in so that there would be room for the woman with the pram. One of the perpetrators answers: "No way will I do that for foreigners." The victim asks them what they have got against foreigners. Then, upon getting out of the elevator, one of the perpetrators grabbed the victim by the collar of his jacket and punches him in the left eye. The victim suffered a broken cheek bone and an injury to the eye. He had to undergo several surgeries.

A teenager carved a swastika and 'SS' into his skin after launching a racist attack on a Nigerian man. The attack was triggered after the perpetrator accused the victim and his friends of kicking a football towards a cat. Following a rant, the perpetrator used racist language including the N-word before striking the Nigerian man with a broken bottle first to his shoulder and then to his face. He admitted a racially aggravated charge of wounding intent to cause grevious bodily harm following the incident and was sentenced to 45 months’ youth detention.

weapon_description: Fence panel with nails, machete, stones, baseball bat and beating/kicking
description: Five young people armed with a fence panel with nails from it, a baseball bat and machete, set upon a religious minister in front of his 14-year-old daughter and two sons while shouting racist abuse. An ordeal had begun hours earlier, when the daughter was walking home from school and passed the group. They called her by the N-word and threatened to attack her brother and dad. When she got home, she told the dad, who had repeatedly suffered abuse from the group over the past two years. Later, the family came across the group again, and this time, the group barricaded the road and was armed with sticks and at least one knife. The perpetrators first threw a rock at the dad's chest, knocking him backwards. Then, the younger son was set upon and kicked to the head. The oldest son was hit with a fence panel with nails and struck by a baseball bat. When the group heard police sirens, they shouted "leave this n******, we'll come back and get them then" and "stab the dad!". The group was sentenced from 11 months to 9 years.

A 36-year-old Iraqi-born kiosk owner was violently attacked by a group of four racists. The assault began around midnight inside his kiosk when one of the perpetrators, who had previously threatened him with a knife at a gas station while declaring hatred for foreigners, demanded to know if the victim recognized him. Again wielding a knife, the perpetrator issued threats, prompting the victim to expel the group from the kiosk. Outside, the perpetrator performed the Hitler salute and repeatedly taunted the victim to come out. Fearing for his safety, the victim locked himself inside. Hours later, at 4 AM, he attempted to go home but was ambushed by the perpetrators, who had waited for him. He was stabbed in the arm, causing him to collapse and requiring emergency surgery. After six days in the hospital, he was discharged. State security police launched an investigation, focusing on a 22-year-old suspect for dangerous bodily harm.

According to the police, a left-wing activist was attacked by a right-wing individual because of his political views. The police investigated the incident as dangerous bodily harm.  No further details are available.

A family waiting at a bus stop was injured in a racially motivated attack, leaving a two-year-old with a lump on the head, a six-year-old with bruises on his legs, and an eight-year-old with bruises on her knees. The father was also struck in the back. The attacker began by hurling racist abuse, shouting, "You come to steal money from my country" and "This is not Africa. Go back to Africa." When the mother asked him to stop because her children were present, he threw his phone at her and then began pelting the family with large stones. The man was subsequently jailed for the assault. The severity threshold is lowered is this case due to the targeting of children.

After two AfD members or supporters accused several anti-fascists of toppling an election poster, one attacker assaulted the victims with a baseball bat while the other threatened them with a knife. Police arriving at the scene recorded the victims' personal details, but AfD supporters continued photographing them up close without interference. At least three victims were injured, one requiring outpatient hospital treatment for severe bruises.

A 12-year-old Asian boy was beaten and racially abused by a 15- or 16-year-old while walking with his 10-year-old brother in Glasgow. Following the assault, the victim returned home and was taken to the hospital, where he was kept overnight due to the assault's impact on a pre-existing medical condition.

A Lebanese man was hospitalized after a racially motivated attack by a right-wing extremist. The perpetrator insulted him with racial slurs upon seeing him working in a garden, kicked him twice in the abdomen, and threatened to kill him if he did not leave the city.

A 28-year-old woman suffered a broken leg in a racist attack. She and her partner were harassed for their "Asian appearance" before passers-by intervened to protect them, prompting the perpetrators to leave. Shortly after, a woman from the group returned and kicked the victim's shin, breaking her leg. The perpetrator escaped, and police suspect the attack was xenophobic.

A man was sentenced to eight years in prison after ordering his two dogs to attack an Asian taxi driver in a racially motivated assault. After finishing his shift around 2:30 a.m., the victim was walking home when he passed the perpetrator’s house and heard him shout, "kill him, kill him." The man, holding a German Shepherd, pointed at the victim, who was then attacked by the dog, which bit him and knocked him down. The perpetrator kicked the victim while shouting racial slurs, and a second dog joined the attack. The victim managed to escape and fled to a nearby taxi office, still pursued by the dogs. The victim suffered severe injuries, including a broken eye socket, a fractured nose, and brain bleeding. In court, it was revealed that the perpetrator was intoxicated during the incident. One of the dogs was later put down, as it was trained to respond to commands to kill.

Two men and a woman were walking at night, around 1am, when a group of three men and two women started directing racist abuse towards them. The perpetrators then assaulted the men and the woman. The victims required hospital treatment. One of them suffred a broken leg and the woman was treated for head injuries. Five people have been arrested in connection to the attack.
According to the police, an Indian man was subjected to insults and beaten for racist reasons. The police investigated for dangerous bodily harm. No further details are available.

weapon_description: Kalashnikov, a pump-action shotgun, hunting rifles and baseball bats
description: Four men associated with Blood and Honour C18 (named after the British group) were arrested. The group published photos on the internet of eight masked men posing with a Kalashnikov, a pump-action shotgun, hunting rifles and baseball bats alongside a declaration that they were ready to take up arms to defend nationalist ideals. The suspects were charged with organizing and participating in an armed group, plotting and defending war crimes. According to the prosecuter, there was no plan of an actual attack and a specific target was not identified during the trial.

Two young counter-demonstrators were attacked with tear gas by an AfD party member at a campaign stand, suffering serious eye injuries that required medical treatment. The perpetrator was later identified as a senior police officer who likely used an unapproved, highly concentrated tear gas. To conceal this, he purchased a legal can of tear gas, partially emptied it in the entrance of a shopping center, and presented it to the police as the weapon used in the attack. In the process, additional bystanders were injured.

A 23 year-old man sustained stab wounds and was racially abused by two men, aged 19 and 22. The victim and his friends were chased by the the perpetrators when leaving a bar they had been at. The victim got separated from his friends, and was then attacked by both perpetrators whom were carrying knives. He suffered three slash wounds which needed stitches, one to the arm, and two to the thigh, causing the victim to suffer walking difficulties for many months. The 19 year-old perpetrator was sentenced to 12 and half years of prison. The other man recieved 9 years of imprisonment.
According to the police, a right-wing extremist attacked two Iranian men for racist reasons.  The police investigated for dangerous bodily harm. No further details are available.

Neo-Nazis attacked three students after a canceled concert. A group of 15 right-wing extremists had gathered in a bar when the victims confronted them outside. The students were then assaulted, leaving one with a fractured skull and in intensive care, while another suffered a black eye from being punched in the face.

A Senegalese street vendor was brutally attacked by two brothers, aged 43 and 50. The perpetrators first violently beat the victim and then slashed his face with a knife. The victim was hospitalized and required several stitches. The brothers have been charged with aggravated assault due to racial discrimination and the illegal use of weapons. Motive not explcitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

weapon_description: Home-made explosive devices, hexamethylene triperoxide Diamine(HMTD) chemical
description: A student of Russian origin was arrested and jailed for 2 years for making peroxide bombs. The perpetrator bought chemicals online, mixed them together and built six explosive devices and detonators for them. The police found the explosives in his room. He boasted he would use the bombs to "whiten n******" on a Russian social platform, VK. The perpetrator had watched videos on YouTube explaining how hexamethylene triperoxide Diamine(HMTD) could be detonated and cause explosions. One earlier explosion left him deaf on one ear. The perpetrator once made the fire alarm go off at the residence, but said he caused it by lighting a match. He was arrested in London under anti-terrorism provisions. The perpetrator admitted making an explosive substance. The hearing was told bomb disposal officers used a robot to recover the chemical hexamethylene triperoxide diamine (HMTD) - a substance too volatile for military or commercial use.

A 30-year-old man was brutally beaten by a group of five to six neo-Nazis, presumably because he was wearing patches with the words "Antifa" and "Against Nazis". The attack took place in the on the street in the morning. The victim was knocked down with a punch and the perpetrators then continued to beat him. The perpetrators, who according to the victim were clearly part of the right-wing scene based on their appearance and clothing, hit him over the head with a baton and kicked the victim in the head. The victim suffered injuries and was treated at the hospital. The state security police investigated the incident. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

A group of six skinheads attacked a left-wing activist on the subway because of his clothes. The perpetrators punched, kicked, and eventually stabbed the victim in the lung. The victim was seriously injured. Two of the perpetrators, aged 17 and 18, were arrested.

Two housemates of Pakistani origin were awaken when their window was smashed by a bottle around 3 am. The two men then called the police to investigate the incident. Later the same day, when cleaning up, the men were racially abused outside their home by a group of people. One of the perpetrators attacked one of the victims,  and forced his way into the house along with two other perpetrators. Both housemates were then attacked inside the house. One of the victims was taken to the hospital for treatment of a broken foot and minor cuts and bruises. The other was also beaten but to a minor extent as he managed to hide and call the police. Police are treating the incident as a hate crime. They arrested a 18 year-old woman in connection to the attack, and another 57 year-old man was later released on bail. The attack happened the day after the victims had attended an anti-racist event, due to the surge of racist attack in Northern Ireland. This attack comes in a period of sustained racial incidents in Belfast (see e.g. caseID 2014-6-10-2 and 2014-6-11-2).

A ten-year-old girl was assaulted by a man in his 20s to 30s on a playground in Linköping. The man hit the girl on the cheek, grabbed her by the neck, and pushed her to the ground while shouting racist remarks at her and her friends, who had foreign backgrounds. Several parents witnessed the incident and reported it to the police, who have opened an investigation for assault and hate speech. The severity threshold of this case is lowered due to children being assaulted.

The police confiscated a ten-centimeter functioning nail bomb in the home of a 33-year-old suspected right-wing extremist. Prior to the house search, the perpetrator had attracted the attention of the authorities for violent crimes, drug dealing, xenophobic offences and swastika graffiti. After finding the bomb, the police initiated an investigation into whether the perpetrator had any attack plans with a right-wing extremist target, or if he had connections to politically organized groups. The perpetrator was charged with violation of the Explosives Act and for drug trafficking.

A man was walking outside when a female passer-by described as black told him his  headphones were trailing from his pocket. The man's response was to make racist comments like "f*** off n*****", follow her down the street, and slash her across her forehead with a knife. The woman suffered a head wound and a black eye. The man was convicted for racially aggravated assault and  jailed for 11 years due to other unrelated criminal charges.

A 36-year-old college student was arrested  after his half-brother and mother uncovered chemicals and papers detailing his racial hatred stashed in his bedroom. The perpetrator had bought the ingredients over the internet, and stockpiled dust masks, metal filter funnels, plastic syringes and latex gloves. He allegedly plotted to kill non-Aryans or Prince Charles, so that Prince Harry could be king. He stated "I don't want to be a serial killer. I'm more of an Anders Breivik." He added he wanted a "silent rifle...take up a good position and put a bullet in Charles's head". Prosecutor said the perpetrators' notes expressed hatred for "non-Aryans" whom he referred to as "blacks and Caucasian idiots". He was found guilty of preparing terrorist acts after a retrial after the previous jury failed to reach a verdict. The court heard how he felt alienated and marginalised for being a white, ginger-haired man and also suffered from agoraphobia and depression. He lived with his mother.

A 63-year-old Black man narrowly escaped harm when his apartment was set on fire while he slept. The attackers set a fuel-soaked mattress ablaze and smashed his bedroom window. The victim suspected two women, aged 60 and 30, who had been tormenting him for a year, including damaging his car and attempting to smash his front door while shouting racist slurs like, "You n*****s come here to take our jobs." The attack prompted an anti-racism rally in the neighborhood, and the victim eventually returned to Germany, where he had grown up.

U17 football players, attending a national tournament for young players, were subjected to a racial attack by a group of youths waiting by their hotel. The perpetrators racially insulted the dark-skinned players from various teams and proceeded to physically assault them. A physiotherapist for one of the teams, who himself had Asian origins, intervened, and tried to protect the players. The physiotherapist was beaten and suffered a broken nose, abrasions, and bruises.

A man originally from Nigeria was attacked just outside his home on his way to a night shift around 8 pm. A gang of four to six people racially abused him, telling him to go back to his own country. The victim asked them why they were calling him names and told them to "go and get a job. I'm going to my work". When the victim picked up his phone to call his wife, the group threatened to burn his house down and to run over him and his two year old daughter. Then the gang physically assaulted him, with punches and a bottle over the head. Shortly after his wife ran to his aid, with their daughter. The victim needed hospital treatment, including stitches to his face. Police are treating the incident as a racially motivated assault. A 19 year-old has been arrested. Two other men aged 25 and 32 were arrested but released on bail awating inquiries. This attack comes in a period of sustained racial incidents in Belfast (see e.g. caseID 2014-6-1-2 and 2014-6-11-2).

A Turkish man was beaten up by two men, aged 18 and 25. The victim was standing by his stall in the city center when the two men passed by and called him a "P*** b******". When the victim asked what the two men had called him, they got aggressive. They punched him to the ground, beat and kicked him to the face, and ripped off his clothing. The attack left the victim with a broken wrist requiring hospital treatment. The police are treating the attack as a hate crime. This attack comes in a period of sustained racial incidents in Belfast (see e.g. caseID 2014-6-1-2 and 2014-6-10-2).

On the sidelines of a demonstration against right-wing agitation and racism, two men from Guinea-Bissau, aged 18 and 27, were attacked by three unknown men. When police officers intervened, two of the perpetrators actively resisted their temporary arrest. The state security police investigated the perpetrators, aged 28, 29 and 38, for dangerous bodily harm. The police classified the perpetrators as belonging to the right-wing spectrum. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

Two members of Golden Dawn attacked a migrant. They got out of their car and jumped on the victims head. Witnesses attempted to intervene, whereupon the perpetrators responded 'now you see what Golden Dawn is.' The attack occurred in front of a traffic guard, who did not intervene. The victim was taken to the hospital, bleeding from his head.

According to the police, a right-wing extremist attacked an individual whom the perpetrator perceived as a political opponent. The incident was investigated as a case of dangerous bodily harm. No further details are available.

Two young men were attacked by several right-wing extremists. The perpetrators first beat one of the victims. They justified the attack by saying that the victim was friends with “fucking Zecken [slur for leftists]”. When the other victim tried to confront them, he was attacked by several of the perpetrators. They hit and kicked him so hard that he lost several teeth.

The victim said he was on his way home when he saw two of the perpetrators and claimed they appeared to be waiting for him. They asked the victim whether he was an anti-fascist. When he said yes, they began harrassing him. A third boy arrived and punched the victim in the face. When he fell to the ground, they started kicking him. The victim was hospitalized with a broken nose and numerous bruises. The victim was unsure how the perpetrators recognized him as he was not wearing clothes or symbols associated with the left.

A 21-year-old man of Asian origin was attacked by a 19-year-old and a 18-year-old in a racially motivated attack. The perpetrators were drinking at a party when they saw the victim and his friend walk by. One of the perpetrators called out to the victim and made monkey sounds. The other perpetrator asks him "if it is a perker" ["perker" is a derogatory term for people of Asian or Middle Eastern origin], to which he responds yes. Then the two perpetrators ran after the victim, hit him in the head with a beer bottle, and punched and kicked him. The victim suffered several cuts to his face and broke his hand. The perpetrators were sentenced to four months in prison for a racially motivated attack.

Two Ivorian men were shot in the legs by a 21-year-old Italian man, igniting racial tensions in the area. The victims were on a bike when the assailant’s father stopped them, accusing them of theft. A confrontation ensued, during which the son claimed he shot the men to protect his father. The incident, which left the victims hospitalized, led to a protest by local immigrants condemning racially motivated violence in the town.

Two imprisoned men attempted to send letter bombs to solicitors. The plot was foiled when prison officers at HMP Full Sutton intercepted an incendiary device. The perpetrators, who both expressed violent, anti-Muslim sentiments, sent threatening letters alongside the explosives. One of them was sentenced to an additional seven years, and the other received an extra six years and three months. The men had a history of threats against Asian prisoners, prison staff, and Muslim target.

A 26-year-old man was attacked by four right-wing extremists because he disagreed with their political action. The incident happened at a public viewing of the World Cup match between Germany and Algeria. The perpetrators were shouting “Sieg Heil” und “Heil Hitler” and the victim asked them to stop. As the victim left the venue, he was attacked by the perpetrators, who beat and kicked him repeatedly while he was laying on the ground. The perpetrators were charged with dangerous bodily harm.

A 21-year-old far-right activist was arrested after police found explosive materials, chemicals, and bomb-making manuals at his residence. The arrest followed an investigation into a separate incident involving minor damage to the car of a local Fratelli d'Italia (Brothers of Italy) politician. During a search of the suspect’s home, police uncovered manuals for constructing paper bombs, along with the necessary chemicals and explosive materials. He has been charged with illegal possession of explosives and hazardous chemicals.

A 30-year-old black man was attacked by a stranger. The victim had been watching a football match where Germany won over France. After the match he walked down the street with his friends. He was wearing the German football jersey. The perpetrator aggressively approached the victim and wanted to know why the victim was cheering. The victim replied that he was happy because they beat France. The perpetrator replied “we whites beat France” before walking away. The victim was attending a party in a nearby garden when the perpetrator reappeared a little later. He shouted, “I’ll show you what a German you are.” The perpetrator hit the victim over the head with a baton two times. The other guests intervened and held back the perpetrator. The victim suffered severe head injuries and was taken to the hospital. The police investigated for dangerous bodily harm.

A man was jailed for life for murdering a teenage footballer by stabbing him in the neck with a broken bottle. The attack happened after a friend of the perpetrator referred to the victim's hair as being afro. An argument was then in progress when the perpetrator picked up a broken bottle and stabbed the victim to his neck. The perpetrator used racially abusive language as he walked away from the scene and later told a friend "the f****** n***** deserved it". The court recognized the racial factors in the murder and jailed him to life.

An Asian 19-year-old boy was unprovokedly beaten up by two men on his way home. The two men, under the influence of alcohol, confronted the teenager as he got off a buss and started shouting racial abuse towards him. They then became aggressive, punching him to the head, tripping him up, punshing him to the ground and kicking him over the head and body. The victim managed to escape and run home, but according to the police, he suffered serious injuries that required hospital treatment. The two perpetrators are described as being between 25 and 30 years of age.

At around 1 AM, a 29-year-old woman was subjected to racist and sexist insults by a man and a woman at the subway station. During the journey with the subway, the victim was further insulted by the perpetrators. They then followed the victim to a nearby street, where the woman suddenly attacked the victim with a knife and injured her.

Two Iranian men, aged 17 and 31, were attacked by three men armed with bladed weapons as they walked through a park. The victims sustained serious injuries, but were stable during hospitalization. Investigating officer says the attack was unprovoked and police believe that the attack may have been racially motivated.

A 17-year-old student of foreign background was attacked by two men. The victim was out in the town center together with two friends when they were sprayed with beer from a balcony. The victim asked the perpetrators why they did it, to which they replied, “Go back home” and “We'll stick a stamp up your ass and send you back”. The perpetrators then threw a bottle at the victim that missed, came downstairs and beat and kicked him for several minutes while he was laying on the ground. The victim suffered a broken hand and bruises all over his body.

A homeless young punk couple from Poland, the woman being pregnant, was attacked by a large group described as right-wing extremists in the evening. They victims were beaten, tormented with stones and both injured by a knife. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

The victim was on his way home, when a man began asking where he was from. The man asked if he had ever been attacked in Kallithea, and when the victim asked "why would I be attacked", he replied "There are several Golden Dawn members there". The victim started walking away, when the man made a phone call. The man caught up with the victim and grabbed him. Four other young men wearing black shirts appeared and they grabbed him, covering his mouth and dragging him down the road. They arrived at a Sport Centre where there were more people. They pushed the victim against some railing, and began beating him with brass knuckles. They continued to beat and kick the victim while he was lying on the ground for hours until a bypasser with a dog scared them away. Due to the timeframe, location and Modus Operandi, it may be suspected that Golden Dawn was behind the attack.

A group of left-wing activists from the Collective ZTL WakeUp were attacked by approximately 15 far-right activists, believed to be members of Forza Nuova. The perpetrators, reportedly armed with sticks, initiated the assault, which turned into a brawl. Local residents, alarmed by the noise and shouting, alerted the police. Upon arrival, the police allowed the attackers to leave, instead detaining and charging the victims with aggravated fighting. One victim required hospitalization for a broken hand.

Three neo-Nazis, aged 24 and 29, were arrested after attacking two men, aged 20 and 23. The perpetrators initiated the assault by asking the victims if they were anti-fascists, which led to a discussion. The perpetrators then threatened the victims and revealed tattoos with Nazi symbols before beginning to beat the victims. The victims managed to escape but were followed by the perpetrators. The 20-year-old victim was eventually caught by the perpetrators and brutally beaten. The attack was interrupted by a police patrol, and the victim, who lost consciousness on the way to the hospital, was later hospitalized with a fractured jaw, nasal septum, and stitches to his chin. Both victims sustained similar injuries, likely inflicted with a metal object, possibly belt buckles. Two of the perpetrators were arrested later that day on charges of assault, threats, and xenophobia. The investigation suggested that the perpetrators might be affiliated with skinhead groups. The 23-year-old victim was later attacked again by neo-Nazis later that same month, resulting in a broken nose (see caseID 2014-8-26-1). In this later incident the victim claimed that one of the perpetrators was a member of the neo-Nazi organization Movimiento Social Republicano (MSR), after recognizing the perpetrator in photos on social media where he was giving Nazi salutes alongside the leader of the MSR.

A taxi driver of Pakistani or Bangladeshi background was left with a fractured jaw after being assaulted in a racially motivated attack.The police said the attack occurred shortly after the driver’s taxi was flagged down in by a group of men at approximately at 3am. The driver pulled up outside a club when the men began banging on the cab and hurling racist insults at him. He then stepped out of his car to get help but was attacked by the men who repeatedly punched him, leaving him with a fractured jaw and severe bruising. Three men were captured on CCTV in connection with the assault. The police said: “Due to the language used during the attack, we are treating this as racially motivated.”

Three people on a motorcycle stopped an Iranian man on the street. They asked him where he was from, before two of them punched him. When the victim fell to the ground, he was stabbed 12 times in the chest and abdomen.

A 21-year-old man was attacked by an 18-year-old who identified himself as a CasaPound supporter. The victim, wearing a T-shirt from Ardita San Paolo, a left-wing affiliated football club, was playing table football when the assailant confronted him over his shirt, then threw a glass bottle at him, reportedly declaring his CasaPound affiliation as his motivation. The victim was hospitalized with facial cuts, broken teeth, and a split lip.

According to the police, a Turkish man was physically attacked for racist reasons. State security police were investigating the incident as a case of dangerous bodily harm. No further details are available.

Unidentified perpetrator(s) carried out an arson attack on a house used as a temporary shelter by undocumented migrants. The attack occurred at dawn. The perpetrators firebombed the house, causing an explosion that awakened people living in the area who called the fire department. The fire was quickly extinguished. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

Two men subjected a man to racist abuse before punching him in the face leaving him unconscious. The victim also ended up with a split lip. The attack was said to be "unprovoked assault on a man who was simply doing his job", as the victim was working as a civil enforcement officer. The suspects, aged 24 and 17, came forward to the police after a picture of them was circulated.

A 70-year-old Chechen resident of a refugee home was attacked by two men, aged around 30, near her accommodation. The victim was disabled and used a walker. One of the perpetrators called the victim a "Russian", pulled her hair, hit her twice on the head and kicked her in the hip and knee. He then grabbed her walker, swung it over her head several times and threw it to the ground. Two women who accompanied the victim witnessed the incident. As a racist motive is assumed, the state security police investigated for dangerous bodily harm.

A man kicked an 84-year-old woman, who needed a walking stick, to the ground and attacked a second woman, aged 71. The perpetrator had said: "Sneak back to your homeland! We hate you, we don't want to see you anymore!" before attacking, according to witnesses. The 84-year-old victim was wearing a headscarf and was originally from Turkey. She was kicked to the ground and injured, and had to be taken to the hospital. The other victim was pushed. The perpetrator escaped, despite two witnesses trying to hold him until police arrived.

Two men on a motorcycle approached a gay couple - one an art teacher and the other a Pakistani asylum-seeker. The perpetratos threw a bucket of water on them before they began physically assaulting them with punches and kickcs. A total of twelve to fifteen people joined in on the attack. One of the victims leg was broken in three places. The victims believed they were targeted for their sexuality and the skin colour of one of the victims. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

A man of Sri Lankan origin was hit with a wooden pole in a unprovoked attack. The perpetrator approached the victim while he was loading items into his car. The perpetrator racially abused the man before hitting him over the head with a wooden pole. The perpetrator walked away to a nearby construction site and the victim was taken to the hospital and required stitches.

A 23-year-old man was punched in the face by three neo-Nazis. The victim had previously been attacked by three neo-Nazis some weeks before, an incident that left his friend hospitalized (2014-8-2-a). The victim was sitting at a bar with a friend when they noticed the perpetrators staring at them. According to the victim, the perpetrators began talking among themselves and pointing fingers at him. The perpetrators then approached the victim, with one of them threatening "I'm going to kill you, I really want to." After threatening the victim, the perpetrator slapped the victim twice and threw his cap to the ground. When the victim bent down to pick up his cap, he was suddenly struck with a strong blow to the nose, either a punch or a knee strike. The perpetrators then left the scene. The blow resulted in the victim's nose being broken. The victim believed that this attack was an act of revenge for the previous incident after which the perpetrators had been arrested. The victim also claimed that one of the perpetrators was a member of the neo-Nazi organization Movimiento Social Republicano (MSR), after recognizing the perpetrator in photos on social media where he was giving Nazi salutes alongside the leader of the MSR.

The victim was out walking when he heard someone whispering. He turned around, but could not see anyone. On entering a street, he became aware of a man following him, and when he turned around again, he saw a man running after him with a group of friends. The man uttered racial abuse and threatened the victim to accept a fight. When the victim denied, the perpetrator pushed him on his back causing him to strike a wall. He was then punched in the face. He suffered permanent numbness to parts of his face and a fractured jaw that required three plated and 13 screws.

The victim and his two friends were approached by a man who asked them for a cigarette. After telling him they did not have any cigarettes, the men headed towards their car. The man, who was with a larger group of ten that included several members of Portugal Hammerskins, followed after them with the intent of attacking the victim, thinking he was homosexual. When the three men got in the car, the man who had asked for the cigarette began kicking the driver's door and tried to open it. At the same time, another member of the group jumped on top of the car and started jumping up and down until it cracked the front window. At that point, the victim opened the door and was immediately pulled out into the street. He was stabbed in the face, stomach and chest, and punched and kicked until he fell to the ground.

Unknown perpetrators tried to set fire to a home for asylum seekers. The perpetrators set fire to the entrance area of the building. A piece of furniture was slightly damaged and xenophobic slogans were smeared on the walls of the hallway. Around 70 victims lived in the building at the time.

Six men in black with shaved heads, riding on motorcycles, attacked and beat two Somali immigrants outside their house (modus operandi similar to that of Golden Dawn). According to the victims, they were attacked because they were black. Both victims ended up in the hospital, each requiring ten stitches on their heads. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

A young anti-fascist was attacked by four skinheads. The incident occurred during a heated period in the Tetuán district between far-right and far-left groups, triggered by the occupation of a building by a neo-Nazi group. The attack took place near the squatted building as the victim was distributing leaflets for an anti-fascist event. The perpetrators attacked the victim. The marks on the side of the victim's skull indicated that the perpetrator had been using brass knuckles. A few days before this attack, a Chilean man was beaten up by five skinheads in the same area (case does not meet inclusion criteria).

weapon_description: Beating/kicking, metal chairs, tables and bottles
description: Six men attacked families of Turkish and Portuguese origin at an ice cream café. The perpetrators were on their way from a bachelor party, singing and shouting racists songs and slogans. When a person yelled "fuck off" to them, the perpetrators attacked several people at the café. One of the perpetrators threw metal chairs at the victims and kicked a man of Turkish descent after he had fallen to the ground. They smashed a beer bottle on the head of another victim, hit him and kicked him. The main imitator of the attack was a well-known figure in the regional neo-Nazi scene, who got involved with "Free Nationalists Kraichgau" and then with "Dierechte." He admitted singing right-wing extremist songs, shouting racist slogans ("Ausländer raus", "Deutschland den Deutschen"), repeating the "Hitler salute" and going to the ice cream parlour to humiliate and injure people "with a recognizable migration background." Two of the other perpetrators have no connection to a right-wing milieu according to their defence lawyer. There were five injured, two of which needed hospital treatment, including one of the perpetrators.

A 13-year-old Libyan refugee was first subjected to racist abuse, then beaten and finally strangled by several people in the evening. The victim suffered numerous injuries to his face. The group of attackers consisted of around ten young people and at least one adult. The state security police launched an investigation.

Two men beat a black man unconscious. When the victim walked passed a playground around 11:20 pm and asked the two men to keep the noise level down. They aswered by hurling racial abused and beating and kicking him in the face. A passer-by tried to stop the violence, but the two men kept beating and kicking the victim until he was unconscious. The victim was taken to the hospital for treatment of a fractured eye socket.

A 28-year-old man of Somalian origins was attacked by a 28-year-old drunk man and his two companions. The victim was on a bus with two friends, when the perpetrators insulted them because of their skin color. When the victim left the tram, he was followed by the perpetrators. The main perpetrator knocked the victim to the ground and hit him over the head with a bottle. The victim was taken to the hospital where he received treatment for at least four days. The main perpetrator was arrested.

At nighttime, an asylum seeker was followed from the tram by two young men and two young women. They hit him on the head with a bottle and then kicked him. One of the attackers said "I am racist".  In the same area the following night, a group of around 20 people attacked three asylum seekers with bottles (case does not meet the inclusion criteria due to lack of information).

A Nigerian man was stabbed by two Italian brothers, owners of a nearby fruit and vegetable shop. The attack occurred as the victim was begging for money at the neighborhood market. Swift medical attention prevented potentially severe injuries. The perpetrators were charged with racially aggravated assault due to their history, having committed a similar attack in 2007. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

According to the police, a Somali man was attacked by two individuals of non-German origin for racist reasons. State security police were investigating the incident as a case of dangerous bodily harm. No further details are available.

An asylum seeker was attacked by three men in a culture center and bar. The victim was first subjected to racist abuse and harassment by the perpetrators. The help of other guests prevented anything worse from happening. However, when the victim was alone and met the perpetrators later in the evening, they knocked him to the ground, beat him, and cut his legs. The victim was taken to the hospital for inpatient treatment.

A close friend of a Greek anarchist rapper who was killed by members of Golden Dawn (see CaseID 2013-9-18) was attacked by three men from the far right. The attack took place a few hours after the end of a rally in memory of the rapper, at the spot where he died in Keratsini. The three perpetrators appeared in front of the victim and his companion, and hit the victim repeatedly with a screwdriver, injuring him. The perpetrators also robbed his companion. The victim told the police that the motive of the attack was the perpetrator's hatred for the antifascist rapper's friends and suggested the far right knew the victim had a close friendship with the rapper in the past.

A 28-year-old Pakistani man was brutally beaten and killed by a 17-year-old Italian boy. The victim was walking through the neighborhood, reciting the Quran aloud to mourn a recent family loss, when the assailant approached him on a bicycle with a friend and punched him. After the victim fell to the ground, the attacker repeatedly kicked him in the head. Some residents shouted for the boy to stop, but were met with insults from the boy’s father, who reportedly yelled, "Mind your own business," "I told him to do it," "Go back to the Parioli [a bourgeois neighborhood in Rome]," and called them "ticks" (a derogatory term for leftists). The victim suffered a fatal head hemorrhage as a result of the assault. The perpetrator initially lied to police, claiming that the victim was drunk, had spat at him, and pushed him off his bicycle. He was later sentenced to eight years in prison for voluntary manslaughter, while his father received a ten-year sentence for encouraging the attack.

At a graduation party, a group of right-wing extremists attacked several political opponents and injured at least six people. The incident began when several young people were insulted over the course of the evening, because of their left-wing clothing. One of the victims was beaten so badly in the parking lot of the venue that he had to be taken to hospital with injuries to his spine and face. When his friends came to help him, one of them was hit in the face with a bottle. Two other victims were also injured by the perpetrators outside. When some of the perpetrators forced their way into the building where the party was taking place, they attacked and injured two more victims. The perpetrators shouted slogans like "Free, social and national" and "Shitty Zecke [slur for leftist] pack". According to the police, the perpetrators had already shouted right-wing slogans near the venue before attacking.

A migrant hunt took place in the small locality of Corcolle, near Rome, in which hundreds of residents, many armed with helmets and clubs, blocked the street and attacked migrants returning to nearby welcome centers. At least three men were hospitalized after being assaulted. The violence was allegedly sparked by an earlier incident in which a migrant reportedly disrupted a bus. Witnesses, including center workers, noted that some violent attacks happened in view of a police patrol.

A 23-year-old medical student attacked five people in the streets with a machete and a kitchen knife. Before the attacks, he set his apartment on fire. The first victim was a Peruvian man who received two wounds to his back. The second victim was an Algerian woman stabbed twice in the back. Then he stabbed a man from Lleida in the adbomen before attacking a citizen of Chinese origin, who had to be operated on several wounds in his chest. Lastly, he stabbed a man of Pakistani origi sitting on a bench. The perpetrator did not manage to extract the weapon from the victim, so he left, fleeing the scene. The next day he surrendered himself to the police. Prior to the incident, the perpetrator had established an extreme right group group called Nueva Època. He also had neo-Nazi symbolism on his wall. The perpetrator was also involved in CaseID 2012-12-0.

A shopkeeper was injured in a knife attack. This is the first of two knife attacks on the same day, by the same perpetrator (see caseID 2014-9-23-2). The first attack happened around 7:15 pm when the perpetrator had been brandishing a knife towards the victim during the attack. The victim suffered cuts to his hand and his head as he tried to defend himself in the assault. The perpetrator was sentenced to 8 years of imprisonment in March 2015. The perpetrator allegedly said to the second victim during the attack that he  “wanted to kill a Muslim”. The judge said “Overall, this was an extremely serious series of offences, which involved the appellant repeatedly arming himself with knives which he was prepared to brandish towards vulnerable victims. At least one of the offences was racially aggravated and the victims have suffered lasting psychological harm".

A shopkeeper was injured in a knife attack. This is the first of two knife attacks on the same day, by the same perpetrator (see caseID 2014-9-23-1).  The attack happened around 9pm in the same area as the first attack, but a different store. The perpetrator had retured and brandished two knives during the second attack. The victim tried to grab the knife from the perpetrator, but fell to the floor when he was punched. He suffered injuries to the hands. The perpetrator was sentenced to 8 years of imprisonment in March 2015. The perpetrator allegedly said to the second victim during the attack that he  “wanted to kill a Muslim”.The judge said “Overall, this was an extremely serious series of offences, which involved the appellant repeatedly arming himself with knives which he was prepared to brandish towards vulnerable victims. At least one of the offences was racially aggravated and the victims have suffered lasting psychological harm".

A 50-year-old Pakistani immigrant was attacked by four men, dressed in black and with shaved heads, who had set up a barricade in the street. They attacked the victim with kicks and hit him in the face with brass knuckles. According to eyewitnesses, the perpetrators had shouted at the victim "to leave the country". The victim was taken to the hospital where he received first aid.

The incident began when the victim was falsely accused of stealing £120 from one of the perpetrators on a train. When the victim got off the train, six men followed him, shouted racial abuse and kicked and punched him to the ground. They also struck him over the head with a bottle and a traffic cone as he layed down. Witnesses described how the group referred to the victim as a black b****** and a monkey during the attack. When the perpetrators' phones were investigated by police, they found text messages bragging about the incident like "Kicked f** out of a n*****". All six pleaded guilty to racially aggravated assault.

A Muslim 12-year-old was playing outside when he was set upon by two men who shouted racist abuse. The perpetrators suddenly proceeded to beat the child until his lip was cut and face was swollen. This happened the same week and area where three Asian men were attacked when walking to church and accused of belonging to a terrorist group (the case does not meet the RTV severity inclusion criteria).

Two men were jailed after a near-fatal stabbing of a Chinese takeaway owner, after he tried to stop them from stealing his car. The victim was on his way to make a takeaway delivery, and left his car engine running while picking up something inside. When he saw two people getting in the car and driving away, he followed the car by bike. The car then stopped, and two men came out and stabbed the victim repeatedly. One of the perpetrators admitted the behavior was racially motivated and told the police "I think it's funny - Ch*****s dying everywhere". The perpetrator's brother had some years earlier been sentenced for a killing of another Chinese takeaway driver.

Two young men were seriously injured during a party in Reinshagen on German Unity Day, which spiraled into violence early in the morning. A 24-year-old man suffered severe burns on his back and arms after being thrown onto embers, requiring days of hospitalization, while a 22-year-old sustained a deep neck injury. Witnesses reported the attack followed a political dispute and escalated as the heavily intoxicated perpetrator, a 26-year-old man, assaulted police officers, attempted to damage patrol cars, and performed a Hitler salute while shouting extremist slogans. The suspect, with a blood alcohol level of 2.1 promille, is being investigated for dangerous bodily harm, resisting law enforcement, and using unconstitutional symbols.

An employee in a drinks shop was attacked and injured with a sharp-edged bottle neck by a right-wing extremist. While paying for his drink bottle, the perpetrator loudly uttered "Sieg Heil", whereupon the victim asked him to leave the shop. A verbal argument broke out, after which the perpetrator smashed the glass bottle he had bought and attacked and injured the victim with the sharp-edged bottle neck. The victim was injured but managed to flee. A witness who was present gave the victim first aid and sent him to the hospital.

Two men, aged 25 and 26, threw two Molotov cocktails at a house where 38 refugees, including 18 children, were sleeping inside. The attack caused material damage, but no one got injured as the building did not catch fire. The perpetrators were sentenced to five years in prison for attempted murder motivated by xenophobia.

A 67-year-old man sustained serious facial injuries following what the police calls a racially motivated, unprovoked assault by two men described as white and approximately 30 years old. There is limited information about this case.

A 37-year-old man was attacked by a group of approximately ten individuals in Stadsparken. During the assault, he was threatened with knives, resulting in a stab wound to his left hand. One assailant held a knife to his throat, while another punched and kicked him. The victim believes the attack was motivated by his skin color, as comments made by the assailants suggested racial animosity. After managing to escape, he was transported to Malmö for medical treatment. The case is being investigated as aggravated assault and a hate crime.

A man was attacked by two skinheads, aged 19 and 22, after they spent the day drinking. In the evening, they decided "it would be fun to beat up a homosexual." The perpetrators walked through an area known for homosexual encounters and vandalized a scooter. When the scooter’s owner discovered the damage and called the police, he mistakenly signaled the attackers, thinking they were law enforcement. The perpetrators then attacked him with a baton, knocking him to the ground and repeatedly hitting him. The victim managed to flee but was followed into a parking lot, where he was assaulted again. During the trial, the perpetrators expressed their hostility towards homosexuality, stating they "do not tolerate it."

The perpetrator entered a shop with a knife under his jumper and screamed "you f****** foreigners, coming to the UK to poison the British people". He then stabbed the Turkish shop worker in the neck. The victim was left millimeters from death. The perpetrator was suffering a 'paranoid delusional psychosis' at the time of the attack. He was sentenced to life imprisonment.

A man stabbed a Turkish shopkeeper in the neck with a kitchen knife in an unprovoked attack while shouting “you f*****g foreigners, coming to the UK to poison the British people” at him. The perpetrator shouted abuse at his victim before slashing him in the neck, chin and arm. The victim also suffered an injury to his leg after falling on broken glass. The cut to his neck required 12 stitches. The perpetrator was found guilty of attempted murder and handed a life sentence with a minimum of 10 years in July 2015. The perpetrator was said to be suffering from “paranoid delusional psychosis” at the time of the attack and will remain in a medium-secure mental health unit before moving to prison if treatment is successful.

Two perpetrators, aged 22 and 43, beat a 55-year-old man of Rwandan origin to death in a homeless shelter in which they all lived. One of the perpetrators admitted beating and kicking the victim. Prior to the fatal assault, there had been an argument linked to an accusation that the victim had hit one of the perpetrators' roommate's dog. However, evidence from the perpetrators' phones show that they had photographed eachother in a Nazi salute pose just before the incident. Both the court and the public prosecutor's office assume a xenophobic motive for the murder. A witness who also lived in the house supported the prosecution's assumption that racially insulting statements had been made about the Rwandan victim.

A 29-year-old man was racially insulted and seriously injured before being robbed by three men. The victim was walking alone when he was approached by the perpetrators at around 1:45 AM. The victim was asked by the perpetrators where he was from. When the victim answered that he was born in Syria, he was verbally abused in a racist manner. He was also told to return to his homeland. One of the three attackers twisted the victim's arm behind his back so violently that he suffered a fracture in the elbow area. After the victim fell to the ground, the perpetrators kicked him in the head. The victim was robbed of the money in his wallet and his cell phone. The victim was treated as an inpatient at the hospital. The perpetrators fled.

Over 50 police officers were injured in riots connected to a demonstration organized by the right-wing extremist association “Hooligans gegen Salafisten” (HoGeSa). The march was preceded by a concert by the neo-Nazi band “Kategorie C”. Around 4,800 people took part in the rally that quickly escalated into violence. The perpetrators shouted xenophobic slogans, attacked counterdemonstrators and the police by throwing firecrackers, stones and bottles. A police officer was seriously injured. Journalists and foreign-looking people were insulted, threatened, and pushed. A police car was overturned. The police used water cannons, batons and tear gas in an attempt to regain control. The perpetrators were described as heavily intoxicated and highly aggressive. Around 20 perpetrators were taken into custody. It was reported that the perpetrators were people from all over Germany. The HoGeSa demonstration was registered by a member of the right-wing extremist party "Pro NRW". A spokesperson for the police stated, "There has not been such an escalation of violence in Nordrhein-Westfalen for a long time".

The police arrested four young individuals, one minor and the others aged 19, 20 and 26, after an attack on a 30-year-old anti-fascist. The incident occurred at night while the victim was out having drinks with friends. When the victim stepped outside the bar to smoke, he encountered the perpetrators in the street, and they exchanged a few words. The situation did not escalate initially, as the victim returned to the bar. However, the perpetrators waited for the victim to exit the bar and started the fight. As a result, the victim sustained bruises all over his body and a fractured nasal septum, requiring hospital treatment after the attack. The perpetrators were linked to the Zaragoza Ligallo Fondo Norte club, an extreme right-wing group associated with the Real Zaragoza football team. Some of the perpetrators were of Italian nationality. They were arrested and charged with assault aggravated by ideological motivations.

Four or five men in dark hooded jackets attacked a refugee home with fireworks in the middle of the night. According to a witness, the perpetrators had shouted: "Foreigners out!" And: "We'll kill you! You pigs!" during the attack. One of the perpetrators had a gun and fired it five times into the air. The perpetrators then shot fireworks at the windows. Around 120 refugees were living at the facility at the time, but no one was injured.

A Vietnamese owner of a snack kiosk was bullied and attacked by a group of youths, aged 14 to 16. The day before the incident, the perpetrators had rioted in the kiosk, throwing chairs, destroying flowerpots, made faces and mimicked the Vietnamese wife of the victim, who worked in the kiosk. They also shouted xenophobic slogans. When the perpetrators returned the next day, the victim tried to take photos of them and ran after them to confront them. He was subsequently attacked and suffered a fractured scaphoid bone, an injury to his hand that had to be treated by surgery, as well as bruises and abrasions. He was unable to work for several weeks.

Unknown perpetrators threw several stones at an accommodation for asylum seekers. The perpetrators smashed three windows, including in the kitchen where several of the victims were sitting at the time of the attack. One small and one large stone flew through the room, but no one was hit. The perpetrators fled undetected. A few weeks before the attack, unknown perpetrators hurled white paint at the façade of the building. The next night, people dressed in dark clothes threw stones at the building (case does not meet the inclusion criteria due to lack of information). Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

weapon_description: Bricks, beating/kicking, glass bottles and distress flares
description: Far-right demonstrators attacked police and people of Moroccan origin during a demonstration. 120 000 people marched to protest reforms by the moderate right-wing government. At the same time and place, several hundred people who were assumed to be connected to the far-right gathered. However, they were not there to join the other protesters, but left the protest-route to attack the police. Among them, many wore blue-collar work clothes. Some were recognized as well-known men from the European far-right, one of them a Dutch man with a Hitler tattoo on his neck. For more than two hours, they threw distress flares, bricks and glass bottles at the police, who responded by using tear gas and water cannons. The perpetrators also attacked people of Moroccan origin, who were, according to the media, attacked simply because of their appearance and they had not taken part in the demonstrations. While attacking them with punches, the perpetrators shouted racist insults. At least 111 were injured, around 100 of them police. 24 of the injured were taken to emergency treatment at hospital, some unable to work for weeks. The perpetrators damaged more than 70 vehicles. At least 43 people were arrested.

A German-Turkish family was attacked by two suspected right-wing extremists. The victims, five adults and three children aged 3 to 6, were standing on the sidewalk in the afternoon, when the perpetrators approached them. The perpetrators insulted the victims xenophobically before spraying pepper spray in their faces. The perpetrators also shouted right-wing extremist slogans. Five of the victims, including two of the children, were treated as outpatients at the hospital. The severity threshold in this case is lowered due to the deliberate targeting of children.

A man brutally beat a pregnant woman who worked in a bakery, when she refused to serve him a sandwich early in the morning before opening hours. The perpetrator pushed, shook and threw the victim against a wall, while he yelled and threw racist insults at her, such as "you go back to your country or I send you to your country in a box". The victim was of Argentine origin. The beatings caused the victim, who was five months pregnant, to lose the baby.

A young man was attacked with a knife by a right-wing extremist because of his political views. The perpetrator tried to stab the victim several times, but he was able to dodge the blows and alerted passers-by. The perpetrator then fled.

A 17-year-old man was attacked by several individuals in the park. The incident happened at nighttime. The victim was ambushed by the perpetrators, who called him a “Shitty Jew” and “Communist” and sprayed him with pepper spray. The perpetrators beat and kicked the victim before stealing his phone. The victims suffered severe injuries that had to be treated in the hospital for several days.

Two men with an Eastern European accent attacked two young Cameroonian men and a 21-year-old Italian man who intervened. The victims were on their way home when they heard the perpetrators shout racial slurs: "N******, you two n******, pieces of s***." The intervener, a friend of the victims, confronted the perpetrators, saying, "They are friends of mine, how dare you insult them? You’re also foreigners, would you like to be treated like this?" In response, one of the perpetrators punched him in the face, causing him to fall to the ground. The intervener suffered a broken nose, while the victims, who were also assaulted, sustained minor injuries and bruises.

Supporters of the left-wing football club Asd Ardita were attacked during a match by a group of 40 neo-fascists. The victims were cheering for their team when the perpetrators arrived, armed with wooden sticks and iron bars, and began assaulting them. One victim recognized the attackers as being linked to the far-right scene. The attack lasted only a few minutes before the perpetrators fled. Six victims were injured, including one with a serious head injury and three with broken arms. Nine perpetrators were arrested, some of whom were connected to far-right supporter groups of the Viterbese football club. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

An unknown perpetrator set fire to a tent in a camping area for EU migrants. A 54-year-old man slept in the respective tent at the time, receiving burns to his legs. He was later taken to hospital. The police suspect hate crime and arson. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

Two asylum seekers, one Syrian and one Kenyan, were assaulted by a neo-Nazi at a fast-food restaurant. The perpetrator initially directed racist insults at the Kenyan individual. When the Syrian intervened, he was also subjected to racist insults and threats. The perpetrator then punched the Syrian in the face, causing him to lose consciousness and fall to the ground. The victim required medical treatment at the hospital.

Two brothers and a third man seriously injured an 18-year-old asylum seeker from Mali with an emergency hammer, beatings and kicking on a train from Straubing to Niederlindhart. They also insulted the victim. The perpetrators pulled the victim's jacket over his head and beat and kicked the 18-year-old. One of the brothers also struck twice with an emergency hammer. The victim was hospitalized. The three perpetrators denied a racist motive and claimed they were under the influence of drugs. The representative of the  prosecution however is convinced that the attackers acted for racist motives. Above all, the older brother has an "unbearably hostile attitude towards foreigners," said one of the lawyers.

Participants of an anti-racist demonstration were verbally abused at a tram stop on their way home. The perpetrator smashed a bottle on one of the victims’ heads. The Berlin district of Treptow-Köpenick had had an open neo-Nazi scene for years, and there was a documented increase in right-wing motivated crimes in the area at the time of the attack.

A 36-year-old man of Turkish origins and his 31-year-old German girlfriend were ambushed and brutally beaten by four suspected right-wing extremists. The victims had been on a market in the evening and were going back to their car. The perpetrators approached the victims and insulted them with racist slogans and called the girlfriend a "German whore" who is "messing around with a Turk". The male victim was knocked down with a glass bottle from behind. The perpetrators kicked the victim while he was laying on the ground and dragged him along the ground by his jacket. The female victim was knocked down by a punch to the ear and held down while being kicked several times. The victims suffered numerous bruises, a concussion among other injuries. The male victim lost a tooth. The victims fled by car to a doctor and received medical treatment.

Three rugby players were injured during a fight after one of them was Islamophobically insulted. Around twelve people were involved in the fight outside a bar. The incident began when one of the victims, who had dark skin and a full beard, was assaulted as “Salafist”. A few months before the attack, there had been massive violent demonstrations against Salafists mobilizing right-wing extremists and hooligans. Two of the victims had to be taken to the emergency room and treated for facial injuries. The perpetrators fled. The police initiated an investigation for assault.

A Nigerian woman was beaten by a 43-year-old man who said he hated "n*****s" and told her wanted to kill all Black people. The victim was waiting in line to cash cheques at an exchange bureau with a friend, when the perpetrator told them to hurry up, while also saying things like "You fucking blacks, just go back to your country." The victim initially put up with the racial insults and told him to calm down. The perpetrator continued a tirade of racial slurs and said he wanted to "shoot them" and "kill them all." An argument erupted between the perpetrator and the victim. During the argument, the perpetrator assaulted the victim, punching out two teeth in the process. A third tooth had to be removed later as a result of the assault. When the police arrived, the perpetrator was found standing over the victim, punching her in the face. A police officer told in court that she saw a lot of blood and a couple of teeth on the ground. The perpetrator was charged with grievously injuring the victim, as well as inciting racial hatred and to breaching public peace.

A 15-year-old Somali boy was stabbed outside his asylum seeker accommodation by a 24-year-old autistic male who reportedly suffered from psychotic delusions. The victim was seriously injured and had to receive more than a hundred stitches in the hospital. A selfie was found on the perpetrator's cell phone showing a swastika on his arm. His concerned mother also explained that she had heard her son talk about "wanting to stab a n****". According to the mother and a neighbor, the perpetrator often spoke negatively about dark-skinned people. However, the perpetrator himself said that he had previously been threatened by a black man and when he encountered the victim, he mistakenly believed he was the one he had been threatened by. The perpetrator was sentenced to psychiatric treatment (TBS).

weapon_description: Six weapons, including a sawed off shotgun, AG-3 and Uzi submachine guns
description: The police conducted several razzias against right-wing extremists, seizing illegal automatic weapons, 2kgs hash, 30 g amphetamine and nationalistic propoganda. Six weapons were confiscated, including a sawed off shotgun, AG-3 and Uzi submachine guns. The men were aged from below 20 to 40 years and were connected to Norske Motstands Bevegelsen [Norwegian Resistance Movement]. Several of the weapons had a NMB-sticker on them.

Two women from Gambia, aged 28 and 37, were unprovokedly attacked by a 21-year-old man shouting derogatory comments about their skin color. The perpetrator is first said to have grabbed the younger victim by the hair. When the older victim intervened, the perpetrator grabbed her, pushed her to the ground and kicked her with his steel-capped shoes. During the attack, the perpetrator continued his insults. He attempted to kick one of the women in the head, but missed. The attack stopped when a passer-by intervened. The perpetrator had several other convictions, among them assault and threats to other African women, and for doing Hitler-salutes. He was sentenced to three years in prison.

weapon_description: Plans included bomb attacks and they had acquired unspecified weapons
description: The police arrested 14 people belonging to the clandestine group 'Avanguardia ordinovista' suspected of planning attacks on institutional targets and the public. The group planned a 'double track' in which they would carry out bomb attacks throughout the country with the aim of destabilizing public order and at the same time work to promote their own party. The group aimed to kill unescorted politicians, magistrates, members of the police, carry out attacks on police headquarters and kill the prime minister. They had recovered some buried weapons after World War II and bought further weapons from Slovenia. The leader, a 48-year-old man, was a former policeman. The group was based on the banned banned New Order far-right group and included one of their former members. The arrests took place in L'Aquila, Montesilvano, Chieti, Ascoli Piceno, Milan, Turin, Gorizia, Padua, Udine, La Spezia, Venice, Naples, Rome, Varese, Como, Modena, Palermo and Pavia.

The perpetrator approached the victim, whom he did not know, outside a pub to ask for a cigarette. When the victim, a young Saharawi, denied the perpetrator a cigarette, he insulted the victim saying "shitty Moor" and attacked him with a piece of glass from behind. The glass broke in the victim's eye, causing the victim to have to undergo surgery to implant an intraocular lens in the right eye, and his vision was severely reduced. The perpetrator was sentenced to nine years in prison. The perpetrator, however, denied that the attack was due to racism, and argued the incidence was a case of "bad luck" in which he was drunk and a door opened that caused him to "accidentally" hit the victim with a glass.

Two African men, aged 26 and 34, were attacked by a group of five men outside a discotheque around 5 AM. The perpetrators approached the victims with racist insults, questioning their presence and asking when they would go home. One victim was struck in the back, prompting a witness from the discotheque to intervene. As the victims made their way home, they were followed by the group. The 34-year-old was punched to the ground, repeatedly kicked, and struck on the head with a beer glass, resulting in a laceration that required hospital treatment. Police suspect the attack was motivated by xenophobia.

After a series of attacks in Freital, the police conducted a search against five individuals. The police found several hundred fireworks, similar to those used in the previous attacks. Three people had previosly been arrested and they were referred to as the Freital Group by the authorities, consisting of seven men and one woman. They were put on trial in March 2017 for the involvement in five bomb attacks against refugee centres, offices belonging to left-wing politicians and the car of a left-wing leader in the small town of Freital in 2015 and accussed of planning more attacks (See Case ID's 2015-10-19, 2015-11-1, 2015-9-19- The other two attacks were against material targets). The group was categorized as a terrorist organization during trial, and was charged with forming a terrorist organization. The members initially met during a demonstration against the Leonardo Hotel, which was designated as a temporary refugee home, sparking demonstrations and attacks in Freital. The leader of the group was known to participate in neo-nazi marches, worked as a bus driver in Freital and had created a group called FTL/360 on Facebook after two Moroccans were accused of molesting school children on bus route 360 to Dresden. The FB group gained 2,600 followers by November 2015.  "The aim of this group was to carry out bomb attacks on asylum-seeker shelters, as well as on the apartments, offices and vehicles of those with differing political views," federal prosecutors said in a statement released in November 2016. "In this way the accused wanted to create a climate of fear and repression."

A family of six from Turkey celebrated New Year's Eve in their kebab shop when four people - two 24- and 26-year-old brothers and the mother and wife of the younger one - interrupted them. The perpetrators first knocked on the door to the shop and shouted racial slurs, but the victims asked them to leave. The group then left, but returned again, shouting more racist slogans like "Shitty Turks". One of the perpetrators then smashed the windows with a combat knife, while one of the others pulled out a blank gun. One of the victims was stabbed in the arm by the 24-year-old perpetrator and subsequently hospitalized.

Unknown perpetrators threw smoke bombs into an asylum seeker's home. Due to the heavy smoke development, two people with smoke gas poisoning had to be hospitalized. Schleswig-Holstein's SPD leader blamed the "Pegida" movement for the smoke bomb attack, but the perpetrators remain unknown. Motive not expicitly stated but sufficiently evident to be included.

A 46-year-old man was taken to hospital suffering from a stab wound to his leg following an assault by the 17-year-old perpetrator. The perpetrator was charged with racially aggravated grevious bodily harm and possession of an offensive weapon. There is limited detailed information about this case.

A Chinese woman and her two-year-old child were in their house when a masked person hurled a petrol bomb at their window. The petrol bomb failed to ignite. It was one of three hate crimes in South Belfast in a three-day period, where windows were smashed and graffiti stating "scum out locals only" was scrawled on doors at different homes. Police investigated it as a hate crime. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

A 25-year-old man armed with a machete and a hammer shouted ‘white power’ and 'this is for Lee Rugby' as he attacked an Asian shopper inside a Tesco. The victim, a 24-year-old Sikh man, suffered what police described as 'life-changing injuries', but was saved by a soldier who intervened to stop the attack. The perpetrator told police: 'It did not matter to me what religion he was, it was his racial appearance.' In a police interview read to the court, the perpetrator stated: 'Rising Jihadi violence, most recently in France, the rise of Isis in the Middle East, and what happened to [name of British soldier] – it was like Europe was under siege. My personal issues and paranoia and political world events all combined.' The perpetrator had posted an image of himself in a balaclava with a large knife and the flag of the far-right group National Action hours before he carried out his violent racist attack. He had built up relationships online with members of the group, sharing childish and offensive far-right images. He had a YouTube channel filled with neo-Nazi videos. There were unconfirmed reports that he had been in the Army.

Two members of the Greek Anticapitalist Left were severely beaten up by a group of 10-15 people who arrived on motorcycles and wore black clothes, camouflage pants, helmets and motorcycle gloves, outside a polling station. The victims were beaten and kicked, also with helmets. The victims' statements to the police led to the arrest of two Golden Dawn members.  Trying to deny their involvement in the incident, the perpetrators told the police that they were at the incident as "observers" for the Golden Dawn for the election process. One of the perpetrators died before the trial, while the other was sentenced to 20 months in prison with a three-year suspension.

weapon_description: A ring or a knuckle duster and beating/kicking
description: [Potential revenge attack after the Islamist January 7 Charlie Hebdo attacks] A 32-year-old man was racially insulted and beaten up when picking up breakfast for his children. Two young people approached the victim and unprovokedly grabbed him by his hoodie, and then beat him up, leaving him in need of eight stitches in the face. The injury was most likely caused by a ring or a knuckle duster. The incident occured about two weeks after the Charlie Hebdo attacks.

A Moroccan 34-year-old became a victim of a racist assault in a train station when the 24-year-old perpetrator, a well-known right-wing extremist, kicked him with combat boots. The victim fell on his back after the kick in the chest and hit the back of his head on a concrete base. An alerted ambulance and paramedics took care of the bleeding and unconscious victim on the platform before he was hospitalized. Three witnesses confirmed that there had been no provocations leading up to the incident and that there was no apprent reason for the attack.

Around sixty people from CasaPound attacked a left-wing social center, leaving one person in coma after he was struck in the head with an iron bar. When the person fell to the ground, the perpetrators continued to beat him with kicks in the head until the people at the centre managed to drag him inside and close the door.

A 37-year-old man set fire to a group of scooters parked in the hallway of a building in which ten African men with residence permits lived. Four of the victims ended up in the hospital due to  heavy smoke intoxication. The perpetrator admitted a racist motive to the police, but clarified he only intended to damage the scooters and not the entire building.

About a dozen unknown people attacked migrants who were sleeping in a van. The perpetrators threw stones through the windows of the car, which hit one woman at the back of her head. They then got a number of people out of the car and attacked them with beatings and kicking, one of which needed hospital treatment. The bus was used by the victims, all Romas, to sleep in - as they are "beggers" in Sweden. The attack stopped when a security guard drove past them in a car, shouting at the perpetrators.

An unknown man followed a 12-year-old Turkish girl who was walking home from school. While carrying a banner with xenophobic slogans, he started speaking to the girl and then punched her in the face with his fist. The girl complained of pain following the punch.

Seven masked people attacked three refugees at a bus station with clubs while shouting racist insults. One of the victims was injured so badly that he had to be taken to the hospital. Charges were brought against five of the attackers, aged 17 to 19, half a year later.

18 PSP agents (police officers) were accused of torture, kidnapping, physical injury, and offense to qualified physical integrity, aggravated by hatred and racial discrimination against a group of youths of African descent.
