The police found a USB thumb in his room with folders named "Boogaloo", in reference to "race war", containing guides on constructing a shotgun, homemade plastic explosives, and conducting arson attacks. The perpetrator had also expressed online that minorities should be shot. The police arrested him after receiving a tip, due to concerns about his threat to innocent lives.

A 17-year-old and an 18-year-old were attacked by a man aged between 35 and 45. The attack took place on a subway train, after the perpetrator allegedly was disturbed by the victims' phone usage. He racially insulted one of the victims and headbutted him, he then stabbed the other victim with a knife. The victims fled the train at the following station. The victim of the stabbing was hospitalised in serious conditions.

A 32-year-old man with links to the Nordic Resistance Movement killed a 64-year-old woman, the psychiatry coordinator for the Swedish Association of Local Authorities and Regions (SKR). The perpetrator stabbed the victim to death in front of numerous witnesses during the Almedals Week, an annual event that Swedish politicians attend. The perpetrator was arrested and, according to the prosecutor, was planning of committing more murders, including that of the leader of the Centre Party, Annie Lööf. The perpetrator participated in Nordic Resistance Movement demonstrations in the past and called himself in his own notebook "Swedish Breivik". The perpetrator claimed he attacked the victim because she was an easier target than politicians, who have bodyguards, and that he chose to attack at the event to symbolically "attack the whole society". According to the forensic psychiatric evaluation the perpetrator suffered from severe mental illness during and after the attack and he was therefore sentenced to psychiatric treatment instead of prison.

A 13-year-old boy was attacked by an unknown man, aged between 20 and 25. The victim was traveling by tram together with his German ethnic girlfriend. When the victim said goodbye to his girlfriend and walked off the tram, the perpetrator fallowed him and told him to "keep his hands off German girls" and hit him. The victim tried to flee but fell on the ground. He was followed by the perpetrator who kicked him in the head several times while he was laying on the ground. An ambulance that was passing by rescued the victim. The victim was hospitalized.

A 49-year-old SPD local politician was racially insulted and attacked in front of his house by a 35-year-old man and a 39-year-old woman. The perpetrators first insulted the victim in a xenophobic manner, saying "Shit Kanake [slur referring the people of Middle Eastern origin], shit Turk". The male perpetrator then suddenly headbutted the victim. They then fled. The victim suffered from a double broken nose.

Four adults and two children were subjected to an arson attack by unknown perpetrator(s). The victims were asleep when the perperator(s) placed a tire in front of the door and set it alight. One of the victims smelled smoke and the family was able to escape through the back door. Substantial damage was caused to the front door and hallway while other smoke damage was caused throughout the house. The police is treating the incident as a racially motivated hate crime. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

A 37-year-old woman launched a racially motivated attack on a pizza delivery man, threatening to kill him. The incident began when the victim overheard the woman talking to his supervisor and asked, "Excuse me, are you talking to me?" The woman responded with racist remarks, calling him a "bloody foreigner" and insisting he wasn’t Irish, despite his claim of being born there. She then pushed him, shouting, "Don’t come near me, you P***." When the victim pushed back, she violently attacked him, punching, kicking, and biting his leg. After the initial assault, the woman got into her car and drove toward the victim in a threatening manner, forcing him to jump back and fall to the ground. She then circled back, again driving at him aggressively and shouting that she would kill him if she knew where he lived, promising to return. The victim required medical treatment and continued to suffer shoulder pain over a year after the attack.

A boy aged between 11 and 14 was hit over the head with a bottle by a man on a bus. The perpetrator made racist comment to the victim and his mum before trying to link arms with the boy and hit him on the head with a bottle. The child was not severely injured. The police has not been able to identify the perpetrator.

A Nigerian man and his friends were attacked by the bouncers of a popular club. The victim had a VIP table booked at the club, but when he and his friends arrived at the entrance, the bouncers told him that "This is not a black club". They were then beaten up. The victim ended up with a double fracture to the jaw and two broken teeth.

A 23-year-old migrant farm worker was brutally beaten by an "organized group of nationalists", numbering six to seven people. The victim was surrounded by the perpetrators, who asked "Where are you from?" Upon replying "Muslim Pakistan", the group immediately started beating him, including with brass knuckles, threw him on the ground and kicked him. He was hospitalised with injuries including on the shoulder, on the knee and on the head, which required stitches.

weapon_description: Components for making explosives, weapons and ammunition
description: A 25-year-old man linked to the far-right was sentenced to 3 years and 6 months in prison after components for making explosives, weapons and ammunition were found in his residence. He was acquitted of suspicions regarding preparation for public destruction, as the district court could not prove that the man had a concrete plan to detonate a bomb in a specific area.

A 47-year-old man stabbed a younger Moroccan man, leading to charges of attempted murder aggravated by racial hatred. The incident occurred at a bar where the victim was socializing with friends. The perpetrator, also at the bar, became irritated by the noise and verbally attacked the victim with racial slurs, saying, "Moroccan f***, go home, it's always you who makes a mess." Later, as the victim entered the bar, the perpetrator followed him and attacked with a switchblade, stabbing him five times in the back, forearm, and chest. Bystanders intervened, preventing further harm. The victim was rushed to the hospital in critical condition. The perpetrator was sentenced to eight years and eight months in prison.

A 27-year-old pregnant woman, wearing a scarf, was insulted and attacked by a 20-year-old man in a bus. The perpetrator insulted and showed her the middle finger while on the upper deck of the bus. The victim moved downstairs, where the perpetrator followed her. He spat on her face, held her head, slapped her on the shoulder, kneed her on the stomach, and tried to rip off her scarf. People intervened and stopped the perpetrator. The victim was hospitalised.

A 20-year-old neo-Nazi set fire to the basement of a building that housed immigrants, before distributing threatening letters to the authorities in the area. A local politician from CDU received a handwritten letter reading "Stop Islamization" if the demand were not met the perpetrator stated that "Berlin will continue to burn" and "Have fun extinguishing". In addition, the letter read: "We are in possession of weapons of war", "This is a declaration of war on the state!" and "Civilians will die in the next attack". No one was injured in the attack, but the property damage was serious. A former classmate of the perpetrator pointed him out for the investigators. According to the former friend, the perpetrator conducted the arson attack because he thought too many foreigners lived there. The perpetrator was a Facebook member of the group "NSD Family: Neuer Deutscher Standard". He was charged with aggravated arson, disturbing public peace and using anti-constitutional signs.

weapon_description: Three handmade and not fully functional pipe bombs, axe, air pistol
description: The police searched the house of a 62-year-old Reichsbürger on suspicion of illegally growing drugs. The perpetrator met the police armed with an axe and threatened with a shootout. The perpetrator was disarmed. The police found three homemade and not yet functional pipe bombs, an air pistol, and 13 cannabis plants in the home of the perpetrator. The perpetrator had an obvious affiliation with the Reichsbürger movement. He had documents hanging on his front door reading the "Laws and Regulations of the Military Government of Germany". A sign in the garden had the inscription "German Reich". The public prosecutor's office did not arrest the perpetrator at the time. Seven months after the raid, the police searched the house of the perpetrator again, leading to his arrest (see caseID 2023-4-18).

Three men of Brazilian and Venezuelan origin were physically assaulted at a nightclub by security guards. While other groups were dancing and singing, the security guards asked the victims to shut up in an aggressive tone. Right after, the victims were violently removed from the disco. They were kicked and one of them kept being beaten to the ground on the sidewalk by the nightclub. He received hits in the head and ended up fainting. The perpetrators continued to strike him with kicks and beatings on the back, face and head. One of the three victims was severely injured and required two surgeries and several days at the hospital. Another required an eye surgery. The perpetrators had a previously known history of xenophobia and according to the victims, "there was xenophobia from the moment they started singing Latin songs."

A 69-year-old man's house was raided by police, where they found an arsenal of weapons and ammunition. The perpetrator, a former soldier, had already been convicted of arms smuggling for the mafia in Italy. The perpetrator wrote letters full of hate for state instutions and political representatives at that time, and the police found extreme-right material at his house, including swastikas and Nazi devotional items. The man accumulated the weapons during his time as a soldier by diverting dismissed Bundeswehr weapons that he was supposed to destroy. The day after the raid, the perpetrator committed suicide either with a gun or with explosives in a bunker in the forest.

A 7-year-old girl was injured by two men, aged 34 and 40. The two perpetrators were shouting xenophobic slogans at children and families at a park. The parents of the children confronted them. During the confrontation, the perpetrators threw a glass bottle and hit the victim, who was severely injured.

Two teenagers were attacked by a man. The victims were assaulted with an unknown weapon and had to be treated in the hospital after sustaining head injuries. The police treats the incident as a racially motivated hate attack, which was "completely unprovoked."

Unknown perpetrators threw incendiary devices at a refugee accomodation during night, and a small fire ensued. Security guards managed to extinguish the fire quickly and not a lot of damage was reported. 180 refugees were hosted in the facility, but it is not clear how many were inside. Security protocols on the weekend and at night were reduced, so the attack could have had much more severe consequences. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

A 33-year-old man from Eritrea narrowly escaped death after a violent attack by a 32-year-old German man. The two men encountered each other on the street in the early morning hours, where a verbal dispute quickly escalated. The perpetrator physically attacked the victim, choking him until he lost consciousness, among other injuries. The investigating authorities identified xenophobia as one of several motives behind the attack, and the incident was officially classified as being driven by right-wing extremism. As a result, an arrest warrant was issued against the perpetrator for attempted murder and dangerous bodily harm.

A 45-year-old migrant from Pakistan working as a food delivery man was brutally attacked by four men. The victim was on sick leave, and left his home to go to a kiosk on the street to get some refreshments. The perpetrators, on motorbikes, spotted him and moved aggressively towards him. Two of the perpetrator took some clubs lying nearby, and shouted "what are you doing here? Go away!" Then, they beat him up brutally with punches, kicks and with the clubs. During the beating, one of the perpetrators said "You soft black, we are going to f*** you". The beating stopped when police arrived. The victim was hospitalised and received multiple stitches to the head. Police officers tried to get the victim not to sue the perpetrators.

A 22-year-old man of North-African descent was attacked by a group linked to the right-wing association Action Française at a bar. While the victim was with his friends, around 15 individuals wearing Action Française-branded t-shirts and caps arrived, singing military songs and directing their attention towards the victim. After some time, the victim asked them to stop, which led to a confrontation. He was subjected to racial insults, including being told "you are not French" and "your grandfather is a terrorist." Five to six perpetrators then physically attacked the victim, kicking and punching him, dragging him to the ground, and hitting his head against the cobblestones. The victim, the only black person in his group, suffered hematomas, bruising, and abrasions to his face and was hospitalized. Only one perpetrator was brought to court and received a one-year suspended sentence.

A 51-year-old black woman was stabbed by a 38-year-old woman. The perpetrator was drunk, drugged, and self-harmed. A friend of hers was bringing her to the doctor, when the perpetrator saw the victim on the street. She took a 19cm long knife out of her pocket, shouted "I do not like blacks" and lunged at the victim, aiming for the neck. The victim was injured with a superficial 6cm cut on the neck, avoiding a deadly wound by about 1cm. She was hospitalised. A psychiatrist assessed the perpetrator as fit to stand trial and as sane.

A 19-year-old was arrested at his parents' home by the police, suspected of preparations for a violent action. He had tried to obtain weapons and recipes to produce explosives. The attack plot was still in its early stages and no target was chosen yet. The perpetrator had shared anti-Semitic and racist posts and messages online, and claimed being part of the accelerationist movement - a movement trying to spark chaos and a racial war between blacks and whites. The police was alerted by a friend of the perpetrator, a soldier who lived in the vicinity, who one day did could not find his service weapon and alerted the police thinking the perpetrator must have gotten it.

A 53-year-old man was sentenced to 28 years in prison for the attempted murder of a 24-year-old Muslim doorman after cutting his throat with a razor, millimeters from having a fatal outcome. The perpetrator had been drinking at a bar before the incident. Initially, he became aggressive towards customers, prompting two security staff members, one of whom was the victim, to intervene and warn him. Then, the perpetrator made anti-Muslim remarks directed at the victim. Half an hour later, a group of women reported the perpetrator's harassment, leading to another intervention by the security guards, where the perpetrator again made anti-Muslim remarks. Following this altercation, the perpetrator threw a drink at the victim, flicked a cigarette at him, and issued death threats before being kicked out of the bar. Later that evening, the perpetrator returned to the bar wearing a hood and immediately targeted the victim. Using a razor, he slashed the victim's neck, causing a severe wound that required urgent medical attention to prevent loss of life. During the court proceedings, the judge highlighted the incident's significant and disturbing anti-Muslim undertone. Charges against the perpetrator included attempted murder and racially aggravated harassment.

Two blonde perpetrators in sweatpants, aged between 20 and 30, attacked a 33-year-old Jewish man. The vicitm was traveling by train when the perpetrator approced him with antisemitic insults and started beating him to the head and upper body. Another passenger intervened and stopped the attack. The victim suffered several head injuries. The police managed to idetify one of the perpetrators. The state police investigated the incident as dangerous bodily harm, insult and incitement to hatred.

weapon_description: Firearms, including an AK-47, AR-15 assault rifles and other semi-automatic guns, thousands of rounds of ammunition, 3D printing equipment used for making firearms, document detailing bomb-making
description: Four right-wing extremists, all men in their 30s, were arrested on suspicion of plotting terrorist attacks targeting public and government institutions and suspected to be connected to Nordic right-wing extremist groups. Police had been investigating the perpetrators for weeks. During the investigations, they found "fanatical propaganda", some of which glorified the neo-Nazi terrorist Anders Breivik (CaseID 2011-7-22) along with other like-minded extremists. Only two of the four men remained in custody. The police seized a significant quantity of firearms, including AK-47 and AR-15 assault rifles and other semi-1utomatic weapons, as well as 3D-printed ones, document detailing bomb-making and thousands of rounds of ammunition. The targets included the parliament and police, more specifically, a planned attack against Iceland's annual police party of October 1st. The perpetrators showed hate towards homosexuals, Jews, foreigners, communists and the police. The perpetrators talked about targeting the Althingi Parliament, Reykjavík police station, Sólveig Anna Jónsdóttir, chairman of Efling trade union and member of the Socialist Party, Gunnar Smári Egilsson, leader of the Socialist Party, and driving into the the LGBTQ+ parade in Reykjavík. While they named specific targets, their communications indicate that they were interested in committing mass murder in general rather than planning a specific attack. In court, one perpetrator was accused of planning to commit a terrorist act and the other for inciting him and aiding him in the production of weapons. The plot is suspected to have been inspired by the atrocities of Anders Behring Breivik, who massacred 77 young political activists in Norway in 2011.

A young black man was stabbed by a group of neo-Nazis. When the victim was walking with his girlfriend, a group of neo-Nazis passed by and started targeting him for his skin colour. The perpetrators then stabbed the victim. The victim was severely injured and later hospitalized. The crime was treated as both attempted homicide and hate crime. The investigations confirmed that the detainees were related to Nazi ideology but no specific group name was given.

weapon_description: 100 firearms and a large quantity of ammunition
description: Police searched a dozen houses and arrested six people, linked to the extreme right milieu. In one search, there was a shootout between the perpetrator, a 36-year-old man, and the police that resulted in the death of the perpetrator. He shared "sovereign citizen" content on social media, a far right anti-government movement akin to the Reichsbürger movement in Germany. Police found over 100 weapons and a very large quantity of ammunition as well as bulletproof vests, night vision goggles and thermal vision goggles. Police suspects that the group "wanted to set up an armed resistance against the government". There was no concrete attack plot.

weapon_description: Parts of a 3D printed semi-automatic firearm
description: A 14-year-old boy was arrested as he was planning to carry out a terror attack based on right-wing extremist motives. The perpetrator wanted to attack a synagogue and/or a mosque in a nearby town and/or an asylum centre somewhere in the Netherlands. The perpetrator stated that he had an extreme right wing ideology. He had online conversations, including through Telegram and Signal, where he talked about the planning of the attacks. He approached people via email to obtain Glock handguns, firearms, and ammunition. He watched instructional videos on how to make bombs (IEDs and molotov cocktails) and 3D printed parts (lower receiver, trigger device/fire regulator/cocking handle/cartridge ejector) for a FGC-9 MKII, a semi-automatic carbine. He was sentenced to 120 days in juvenile detention and two years probation.

A 35-year-old Spanish man with SS-Nazi tattoos stabbed a Moroccan man. The perpetrator was later arrested for attempted homicide and hate crime. The attack was triggered by an argument the perpetrator had with the victim that same morning. The perpetrator was already known to the police for a previous similar xenophobic stabbing on 16 January 2022. However, there is too little information about this case to include it in the RTV dataset at this point (2022). The perpetrator admitted to the police that the motive behind the attack was xenophobic.

A group of 22 migrants, among which three handcuffed and four injured, were found on a mountain by an MSF team. The victims arrived on the island illegally and were approached by a group of seven or eight people, saying they were doctors and that they had food. The perpetrators, not from MSF, started beating them and handcuffing them, but ran away when the MSF team was approaching. The victims were hospitalised. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included. Similar events took place in other Greek islands, but they were excluded from the RTV dataset due to limited information.

Two victims were attacked by two Nordic Resistance Movement (NRM) activists. A 16-year-old girl was punched, and a 21-year-old man was hit and had his leg broken. The Helsingborg district court sentenced the two representatives of NRM for assault during the election weekend in Örkelljunga, Scania. The beating happened when the NRM-members were out to check that their election posters were still up. In that context, they found the 16-year-old girl taking down the NRM posters. During the beating, one of the men was wearing boxing gloves. One of the perpetrators was also involved in a similar attack in the same city only weeks before (CaseID 2022-9-4), and in another case in 2019, in which counter-demonstrators and a freelance journalist was attacked (2019-6-1).

Two women were attacked by three unknown white men, most likely aged between 30 and 50. The victims were at a shop around 3 am when the group of men approached them and started to verbally abuse them with homophobic and racist comments. After leaving the shop, the victims were followed by the men, continuing their abuse. The victims then confronted the men, resulting in both victims being punched and knocked unconscious. The police are investigating this as a homophobic and racial assault.

A 66-year-old man tried to burn down a migration centre by throwing two or three petrol bombs with fireworks attached at the facility. A large ammount of immigrants were waiting outside or staying inside the building when the attack happened. 700 migrants were evacuated and two of the staff members suffered minor injuries after the incident. Minutes after the attack, the perpetrator killed himself in his car. The perpetrator was identified as a man who lived two-three hours away from the crime scene. He had been observed the night before around the car park of the migrant centre. The police said the firebombing was motivated by extreme right-wing ideology because the perpetrator had expressed anti-Muslim setiments in social media, eg. that he planned to “obliterate Muslim children” just an hour before the attack.

A 21-year-old Moroccan man and an 18-year-old Albanian woman were attacked by the Albanian woman's family. The family opposed their relationship, arguing that the man was a "lazy Moroccan" and not of a high enough social status. They had threatened her multiple times prior to the attack, warning that "you don't have to stay with that African, we don't want to see you with him anymore, if we meet you together we'll break his head and send you back to Albania." When the family saw the couple together in the city, at least ten people attacked them and beat them up, also using metal bars and bottles. They also threatened to use a knife. After the attack, the Albanian woman was sent back to Albania.

A 63-year-old carpenter killed a 41-year-old Peruvian man using a bow and an arrow. The victim was watching a football match with a friend and celebrated the birth of his second son in a bar near his house. The perpetrator first shouted at them from the window of his apartment to stop talking loudly, before racially insulting them with phrases like "go away dirty immigrants, dirty foreigners". He then grabbed his bow and arrow and shot from the window, hitting the victim on his side. After the shot, the perpetrathor shouted "I told you." Thereafter, the perpetrator went down to the victim and tried to remove the arrow from his body, making his situation worse by doing so. The victim died later at the hospital. The perpetrator had 30 arrows and 3 bows that he made himself.

A 20-year-old Italian woman of Senegalese origin was punched in the face and stabbed by an unknown man, aged between 25 and 30. The victim was with a friend at a pub at 23:30. Sitting outside, she overheared the perpetrator talking about her, referring to her as "little n*****", "these dirty n******", and talking about concentration camps. When the victim and the friend went to smoke a sigarette, the perpetrator followed them. When bumping into her, the victim confronted him and asked what he was doing, to which he replied "You must shut up, dirty n*****". He then punched her on the face and stabbed her using an utility knife, fortunately hitting her only with the very end of the knife. Two customers intervened and managed to stop the attack, but the perpetrator was able to flee. The victim had to go to the hospital.

weapon_description: Iron bars, wooden sticks and flares
description: Members of Los Casuals, the most violent faction of the far-right football club Boixos Nois, launched a premeditated attack on Indar Gorri, a far-left football club. The incident occurred at an establishment where Indar Gorri supporters typically gathered before matches. Armed with iron bars, wooden sticks, and flares, the attackers caused serious injuries to several victims, including one who suffered fractures to the nasal septum and cheekbones. The perpetrators, some of whom had traveled from other parts of Spain, were arrested six months later following a police investigation. Boixos Nois had previously been banned from their team’s stadium.

A group of five members of the right-wing extremist group "Wolfsschar", aged 19 to 48, tried to set fire to a left-wing building complex, before attacking residents with stones and beer bottles. The perpetrators had been together in a bar in the evening. The bar was located in a building complex housing the left-wing associations "Utopia" and "Vereins Flexible Jugendarbeit". The building also contained family apartments and shared flats. The perpetrators made their way to the backyard of the building and tried to set fire to a wooden terrace. Residents called the fire brigade, but when they arrived the fire was already out. In the meantime, the perpetrators had gone back to the bar. Local guests asked the bar staff to expel the perpetrators. The perpetrators then stormed the backyard of the building again and attacked residents with beer bottles and stones. When the victims were able to flee into the stairwell, the perpetrators tried to break open the doors. During the attack, the perpetrators did the Hitler salute and shouted hateful insults and threats.

weapon_description: Knives, hatchets, and other unspecified sharp objects, replica handguns, ammunition, airsoft handguns
description: Police raided people connected with the neo-Nazi and white supremacist organization "Ordine di Hagal". The raids were carried out in the provinces of Naples, Avellino, Caserta, Milan, Turin, Palermo, Ragusa, Treviso, Verona, Salerno, Potenza, Cosenza, Crotone, while the organization was based in the province of Naples. Four people were arrested, as they were suspected of plotting to attack a police station and a shopping centre. The plot was partially detected through police monitoring one of their conversations revealing that, in addition to anti-Semitic and racist propaganda, they were speaking between themselves about organizing a massacre "like the one that guy did in New Zealand, but I would go to the n******, I would go to the police station." The group had contact with Ukrainian groups with neo-Nazi members, such as the Azov Battalion. The weapons seized were knives, hatchets, and other unspecified sharp objects, replica handguns, ammunition, and airsoft handguns. While there was stated intent to carry out an attack among group members,  few concrete plans of an actual attack have been uncobvered. The same organization was raided in 2021 (CaseID 2021-10-19), when police found modified automatic and semi-1utomatic firearms, handguns, a grenade launcher and ammunition.

A black Brazilian man living in Portugal was severely beaten by six police officers in a racially charged attack. The incident began when the victim was waiting for a job interview on the street, and the perpetrators approached him without warning. The officers physically assaulted him with kicks and punches, continuing the violence even after he was handcuffed and immobilized. At the police station, the brutality escalated, with the officers using a baton while hurling racist slurs, including: "Where's the drugs, fucking n*****?", "I'm here to put an end to your race," and "I wanted to go to Brazil to clean up your race." They falsely accused him of drug trafficking, a claim with no basis in fact. After four hours, the officers took the victim to his home, where they searched for drugs but found only boxing gloves, which they used to further beat him. Before he was taken to the hospital, the perpetrators threatened him, warning him not to testify against them: "If you tell the court who did it, I know where your mother works, where your mother lives and where your girlfriend studies." The victim sustained serious injuries, requiring a period of recovery in a wheelchair. His lawyer later filed a complaint of racist police abuse, stating that there was no doubt the attack was motivated by racial hatred. Despite this, the victim was harassed by the same officers in the following months.

Five perpetrators, aged 19 to 23, were suspected of planning "a serious act of violence that is dangerous to the state". The perpetrators were members of the the far-right 'Neue Stärke Partei' (New Strenght Party), an organization mainly active in Thüringen, but that the perpetrators wanted to expand to Southern Germany. They also tried to obtain weapons in Eastern Europe to prepare for Day X. Police raided their homes in Baden-Württemberg and Bavaria and found Nazi memorabilia, weapons that do not require a licence [unspecified, but includes starting pistols, flare guns, or anything that can only shoot blanks or irritants] and electronic data carriers. The police had been investigating the group since September. The group's Telegram channel did announce the expansion of the organization to Southern Germany before the police started the investigation.

weapon_description: Molotov cocktail, knife, skirting board with nails
description: An 18-year-old Ukrainian man with neo-Nazi views made threats and planned arson and violence towards an LGBTQI+ cafe. The perpetrator had accessed a video with details about production and use of a Molotov cocktail. He posted at photo of the specific cafe and a rainbow flag on a Nordic Resistance Movement Telegram channel, asking "does anyone know how to make a Molotov cocktail?". A few days later he posted the address to the cafe on this channel. The perpetrator also accessed a video demonstrating instructions for knife fights, after which he walked by the cafe with a spring knife and posted a picture on Telegram with the spring knife unfolded writing "there is an old but proved method". The perpetrator had also made a video swinging a skirting board with nails in it. The police received a tip after someone raised concern about the perpetrator's social media posts about LGBTQI+ people, which led to a search of the man's room and access to the Telegram messages. The Telegram-posts were posted on a channel belonging to the Nordic Resistance Movement, which he claimed in court he was not a member of. He explained in court that the code for his phone was '1488', a combination of the Nazi numerical codes 14 and 88, and that he was in possession of a ring with a swastika because it was "a beautiful ring." He also had a tattoo of a swastika on his arm, which he used as a profile picture on Telegram. In court, the prosecutor said there was no doubt that the perpetrator planned an attack against the LGBTQI+ community. However, the court did not find it sufficient to convict him of the attempted violence. He was sentenced to 40 days in prison for threats against the LGBTQI+ community and violation of knife regulations.

weapon_description: Beating and hitting with a large and heavy Christmas decoration bauble, and stabbing with the broken bauble
description: A 21-year-old man attacked a couple, two men, in an unprovoked attack at a metro station. The perpetrator began shouting homophobic and racist language at the couple and then punched one of the victims in the face. The perpetrator continued to homophobically abuse them and then struck the second victim on the head with a large and heavy Christmas decoration bauble, which split in two. The first victim was then stuck with a sharp object, believed to be part of the broken Christmas bauble. Both victims were left covered in blood and required hospital treatment. The perpetrator pleaded guilty to racially aggravated assault occasioning actual bodily harm.

weapon_description: 17 explosive devices, 362 firearms, 148761 rounds of ammunition and 347 cutting and stabbing weapons
description: More than 3000 police officers raided 130 locations in Germany and arrested 25 members of the group 'Patriotische Union' and of the Reichsbürger movement. One arrest was conducted in Austria and another one in Italy. The perpetrators were organized and aimed at carrying out a coup d'état, including storming the Reichstag, the German parliament building. Among the arrests there was a judge and former MP for the far-right party AfD, a prince from the House of Reuss and several members of the police/security services. The prince was the head of the central body of the organization, the Council, and he was supposed to become the new head of state after the coup was successful. The organization was divided in a civil branch, headed by the prince and the Council, and a military branch, headed by a former paratrooper. The members were well-organized, and met in small groups, divided the tasks to be carried out, communicated via a messaging app, and even signed an NDA upon entry. Initially, 93 weapons were seized, including 19 handguns and 25 rifles, knives, crossbows, decorative weapons, and blank pistols. Information that surfaced in August 2023 revealed that the complete amount of weapons was much larger. According to investigators, the weapons seized included 362 firearms, 148,761 pieces of ammunition, 347 cutting and stabbing weapons and 17 explosive devices. The organization attempted (unsuccessfully) to gather support from Russia to carry out their plan. The investigation started after police raided the group 'Vereinte Patrioten' earlier the same year (CaseID 2022-4-13). One year later, in December 2023, charges were brought against 27 defendants who were accused of membership or support of a terrorist organization, high treason and violations of the Weapons Act.

Some left-wing militants were attacked by nine far-right militants after three of the perpetrators entered a left-wing social space during a bar night. They were asked to leave by the victims, who followed them outside to check that they really left. When the perpetrators saw the victims following them outside, they attacked them, with six other perpetrators joining in. One of the victims was hit in the face with a helmet. He suffered a broken jaw and required surgery. During the attack, the perpetrators shouted: "We will slaughter you", "We will kill you".

An unknown perpetrator racially insulted a group of young teenagers and stabbed one of them with a hunting knife. The victim, a 14-year-old, suffered non-life-threatening injuries on his upper body. The perpetrator racially insulted other people before fleeing by bike.

weapon_description: Baton, tear gas, smoke bomb, unspecified category D weapons
description: A group of 38 men, aged 17 to 36, were arrested on suspicion of planning violence against Morocco World Cup fans. The men, affiliated with various far-right groups, included 15 individuals listed on the "S"-list, a surveillance roster for national security threats. Among them was a prominent figure in French right-wing extremism, previously convicted for violence (see cases 2020-6-4 and 2021-12-5) and a leader of the militant Zouaves group. Most of the men were from the Paris region, with others from Rouen and Rennes. They were observed leaving a bar in the 17th arrondissement after the World Cup final between France and Morocco, wearing ski masks and displaying aggressive behavior, which drew the attention of nearby police. Searches revealed tear gas, smoke bombs, batons, shin guards, mouth guards, military hoods, and tactical gloves. Police also found a backpack with "category D weapons," legally purchasable items. One man had stickers from "Groupe Union Défense," a violent far-right group making a resurgence, while another's phone showed he was part of messaging groups named "Hitler" and "ANTI FAG." Seven men were brought to court, but the judge dismissed the case due to a procedural error, ruling that the police lacked the mandate to carry out the arrests.

A 15-year-old alleged neo-Nazi was arrested and sentenced for planning an attack at a Jewish family's home with fireworks to scare them from his village. The perpetrator made a launcher to fire the fireworks at their home after he heard a synagogue might be built nearby his home. The perpetrator made videos where he showed off his improvised launcher. He allegedly posted propaganda and recruitment videos for the neo-Nazi group Atomwaffen Division. On December 9, he wrote that he was going to "light up the house with rockets' to scare the s*** out of them". A video posted on TikTok on December 11 included statement that read "the Jews have oppressed and controlled us long enough, this is why we are starting an unwinnable guerrilla war to liberate our people from this modern day slavery". On December 13, the perpetrator told group members he was going to "do it" tomorrow, and another video showing a box of firewokrs saying "it's time to f****** kill some Jews". He was arrested the next day, and later sentenced to a two-year rehabilitation order.

A 51-year-old man strangled a taxi driver after making several racist comments. Prior the attack, the perpetrator said to the victim "why have they sent a black person to pick me up? I do not trust any black person" and "you need to go back to your country", listing African nations. The perpetrator was informed that he was being recorded, and he became increasingly aggressive and grabbed the victim’s arm while he was driving. The perpetrator said "I'm going to strangle you" and proceeded to take off his belt and wrapping it tightly around his neck, according to the victim. The strangulation continued for approximately three minutes, with the victim fighting for breath and struggling to remain conscious while maintaining control of the vehicle. The victim managed to pull over and fought the perpetrator which then fled the car. The perpetrator admitted intentional strangulation ad racially aggravated threatening behavior.

A 69-year-old French pensioner killed three people and injured three others in an attack targeting a Kurdish cultural centre, a Kurdish restaurant and a Kurdish hairdressing salon. The perpetrator first went to Saint-Denis [an immigrant neighbourhood on the outskirts of Paris] planning to "kill foreigners", but did not do so because no one was around. He then went back home, walked to the Kurdish cultural centre, and shot the victims using a Colt 45 mm handgun, which he had obtained illegally. All the victims were of Kurdish ethnicity. The perpetrator admitted that the attack was racially motivated, and declared that he "didn't like the Kurds". In 2021, the same perpetrator entered a migrant camp with a machete and slashed several tents in addition to injuring two people living there (CaseID 2021-12-8).

A 47-year-old Turkish man stabbed a 27-year-old Kurdish man. The victim worked as a barber where the perpetrator was a client. During the haircut, the victim played some Kurdish music in the shop. The perpetrator, bothered by it, stabbed the victim with a pair of scissors multiple time in the chest. The victim was hospitalised. The judge retained the racist character of the incident.

A 35-year-old Roma with a reported mental disability was set on fire and racially abused by a group of men. The incident happened in a car dealership store. The victim asked to sing a New Year’s Eve carol for the perpetrators, in exchange for money. The perpetrators began to racially mock and make fun of the victim. The perpetrators said that they would accept a carol but only if the victim was kneeling. The victim obeyed the perpetrators, who then began to throw flammable liquid at him. The perpetrator set the victim on fire. The victim screamed and fought to put out the flames. The victim avoided burn injuries. The incident was filmed and posted on social media by one of the perpetrators.

A 51-year-old man from the Reichsbürger scene planned to attack police officers with the use of homemade flamethrowers. The police became aware of the plot after getting a private tip from an acquaintance of the perpetrator. Under the subsequent police raid, eight fire extinguishers, large amounts of flammable liquid, and drugs were found. The perpetrator's garden and outer fence were covered in flags and posters with references to Reichsbürger ideology. The perpetrator aimed to construct a flamethrower that he would use on police forces during demonstrations. The police investigated the perpetrator for preparing a serious act of violence endangering the state.

A 28-year-old man racially attacked a hotel cleaner while leaving his room. As the victim, who was cleaning nearby, went about his duties, the perpetrator asked what he was looking at and then called him a racial slur. When the victim questioned the slur, the perpetrator punched him in the face and tried to drag him into the lift. He then pressed his thumbs into the victim's eyes, pushed him to the floor, and repeatedly punched him while he lay there. The victim suffered a cut and swelling to his lip, eye injuries, and a hemorrhage. The judge described the incident as a "nasty and racially aggravated assault", and sentenced the perpetrator to 12 months in prison.

A 12-year-old boy was attacked by a stranger because of his skin color. The victim got off the tram and the perpetrator ran after and insulted him. The perpetrator then kicked the victim vigorously, called him the N-word and tried to hit him with a glass bottle. The victim managed to escape.

A 28-year-old man slapped and kicked a woman down an escalator after chanting Nazi slogans and racially insulting her. The perpetrator shouted "Sieg Heil" out in public. The victim, who was out walking with a friend, asked the perpetrator if he was okay. The perpetrator began yelling at the victim, racially insulting her, and spitting on her. He then slapped the victim in the face with a flat hand, before kicking her down an escalator. The victim could not remember what followed, just that she was lying on the escalator a short time later. Earlier the same day, the perpetrator had punched a woman in the face with a clenched fist (see CaseID 2023-1-10). The perpetrator was close to various right-wing extremist groups. He was believed to be a member of Tanzbrigade Wien, a right-wing extremist group with ties to a small far-right German party. He had also sought contact with other right-wing extremists in Austria, among those a convicted Holocaust denier. Unknown persons had warned that he is a "violent racist." The perpetrator was sentenced to one and a half year in prison.

A 28-year-old man beat a woman in the face and shouted Nazi slogans. He was observed by the victim while she was urinating in public, and therefore he followed her. He shouted: "Stop, you left-wing pig". He caught up with her and hit her in the face with a clenched fist. He then raised his right arm in a Nazi salute and shouted "Sieg Heil". The victim suffered a skull contusion [head trauma from blunt force, without a complete concussion] and a bruise. Later the same day, he kicked another woman down an escalator (see CaseID 2023-1-10-1). The perpetrator was close to various right-wing extremist groups. He was believed to be a member of Tanzbrigade Wien, a right-wing extremist group with ties to a small far-right German party. He had also sought contact with other right-wing extremists in Austria, among those a convicted Holocaust denier. Unknown persons had warned that he was a "violent racist." The perpetrator was sentenced to one and a half year in prison.

A shop worker of foreign background was beaten and racially abused by two men and one woman. The perpetrators were drunk, throwing things around the shop where the victim worked and shouted racial slurs like "P*** bastard". The victim asked them to stop. The perpetrators then attacked him. The victim was knocked to the ground and kicked multiple times in the back, the face and the head. A shop window was shattered. He was brought to the hospital with head injuries and stayed overnight.

weapon_description: Ten long guns, three handguns and 3000 rounds of ammunition
description: The police searched the home and office of a 48-year-old suspected member of the Reichsbürger movement. The police found ten long guns, three handguns and 3000 rounds of ammunition. The police executed the search warrant because the district office had revoked the perpetrator's firearm license due to his alleged proximity to the Reichsbürger scene. The perpetrator had previously owned the weapons legally but was not able to provide a permit for all the ammunition. The perpetrator was investigated for violation of the Weapons Act.

A group of Irish men attacked a camp of homeless migrants, consisting of about 15 tents, in a reportedly racist attack. Two victims stated that they had been threatened by four men who appeared on the site. Three hours later, the perpetrators were observed with sticks and four dogs, shouting things like "pack up" and "get out now". Multiple people were punched and threatened. One perpetrator attacked a victim, a young man, with a baseball bat. Another victim came to defend him, and was also hit with the baseball bat. At least one of the victims needed hospital treatment over the weekend. The attack happened amid protests against housing asylum seekers in the city. An unknown man had visited the camp a day or two earlier and allegedly posted a video complaining about the migrants' presence, which led to comments online that they needed to be "ran out".

A group of young people belonging to the organization Jeune Communistes Vienne was attacked by a group of around 15 individuals with right-wing sentiments. The incident took place on the terrace of a bar. The perpetrators had just attended a conference hosted by the right-wing student organization la Cocarde Étudiante. When coming out of the conference, the perpetrators attacked the victims sitting at the terrace. One of the victims was hospitalized after the incident. The victim received five days of ITT (sick leave). There were others who were slightly injured. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

A 35-year-old man was attacked after defending a woman who was being racially abused. He noticed a young man shouting racist insults to a woman, and as he passed them, he told him to shut up. The perpetrator then told up to ten of his friends to follow him and they attacked the victim. They kicked and punched him repeatedly. The victim managed to run to a nearby hotel and emergency services were called. The receptionist at the hotel had allegedly been subjected to racial abuse from the same group. The victim needed hospital treatment for a fractured orbital bone below his left eye socket and two breaks in his nose, injuries the doctor had said was akin to what he would have seen from a car crash. The victim thought the perpetrators were aged between 18 and 40.

A 28-year-old man of Malian origin was assaulted by three men in their 20s. The victim, employed as a cleaner at a fast-food store, politely requested the perpetrators to move from the marked area where he was cleaning. In response, the perpetrators began physically attacking by beating and kicking the victim, while also hurling racist insults and remarks targeting the victim's skin color. The victim sustained injuries and had to be transported to the hospital by ambulance, where he had to stay overnight.

A 31-year-old man was assaulted by a group of four young boys at night while walking alone from the train station. The perpetrators initiated the attack by hurling racist insults at him, including "you're a shitty n****r". The perpetrators then pushed him to the ground and started to kick and punch the victim. One of the perpetrators attempted to strike the victim in the head with a brick, but missed. The victim sustained injuries requiring hospital treatment, where he stayed overnight.

A group of right-wing extremists attacked a group of leftist youths. The victims were about to leave a city square where they had been partitioning in a rally for the teachers' union. They were harassed and insulted by the perpetrators, who were known from the dissolved neo-Nazi group "Neue Stärke Partei". A video of the attack showed two perpetrators grabbing and hitting a victim, while calling him "Zecke [slur for leftist]" and "left-wing f***". One of the other perpetrators shouted, "Heil Hitler!" and did a Hitler salute. One of the victims suffered a cheekbone contusion and a concussion.

A 20-year-old man was subjected to a knife attack by a 23-year-old suspected right-wing extremist. The victim and the perpetrator were both attending a clubhouse of a student fraternity where the perpetrator played right-wing extremist music. The victim belonged to the clubhouse where crime took place, while the perpetrator was visiting from another fraternity. When the victim asked the perpetrator to turn off the offensive music, an argument broke out between the two. The perpetrator attacked the victim with a knife and inflicted several stab wounds to his upper body. The victim was critically injured. The federal government reported the crime as a case of attempted homicide allegedly motivated by right-wing extremism.

A 39-year-old woman was attacked by five Casapound militants - four men and one woman aged between 25 and 30 years old - after she was caught removing a fascist poster at a bus station. When the victim was tearing the poster apart, one of the perpetrators confronted her. The perpetrator asked the victim what she was doing while calling others on his phone. Within minutes, the four other perpetrators arrived at the scene, and the victim was violently attacked. The victim was thrown to the ground and subjected to a severe beating, with the perpetrators holding her down while repeatedly striking her in the face and head. The perpetrators fled the scene before the police arrived. The victim went to the emergency room and was hospitalized.

A 52-year-old Reichsbürger member shot at police officers and a gas station tenant with steel balls. The tenant had called the police because there were two bullet holes on the windows of the gas station. When the police arrived, and the officers and the tenant were standing by the window, they were shot at with steel balls. The perpetrator, who had previously verbally attacked the police officers with slogans known to the Reichsbürger movement, was caught by the officers close by. The perpetrator carried a knife that he refused to put down. The perpetrator was taken to the police station. In the home of the perpetrator, the police found the packaging of the slingshot that the perpetrator had used, and steel balls. In addition, a blank gun and several knives were seized. The perpetrator also owned objects connected to the Reichsbürger scene. The perpetrator was charged with assault on law enforcement officers, attempted dangerous bodily harm and damage to property.

The police searched the apartments of six people from the prepper and Reichsbürger milieu who had planned to cause a large-scale power outage. The raids took place in Oberpfalz and Oberbayern. Around 70 police officers were involved in the operation. Investigations that had been ongoing since 2022 found that the perpetrators wanted to sabotage electric pylons, with the intent to enable other groups to take power in Germany through a political overthrow. The plotting had been going on since September 2020. Evidence was seized from the perpetrators' residences, but the police was not able to provide further information as investigations were ongoing (2023). The perpetrators were charged with membership in a terrorist organization. This case is suspectedly linked to CaseID 2022-4-13 and CaseID 2022-3-30-1.

weapon_description: Explosives in the form of black powder, knives, two cartridges
description: A 15-year-old boy adopted far-right ideologies and planned an attack on his school. He posted TikTok videos wearing a skull mask, a homemade Nazi uniform, and wielding a knife, glorifying school shooters and right-wing terrorists. One video showed him detonating a homemade bomb in a forest. In a Snapchat group with extremists, he received advice on making a more powerful bomb. On TikTok, he declared, “On May 11, I will make Sweden Swedish again,” and specified on Telegram that his target was immigrants. The boy communicated with right-wing sympathizers online, including individuals previously convicted of school attacks in Sweden. One such convict helped him prepare for the attack. Acting on a tip, police found knives, explosives, cartridges, a protective vest, extremist materials, Nazi symbols, a manifesto, and a "death list" at his home. His phone contained over 600 videos of school and racist attacks. The boy admitted to being radicalized online. The court ruled that his plans stemmed from far-right and anti-Semitic beliefs. He was convicted of preparing murder and sentenced to ten months of juvenile supervision.

weapon_description: Three hand grenades, a semi-automatic pistol, a grip with a trigger device for a handgun, several thousand rounds of ammunition, a crossbow, knives and batons
description: The police arrested a 55-year-old man from the Reichsbürger scene after discovering an arsenal of weapons in his home. The apartment was initially searched because the perpetrator had endorsed the police murders of January 2022 (excluded from the RTV data set due to limited information and motive) on Twitter. The police found three hand grenades, a semi-automatic pistol, a grip with a trigger device for a handgun, several thousand rounds of ammunition, a crossbow, knives, and batons in the perpetrator's apartment. The investigations against the perpetrator were expanded to include allegations of violations of the War Weapons Control Act and the Weapons Act.

Three men in their 20s were convicted of terrorist crimes with extreme right motives after 3D printing weapons between 2021 and 2023. The perpetrators had practiced shooting with homemade weapons together. For instance, they had shot at watermelons with The Star of David on them. One of these shootings caught the attention of bystanders who called the police. The main perpetrator had manufactured weapons and obtained instructions for making explosives. He had guns, gun parts and cartridges in his possession. Another perpetrator had used a 3D-printed gun to shoot at the mailbox of a non-white family. One perpetrator had also shot his cat and filmed it. According to the verdict, the perpetrators were preparing for a race war. The police found lists of names and addresses that the perpetrators considered to be political opponents. The authorities treated the document as a list of possible attack targets. The perpetrators had also communicated about the possibility of assassinating Prime Minister Sanna Marini and attacking an event called "Helsinki without Nazis". They also wanted to target immigrants, ethnic and religious minorities, and critical infrastructure. Police said they believed the group was influenced by accelerationist ideas. At least one of the perpetrators had been connected to the Finns Party, as he had been a candidate for the party in a local election a few years before he was arrested. The perpetrators got prison sentences ranging from seven months to three years and four months. A 66-year-old man was also sentenced to prison because he had sold a gun and cartridges to the perpetrators while knowing their motives. The perpetrators had reportedly been in contact with the 43-year-old perpetrator of CaseID 2023-6-21.

A 22-year-old man was xenophobically insulted and injured by a 46-year-old man. The victim got into a verbal dispute with another 22-year-old man on the street in the afternoon. Suddenly, the perpetrator intervened, insulted the victim xenophobically, and hit him on the head with a glass bottle. The bottle broke and the perpetrator stabbed the victim twice in the back of the head with the bottle neck. The victim was treated in the hospital. Because the perpetrator was in a poor physical condition, he was also taken to the hospital for treatment and a blood sample.

Three students were attacked by five masked men at a metro stop. The students had encountered posters with far-right references and decided to take them down. The posters portrayed "Oriflamme" which is a French far-right group. As the victims were taking down the posters, the perpetrators observed them and immediately attacked a male victim in the group. A female victim ran to get help, and when she came back the male victim was sitting alone on the ground, bleeding. The perpetrators had run off. The victim was taken to the hospital, where there were several fractures revealed, among them a broken arm. The perpetrators were not found.

A Pakistani man was subjected to a racial attack by a 41-year-old man. The perpetrator had a dispute with two of his employees from Pakistan and went to look for them at their residence. The employees were not home, unlike the victim, a roommate of the employees. The perpetrator began racially insulting the victim, threatening him, and grabbing his cell phone. When the perpetrator left the apartment, the victim followed him to the entrance of the building. The perpetrator continued to swear and shouting racist threats before attacking the victim with several blows to the head. The perpetrator hit the victim against a glass wall, so it broke and then hit the victim's head on the glass fragments. The victim was rushed to the hospital in a state of unconsciousness. The perpetrator was arrested. The investigators classified the incident as racially motivated.

The mayor of Saint-Brevin-les-Pins was subjected to an arson attack on his home. The attack happened at 5 AM when both him and his wife were inside the house sleeping. Police suspects that an explosive device was thrown in direction of two cars parked by the wall of the house. The fire started in the cars and then spread to the walls of the house. The mayor and his wife were awakened by people who saw the fire when walking outside, and there were not any injuries reported. There has not been any reports of suspects in the case. There were plans to move a centre for asylym seekers near an elementary school in the town, something that stoked the anger of extreme-right groups. The mayor had previously received death threats, and was a regular target of far-right protests. The discourse in newspapers and among politicians is that the mayor was subjected to an attack from the far-right. The mayor resigned and moved away after the incident. The mayor's successor was also harrassed by the far-right. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

A police officer of the Special Operations Command (SEK) was shot by a 46-year-old member of the Reichsbürger movement during a house search. Based on information detected from the raid on the Reichsbürger scene in December 2022 (CaseID 2022-12-7), over 20 residences in eight German states and in Switzerland were searched. When the victims approached the house of the perpetrator, he was waiting for the them with a pointed AR 15 assault rifle. The perpetrator did not comply with repeated requests to put down the weapon. There was an exchange of gunfire between the police and the perpetrator. One of the victims was hit in the arm and had to be treated in the hospital. The perpetrator surrendered and was arrested. The perpetrator was a gun enthusiast and owned 22 legal firearms and other illegal weapons, including a machine gun, nine long guns, hand grenades and handguns (CaseID 2023-3-22). The perpetrator was investigated for multiple attempted murders. Furthermore, he was accused of violating the War Weapons Contol Act and the Weapons Act, because he had provided the plot makers of terrorist group "Patriotische Union" with weapons (CaseID 2022-12-7).

weapon_description: Illegal hand grenades, a machine gun, nine long guns, handguns, and 22 legal firearms
description: The police detected large amounts of weapons in the possession of a 46-year-old member of the Reichsbürger movement. Based on information detected from the raid on the Reichsbürger scene in December 2022 (CaseID 2022-12-7), over 20 residences in eight German states and in Switzerland were searched. The perpetrator owned 22 legal firearms and other illegal weapons, including a machine gun, nine long guns, hand grenades and handguns. During the house search, there was an exchange of gunfire between the perpetrator and the police. One police officer was shot (CaseID 2023-3-22-2). The perpetrator was investigated for multiple attempted murders. Furthermore, he was accused of violating the War Weapons Contol Act and the Weapons Act, because he had provided the plot makers of terrorist group "Patriotische Union" with weapons (CaseID 2022-12-7).

weapon_description: Unspecified long blunt instruments and beating/kicking
description: There were nationwide demonstrations and clashes between right-wing and left-wing groups in France during the first months of 2023 (see e.g. also caseID 2023-3-25 and  2023-6-6). This was rooted in political disputes concerning the pension reform. A student procession protesting the pension reform was attacked by the far-right group Waffen Assas, a subdivision of Groupe Union Défense. The victims had been demonstrating by blocking the entrance of the Université Paris-Panthéon-1ssas earlier in the day, and the attack was reportedly a retaliation because of this. The perpetrators – around twenty hooded people armed with gloves, motorcycle helmets and iron bars – attacked and beat the victims. One victim was bleeding from the head after being hit with an unspecified long blunt instrument. An ambulance was called, and the victim was hospitalized. Two days after the incident, members of Waffen Assas attacked and injured demonstrating students again (CaseID 2023-3-25)

A group of three cultural workers from Germany, Greece, and Slovenia was attacked by a group of seven suspected right-wing extremists, aged 18 to 30. The victims were in Chemnitz for a network meeting for people from Germany and Eastern Europe. The victims and the perpetrators had been attending the same club. When the victims left the club, they were followed by the perpetrators who asked them, "Are you Zecken [slur for leftists]?" and demanded that they stopped speaking English. After a verbal dispute, the perpetrator attacked the 33-year-old German with kicks and punches. The victim suffered a laryngeal fracture and had to be treated in intensive care. The police investigated the incident as a politically motivated crime.

There were nationwide demonstrations and clashes between right-wing and left-wing groups in France during the first months of 2023 (see e.g. also caseID 2023-3-23 and 2023-6-6). This was rooted in political disputes concerning the pension reform. Around 30 hooded far-right activists attacked students who were demonstrating at a university in Paris. The perpetrators, who were armed with knives and iron bars and wore hoods, attacked the victims. Most of the victims were able to take refuge in a medical center nearby. One victim was taken to the hospital with a fractured jaw and a broken nose. Reports say that Groupe Union Défense claimed the attack, and that "Waffen Assas" (a subdivision of GUD made up by students) carried out the attack. The incident happened two days after an attack by members of Waffen Assas on demonstrating students (CaseID 2023-3-23)

Three football players of African origin were assaulted by a group of seven men aged between 24 and 44. Racial insults were directed at the players from the beginning of the match, with phrases such as "shitty n****r, you must sink with the boats" being hurled at them. After the match was over, a brawl broke out. The three victims were transferred by ambulance to the emergency room, where one of them was diagnosed with a fracture of the nasal septum. The victims were on the losing team, ruling out the possibility that the motive behind the attack was related to the perpetrators being on the losing team. The case is being reported in the media as a racially motivated brawl. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

weapon_description: Homemade explosive devise made of pyrotechnic-type mixture based on potassium perchlorate, black powder and aluminium
description: Three Italian men, aged 18 to 23, were arrested for causing significant damage to the entrance of an apartment building with a homemade bomb. Under investigation for attempted multiple homicides, the men placed the bomb at the entrance of a building primarily inhabited by foreign residents, including children, around 10 pm. The building is also located 100 meters from a migrant reception center. The device, a pyrotechnic mixture of potassium perchlorate, black powder, and aluminum, caused extensive damage, shattering the glass doors and windows and destroying the entrance hall, while uprooting three doors on the first and second floors. No injuries were reported. The perpetrators masked their identities with balaclavas and covered their vehicle's license plate. The investigation suggests the attack was xenophobic, though the men were not affiliated with activist groups or political movements. The judge ordered house arrest for possession and use of explosives in public and attempted multiple murders. The same individuals carried out a similar attack months later (see CaseID 2023-7-29).

A 21-year-old man, originally from New Guinea, was subjected to an unprovoked attack by a group of approximately 15 people, where most of them were minors. The incident took place when the victim was on his way home from work around 8:30 pm at the train station, shortly after disembarking from the train. The perpetrators surrounded the victim and said "you can't pass through here, you can't go home". When the victim asked for an explanation, the perpetrators began hitting him, including the use of a sharp object. The victim was left unconscious on the train station platform. When the victim was found he was urgently transported to the emergency room with head and neck trauma, as well as bruises and cuts. The victim's friend said that the incident appeared to be a case of racism. The case is being reported as a "racist ambush" in the media. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

A 55-year-old man was racially abused and attacked by three unknown men. The incident happened on a tram around 10 PM. The victim was first insulted because of his skin color. The perpetrators then poured beer over the victim's trousers and hit him over the head with a bottle. The victim was injured. The state security police investigated for dangerous bodily harm.

A 32-year-old Albanian man was shot by a 59-year-old man outside a bar after being racially insulted. An altercation began when the perpetrator's girlfriend started hurling racist insults at the victim's girlfriend about her and her boyfriend's origin, such as "f*****g Albanian", which the perpetrator supported. According to several witnesses, the victim had not participated in the argument. Following the insults, the perpetrator went to his house where he retrieved a magnum pistol and returned to the bar where he fired three shots in the direction of the victim while saying "I'll kill you". The victim was shot in the arm, which required surgery. The perpetrator fled the scene before the police arrived. The police found the perpetrator 12 hours later in his car with the loaded gun, his passport and his suitcase, presumably trying to leave the country. The perpetrator was sentenced to 7 years and 4 months in prison for attempted murder and illegal possession of weapons.

The police searched the house of a 62-year-old Reichsbürger on suspicion of violation of the Explosives Act. Because the perpetrator had threatened the police during a house search seven months earlier (case does not meet inclusion criteria), almost 100 police officers broke into the residence during the night. The perpetrator was asleep and did not resist. The police found several containers of chemicals that could be used for bomb making. The perpetrator had an obvious affiliation with the Reichsbürger movement. He had documents hanging on his front door reading the "Laws and Regulations of the Military Government of Germany". A sign in the garden had the inscription "German Reich". The perpetrator was arrested.

A 37-year-old migrant worker was attacked by his employer. The victim was working at a livestock farm supporting his wife, parents and five children. The perpetrator had been swearing at the victim and insulting him in the days leading up to the incident. On the day of the attack, the victim's employer was late with the monthly pay, so the victim asked to get his earnings. The perpetrator responded by saying “Pakistani, you will get nothing" and showing the victim his genitals. The victim left due to derogatory treatment. When the victim was on his way to send the money to his family, he was picked up by the perpetrator who shouted, “Pakistanis are trash!” The perpetrator beat the victim with a bat on the head and body. The victim was seriously injured and left unconscious and covered in blood on the ground with a fractured head. The victim was treated in the hospital for eight days.

A young punk was attacked by two men while he was waiting for a train in the night. The perpetrators appeared and began calling the victim “asshole”, “Zecke [slur for leftist]", and “shitty punk”. The victim tried to escape but was hit on the nose, head, and kicked in the leg. The attack was stopped by the police. The victim suffered a broken nose among other injuries.

Four people were brought to the hospital after meeting hooligans with a right-wing association in a metro stop. One of the victims was the assistant of a left-wing politician and was handing out leaflets opposing the pension reform in a metro station. The perpetrators – a large group of right-wing nationalists – were on their way to a football match, making noise and shouting "France for the French". They were allegedly also harassing people in their vicinity. The victims observed that the perpetrators were attacking passersby of foreign origins. One of the perpetrators had numerous neo-Nazi tattoos and performed a Nazi salute. One of the victims took out his phone to film them, which caught the attention of the perpetrators. The victim who had tried to film was severely beaten. He woke up in a bathroom stall not remembering how he got there. A visit to the hospital revealed that he had been punched in the head, face and back, and needed staples for wounds on his scalp. There were reportedly three other people transported to the hospital as a result of the encounter with the perpetrators, but there was no report of injuries sustained by them.

weapon_description: A semi-automatic pistol, a bolt-action rifle, a rifle, two pistols, a revolver, guns, a crossbow with a telescopic sight, slingshots, stun guns, 13.000 rounds of ammunition and 2.000 steel bullets
description: The police found weapons in the possession of a 47-year-old member of the Reichsbürger movement. When the police arrived at the residence, the perpetrator handed over a revolver, a bolt-action rifle, and a semi-automatic pistol. The police insisted on searching the apartment and business premises where they found two pistols, a rifle, stun guns, a crossbow with a telescopic sight, more guns, slingshots, 13.000 rounds of ammunition and 2.000 steel bullets. A weapons permit had been withdrawn from the perpetrator one month before, based on his affiliation with the Reichsbürger scene. The perpetrator was investigated for violation of the Weapons Act.

An emergency accommodation center for asylum seekers, hosting about 50 people, was attacked with fireworks. CCTV footage of the incident captured the perpetrator throwing an object at the front of the building. The owners of the center said the footage shows there was a clear attempt to throw a firework through an open window on the roof of the building, but it exploded on the roof instead. No one was injured. No arrests were made as of May 2024. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

A 19-year-old self-confessed fascist carried out an assault on a trans woman, leaving her hospitalised with severe injuries, including a trainer imprint on her face. The perpetrator used mixed martial arts moves in an unprovoked attack, motivated by extreme transphobic, racist, and homophobic views. Previously convicted of terrorism-related offences and subject to a Criminal Behaviour Order, the perpetrator had shared far-right extremist content online, including Nazi and Ku Klux Klan material, and made threats of violence against non-white and LGBTQ+ individuals. He was sentenced to five years and four months in custody, with an extended five years on licence, for the assault and additional terrorism offences.

A 36-year-old Uber driver was racially attacked by a 27-year-old passenger during a ride. The perpetrator began using racial slurs shortly after the journey started, then punched the windscreen, shattering it, and assaulted the victim, causing him to nearly lose control of the car. The victim was repeatedly punched and forced to flee the vehicle, with the perpetrator briefly chasing him before turning his attention to his partner. The victim escaped to a nearby housing estate and called the police, later requiring hospitalization for severe injuries, including a broken nose, black eyes, three missing teeth, and a cracked jaw. The perpetrator admitted to causing grievous bodily harm and was sentenced to 31 months in jail.

A 48-yer-old right-wing extremist shot through the door of his 24-year-old Muslim neighbor, who was pregnant. The victim of Pakistani origin was standing in the hallway of her apartment when the perpetrator shot through the closed entrance door with a rifle. The victim's mother-in-law was also in the apartment. The women were unharmed, but the 24-year-old was taken to the hospital for a check. The perpetrator was arrested. The police found a picture of Hitler, an SS dagger, and several other weapons, as well as Ku Klux Klan documents and material form "Die Heimat" and "Alternative für Deutschland". Before the attack, the victim had been subjected to persistent racist insults and threats by the perpetrator. Other neighbors reported that the perpetrator repeatedly attracted attention by proclaiming right-wing extremist statements. The perpetrator was charged with attempted murder.

A man was severely injured in a premeditated attack by 60 to 70 right-wing football fans on a restaurant where left-wing UE Cornellà supporters had gathered. The incident occurred on the evening of a match between CD Numancia and UE Cornellà. The perpetrators, linked to the groups Orgullo Numantino, Ligallo Fondo Norte, and Guetto 28, had been celebrating Numancia's anniversary before traveling by bus to a location near the stadium. Armed with stones and bottles, some with faces covered, they assaulted people trying to block them from entering the restaurant. One victim, who attempted to flee, was beaten unconscious and later required emergency surgery to relieve pressure on his brain. He remained in a coma for two and a half weeks. Months later, 20 perpetrators were arrested. The Interior Ministry confirmed the attack was motivated by ideological hatred.

A 48-year-old taxi driver was attacked by a 67-year-old drunk passenger. The perpetrator was talking to the victim and asked him about his origins. When the victim answered that he was a German citizen, but originally from Afghanistan, the perpetrator snapped. He began insulting the victim with xenophobic comments stating that he "always carries a gun for people like him". The perpetrator punched the victim several times and kicked him in the upper body. The kick made the driver almost losing control over the car. The victim stopped the car and called the police. The perpetrator was taken into custody.

weapon_description: Axes, knife saw, carpet knife, knife
description: A man in his 30s prepared a violent attack on ethnic minorities. While serving time in prison for a previous conduct, he had stated that he intended to commit a crime in order to be re-incarcerated. He was released from prison in April. In May, the perpetrator sent messages that pointed to an intent of a violent crime against foreigners. After the perpetrator had been in contact with employees at the Criminal Sanctions Agency and hinted about a crime he was going to commit, a concern was reported to the police. Later in May, the perpetrator acquired a knife saw, matching blades, two axes, a carpet knife, a knife and a helmet hood covering his face. According to the prosecutor, the perpetrator's intention was to carry out the attack on 6 June at Helsinki Railway Square.
