The prosecution stated that the perpetrator had a detailed plan to commit a violent crime. On 6 June the perpetrator left home with an axe, a knife and other supplies. He was shortly arrested by the police. The perpetrator had previously said that society "wanted him to commit a crime". He had expressed racist views and said that black people and drug users were getting all the money. He had also stated to a friend, who also had racist sentiments, that if he got a gun and a couple of magazines, he could go "to Rauttis [railway station] to kill the gang." After the arrest, the perpetrator said he wanted to commit a crime because he felt he had been left alone and without help after his release from prison. He had previously stabbed a family member to death and was according to examination "impaired at the time of the act."

weapon_description: Tear gas, baseball bats and batons
description: Five left-wing activists were attacked by several people linked to the far-right while they were putting up posters against the pension reform. The pension reform became a polarized subject in France, with the right supporting the reform and the left opposed it. The perpetrators were wearing hoods, armed with batons, baseball bats and tear gas attacked the victims. Five people were seriously injured. This was one in a series of incidents in 2023 where right-wing groups targeted and beat up leftists because of their opposition to the pension reform (see e.g. also caseID 2023-3-23 and 2023-3-25).

A 37-year-old American was critically injured by an 18-year-old stranger. The victim was walking on the street in the area of a well-established leftist culture center in the middle of the day. Out of nowhere, the perpetrator appeared and attacked the victim with a sharp object. The victim sustained life-threatening injuries and was rushed into intensive care. The perpetrator initially fled but was arrested nearby. Two months after the incident, the crime was officially classified as motivated by right-wing extremism by Federal authorities.

A 51-year-old Brazilian national was violently assaulted by another man in a café. The victim was talking to the owner when the perpetrator, visibly intoxicated, questioned the victim's nationality. The victim said that the perpetrator could probably hear his Brazilian accent. The victim was then punched and kicked several times in the face and ribs and sustained injuries from which he had to be hospitalized overnight. The victim later stated, "He started kicking me in the face as if he wanted to kill me. It was attempted murder. I have no doubt." He believed that the perpetrator acted out of xenophobia because the only thing he had said to the perpetrator was that he was from Brazil.

A leftist demonstrator of non-French origin was beaten by two men, aged 22 and 24, at a campsite where an extreme far-right political party held a "patriotic banquet". The perpetrators were the son and the nephew of the owner of the campsite. The victim had come to the campsite to demonstrate against the event with 30 other people. The victim shouted to the perpetrators and called them fascists. He was then punched and kicked by the perpetrators. The victim suffered a broken arm, head trauma and a sprained neck. The victim believed that the attack was aggravated by racism. The perpetrators were sentenced to a fine of 5000 euros. The victim was a lower ranking elected municipal official in the EELV party, but there was no information indicating that the perpetrators knew his association to the party.

A Pakistani employed at a gas station was subjected to a racist attack by a costumer. The victim was at work when the perpetrator rushed into his lot. The victim asked the perpetrator to slow down the speed. He responded by screaming "You fucking Pakistani, Muslim, I'll kill you" and beat the victim with a bat and fists. The victim was hosptalized.

weapon_description: Headbutting, and a punch to the face, probably with a brass knuckle
description: Racist football supporters attacked a 30-year-old black man. The victim was walking in the street when he passed a large group of AS Nancy-Lorraine supporters who were on the terrace of a bar. The perpetrators had reserved the bar for the evening. One of the perpetrators shouted, “We don’t want black people here”, whereupon many others followed, shouting racist slurs, and eventually also homophobic insults. One of the perpetrators broke away from the group and immediately headbutted the victim. As the victim was grappling what happened, he was punched in the face by a second perpetrator. The punch split the victim's eyebrow. The victim went to the hospital, where he received nine stitches. The doctor told the victim that the second perpetrator who punched him must have used a brass knuckle to inflict the damage he did.

A 29-year-old man shot a 22-year-old man with Syrian origins with a crossbow. The perpetrator, who was carrying a crossbow and a machete, calmly approached the victim on the train station. The victim said "Hey, what's going on? Get away from me!". The perpetrator then lifted his crossbow and followed the victim into the train station building where he shot the victim in the back. The police arrived and managed to arrest the perpetrator. The arrow was stuck to the victim's back, and he was rushed to the hospital. The perpetrator was wearing a T-shirt of the neo-Nazi band "Landser" which was classified as a criminal organization in 2005. A witness reported that prior to the attack, the perpetrator had opened a door to a taxi and saw that the taxi driver was white, before searching out the more "foreign looking" victim. The perpetrator had no previous criminal record but was known to suffer from paranoid schizophrenia. He was in psychiatric ward at the time of the attack. The perpetrator was accused of attempted manslaughter in conjunction with dangerous bodily harm but was acquitted to remain in a psychiatric hospital. The incident was officially registered as a crime motivated by right-wing extremist beliefs.

Two Gambian boys were violently assaulted by a group of five men, aged between 19 and 27. The victims were playing football when the perpetrators arrived in a car at full speed and began attacking them with metal bars, inflicting serious head injuries. One of the victims was left in a critical condition after the assault. Five individuals were arrested, with the main perpetrator charged with attempted murder, aggravated by ethnic and racial hatred. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

A 24-year-old Muslim man was shot by his 59-year-old racist neighbor outside their apartment building. The victim, who was with his cousin and girlfriend at the time, intervened when the neighbor approached the women aggressively. In response, the neighbor drew a pistol, forced the victim into an elevator, and shot him in the thigh. Despite severe bleeding, the victim managed to call for help and subsequently spent five weeks in the hospital. The attacker, previously linked to the 2020 Hanau shooting (CaseID 2020-2-19) investigation, was a known racist who posted inflammatory content online. The crime was investigated as attempted manslaughter and other related charges. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

Demonstrators were attacked by a group of far-right activists during a demonstration where around 400 people took part. The march was interrupted when around 50 individuals from the far right charged at the demonstrators. The perpetrators beat the victims, also using iron bars. Construction equipment that was in the vicinity were thrown at the victims. Four people were injured, and one of the victims was transported to the hospital. No arrests were made.

A 32-year-old man of Tunisian origin was brutally assaulted by eight bouncers using knives, batons, and a taser at a nightclub. The victim had been inside the club for some time and had stepped out to buy cigarettes. When he tried to re-enter, the security refused, saying "we don't want foreigners". As the victim was about to leave, the perpetrators attacked the victim, using a taser, knives and batons as they were beating the victim. Even when emergency services arrived, the attackers persisted in their violent assault. The victim sustained severe injuries, including a fractured rib, a broken nose, and head trauma, requiring hospitalization.

A 19-year-old was convicted of terrorism offences after planning a suicide bomb at a synagogue during a Jewish holiday. The police discovered pictures of the synagogue on the perpetrators phone, with comments on where it would be "good for surprise attack", as well as pictures of the entrances, exits and a camera. On the perpetrator's notes, police discovered a plan to attack the synagogue and text about Jewish holidays that tend to have the most people in synagogues. Additionally, the perpetrator ran a channel on Telegram where they discussed previous far right attacks, encouraged terrorism, and also where he wrote that he wished to "blow himself up inside a synagogue". During investigations, the police found a collection of antisemitic materials, designs of 3D printed guns, and bomb instruction manuals.

weapon_description: Hand grenades, firearms, potentially explosive chemicals and ammunition
description: Weapons were found in the possession of a man affiliated with the Reichsbürger milieu. The police issued a search warrant on several residences owned by and connected to the perpetrator, in Deutsch Wusterhausen, Wünsdorf, and Kummersdorf, after receiving a tip. During the search, the police found hand grenades, firearms, potentially explosive chemicals, and larger quantities of ammunition. The perpetrator worked in the Explosive Ordinance Disposal unit of the Central Police Service, and it was investigated whether he had diverted the weapons from his workplace. The perpetrator was arrested on suspicion of violation the Weapons Act, the War Weapons Control Act, and the Explosives Act.

organizational_affiliation: Rassemblement des Étudiants de Droite Angers
weapon_description: Baseball bats, sticks, and smoke bombs
description: Following the death of a 17-year-old boy of African ethnicity in Nanterre, there were demonstrations against police violence throughout France. In Angers, there were held several demonstrations between June 30th and July 3rd. There were several clashes between left- and right-wing groups during this period. On the 30th of June, there was an attack on left-wing demonstrators. A building previously housing the offices of the far-right group "Alvarium", that was banned by the French government in 2021, was later used by a new far-right group called "Rassemblement des Étudiants de Droite Angers" (RED Angres). The victims had called for demonstrations in front of the town hall and in front of the RED premises. The perpetrators, who were masked and armed with sticks and baseball bats, came out of the building and hit multiple victims. The perpetrators also used smoke bombs to hinder intervention by the police. One victim was beaten several times while on the ground with a baseball bat. One victim was rushed to the hospital in a relatively critical condition. One of the far-right activists was sentenced to three months in prison for intentional violence against an anti-fascist activist. Three other far-right activists were acquitted.

An anti-facist solidarity festival was attacked by around 20 masked men, reportedly from the far-right scene. The perpetrators entered the festival grounds armed with batons. They first attacked the catering area of the festival. The organizers eventually managed to remove the perpetrators from the festival grounds. Seven people were injured in the attack, and one of the victims suffered a broken nose. Two arrests were made.

A 22-year-old disabled Egyptian citizen was assaulted by a 47-year-old man. The altercation began on the bus when the perpetrator started insulting the victim based on his skin color and disability. The victim was feeling threatened and called his father, asking him to meet at the bus stop. When the victim left the bus, the perpetrator chased the victim and punched him to the ground just as the victim's father arrived. The perpetrator managed to dodge the parent and hit the victim with his fists while continuing to insult both of them. The victim's father called the police who intervened and arrested the perpetrator. The father was also attacked by the perpetrator. The victim was transported to the emergency room for medical treatment.

A migrant was attacked by a suspected right-wing extremist. The victim was shopping for groceries when he was approached by the perpetrator. The perpetrator said to the victim: "What are you looking at?", to which the victim responded "I don't know". The perpetrator began shouting and verbally assaulting the victim, before repeatedly punching him in the face with a brass knuckles. The victim was left bleeding on the street. The perpetrator was wearing a black T-shirt and had a so called "buzz cut", a look symbolizing adherence to the "attack squads" of Golden Dawn. The victim sustained bruises and a cut above the eye that required stitches. Motive not explicitly stated but sufficiently evident to be included.

A 61-year-old right-wing conspiracist carried out a bomb attack on a masonic lodge at 7 AM, placing an improvised explosive device at the building's entrance on a busy street corner, followed by a threatening call to police. A second bomb, made from a gas cylinder and black powder, was safely detonated by experts. Before the attack, the perpetrator posted extremist views online, including conspiracy theories about Freemasons infiltrating the state and anti-Semitic remarks, referring to himself as "God's Warlord." Arrested weeks later, police discovered large quantities of explosives at his residence. He had previously committed two bombings: one on the Holy Synod of the Church of Greece in 2020 and another on a Magistrates' Court in 2023, though neither met inclusion criteria due to lack of severity or information. Linked to the "Guardians of the Constitution," a group associated with Golden Dawn, he was charged with multiple crimes, including manufacturing explosives and planning future attacks (CaseID 2023-7-25).

weapon_description: Poles, metal bars, hammers and beating/kicking
description: Four right-wing extremists broke into a house inhabited by refugees from Afghanistan and Algeria and attacked several residents. Two of the perpetrators entered the building by kicking in the back door. They were armed with metal bars and hammers and shouted xenophobic slogans. Two of the perpetrators were masked, one was wearing a shirt with the Reichsflagge and a picture of a Wehrmacht soldier. The perpetrators punched an 18-year-old victim and beat them with poles. The perpetrators also threw metal bars and hammers at the 18-year-old and his 16-year-old brother, while chasing them up the stairs. The 16-year-old was hit in the arm. The perpetrators fled when several other residents rushed to help the victims. The police identified a 20-year-old suspect who lived nearby. When the police searched the his house, they found swastika flags, brass knuckles, and the shirt with picture of the Reichsflagge and soldier. The perpetrator was investigated for dangerous bodily harm, insult, and trespassing.

The husband of a deceased left-wing activist was subjected to an arson attack in his home. The victim's wife had previously set up a local branch of a left-wing political party. At 2.30 in the night, the victim was awake and saw a light coming from outside of the house. He went to check what it was, presuming it was fireworks. The victim reported that he saw flames that were running the length of his house. The house was severely damaged in the fire. The victim had received threats due to his wife's activism in the past. He had had his car vandalized, tires punctured, and pig trotters left on his porch. The political party the wife was connected to, believed the arson attack was committed by activists from the far-right scene. The wife's grave was also vandalized a couple of months after this incident. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

weapon_description: Baseball bats, iron bars and beating/kicking
description: A 43-year-old Kurdish man was attacked by a gang of known neo-Nazis, after allegedly being lured into a trap. The incident started a few weeks earlier when the victim's cell phone was stolen from his garden. The later perpetrators tried to blackmail the victim and wanted money in return for the phone. The request led to an argument over the phone, but the victim agreed to meet the perpetrators to get the phone back. The perpetrators, three men and one woman, stepped out of the car armed with baseball bats and iron bars and attacked the victim with multiple brutal blows to the head. They were screaming hate speech throughout the attack and beat and kicked the victim while he was laying on the ground. The incident was disrupted by an intervening neighbor. The victim suffered bruises, a concussion, and a laceration to the head that had to be stitched. The racial motive for the crime was investigated by the state security police.

A 61-year-old right-wing conspiracist was arrested for plotting additional bomb attacks following a bomb attack on a masonic lodge (CaseID 2023-7-13). Investigators discovered that the perpetrator had been stockpiling explosives, materials for bomb-making, and other equipment, including eight shotguns, thousands of cartridges, and disguises, at his home. Online, he had posted extremist views, anti-Semitic conspiracy theories, and declarations of being "God's Warlord" fighting "enemies of the homeland." The perpetrator had a history of similar attacks, including a 2020 bombing of the Holy Synod of the Church of Greece and a 2023 attack on a Magistrates’ Court, though neither met inclusion criteria due to insufficient severity or information. A self-proclaimed member of the "Guardians of the Constitution," a group linked to extremist networks like Golden Dawn, he was charged with multiple offenses, including manufacturing explosives, incitement, and endangering public safety.

An 18-year-old was attacked by an unknown man. The victim was walking on the street together with a friend when the perpetrator asked him about his ethnicity. The perpetrator then insulted the victim racially and hit him with a glass bottle. The perpetrator fled. The victim suffered a laceration to the head, which was treated by rescue workers.

A Syrian refugee was beaten by suspected members of an anti-immigration militia. The victim was stranded on an island in the border river between Greece and Turkey together with 50 other refugees. The victim was hit repeatedly in the head, while he was laying in the shallow water. The perpetrators were carrying a baton and wore military clothing presumably without insignia. The other refugees fled the deflated rubber boat at the shore and into the water. The incident was filmed and a picture of a young man, presumably the victim, with a bleeding wound to his head surfaced on social media. The group of refugees, including 28 children and two pregnant women, were stranded on the island without food or water for three weeks. Repeated requests by NGOs to rescue them were rejected by the Greek authorities. The refugees reported that this was the second time in nine days that they had been attacked by a Greek militia (the second case does not meet the inclusion criteria due to limited information).

Individuals identifying as Nazis attacked two left-wing sympathizers in a nightclub. The victims were attacked in the bathroom, reportedly for being left-wing sympathizers. The perpetrators threatened to stab the victims with a knife. They were subsequently beaten and left unconscious on the floor. The victims were treated in the hospital.

weapon_description: Unspecified sharp object (assumingly a key) and beating/kicking
description: A woman was subjected to a racial attack by an unknown man. The victim was standing on the tram station when she was xenophobically insulted by the perpetrator, pushed to the ground and kicked several times. One of the passer-bys who intervened were stabbed in the hip with an unidentified object, presumably a key. The perpetrator fled and could not be identified by the police. The intervening victim was taken to the hospital by the emergency services.

Three Italian men were accused of throwing homemade explosive devices at an apartment complex, mostly inhabited by families of foreign origins. The perpetrators caused three explosions around 4 in the morning. No human injuries were reported. Technical investigations suggest a xenophobic motive. The same perpetrators committed a similar attack on families of foreign origins a few months earlier.

Two transgender men in their 20s were followed and attacked by two individuals, one allegedly linked to the far-right. After noticing he was being followed, one victim called his friend for help, and they met to hide in a courtyard. When they checked if the perpetrators had left, the attackers confronted them, shouting homophobic insults, and punched them repeatedly. Passersby intervened, causing the attackers to flee. One victim suffered a broken nose. The victims recognized one of the attackers as a known fascist in Besançon who had previously insulted them.

A mosque in Harlow was set on fire around 9:30PM. Two teenage boys were arrested over what the police suspected was a racially aggravated arson at the mosque. No one was injured, but carpets and curtains in the prayer space were damaged. The mosque is open until 10:30PM every day.

A group of right-wing extremists, aged between 18 and 24, attacked people on the street who disagreed with their political views. The perpetrators had first been together in an apartment, shouting right-wing extremist slogans so that it could be heard from the street. The perpetrators continued their demonstration on the street where they shouted “Sieg Heil” several times. The victims confronted the perpetrators about their behavior, leading the perpetrator to physically attack them. Around 20 people were involved in the brawl. A 31-year-old woman who tried to mediate had her head kicked while she was laying on the ground. A second woman was strangled so she could not breathe, after she tried to intervene. The perpetrators also sprayed animal repellent spray, injuring a 32-year-old man and a 52-year-old woman. Two people were seriously injured and six people were slightly injured. The perpetrators were identified as Hessian neo-Nazis who were visiting Erfurt. They were charged with dangerous bodily harm.

A Chinese bar owner was attacked by a 22-year-old Nazi and a friend of his. The perpetrator entered the victim's bar without a shirt on, and the victim asked him to cover up for hygiene reasons. The perpetrator reacted violently, racially insulting the victim, breaking furniture, and threatening to return with friends. The perpetrator left the establishment and returned with another man hours later. The xenophobic insults continued, telling the victim to leave Spain. The victim was then physically attacked, an attack which resulted in him receiving emergency care at the hospital. When the police tried to arrest the perpetrators, they escaped through a window, shouting xenophobic proclamations and slogans of Nazi ideology. The perpetrators also did a Nazi salute.

weapon_description: 40 long guns and handguns, knives, crossbow with scopes, 10.000 rounds of ammunition, several magazines for a rapid-fire rifle, and four non-ignitable hand grenades
description: The police seized an arsenal of weapons from a 51-year-old right-wing extremist. After the perpetrator had attracted attention through online publishing of hate posts, including portraits of Adolf Hitler, police officers carried out a raid on the perpetrator's home. The police found around 40 handguns and long guns, of which he had a hunter's permit to own four of them, over 100 prohibited knives, a crossbow with scopes, more than 10.000 rounds of ammunition, several magazines for a rapid-fire rifle, and four non-ignitable hand grenades. Some of the weapons were lying spread around in the apartment. The police revoked the weapons and weapons permit after the search. The perpetrator came under investigation for using symbols of unconstitutional organizations and violations of the War Weapons Control Act.

13 refugees from Pakistan and Syria were attacked and kidnapped by a 45-year-old far-right activist and his accomplices. The incident happened close to the Greek-Turkish border, during a time of massively devastating wildfires in the area. Conspiracy theories stating that illegal immigrants were purposely burning down the woods, were spreading online. The perpetrator published a video in social media, showing that he had captured the victims in the trailer behind his car. In the background of the video, the perpetrator was heard accusing the victims of being "sworn to burn us" and calling for a pogrom against immigrants. The victims later reported that the perpetrator had beaten them with metal bars, taken off their clothes and filming them, before locking them up. Many of them were not able to brethe. A few days after the incident, the perpetrator published a second video showing that he had detained four more victims (CaseID 2023-8-27). The perpetrators suspectedly had affiliation to local branches of Golden Dawn and Greek Solution. A supreme court judge requested an investigation into the racist violence against immigrants in the wake of the wildfire. The fire was caused by lightning, according to the fire department. 19 immigrants hiding in the woods were killed by the flames. It remains unknown how many were injured by the racist violence.

Four refugees were kidnapped by a 45-year-old far-right activist and his accomplices. The incident happened close to the Greek-Turkish border, during a time of massively devastating wildfires in the area. Conspiracy theories stating that illegal immigrants were purposely burning down the woods, were spreading online. The perpetrator published a video on social media where he was filming the victims who were on the ground behind his car. One of the victims were half lying and in a bad shape surrounded by the perpetrators. There were no reports on the violent actions executed in relation to this specific kidnapping. However, a similar incident had been filmed by the same perpetrator a few days earlier (CaseID 2023-8-22). The perpetrator had "arrested" 13 refugees, beaten them with metal bars, called for a pogrom of immigrants, and locked them up in a truck unable to breathe. It is therefore reasonable to assume that the victims in this second incident endured violence. The reason for the attacks was the perpetrator's assumption that illegal immigrants had caused the wildfires. The perpetrators suspectedly had affiliation to local branches of Golden Dawn and Greek Solution. A supreme court judge requested an investigation into the racist violence against immigrants in the wake of the wildfire. The fire was caused by lightning, according to the fire department. 19 immigrants hiding in the woods were killed by the flames. It remains unknown how many were injured by the racist violence.

A homeless man from the Ivory Coast was attacked by two individuals and a pit bull. The victim was sleeping behind a flowerbed when two men approached him and saying "you're not Italian, so go to your house". The perpetrators then physically assaulted the victim with kicks and punches, and they incited the pit bull to attack him. The victim tried to defend himself with an iron bar, but to no avail. Following the incident, the victim was taken to the hospital for treatment. The police identified a 49-year-old Italian as one of the attackers, who was charged with aggravated assault and incitement to racial hatred.

weapon_description: Explosives, long guns, handguns, alarm guns, airsoft guns, dogs and 8,500 pieces of ammunition
description: A 45-year-old man with connections to the far-right political scene was arrested after the police found a large number of weapons and 44 neglected dogs at his property. The large-scale police operation and house search was carried out on suspicion of animal cruelty. The weapons found was 26 firearms (including long guns, handguns, alarm guns and airsoft guns) and explosives. They also found 51 magazines and over 8,500 pieces of ammunition, Nazi memorabilia, and drugs. Allegedly, the dogs were bred and trained for illegal dog fighting. Local authorities described the case as a part of a larger problem with right-wing extremism in Upper Austria.

weapon_description: Carbine-type long weapon with ammunition, 3D printer
description: A 26-year-old right-wing extremist was arrested after posting threats online and procuring weapons. The search for the perpetrator began in 2022 when he stole a sign or poster from the Equality Council of the Lloret de Mar municipality. In the same time period, the perpetrator appeared in an anonymous video online where he made threatening statements towards the Equality Council. During the investigation, the police was able to identify the perpetrator who had been active in social networks between 2021 and 2023. Under several anonymous profiles the perpetrator had transmitted hate speech and threats towards the LGBTQ+ community, ethnic minorities, and Catalan separatism. The perpetrator was arrested in September 2023. The police found a carbine-type long weapon with ammunition, ultra-right-wing texts and writings, a 3D printer, the stolen sign or poster from the Equality Council, and various symbols of the Franco dictatorship period. Information analysts stated that the perpetrator had the necessary skills and knowledge, as well as easy access to material to be able to manufacture functional firearms. According to sources involved in the investigation, although the man had not carried out violent actions, he had become radicalized and his content was increasingly hostile. The perpetrator was accused of a crime against the exercise of fundamental rights and public freedoms and a crime of illegal possession of weapons.

A 40-year-old woman was subjected to an acid attack by an unknown woman, reportedly because she was politically active. The victim was hanging up election posters for the Green party in a metro station when the perpetrator suddenly appeared. The perpetrator threatened and racially insulted the victim, before pulling up a bottle of highly concentrated vinegar essence out of her pocket and splashed it in the direction of the victim. The victim barely managed to evade the acidic substance and was unharmed. The perpetrator fled. The police investigated for attempted assault.

weapon_description: Knife, road sign, bag filled with bottles and beating/kicking
description: A 32-year-old man was subjected to a knife attack by a stranger. The victim and his 35-year-old girlfriend were walking on the street in the evening when they were both racially insulted. The perpetrator began beating the 32-year-old with a bag filled with glass bottles, before ramming a road sign in the victim's stomach. The victim fled into the road and fell where the perpetrator continued to hit him several times in the head. When a passer-by came to help, the perpetrator took out a knife and attacked the victim again. The victim suffered cut injuries to his hand and bruising and was treated in the hospital. The state security police took over the investigation.

A group of people of Somali background were attacked by a 29-year-old man. The perpetrator passed the victims on the street and racially insulted them, which led to a confrontation. The perpetrator hit a 41-year-old woman with a beer bottle so that it broke. He then attacked an 18-year-old from the group of victims with the broken beer bottle. Four people were injured, including a 12-year-old. The perpetrator walked away but was arrested shortly after. He was charged for grievous bodily harm, among other things.

Two men of foreign backgrounds were attacked by two strangers while walking on the street. They were racially insulted and beaten with brass knuckles, resulting in one of the victims being slightly injured.

60 far-right activists tried approaching the venue where a conference for a local project to house asylum seekers took place. The police spotted the perpetrators, some with batons, baseball bats and balaclavas, on their way to the conference grounds. Six of the men, aged between 21 and 29, were charged with carrying a weapon and "participation in an armed group with a view to preparing one or more acts against people or damage to property". The police had taken much precaution before this event, checking 550 vehicles, and using drone surveillance around the conference. The town had previously experienced many far-right demonstrations as a response to the project. A former mayor of the town resigned after being subjected to an arson attack in his home, an act which was attributed to the far-right (case does not meet inclusion criteria).

weapon_description: Two explosive devices, several long guns (only partly functional), several small-caliber weapons, a crossbow, several daggers, and live ammunition
description: The police searched five properties on three locations of central members of the right-wing extremist group "Hammerskins" in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern. This state was at the center of nationwide raids against Hammerskins. The group had been banned nationwide a week before, due to the members' anti-constitutional outlook. The police seized two explosive devices, several long guns (only partly functional), several small-caliber weapons, a crossbow, several daggers, live ammunition, practice ammunition, and a four-digit number of Euro. The police did not want to comment on a possibly functional grenade. In addition, the police found several tons of Nazi memorabilia and gear. The perpetrators were investigated for violations of the Weapons Act, War Weapons Control Act and Explosives Act.

weapon_description: Bombs, modified firearms, incendiary devices, and cutting and stabbing weapons
description: A 25-year-old woman was arrested after plotting to commit acts of terrorism. The perpetrator was living in a social housing facility when the police was notified that she was in possession of suspicious documents and objects. The investigation revealed that the perpetrator had planned to commit terrorist attacks on the town hall of Fellbach and the Waiblingen district court, presumably for anti-state and xenophobic reasons. The perpetrator had singled out certain employees of the two institutions, and wanted to kill or injure as many people as possible. She planned to use bombs, incendiary devices, cutting and stabbing weapons, and wanted to commit a shooting spree with modified firearms. At the time of the arrest, she had illegally acquired blank-firing and gas-pressure pistols, cutting and stabbing weapons. She had also manufactured black powder for pipe bombs. The perpetrator was charged with preparing an act of violence endangering the state, preparing an explosive crime, and violating the Weapons Act.

weapon_description: 100 rifles, pistols and revolvers, 250 kilograms of ammunition, and one kilogram explosive material
description: The police raided the home of a middle-aged couple who were members of the Reichsbürger movement. The police had previously withdrawn the perpetrators' weapons, hunting, and explosives permit due to their ideological affiliation, and demanded the perpetrators to surrender their arsenal of weapons. When this did not happen, a raid occurred early in the morning. The police blew out the front door using explosives. The female perpetrator was injured and sent to the hospital. The police sized 150 weapons, including 100 fully functional rifles, pistols, and revolvers. Furthermore, 250 kilograms of ammunition and one kilogram of explosive material were also secured.

A 44-year-old photographer was attacked by a group of fascists aged between 28 to 39 years old. Three of the perpetrators under investigation are members of CasaPound, while one is believed to be associated with the Ukrainian neo-fascist group Azov Battalion. The victim was wearing a jacket with a pin with an anti-fascist logo. The altercation began when the perpetrators insulted the victim by saying "piece of shit, what's this jacket, take off your badge". The situation escalated when the perpetrators threatened the victim with a knife and proceeded to physically attack him, kicking and punching him before taking his jacket from him. The victim received hospital treatment and was diagnosed with severe head trauma. Following an investigation using video surveillance footage, four men were arrested, while a fifth individual is currently under investigation. However, CasaPound did not officially claimed responsibility for the incident.

Police arrested and dismantled the Spanish network of the far-right group Combat 18, consisting of 16 individuals. The police had surveilled them for two years before the arrest and believed that they were preparing for violent action. 13 men and 3 women were detained, all aged between 29 and 49 and living in various locations in Spain. The group was organized through a hierarchical structure and had connections to Combat 18 members in other countries. The French group of Blood and Honor was helping to fund the group. They were working on recruiting militants, supplying firearms, and planning future violent actions. They wished to attack mosques, Jewish interests, or anti-fascist groups. The perpetrators were trying to procure firearms through contact with Combat 18 headquarters but had not managed to obtain any at the time of the arrest. Upon searching their residences, the police found 50 bladed weapons, 10 simulated weapons, publications of right-wing ideology and a manual on how to make explosives. The perpetrators were discovered in 2022 when intelligence services located them online.

A punk, who was begging in the subway station, was repeatedly insulted in a social-chauvinistic/classist manner by a 42-year-old man. The perpetrator then attacked the victim with  a cutter knife. A passerby gave the victim first aid to the 3-4 cm wound on his hand, inflifted by the perpetrator. The victim was treated in the hospital.

weapon_description: Metal shields, wooden sticks, and beating/kicking
description: Neo-Nazis from the group Propatria attacked people who were traveling with the metro train. The incident happened shortly after an afternoon of civil unrest in relation to the 10-year anniversary of the murders of two members of the Golden Dawn. Far-right activists had called for a pan-European memorial in Athens. Fascist commemoration rallies were met by anti-fascist counterdemonstrations. The perpetrators entered the metro train wagon and began shouting Pro Patria slogans and harassing those believed to be anti-fascists. The perpetrators attacked people with metal shields and wooden sticks, targeting leftist youths and immigrants. One of the perpetrators then took out a can of what appeared to be gasoline and thew the liquid around while others shouted, "burn them!" The liquid later turned out to be water. The riot police intervened and fired tear gas inside the metro wagon. Five of the victims were injured, including a young woman who was treated in the hospital for head injuries. 60 people were detained, and 13 were arrested for various offences after the incident.

Police found explosives and ammunition at a 32-year-old man's home. A witness had alerted the police after seeing rifle barrels in a parked utility vehicle. The perpetrator's apartment and a vehicle were then searched. For security reasons, the police's special intervention unit went to the scene and the neighboring homes were evacuated. The search of the apartment yielded no results, but ammunition and detonators were seized in the vehicle. These were destroyed on site because they posed a danger. The perpetrator was already known to the police as he had thrown firecrackers at officers during a protest against Covid-19 measures (case does not meet inclusion criteria) and been arrested for having explosives in his home shortly after (see caseID 2021-12-18-3). According to one media outlet, the perpetrator's appearances on social networks revealed a clear right-wing extremist profile. He was arrested for illegal possession of weapons. The anti-terrorist unit of the judicial police was tasked with continuing the investigation. The perpetrator was placed in preventative detention and charged of illegal transport and possession of ammunition and explosives prohibited under the Weapons and Ammunition Act.

A 30-year-old Jewish woman was stabbed by an un unidentified individual. The perpetrator rang the victim's doorbell, posing as a delivery man. When the victim opened the door, she found herself face-to-face with the perpetrator, who was armed with a knife. The perpetrator stabbed her twice in the abdomen before fleeing. The victim was treated in the hospital and survived. According to the investigation, a swastika was found carved in on the victim's door after the attack. However, it was not possible to put an exact date to the creation of the symbol. A mezuzah (a Jewish object of worship) had been standing on the victim's doorstep at the time of the attack. No arrests were made. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

weapon_description: Materials for making a TATP explosive device, unspecified category B and C firearmes
description: Ten people, aged 17 to 60, were arrested for illegal possession of weapons. Four of them were indicted, among them a soldier and a former police officer. These indicted perpetrators had strong commitment to far-right ideology. Police found more than a hundred pieces of weapons and ammunition in their homes. Firearms and elements used in manufacturing TATP explosives (a common type of IED) were found. The firearms found were category B and C. The perpetrators were also suspected of acquisition, possession, and transfer of category A weapons. The perpetrators claimed that they were obtaining weapons for protection and defense purposes. They had uttered comments which were extremely hostile towards immigrants and Jews, and some expressed a hatred of leftists. The perpetrators had been under investigation for criminal terrorist association by the General Directorate of Internal Security, and the search was conducted after investigators realized that the 20-year-old in the group had received weapons and/or ammunition from a soldier by mail.

weapon_description: Materials for pipe bombs and Molotov cocktails
description: A man and a woman, aged 23 and 21, were arrested and suspected of preparing bomb attacks, participating in a far-right terrorist group and inciting violence. Simultaneous searches were carried on at least two locations in Belgium, but also locations in Italy, Germany, Croatia, Romania, and Lithuania (cases do not meet inclusion criteria). Authorities said they had indicators that showed there was an increased risk that some of them would take action soon, and that the operation hindered a terrorist act. The searches lead to five arrests in total. Police found materials for pipe bombs and Molotov cocktails, Nazi flags, swastikas, and other objects bearing the image of right-wing extremist ideology. The perpetrators were arrested as a consequence of the searches. The perpetrators had incited terrorist acts online and recruited new members. They also distributed manuals for 3D printed firearms. The male perpetrator was suspected of being the leader of a far-right group that was linked to The Base (a group founded in the US that aim to create a white ethnostate by using violence). The male perpetrator had shared a video of Nazi soldiers on his Facebook page. He had also shared an image of a man waving a flag of the far-right organization De Voorpos, and there was evidence that the perpetrators were active on various far-right encrypted online platforms.

Around 50 far-right individuals attacked a pro-Palestinian conference following an anti-racist demonstration in the city. About 100 attendees were present when the attackers, armed with iron bars and baseball bats, attempted to force their way in. Some attendees were beaten while trying to lock the doors. When they couldn't enter, the attackers threw firecrackers at the windows. The victims barricaded the doors with tables and chairs, preventing further access. Seven people were injured, three of which were taken to the hospital. The far-right group "Guignol squad" claimed responsibility, and one suspect was arrested.

A trans woman was unprovokedly attacked on the street by four men. The perpetrators pulled the victim’s hair and forced her to the ground. The victim landed on her tailbone and received several blows to the face, jaw and temples. She was also kicked in the stomach, ribs and knees. The attackers shouted, “stupid tranny” and “fucking tranny” at the victim during the attack. The perpetrators escaped. The victim spent a week in the hospital with a traumatic brain injury and other injuries. The incident sparked demonstrations against the rise in queer and transphobic violence in Pankow committed by right-wing extremist actors (due to lack of information, other cases are not included). Pankow was known as a stronghold for neo-Nazis in Berlin. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

An 18-year-old neo-Nazi was arrested on suspicion of planning a serious act of violence endangering the state. According to the investigation that had been ongoing for months, the perpetrator had a solidified violent, anti-Semitic, and right-wing extremist attitude. The perpetrator had repeatedly threatened to kill people as part of the pursuit of political goals, in online forums. The police confiscated weapons and ammunition, as well as digital storage media. The perpetrator did not pose any acute danger but tried to gain access to a 3D-printer, a tool commonly used for the illegal manufacture of shooting weapons. The police stated that they had prevented an attack plan in the early stages. The perpetrator was accused of "preparing an attack on the lives of others" and of violating the Weapons Act. Investigations are ongoing (2023).

A 29-year-old gardener was stabbed in the throat with a box cutter by a 75-year-old man. The incident occurred outside the house of the perpetrator's daughter. The incident started when the perpetrator realized that his parked car was blocked by the victim's van. The perpetrator said "Bou***ule!" [derogatory word for Arab people]. This is my place, donkey". The victim was busy loading the van with branches. The man continued to racially insult him, screaming "Bou***ules" multiple times. The perpetrator then retrieved a box cutter from his vehicle. The victim took out his phone and videotaped the perpetrator. The perpetrator leaned forward with the cutter in his hand, to which the victim replied, "Go ahead, stab me with the cutter, everything is being filmed". The perpetrator then launched the box cutter into his throat, causing a 15 cm wound. The perpetrator fled by car. The victim was taken care of by emergency services and the perpetrator was later arrested.

A man was beaten in the parking lot of a supermarket by three strangers. The victim was on a break from working at the supermarket and was sitting in his car. A car, where the three perpetrators were seated, parked next to him. One of the perpetrators slammed the car door into the victim's vehicle, to which the victim responded by getting out of his car. The perpetrators then attacked the victim, threw him to the ground, and severely beat him. The perpetrators called the victim a "dirty piece of shit n*****" while kicking him. The victim eventually managed to flee into the supermarket, and the attackers escaped. The victim went to the hospital with a broken rib and bruising. The perpetrators have not been identified.

Following the death of a 16-year-old boy who was killed by a gang of non-French origins in Crépol, the far-right was arranging several demonstrations in the region (see e.g. CaseID 2023-11-26). In Romans-sur-Isère, far-right activists attacked the police forces. Around 80 far-right activists were shouting "France belongs to us" and "Justice for Thomas". Several newspapers reported that the perpetrators were roaming the streets to attack the inhabitants in the area where some of those suspected of murdering the 16-year-old allegedly lived. The police forces who were present at the rally reported that firecrackers and stones were being thrown at them. Some of the perpetrators also carried baseball bats. Five police officers were injured. 20 perpetrators were arrested. During their trial, there were messages found in a Telegram group saying, "When we come with batons, we do not come to defend a cause but to attack". Six of the perpetrators were sentenced to between six and 10 months in prison.

Following the death of a 16-year-old boy who was killed by a gang of non-French origin in Crépol, the far-right was arranging several demonstrations in the region (see e.g. CaseID 2023-11-25). The far-right political party "Reconquête" was arranging a demonstration where around 130 people attended in a procession. One the sidelines of the procession, participants of the demonstration attacked a journalist. The victim had intended to interview the perpetrators but was insulted instead. The victim’s phone was snatched out of his hand, he then fell over and kicked in the head while on the ground. The victim was injured in the head and transported to the hospital where he received stitches. The victim filed a complaint against the perpetrators.

weapon_description: Explosive precursors, firearms, 34 bottles of acid, brass knuckles, knives and defense sprays
description: A group of 11 individuals were arrested by the police after having been under surveillance for two years. The perpetrators were considered leaders of what the media referred to as a paramilitary organization based on Nazi ideology. The association had a hierarchical structure with military ranks, an anthem, and a flag. One of the perpetrators were prominent online with around 2800 followers. The perpetrators intended to create an army, and urged followers to arm themselves, with several members obtaining weapons licenses and acquiring rifles, shotguns, and pistols. The perpetrators spread propaganda against women, the LGBTQ+ community and immigrants. Upon searching the perpetrators' residences, the police found ten firearms, explosive precursors, 34 bottles of acid, brass knuckles, knives, and defense sprays.

Two individuals of North African origin were attacked by around ten members of the far-right. The victims had been drinking and was on the street near a bar when the incident happened. They were attacked for no apparent reason. One of the victims was seriously injured and had to be hospitalized as a result of the attack. One of the perpetrators, who had a known association to the far-right (Génération Identitaire), was arrested. The investigation established that the attack was unprovoked, and that the attack had no other motive than the North African origin of the two victims. Motive not explicitly stated, but sufficiently evident to be included.

weapon_description: Toxic mixture of ammonia with bleach, several firearms, ammunition and butterfly knives
description: The police carried out house searches at three addresses in May 2023 and later arrested a 20-year-old man with right-wing extremist views, who had posted about committing toxic attacks in online chat groups. He was also accused of calling for right-wing terrorist attacks and distributing or providing instructions on how to build bombs or weapons from 3D printers. The police found several firearms, ammunition, butterfly knives, gas masks, Nazi memorabilia such as a Wehrmacht uniform, a Reich war flag and a swastika armband. He had also acquired instructions on how to make bombs and how to make firearms. In online chat groups connected to the far-right group Feuerkrieg Division, he had written "Should I pray with the filthy Muslims or mingle with the Jews when they hold one of their meetings and give it an explosive twist?" In this context, he thought about mixing ammonia with bleach and throwing this toxic mixture, which releases chlorine gas, into a larger group of people. At another point, the perpetrator said that soon "the time will come" to "put the Jews in their place". The perpetrator first came to the attention of authorities in 2020 when he was 17 years old and active in Feuerkrieg Division. The group members repeatedly discussed plans to attack mosques and synagogues, and the perpetrator had in addition to outlining possible attacks himself, encouraged others to execute attacks. He had especially expressed hate towards Muslims and Jews. The perpetrator was temporarily released in February 2024 and instructed to undergo the "Dialogue instead of Hate" program.

A man in his 40s was attacked by another man around 2.15am. According to the police, the victim sustained serious facial injuries. The attack is being treated as a racially motivated hate crime. There is limited information available at the time of reporting.
